title: Efficacy of a volatile pyrethroid spatial emanator (SE) in reducing Anopheles host-seeking in outdoor kitchens in Southern Zambia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a pyrethroid spatial emanator for malaria vector control with reported outcome results on Anopheles host-seeking reduction.
population: households with outdoor kitchens; local mosquito collectors conducting human landing collections
primary_outcome: Anopheles host-landing/host-seeking rate measured by human landing collection
impact_summary: Spatial emanator devices reduced Anopheles host-seeking activity in outdoor kitchens by approximately 65-70%, though efficacy declined to 20-25% by four weeks after deployment and was not significant during early evening hours (18:00-21:00).
transmission_setting: low malaria transmission, outdoor biting vectors

title: Efficacy of ceiling-mounted mosquito nets for malaria vector control in a Peruvian Amazon riverine community: A stepped-wedge cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results (entomological endpoints) testing a malaria vector-control intervention (ceiling-mounted nets) in humans.
population: Households in a riverine Amazonian community
primary_outcome: Indoor and peridomestic Anopheles mosquito density (counts, bites per person per night, bites per person per hour) measured via human landing catches
impact_summary: Ceiling-mounted mosquito nets significantly reduced indoor Anopheles mosquito counts and biting rates but had no significant effect on peridomestic mosquito indices.
effect_metric: percent reduction in indoor Anopheles counts

title: The role of seasonal malaria chemoprevention in the effect of azithromycin on child mortality: A secondary analysis of the CHAT cluster randomized clinical trial.
screening_reason: Secondary analysis of CHAT, a completed cluster-randomized trial with reported mortality outcome results; azithromycin and SMC are malaria-relevant interventions in humans; not early-phase.
population: children under 5
primary_outcome: All-cause mortality among children under 5, stratified by SMC season and coverage
impact_summary: Mass azithromycin distribution was associated with reduced child mortality during SMC season and in areas with lower SMC coverage, but the interaction between AZ effect and SMC season/coverage was not statistically significant.
effect_estimate: 0.77 (SMC season); 0.89 (non-SMC season); 0.73 (<80% SMC coverage); 1.0 (≥80% SMC coverage)

title: HLA-G 14 bp polymorphism: Implications and its associated risk to malaria severity among iron-fortified Ghanaian infants and young children.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported results examining iron fortification (a malaria-relevant intervention) and malaria severity outcomes in children in a malaria-endemic region.
population: infants and young children aged 6-36 months consuming semi-solid foods
primary_outcome: malaria severity and anaemia development associated with HLA-G 14 bp polymorphism among iron-fortified children
impact_summary: Iron-fortified children carrying the HLA-G 14 bp insertion/deletion polymorphism had an elevated risk of severe malaria, which in turn predisposed them to anaemia.

title: Physical integrity and residual bio-efficacy of PBO-pyrethroid synergist-treated and pyrethroid-only LLINs after 1.5 years of field use in Western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing PBO-LLINs and pyrethroid-only LLINs (a malaria vector-control intervention) with measurements of physical integrity and residual bio-efficacy over 18 months.
design: prospective observational field study, cross-sectional household surveys
population: households with LLINs distributed for malaria control
primary_outcome: physical integrity (proportionate hole index) and residual bio-efficacy (mosquito mortality) of LLINs over 18 months
impact_summary: Both PBO-pyrethroid and pyrethroid-only LLINs showed significant declines in physical integrity and bioefficacy over 18 months, with PBO-LLINs maintaining better physical integrity but both net types losing effectiveness against susceptible and resistant Anopheles gambiae.
effect_metric: percentage of torn nets and mosquito mortality
effect_estimate: 45.2% pyrethroid-LLINs vs 21.8% PBO-LLINs torn at 18 months; mortality dropped from 97.6% to 18.4% (pyrethroid) and 98.6% to 18.5% (PBO) against susceptible mosquitoes, and from 36.9% to 6.8% (pyrethroid) and 55.6% to 11.8% (PBO) against resistant mosquitoes
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region with widespread pyrethroid resistance

title: R21/Matrix-M malaria vaccine drives diverse immune responses in pre-exposed adults: insights from a phase IIb controlled human malaria infection trial.
screening_reason: Published Phase IIb RCT of malaria vaccine (R21/Matrix-M) with reported immune response outcomes in controlled human malaria infection trial.
design: controlled human malaria infection (CHMI), phase IIb clinical trial
population: semi-immune healthy adult volunteers with varying prior malaria exposure
primary_outcome: Characterization of vaccine-induced humoral and cellular immune responses (antibody isotypes/subclasses, memory B cells, circulating Tfh cells) following R21/Matrix-M vaccination and CHMI challenge
impact_summary: R21/Matrix-M vaccination induced broad, heterogeneous, and sustained antibody and memory B cell responses along with increased circulating Tfh cells, which may contribute to protection against malaria in previously exposed adults.
transmission_setting: coastal Kenya, malaria-endemic setting with prior exposure

title: Feasibility and effectiveness of tailored interventions for two populations at high-risk of malaria in Senegal: Koranic school children and gold miners.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results for malaria prevention interventions (LLINs and case management) in high-risk populations in Senegal.
population: Koranic school children (talibés) and gold miners
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum infection prevalence (by RDT and qPCR) and self-reported LLIN usage
impact_summary: The intervention package significantly reduced malaria prevalence and increased LLIN use among talibés but showed no measurable effect among gold miners.
effect_estimate: -12.6 percentage points (RDT prevalence, talibés); +44.0 percentage points (net use, talibés)
transmission_setting: high transmission season, high-risk populations in Kaolack and Saraya, Senegal

title: LLIN Evaluation in Uganda Project
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria vector-control intervention (LLINs) with reported outcome results (malaria incidence and parasite prevalence).
interventions_raw: long lasting insecticidal nets with alpha-cypermethrin + pyriproxyfen (PPF LLIN, Royal Guard)); long lasting insecticidal nets with deltamethrin + piperonyl butoxide (PBO LLIN, PermaNet 3.0)); Social behaviour change communication
comparator: pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen LLINs (Royal Guard) vs pyrethroid-PBO LLINs (PermaNet 3.0), active comparator
population: residents of all ages in communities surrounding public health facilities
primary_outcome: Malaria Incidence
impact_summary: There was no evidence of a difference in malaria incidence or parasite prevalence between pyrethroid-PBO and pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen LLINs two years after mass distribution in Uganda, and LLIN ownership was low in both arms.
transmission_setting: national LLIN distribution campaign across 32 districts of Uganda, malaria-endemic

title: Indoor Residual Spraying With Fludora Fusion for Malaria Control in Pyrethroid-Resistant Areas of Gujarat, India: A Community-Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial with reported entomological outcomes evaluating an IRS intervention (Fludora Fusion) for malaria vector control in a pyrethroid-resistant area.
population: villages/houses in pyrethroid-resistant malaria vector areas
primary_outcome: Residual efficacy of insecticide on sprayed surfaces and entomological indices (indoor resting density, human landing collections, pyrethrum spray collections, exit trap collections) of Anopheles culicifacies
impact_summary: Fludora Fusion showed longer residual efficacy (6 months) than bendiocarb (3-4 months) and reduced indoor resting density, parous rate, and entomological inoculation rate of Anopheles culicifacies compared to bendiocarb-sprayed houses.
effect_estimate: declined from 1.275 (prespray) to 0.5225 (Fludora Fusion arm) and 0.3802 (bendiocarb arm) postspray
transmission_setting: pyrethroid-resistant malaria vector areas, rural Gujarat, India

title: Targeted distribution of long-lasting insecticidal nets by community health workers to sustain household coverage: A pilot feasibility study in Western Uganda.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT (two villages randomized to control/intervention arms) with reported outcome results (LLIN coverage, net usage, malaria testing); the primary intervention is LLIN distribution for malaria prevention, a core vector-control strategy.
design: pilot feasibility study, cluster-randomized (village-level, two villages), non-blinded
comparator: standard care (regular CHW duties without targeted LLIN distribution)
population: households with children under five, community health worker-served villages
primary_outcome: Feasibility and impact of targeted LLIN distribution on household universal coverage and LLIN use among children under 5
impact_summary: Targeted LLIN distribution by community health workers increased the proportion of households meeting universal coverage and the proportion of children under 5 sleeping under an LLIN in the intervention village, while both measures declined in the control village.
effect_metric: change in percentage of households meeting universal coverage
effect_estimate: increase from 4.0% to 6.5% (intervention) vs decrease from 7.8% to 1.8% (control)
follow_up: not specified (post mass distribution campaign period)
safety_summary: No adverse events reported; CHWs reported no increased burden from the intervention and expressed favorable opinions.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Incorporating Actellic® 300 CS into Soil Wall Plaster for Control of Malaria Vectors in Rural Northeastern Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector control intervention (Actellic in hut decoration) with reported entomological and safety outcomes in humans.
comparator: standard indoor residual spraying (IRS) and untreated control huts
population: rural households in mud-walled huts
primary_outcome: Malaria vector density and feeding rate (entomological indices) at 1.5, 3, and 6 months post-intervention
impact_summary: Huts treated with Hut Decoration for Malaria Control (HD4MC) and IRS showed significantly reduced malaria vector density and feeding rates compared to control huts, with HD4MC being safe and comparably effective to IRS.
effect_metric: reduction in vector density and feeding rate
safety_summary: No significant reduction in acetylcholinesterase activity at 1.5 and 24 hours post exposure; no serious adverse events among household occupants exposed to Actellic 300 CS.

title: Effectiveness of Monthly Versus Two-Dose Regimen of Sulphadoxine-Pyrimethamine for Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy in Southeastern Nigeria: A Randomised Controlled Trial.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results comparing two malaria prevention regimens (IPTp-SP) in pregnant women; primary focus is malaria prevention in humans.
population: pregnant women at gestational ages between 13-24 weeks attending antenatal clinic
primary_outcome: Prevalence of placental and maternal peripheral malaria parasitaemia
impact_summary: Monthly IPT-SP significantly reduced placental and peripheral malaria parasitaemia, maternal anaemia, and neonatal parasitaemia/anaemia compared to the standard two-dose regimen, though low birth weight incidence did not differ.

title: Evaluating artesunate monotherapy and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine as potential antimalarial options for prevaccination radical cures during future malaria vaccine field efficacy trials.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial regimens for malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and clinical malaria incidence.
population: children aged 1.5-12 years
primary_outcome: PCR-confirmed clearance of P. falciparum infection at day 21 post-treatment
impact_summary: Both artesunate monotherapy and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine effectively cleared P. falciparum infections, with artesunate showing earlier time to reinfection and higher incidence of clinical malaria but likely minimal interference with vaccine efficacy evaluation.
effect_metric: proportion free of P. falciparum infection at day 21
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond drugs having good safety and efficacy profiles; no major adverse events reported

title: Genetic Characterization of Plasmodium falciparum Histidine-Rich Protein 2 Deletions and Their Impact on Malaria Interventions in Odisha, India.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating malaria interventions (mass screening and treatment with ITNs and IRS) against a primary malaria focus; diagnostic escape is integral to elimination strategy.
design: observational genetic characterization study with modeling of intervention impact
comparator: mass screening and treatment by RDT alone
population: individuals in malaria-endemic villages with subpatent P. falciparum infections
primary_outcome: prevalence of pfhrp2 gene deletions and relative risk of infection under mass screening and treatment interventions
impact_summary: Mass screening and treatment combined with additional vector control interventions reduced the relative risk of infection for both pfhrp2-deleted and pfhrp2-intact P. falciparum parasites compared with mass screening and treatment by RDT alone.

title: Safety and efficacy of the blood-stage malaria vaccine RH5.1/Matrix-M in Burkina Faso: interim results of a double-blind, randomised, controlled, phase 2b trial in children.
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported interim efficacy results (55% and 40% vaccine efficacy) for a malaria vaccine in children; phase 2b is not early-phase.
population: children aged 5-17 months
primary_outcome: Safety and reactogenicity of RH5.1/Matrix-M; and protective efficacy against clinical malaria (time to first episode) from 14 days to 6 months after third vaccination
impact_summary: RH5.1/Matrix-M vaccine given in a delayed third-dose regimen showed 55% vaccine efficacy against clinical malaria and was safe and well tolerated, while the monthly regimen showed 40% efficacy that was not statistically significant.
safety_summary: Favourable safety profile; most adverse events were mild, most common being local swelling and fever; no serious adverse events reported
funder: The European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership, the UK Medical Research Council, the National Institute for Health and Care Research Oxford Biomedical Research Centre, the Division of Intramural Research, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, the US Agency for International Development, and the Wellcome Trust

title: Long-lasting residual efficacy of a new indoor residual spraying product, VECTRON™ T500 (broflanilide), against pyrethroid-resistant malaria vectors and its acceptance in a community trial in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Phase III RCT of a malaria vector control intervention (indoor residual spraying with broflanilide) that has reported outcome results including efficacy, mortality rates, and safety data.
comparator: Actellic® 300CS (pirimiphos-methyl IRS, active comparator) and untreated control
population: Community households in Vallée du Kou; wild and laboratory Anopheles mosquito strains used for bioassay assessment
primary_outcome: Residual efficacy (mosquito mortality) of VECTRON™ T500 versus Actellic® 300CS measured via WHO wall cone bioassays over time
impact_summary: VECTRON™ T500 achieved 100% mortality in susceptible and resistant Anopheles strains for 12 months post-spraying, outperforming Actellic® 300CS which induced <80% mortality, and showed non-inferiority to the standard reference product with no reported adverse events.
effect_metric: Relative risk of mortality (delayed mortality after 72-h holding period)
transmission_setting: Malaria-endemic area with seasonal transmission, pyrethroid-resistant vectors
safety_summary: No adverse events were reported in households sprayed with VECTRON™ T500
funder: Mitsui Chemicals Crop & Life Solutions, Inc.

title: Azithromycin in severe malaria bacterial co-infection in African children (TABS-PKPD): a phase II randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Phase II RCT with reported outcome results investigating azithromycin dosing in African children with severe malaria and bacterial co-infection; malaria is the primary focus.
comparator: active comparator (different azithromycin dose arms) with concurrent non-severe malaria control group
population: Ugandan children with severe malaria (and non-severe malaria controls)
primary_outcome: Change in C-reactive protein (CRP) at 72 hours and microbiological cure at 7 days, alone and as composite with 7-day and 90-day survival
impact_summary: There was no evidence that azithromycin exposure was associated with reduction in CRP, and no clear dose-dependent difference in outcomes among the 10, 15, and 20 mg/kg arms.
safety_summary: No major safety concerns highlighted; CRP reduced across all dosing arms by 72 hours, with only a few events contributing to the composite survival/microbiological cure outcome.

title: The effect of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine on vaccine-specific responses among schoolchildren in rural Uganda (POPVAC B): a double-blind, randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Double-blind individually randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPT with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in humans with fully reported outcome results on vaccine responses; malaria suppression is the primary intervention focus.
population: schoolchildren aged 9-17 years
primary_outcome: Vaccine-specific responses at week 8 (BCG IFNγ ELISpot, yellow fever neutralising antibody, typhoid IgG, HPV-16/18) and, for tetanus-diphtheria, at week 52
impact_summary: Monthly IPT with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine reduced malaria prevalence but did not improve peak vaccine-specific responses compared with placebo.
safety_summary: Safety population comprised all randomly allocated participants; no specific adverse events described in abstract.

title: Intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy and infant growth: a mediation analysis of a randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing IPTp regimens (DP vs SP) for malaria prevention in pregnancy, with infant growth outcomes measured.
population: infants born to mothers enrolled in a trial of monthly IPTp for malaria in pregnancy
primary_outcome: Infant growth (length-for-age Z-score and weight-for-length Z-score) from 0 to 12 months
impact_summary: SP increased mean LAZ from birth through 4 months while DP increased mean WLZ from 2 to 8 months compared to each other among infants of multigravidae, with different mediating biological pathways, but no differences were observed among primigravidae.
effect_metric: mean difference in Z-scores (LAZ and WLZ)
effect_estimate: SP increased LAZ by 0.18-0.28 Z; DP increased WLZ by 0.11-0.28 Z
funder: Stanford Center for Innovation in Global Health, Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation

title: Why does malaria transmission continue at high levels despite universal vector control? Quantifying persistent malaria transmission by Anopheles funestus in Western Province, Zambia.
screening_reason: Phase III cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results; primary purpose is malaria vector control intervention in humans.
design: secondary analysis of a phase III cluster randomized trial; observational cohort with entomological surveillance
population: children aged 1-14 years
primary_outcome: human behaviour-adjusted entomological inoculation rate (EIR)
impact_summary: Despite high ITN coverage and use, children in Western Province, Zambia continue to experience substantial residual malaria transmission from Anopheles funestus, sufficient to sustain high malaria burden.
effect_metric: personal protective efficacy of ITN against An. funestus bites
transmission_setting: high, seasonal malaria transmission with universal vector control (ITNs) in place

title: Evaluation of bio-efficacy of field-aged novel long-lasting insecticidal nets (PBO, chlorfenapyr or pyriproxyfen combined with pyrethroid) against Anopheles gambiae (s.s.) in Tanzania.
journal: Current research in parasitology & vector-borne diseases
screening_reason: Cluster randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (bio-efficacy data over 36 months) evaluating next-generation long-lasting insecticidal nets for malaria vector control.
population: field-aged long-lasting insecticidal nets used in community households
primary_outcome: Bio-efficacy of nets measured by WHO cone bioassay and tunnel test mortality/sterility against susceptible and resistant An. gambiae (s.s.) strains over 36 months
impact_summary: Next-generation nets (Interceptor G2, Olyset Plus, Royal Guard) showed higher bio-efficacy than standard pyrethroid-only Interceptor nets against resistant mosquitoes, but this superiority diminished over time and was not sustained for the full three years.
effect_metric: mortality (72h tunnel test) and sterility rate
effect_estimate: Interceptor G2 mortality 52-20%; Olyset Plus mortality 84-33%; Royal Guard sterility <10% after 12 months

title: Artemisinin combination therapy at delivery to prevent postpartum malaria: A randomised open-label controlled trial.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment intervention in humans with reported outcome results (slide-positive malaria incidence at 6 months); not early-phase.
population: healthy postpartum mothers immediately following delivery
primary_outcome: Incidence of slide-positive malaria within 6 months of delivery
impact_summary: A course of artemisinin combination therapy given at delivery roughly halved the incidence of postpartum malaria compared to no treatment over 6 months.

title: Efficacy, Immunogenicity and Safety Study of GSK Biologicals' Candidate Malaria Vaccine Evaluating Different Dose Schedules in a Sporozoite Challenge Model in Healthy Malaria-naïve Adults
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (RTS,S) with reported efficacy and immunogenicity results in humans; Phase 2 is acceptable.
interventions_raw: RTS,S/AS01E; RTS,S/AS01B; Sporozoite-infected mosquitoes challenge.
comparator: Infectivity controls (unvaccinated challenge controls) and different RTS,S/AS01 dose schedules
population: Healthy malaria-naive adults
primary_outcome: Number of Subjects With at Least One Occurrence of Plasmodium Falciparum (P. Falciparum) Parasitemia for Each Vaccination Schedule Versus Infectivity Controls
impact_summary: Vaccine-induced antibody measures, particularly IgG1 NANP binding magnitude combined with serum NANP and N-junction Ig binding magnitude-avidity composite, were significant predictors of protection against controlled human malaria infection across RTS,S/AS01 trials.
effect_estimate: Odds ratios 2.6-3.1; ROC AUC combined predictor
transmission_setting: Controlled human malaria infection (sporozoite challenge model), non-endemic setting

title: Efficacy and Safety of KAF156 in Combination With LUM-SDF in Adults and Children With Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (KAF156 plus lumefantrine) with reported outcome results in adults and children; Phase II is appropriate.
place: Burkina Faso, Gabon, India, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Thailand, Uganda, Vietnam
countries: Burkina Faso; Gabon; India; Kenya; Mali; Mozambique; Thailand; Uganda; Vietnam
interventions_raw: KAF156; Coartem; Lumefantrine Solid Dispersion Formulation
population: adults, adolescents, and children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, body weight ≥10 kg
primary_outcome: Part A and Part B: Number of Participants With Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)-Corrected Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR) at Day 29
impact_summary: Ganaplacide combined with LUM-SDF was effective and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria, with drug exposures needed for efficacy achieved using 400 mg ganaplacide plus 960 mg lumefantrine once daily for 3 days under fasted conditions.
safety_summary: Ganaplacide-LUM-SDF was well tolerated; no notable increase in ganaplacide or lumefantrine exposure when co-administered in the PK run-in part.

title: Comparing approaches for chemoprevention for school-based malaria control in Malawi: an open label, randomized, controlled clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (Pf infection, clinical malaria, anaemia) evaluating school-based malaria chemoprevention in humans.
design: open-label, randomized, controlled, three-arm, individually randomized clinical trial
population: primary school students aged 5-19 years
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum infection detected by PCR 6-8 weeks after the final intervention
impact_summary: Both intermittent preventive treatment (IPT) and intermittent screening and treatment (IST) reduced the prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum infection compared to controls, but only IPT also reduced clinical malaria incidence and anaemia prevalence.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio for Pf infection
follow_up: 6-8 weeks after final intervention (approximately 6 months from start)
transmission_setting: peak malaria transmission season (February-June 2022), sub-Saharan Africa endemic setting
safety_summary: No between-group differences in number of serious adverse events were found.
funder: Doris Duke Charitable Foundation Clinical Scientist Development Award 2021191, U.S. NIH K24AI114996 & K23AI135076

title: Enhancing preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy: insights from a trial on targeted information transfer.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with published results of a malaria prevention intervention (targeted information about IPTp) in pregnant women.
population: pregnant women

title: Mosquitocidal efficacy and pharmacokinetics of single-dose ivermectin versus three-day dose regimen for malaria vector control compared with albendazole and no treatment: An open-label randomized controlled trial.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (mosquitocidal efficacy and pharmacokinetics) evaluating ivermectin for malaria vector control; phase not applicable for this type of intervention.
population: healthy volunteers
primary_outcome: Anopheles gambiae survival (time-to-event in days) after blood feeding up to 10 days after drug administration
impact_summary: Single-dose ivermectin showed superior and more durable mosquitocidal effect at 10 days compared with the three-day regimen, while albendazole had no mosquitocidal effect.
effect_metric: adjusted hazard ratio (mosquito mortality, single-dose ivermectin vs control)
safety_summary: All drug regimens were well-tolerated.

title: Population pharmacokinetics of amodiaquine and piperaquine in African pregnant women with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum infections.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin-based combination therapy (artesunate-amodiaquine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in pregnant women with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria that has reported pharmacokinetic outcome results.
population: pregnant women in second and third trimester with uncomplicated P. falciparum infections
primary_outcome: Population pharmacokinetic properties (exposure) of amodiaquine, desethylamodiaquine, and piperaquine in pregnant women
impact_summary: Exposure to desethylamodiaquine and piperaquine in pregnant women was similar to that in non-pregnant women, indicating no need for dose adjustment.
effect_metric: relative bioavailability change with gestational age

title: The bioefficacy of a novel VECTRON™ T500 indoor residual spray formulation in an experimental huts trial against Anopheles gambiae s.l. populations.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing a novel IRS formulation against malaria vectors, meeting all inclusion criteria for vector control intervention.
comparator: Klypson 500 WG (active comparator) and water (negative control)
population: laboratory-reared and wild Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Wall cone bioassay mortality and knockdown of An. gambiae s.l. over monthly evaluations post-spraying
impact_summary: VECTRON T500 showed extended efficacy (mortality over 80% for 6 months) against malaria vector mosquitoes on cement and mud walls, performing similarly to the positive control Klypson 500 WG.
effect_estimate: 97.8-98.1% (laboratory) and 83.2-95.0% (wild) with VECTRON T500; 89.6-99.0% (wild) and 99.0-99.3% (laboratory) with Klypson 500 WG
transmission_setting: malaria endemic areas of sub-Saharan Africa

title: Safety, Immunogenicity, and Protective Efficacy of Radiation Attenuated Plasmodium Falciparum NF54 Sporozoites (PfSPZ Vaccine) During Malaria Transmission Season in Healthy African Adult Women of Childbearing Potential in Mali
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (PfSPZ) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
interventions_raw: PfSPZ Vaccine; Normal Saline
population: MLSPZV3: adults aged 18-35 years; MLSPZV4: non-pregnant women aged 18-38 years anticipating conception within a year of enrolment
primary_outcome: Number of Participants With Adverse Events Within 7 Days After Each Vaccine Administration
impact_summary: PfSPZ Vaccine was safe and well tolerated, and in MLSPZV4 (with presumptive antimalarial treatment before dose one) showed significant efficacy against P falciparum parasitaemia, clinical malaria, and pregnancy malaria over two transmission seasons, whereas in MLSPZV3 (without presumptive antimalarial pretreatment before dose one) it showed no efficacy.
p_value: MLSPZV4: p=0.0069, p=0.0011, p<0.0001, p=0.029 for respective parasitaemia outcomes; not significant for MLSPZV3
safety_summary: PfSPZ Vaccine was safe and well tolerated; most related adverse events were mild (grade 1) and did not differ from saline; first trimester miscarriage was the most common serious adverse event with similar rates across groups; one unrelated maternal death from peritonitis and other unrelated serious adverse events (appendicitis, road traffic accident) occurred; no significant differences in maternal obstetric or neonatal outcomes between groups.
funder: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID)

title: Mosquito Shield™, a transfluthrin passive emanator, protects against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae sensu lato in central Benin.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing a spatial repellent vector-control intervention for malaria in humans; vector-control trials are not early-phase.
population: households in Ganhoua village, Zakpota District, central Benin
primary_outcome: human landing rate of wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae sensu lato
impact_summary: Mosquito Shield™, a transfluthrin passive emanator, significantly reduced human landing rates of pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. compared to placebo over the product's lifespan.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic, pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. vector population

title: Plasmodium falciparum infection status in children less than 10 years old under seasonal malaria chemoprevention and risk of clinical malaria in the Koulikoro health district, Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children with reported outcome results on clinical malaria incidence.
comparator: asymptomatic infected vs uninfected children under SMC
population: children under 10 years old receiving seasonal malaria chemoprevention
primary_outcome: incidence of clinical malaria over a four-week period following SMC drug administration, by infection status
impact_summary: Children with asymptomatic P. falciparum infection at the time of SMC drug intake had a significantly higher risk of subsequent clinical malaria compared to uninfected children.
p_value: p<0.001 (2019 infection prevalence by age); p=0.016 (2020 infection prevalence by age); p<0.001 (2019 survival time); p=0.01 (2020 survival time)
transmission_setting: highly seasonal malaria transmission, endemic area

title: Efficacy of Interceptor G2, Royal Guard and PermaNet 3.0 against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. from Za-Kpota, southern Benin: an experimental hut trial.
screening_reason: Experimental hut trial with randomized allocation comparing ITN products against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles; reported outcome results (mortality, blood-feeding inhibition, oviposition); malaria vector control is the primary focus.
population: wild free-flying Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Mosquito mortality (72-h) and blood-feeding inhibition
impact_summary: Interceptor G2 and Royal Guard nets showed superior efficacy against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae compared to standard PermaNet 2.0, while PermaNet 3.0 remained effective in this resistant setting.
transmission_setting: pyrethroid-resistant malaria vector area, southern Benin
safety_summary: Not reported (entomological study on mosquito mortality and behavior, not human safety)

title: A randomised trial of malaria vaccine R21/Matrix-M™ with and without antimalarial drugs in Thai adults.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (safety, tolerability, immunogenicity, pharmacokinetics) testing a malaria vaccine intervention (R21/Matrix-M™) in humans; not early-phase.
comparator: vaccination alone vs antimalarials alone vs combination
population: healthy Thai adult volunteers
primary_outcome: tolerability, safety, and immunogenicity/pharmacokinetic interactions between R21/Matrix-M vaccine and antimalarial drugs
impact_summary: The R21/Matrix-M vaccine was well tolerated alone and in combination with antimalarials, with no significant differences in vaccine immunogenicity or piperaquine pharmacokinetics between groups.
safety_summary: Vaccine was well tolerated alone and combined with antimalarials; none of the participants failed to complete the 3-dose vaccine course.

title: Extension of efficacy range for targeted malaria-elimination interventions due to spillover effects.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of malaria elimination interventions (chemoprevention and IRS) with reported outcome results on incidence, prevalence, and seroprevalence; phase not applicable for cluster trials.
comparator: no intervention / non-recipients outside intervention radius
population: residents living near confirmed malaria index cases
primary_outcome: malaria incidence, prevalence and seroprevalence among direct and spillover populations
impact_summary: Combined chemoprevention and indoor residual spraying produced no clear direct effect on recipients but substantially reduced malaria incidence, prevalence and seroprevalence among non-recipients living up to 3 km away, indicating strong spillover effects.
effect_estimate: 43% reduction in incidence (within 1 km); 79% reduction in infection prevalence (within 3 km); 34% reduction in seroprevalence (within 3 km)

title: A cluster-randomized trial of client and provider directed financial interventions to align incentives with appropriate case management in private medicine retailers: Results of the TESTsmART trial in Lagos, Nigeria.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported results testing malaria diagnosis (mRDT) and subsidized ACT treatment in Nigeria's private sector; primary focus is malaria case management in humans.
comparator: subsidized mRDT testing only (control arm) vs. subsidized testing plus free ACT for test-positive clients and provider incentive (intervention arm)
population: clients seeking care for fever/malaria at private medicine retailers, including children with fever
primary_outcome: proportion of ACTs dispensed to individuals with a positive diagnostic test
impact_summary: The intervention offering free ACTs to test-positive clients and provider incentives did not improve testing rates or targeting of ACTs to test-positive clients compared to the control arm, though overall mRDT testing reduced ACT overconsumption among test-negative clients.
effect_metric: proportion of test-negative clients purchasing an ACT
transmission_setting: urban, endemic malaria transmission setting in Lagos, Nigeria

title: Pathways through which intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy influences child growth faltering: a mediation analysis.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing IPTp regimens (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) for malaria prevention in pregnancy, with infant growth outcomes measured and analyzed.
population: infants born to mothers enrolled in a randomized trial of IPTp; stratified by gravidity
primary_outcome: Infant growth measured as length-for-age Z-score (LAZ) and weight-for-length Z-score (WLZ) from 0-12 months
impact_summary: Among infants of multigravidae, SP increased LAZ from birth through 4 months compared to DP, while DP increased WLZ from 2-8 months compared to SP, with distinct mediating pathways for each regimen; no differences were observed among primigravidae.
effect_estimate: SP increased LAZ by 0.18-0.28 Z; DP increased WLZ by 0.11-0.28 Z
funder: Stanford Center for Innovation and Global Health, Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation

title: Effectiveness, Safety, and Acceptability of Primaquine Mass Drug Administration in Low-Endemicity Areas in Southern Thailand: Proof-of-Concept Study.
screening_reason: This is a published cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating primaquine mass drug administration for P. vivax malaria elimination in humans, a valid malaria intervention.
comparator: control group (national prevention and control standards without pMDA)
population: residents of low P. vivax transmission areas in southern Thailand
primary_outcome: proportion of P. vivax infections per 1000 population comparing pMDA and control groups
impact_summary: Primaquine mass drug administration was safe, well-tolerated, and highly accepted, but did not show a statistically significant impact on reducing P. vivax transmission compared to control.
effect_metric: proportion of P. vivax infections per 1000 population
effect_estimate: pMDA 8.4 vs control 5.6 at month 3 post-pMDA
transmission_setting: low-endemicity, persistently low P. vivax transmission
safety_summary: No major safety concerns; pMDA associated with high adherence, safety, and tolerability

title: LLIN Evaluation in Uganda Project (LLINEUP)-effects of a vector control trial on Plasmodium infection prevalence and genotypic markers of insecticide resistance in Anopheles vectors from 48 districts of Uganda.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (a malaria vector-control intervention) with reported outcome results on Plasmodium infection prevalence and resistance markers.
population: households/vector populations across 104 health sub-districts, cross-sectional entomological surveys
primary_outcome: Plasmodium infection prevalence and genotypic markers of insecticide resistance in Anopheles vectors
impact_summary: PBO LLINs did not reduce the proportion of infective mosquitoes compared to conventional LLINs, and pyrethroid resistance markers increased over time regardless of net type, suggesting persistence of transmission potential and evolution of resistance.

title: Aggressive Antipyretics for Fever Reduction in CNS Malaria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported results testing antipyretic therapy for CNS malaria, a neurological complication of malaria in humans.
interventions_raw: Acetaminophen; Ibuprofen; placebo for acetaminophen; placebo for ibuprofen
comparator: usual care with acetaminophen alone given only for temperature ≥38.5°C
population: children aged 2 to 11 years with CNS malaria
primary_outcome: Mean Maximum Temperature
impact_summary: Aggressive antipyretic therapy with scheduled acetaminophen and ibuprofen significantly reduced maximum temperature and lowered odds of multiple or prolonged seizures compared with usual care, without affecting parasite clearance.
safety_summary: Severe adverse events occurred in 15% overall, with 20% in usual care vs 12% in aggressive antipyretic group, including 13 deaths (8% vs 2%); increased creatinine led to drug discontinuation in 6% vs 10% (OR 1.74, 95% CI 0.63-5.07).
conditions: Malaria, Seizures, Coma, Parasitemia, Hyperpyrexia, Fever

title: Expanding community case management of malaria to all ages can improve universal access to malaria diagnosis and treatment: results from a cluster randomized trial in Madagascar.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of malaria community case management with reported outcome results on diagnosis and treatment access in humans.
comparator: malaria community case management (mCCM) for children under 5 only (control)
population: rural community members of all ages, including children under 5 and individuals 6-13 years and older, in Farafangana District
primary_outcome: Rates of care-seeking for fever and malaria diagnosis (e.g., RDTs done), assessed via household surveys and health system register data
impact_summary: Expanding community case management of malaria to all ages improved access to malaria diagnosis and treatment, particularly for individuals over 5 years and those living further from health centers, though significance was mainly seen in health system data.
effect_estimate: RR for RDTs done in 6-13-year-olds = 1.65; RR per km distance = 1.21
transmission_setting: rural, endemic malaria setting in Farafangana District, Madagascar
age_range: all ages, with comparisons focusing on children under 5 and 6-13 year olds

title: Trimethoprim-Sulfamethoxazole Plus Azithromycin to Prevent Malaria and Sexually Transmitted Infections in Pregnant Women With HIV (PREMISE): A Randomized, Double-Masked, Placebo-Controlled, Phase IIB Clinical Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (TMP-SMX + azithromycin) as a primary intervention in pregnant women with HIV.
design: randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, phase IIB clinical trial
comparator: placebo (TMP-SMX plus placebo vs TMP-SMX plus azithromycin)
population: pregnant women with HIV at gestational age <28 weeks
primary_outcome: Positive peripheral malaria infection by microscopy or PCR and composite bacterial genital STI (Chlamydia trachomatis, Neisseria gonorrhoeae, or syphilis) at delivery
impact_summary: Adding monthly azithromycin to daily TMP-SMX prophylaxis did not reduce the risk of malaria or bacterial STI at delivery in pregnant women with HIV in Cameroon.
p_value: not significant (preterm delivery P=.3; low birthweight P=.6)
safety_summary: Adverse birth outcomes (preterm delivery, low birthweight) were not significantly different between groups, though numerically lower in the TMP-SMX-AZ arm; no other significant safety differences reported.

title: Intermittent preventive treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine but not dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine modulates the relationship between inflammatory markers and adverse pregnancy outcomes in Malawi.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (IPTp with SP, DP, and DP+AZ) as the primary intervention in pregnant women in a malaria-endemic setting.
design: randomized controlled trial, secondary analysis, phase 3
comparator: dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP), and DP plus single-dose azithromycin (AZ), compared with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Relationship between inflammatory markers (CRP, AGP) and adverse pregnancy/birth outcomes across IPTp treatment arms
impact_summary: SP, but not DP-based regimens, was associated with a reduced risk of adverse birth outcomes among women with elevated AGP, suggesting SP modifies the relationship between inflammation and pregnancy outcomes.
effect_estimate: 1.95 (interaction: DP/DP+AZ vs SP for AGP-adverse outcome association)
follow_up: from enrollment (16-28 gestation weeks) to delivery
safety_summary: Not specifically reported in this analysis; focused on inflammatory biomarkers and birth outcomes.

title: Efficacy, Safety and Immunogenicity Study of GSK Biologicals' Candidate Malaria Vaccine (SB257049) Evaluating Schedules With or Without Fractional Doses, Early Dose 4 and Yearly Doses, in Children 5-17 Months of Age
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine in children with reported efficacy results against malaria infection; phase 2b is not early-phase.
interventions_raw: RTS,S/AS01E (Full dose); RTS,S/AS01E (1/5th dose); Rabies vaccine
population: children aged 5-17 months
primary_outcome: Incidence of Clinical Malaria Meeting the Primary Case Definition
impact_summary: All four RTS,S/AS01E dosing regimens significantly and similarly reduced malaria infections compared with a rabies control vaccine, with greater efficacy in children infected at the time of first vaccination.
effect_metric: vaccine efficacy (1 - hazard ratio) against first new infection
effect_ci: 9-53 (95% CI union); infected subgroup 68% (50-80); uninfected subgroup 37% (23-48)
transmission_setting: endemic malaria transmission settings in Ghana and Kenya

title: Persistent and multiclonal malaria parasite dynamics despite extended artemether-lumefantrine treatment in children.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artemether-lumefantrine regimens in children with malaria; reports outcome results on parasite dynamics and recurrent parasitemia.
population: children with and without HIV
primary_outcome: post-treatment stage-specific parasite dynamics including recurrent ring-stage parasitemia
impact_summary: Extended 5-day artemether-lumefantrine treatment significantly lowered the risk of recurrent ring-stage parasitemia compared to the standard 3-day regimen, though multiclonal parasite dynamics persisted despite effective treatment.

title: Innate immune activation restricts priming and protective efficacy of the radiation-attenuated PfSPZ malaria vaccine.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results from a clinical trial of a malaria vaccine (PfSPZ) with efficacy and mechanistic findings in African infants.
population: African infants
primary_outcome: Protection from P. falciparum parasitemia
impact_summary: Prevaccination innate immune activation and myeloid signatures correlated with protection in placebo controls but with susceptibility to parasitemia in infants receiving the highest, most protective dose of PfSPZ vaccine, suggesting innate stimulation both protects against infection and dampens the CD8+ T cell response induced by whole-sporozoite vaccination.

title: Measuring effects of ivermectin-treated cattle on potential malaria vectors in Vietnam: A cluster-randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing ivermectin-treated cattle for malaria vector control in humans' epidemiological environment.
population: local zebu cattle in six rural villages (vector surveillance study)
primary_outcome: Total nightly Anopheles spp. vector catches from cattle-baited traps, pre- vs post-intervention
impact_summary: Treating cattle with ivermectin did not significantly reduce total anopheline mosquito captures compared to untreated control villages.
follow_up: 6 nights before and 6 nights after intervention
transmission_setting: rural Central Vietnam, Greater Mekong Subregion malaria elimination setting
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Subcutaneous Administration of a Monoclonal Antibody to Prevent Malaria.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Phase 2 RCT with reported efficacy results for a malaria prevention intervention (monoclonal antibody L9LS) in children in an endemic setting.
population: children 6 to 10 years of age
primary_outcome: First P. falciparum infection detected on blood smear performed at least every 2 weeks for 24 weeks (time-to-event analysis)
impact_summary: Subcutaneous administration of the monoclonal antibody L9LS significantly protected children against P. falciparum infection and clinical malaria over a 6-month malaria season compared with placebo.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region with a 6-month malaria season
safety_summary: No safety concerns were identified in either the dose-escalation part (part A) or the randomized part (part B) of the trial.
funder: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

title: Monthly Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine During Pregnancy Prevents Febrile Respiratory Illnesses: A Secondary Analysis of a Malaria Chemoprevention Trial in Uganda.
screening_reason: Secondary analysis of a completed RCT comparing IPTp-SP versus IPTp-DP in pregnant women with reported outcome results (birthweight, NMFI incidence, antibiotic use); malaria chemoprevention is the primary focus.
design: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
population: pregnant women without HIV infection, enrolled between 12 and 20 gestational weeks
primary_outcome: Incidence of nonmalarial febrile illnesses (NMFIs), particularly respiratory NMFIs, and birthweight for gestational age Z scores
impact_summary: Monthly IPTp-SP reduced incident nonmalarial febrile illnesses, especially respiratory illnesses, compared to IPTp-DP, and was associated with higher birthweight for gestational age.
follow_up: from enrollment (12-20 gestational weeks) through delivery
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; 75% of respiratory NMFIs were treated with antibiotics, with similar overall antibiotic prescriptions between arms.

title: Feasibility, safety, and impact of the RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine when implemented through national immunisation programmes: evaluation of cluster-randomised introduction of the vaccine in Ghana, Kenya, and Malawi.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of RTS,S malaria vaccine with reported outcome results on safety, feasibility, and impact; Phase 4 implementation evaluation meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: children aged 1-59 months, vaccine eligible children aged 5-9 months for primary doses
primary_outcome: All-cause mortality (excluding injury), hospital admission with severe malaria, hospital admission with meningitis or cerebral malaria, deaths in girls vs boys, and vaccination coverage
impact_summary: RTS,S introduction was associated with a 32% reduction in hospital admissions for severe malaria and a 9% reduction in all-cause mortality (excluding injury), with no evidence of previously observed safety signals such as excess meningitis, cerebral malaria, or excess female mortality.
effect_estimate: 32% reduction in severe malaria hospital admission; 9% reduction in all-cause mortality
follow_up: 24 months (interim analysis within a planned 4-year evaluation)
age_range: 1-59 months (vaccine doses given between 5 months and 2 years)
safety_summary: No evidence of excess meningitis (IRR 0.63, 95% CI 0.22-1.79) or cerebral malaria (IRR 1.03, 95% CI 0.61-1.74) cases, and no difference in mortality impact between girls and boys (relative mortality ratio 1.03, 95% CI 0.88-1.21), addressing safety signals seen in the phase 3 trial.
funder: Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance; the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria; Unitaid

title: Efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and prevalence of molecular markers of anti-malarial drug resistance in children in Togo in 2021.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in children with reported efficacy outcomes; not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (AL vs DP, no placebo)
population: children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28/42
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were highly effective against uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Togo, with high cure rates and no validated artemisinin resistance markers detected.

title: Insecticide-treated bed nets and residual indoor spraying reduce malaria in areas with low transmission: a reanalysis of the Maltrials study.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria incidence) testing vector-control interventions (ITNs and IRS) in a low-transmission malaria setting.
population: households and persons residing in study clusters
primary_outcome: malaria incidence
impact_summary: Combined ITN plus IRS and ITN alone significantly reduced malaria incidence compared to IRS alone or routine control, with a synergistic effect seen when ITN and IRS were combined.
p_value: ITN+IRS P<0.001; ITN alone P=0.011; IRS alone P=0.28
transmission_setting: low transmission, Rift Valley, Central Ethiopia

title: Pyronaridine Artesunate 3:1 Granule Formulation vs. Coartem© Crushed Tablets in P. Falciparum Malaria Pediatric Patients
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of pyronaridine-artesunate vs. artemether-lumefantrine for P. falciparum malaria in children with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
place: Burkina Faso, Côte d’Ivoire, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Kenya, Mali, Mozambique, Philippines
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Burkina Faso; Cote d'Ivoire; Gabon; Kenya; Mali; Mozambique; Philippines
interventions_raw: pyronaridine artesunate; arthemeter lumefantrine
population: pediatric patients with microscopically-confirmed P. falciparum malaria, body weight ≥5 kg to <20 kg
primary_outcome: Percentage of Participants With PCR-Corrected ACPR on Day 28
impact_summary: Pyronaridine-artesunate pediatric granules were well tolerated and showed clinical efficacy comparable to artemether-lumefantrine, with high Day 28 ACPR rates in trials and effectiveness confirmed in real-world use.
effect_estimate: 97.1% and 100% for PA vs 98.8% and 98.4% for AL
safety_summary: Adverse events occurred in 63.9% of PA patients vs 62.0% of AL patients; vomiting more common with PA (7.8% vs 3.4%, RR 2.3, P=0.004); prolonged QT interval less frequent with PA (3.1% vs 8.1%, RR 0.39, P=0.0007); real-world CANTAM study showed 17.7% adverse events, mainly vomiting and pyrexia.

title: Malaria Diagnostic Testing and Conditional Subsidies to Target ACTs in the Retail Sector: TESTsmART Aim 2 - Nigeria
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria intervention (diagnostic testing and ACT subsidies) in humans; phase not applicable for this implementation-science design.
interventions_raw: Testing incentive; Conditional artemisinin combination therapy subsidy
comparator: Control arm with subsidized mRDT testing only (no ACT subsidy)
population: Clients with fever seeking care at Private Medicine Retailers, including children
primary_outcome: ACT (Artemisinin Combination Therapy) Consumption by True Malaria Cases
impact_summary: RDT testing helped target ACTs to confirmed malaria cases, but the conditional ACT subsidy and testing incentive did not further improve testing rates or appropriate ACT dispensing compared to control.
effect_metric: Proportion purchasing ACT by test result
effect_estimate: 26% of test-negative vs 58% of untested clients purchased an ACT
transmission_setting: Private retail health sector, urban Lagos, Nigeria

title: Mass Azithromycin Distribution to Prevent Child Mortality in Burkina Faso: The CHAT Randomized Clinical Trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (all-cause childhood mortality) evaluating azithromycin mass distribution for disease prevention in children in a malaria-endemic setting.
population: children aged 1 to 59 months
primary_outcome: all-cause childhood mortality, measured during a twice-yearly enumerative census
impact_summary: Mortality in children was lower with biannual mass azithromycin distribution alongside seasonal malaria chemoprevention, but the difference was not statistically significant.
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission with seasonal malaria chemoprevention distributed concurrently

title: Safety and efficacy of malaria vaccine candidate R21/Matrix-M in African children: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT of malaria vaccine (R21/Matrix-M) in African children with fully reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: children aged 5-36 months
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy of R21/Matrix-M from 14 days after third vaccination to 12 months after completion of the primary series at seasonal and standard sites separately as co-primary endpoints
impact_summary: R21/Matrix-M vaccine was well tolerated and provided high protective efficacy against clinical malaria in African children at both seasonal and standard transmission sites over 12 months.
effect_metric: vaccine efficacy against time to first clinical malaria episode
follow_up: 12 months (up to 18 months at seasonal sites)
transmission_setting: seasonal and perennial malaria transmission sites across four African countries
safety_summary: Well tolerated; most frequent adverse events were injection site pain (18.6%) and fever (46.7%); no significant difference in adverse events of special interest or serious adverse events between groups; no treatment-related deaths.
funder: The Serum Institute of India, the Wellcome Trust, the UK National Institute for Health Research Oxford Biomedical Research Centre, and Open Philanthropy

title: Impact of a spatial repellent intervention on Anopheles kdr insecticide resistance allele in Sumba, Indonesia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial comparing spatial repellent intervention to placebo with reported outcome results on insecticide resistance and mosquito susceptibility.
population: Anopheles mosquito populations (entomological study)
primary_outcome: Frequency distribution of kdr resistance alleles (L1014F/L1014S) in Anopheles mosquitoes before and after SR intervention
impact_summary: A statistically significant increase in kdr mutant allele frequency occurred over the 3-year study in both spatial repellent-treated and placebo clusters, with unclear attribution to the SR intervention itself.
safety_summary: All Anopheles species tested showed fully susceptible phenotypes to permethrin, deltamethrin, and transfluthrin via CDC bottle assay, despite increasing kdr mutation frequency.

title: Artemisinin-naphthoquine plus lower-dose primaquine to treat and prevent recurrence of Plasmodium vivax malaria: an open-label randomized and non-inferiority trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artemisinin-naphthoquine plus primaquine versus chloroquine plus primaquine for P. vivax treatment with 365-day follow-up and reported efficacy/safety outcomes.
comparator: chloroquine plus primaquine for 14 days (CQPQ14, active comparator)
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Recurrence-free proportion at day 182/365 (radical cure efficacy)
impact_summary: ANPQ3 showed similar radical cure efficacy to CQPQ14, cleared fever and parasites faster, was safer with no severe adverse effects, and had better patient adherence.
safety_summary: No severe adverse effects in ANPQ3 group; 5 (3.9%) patients had acute haemolysis in CQPQ14 group (P = 0.013).

title: PvDBPII elicits multiple antibody-mediated mechanisms that reduce growth in a Plasmodium vivax challenge trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (human challenge trial with immunized volunteers challenged with P. vivax) testing a malaria vaccine intervention with reported outcome results (parasite multiplication rate reduction).
design: controlled human malaria infection, heterologous challenge trial, delayed dosing regimen
population: healthy adult volunteers immunized with PvDBPII vaccine and challenged with P. vivax
primary_outcome: parasite multiplication rate (PMR) reduction and immune correlates of protection
impact_summary: PvDBPII immunization with Matrix-M adjuvant elicited polyfunctional antibody responses, including antibody titre, receptor-binding inhibitory titre, complement C1q and Fc gamma receptor binding, that correlated with reduced parasite multiplication rate and cross-reacted with diverse P. vivax variants.
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (challenge with Thai P. vivax isolate PvW1)

title: The impact of pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen and pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr long-lasting insecticidal nets on density of primary malaria vectors Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles coluzzii in Benin: a secondary analysis of a cluster randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (malaria vector control intervention) with reported outcome results on mosquito vector density.
population: mosquito vector populations (An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii) collected via human landing catches in study clusters
primary_outcome: Density of Anopheles gambiae s.s. and Anopheles coluzzii indoors and outdoors, measured via human landing catches
impact_summary: Pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen and pyrethroid-chlorfenapyr LLINs did not significantly reduce indoor or outdoor densities of An. gambiae s.s. or An. coluzzii compared to pyrethroid-only LLINs in Benin.
effect_estimate: DR = 0.62 (pyriproxyfen, An. coluzzii); DR = 0.56 (chlorfenapyr, An. coluzzii); DR = 0.52 (pyriproxyfen, An. gambiae s.s.); DR = 0.53 (chlorfenapyr, An. gambiae s.s.)
transmission_setting: malaria endemic setting in Benin with primary vectors An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii

title: Factors associated with malaria infection among children after distribution of PBO-pyrethroid synergist-treated nets and indoor residual spraying in north-western Tanzania.
screening_reason: This is a published cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria vector-control interventions (PBO-LLIN and IRS) in children that has reported outcome results (malaria prevalence by year and intervention arm).
population: children aged 6 months to 14 years
primary_outcome: Malaria infection prevalence in children
impact_summary: Use of PBO synergist LLINs reduced the risk of malaria infection compared to standard LLINs, while other factors such as male sex, older age, open eaves, no IRS, low education and low socioeconomic status increased risk.
transmission_setting: high transmission area with pyrethroid-resistant vectors, Kagera region, north-western Tanzania

title: Community health workers in clinical research at the example of a phase IIIb/ IV antimalarial drug trial conducted in five African countries.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Phase IIIb/IV RCT of an antimalarial drug with reported outcome results assessing real-world effectiveness and safety in 8560 malaria episodes across five African countries.
design: phase IIIb/IV, cohort event monitoring study, multi-center
population: malaria patients treated with pyronaridine-artesunate
primary_outcome: real-world effectiveness and safety of pyronaridine-artesunate
impact_summary: Community health workers effectively supported follow-up in a phase IIIb/IV cohort event monitoring study assessing real-world effectiveness and safety of pyronaridine-artesunate in African settings.
safety_summary: CHWs helped relay information about suspected safety signals and factors affecting therapeutic effectiveness in their communities.

title: Factors affecting haemoglobin dynamics in African children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria treated with single low-dose primaquine or placebo.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported safety and efficacy outcome results for a malaria treatment intervention (single low-dose primaquine) in humans.
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Uganda
population: children aged 6 months-11 years with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria and day 0 Hb ≥ 6 g/dL
primary_outcome: Haemoglobin dynamics (fractional fall in Hb and Hb recovery, D42 Hb > D0 Hb)
impact_summary: Single low-dose primaquine did not adversely affect posttreatment haemoglobin changes, and G6PD-deficient children had favourable Hb recovery, supporting SLDPQ deployment without G6PD screening in Africa.
effect_metric: association with Hb recovery (D42 Hb > D0 Hb)
effect_estimate: not significantly affected by SLDPQ; G6PDd status associated with favourable Hb recovery
safety_summary: Ten blood transfusions given in the first week (5 in SLDPQ group, 5 in placebo group); no significant haemolytic risk attributable to SLDPQ observed.

title: Community evaluation of VECTRON™ T500, a broflanilide insecticide, for indoor residual spraying for malaria vector control in central Benin; a two arm non-inferiority cluster randomised trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (IRS with broflanilide) with reported outcome results on vector density, sporozoite rates, and entomological inoculation rates.
population: Household inhabitants in communities with pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l., surveyed via human landing catches
primary_outcome: Vector density indicated by human biting rate (bites/person/night) indoors and outdoors
impact_summary: VECTRON™ T500 was non-inferior to Fludora® Fusion in reducing human biting rates of pyrethroid-resistant malaria vectors and showed prolonged residual efficacy over 24 months with high acceptability.
effect_metric: incidence rate ratio (IRR) for human biting rate
transmission_setting: High pyrethroid resistance area, high coverage with pyrethroid-only nets, Za-Kpota District central Benin
safety_summary: Perceived adverse events reported by spray operators and householders were generally very low (<6%) in both study arms

title: Efficacy and safety of ivermectin for the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum infections in asymptomatic male and female Gabonese adults - a pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled single-centre phase Ib/IIa clinical trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (parasite reduction) for a malaria treatment intervention in humans; Phase IIa is not early-phase.
population: asymptomatic male and female Gabonese adults with P. falciparum parasitaemia (200-5000 parasites/μl)
primary_outcome: time to 90% parasite reduction
impact_summary: Ivermectin at doses up to 300 μg/kg once daily for three days was well tolerated but did not significantly reduce time to 90% parasite reduction compared to placebo.
effect_metric: hazard ratio for time to 90% parasite reduction
safety_summary: No severe or serious adverse events were observed; ivermectin was well tolerated at doses up to 300 μg/kg once daily for three days.
funder: Centre de Recherches Médicales de Lambaréné and the Centre for Tropical Medicine of the Bernhard Nocht Institute for Tropical Medicine

title: Targeted malaria elimination interventions reduce Plasmodium falciparum infections up to 3 kilometers away.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (artemether lumefantrine) and vector control (IRS) interventions in a low-transmission elimination setting.
comparator: combination of chemoprevention and vector control vs. each alone and vs. control arm
population: individuals near confirmed malaria index cases, including intervention recipients and non-recipients (nearby residents)
primary_outcome: malaria incidence among non-recipients within 1 km of index cases
impact_summary: The combined chemoprevention and vector control intervention reduced malaria incidence, infection prevalence, and seroprevalence among non-recipients up to 3 km from index cases.

title: A cluster-randomized trial of client and provider-directed financial interventions to align incentives with appropriate case management in retail medicine outlets: results of the TESTsmART Trial in western Kenya.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing malaria diagnostic and treatment interventions (mRDTs and ACT subsidies) in humans; phase not applicable for retail/cluster intervention.
comparator: control arm with subsidized RDT testing (no financial incentive for testing/treatment)
population: clients of retail medicine outlets seeking malaria testing/treatment
primary_outcome: proportion of ACT dispensed to individuals with a positive diagnostic test
impact_summary: Client-directed and combined client+provider-directed financial incentive interventions did not significantly improve testing rates or targeting of ACTs to test-positive clients compared to control, though overall mRDT use reduced ACT overconsumption among untested/test-negative clients.
effect_estimate: RD=0.01 (dispensing of ACTs to test-positive clients); RD=0.09 (testing rates)
transmission_setting: western Kenya, malaria-endemic region, private retail medicine outlets

title: Durability of the deltamethrin-treated polypropylene long-lasting net LifeNet® in a pyrethroid resistance area in south western Benin: A phase III trial.
screening_reason: Phase III cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria prevention intervention (insecticidal bed net) with reported durability and efficacy outcomes.
comparator: PermaNet® 2.0 (WHOPES fully recommended LLIN, positive control)
population: households in a pyrethroid resistance rural area
primary_outcome: Bioassay performance (WHO cone assays and tunnel tests), insecticide content, and physical integrity of LLINs
impact_summary: LifeNet® LLINs met WHO criteria for bio-efficacy throughout the 36-month study period, showed lower physical integrity and insecticide retention over time, and were well accepted by the population though with more reported side effects than PermaNet®.
effect_metric: proportion of LLINs meeting WHO efficacy criteria at 36 months
effect_estimate: 100% of both LifeNet® and PermaNet® met WHO efficacy criteria after 36 months
transmission_setting: pyrethroid resistance area, malaria endemic rural Benin
safety_summary: Complaints of side effects were significantly higher among LifeNet® users than PermaNet® users

title: Larviciding intervention targeting malaria vectors also affects Culex mosquito distribution in the city of Yaoundé, Cameroon.
journal: Current research in parasitology & vector-borne diseases
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector control intervention (larviciding) in humans.
population: households in urban clusters (mosquito surveillance, indoor/outdoor)
primary_outcome: Reduction in Culex mosquito aquatic habitats and adult Culex densities
impact_summary: Larviciding intervention targeting malaria vectors led to a 69% reduction in aquatic habitats with Culex larvae and a 36.65% reduction in adult Culex densities in houses, with no change in Culex species composition.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in adult Culex density

title: Randomized Field Trial to Assess the Safety and Efficacy of Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine for Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention in School-Aged Children in Bandiagara, Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of seasonal malaria chemoprevention (DHA-PQ) in school-aged children with reported outcome results on efficacy and safety; malaria is the primary focus; phase is not early-stage.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (SP-AQ) and no chemoprevention (albendazole)
population: school-aged children
primary_outcome: Safety and efficacy (incidence of clinical malaria) at Day 120 of follow-up
impact_summary: Both DHA-PQ and SP-AQ significantly reduced the incidence of clinical malaria compared with control, with DHA-PQ causing fewer adverse events than SP-AQ.
safety_summary: Abdominal pain, headache, and vomiting were more frequent in the SP-AQ arm (29.2%, 19.2%, 15.2%) than in the DHA-PQ arm (11.8%, 11.2%, 5.7%); DHA-PQ had fewer adverse events than SP-AQ.

title: Efficacy of the spatial repellent product Mosquito Shield™ against wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles arabiensis in south-eastern Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (spatial repellent) with reported efficacy outcomes in humans; cluster-randomized hut design with phase designation not applicable to vector-control studies.
population: wild, free-flying, pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles arabiensis mosquitoes; volunteers conducting human landing catches
primary_outcome: Mosquito landing (biting) and blood-feeding inhibition measured via Human Landing Catch and blood-feeding assays
impact_summary: Mosquito Shield spatial repellent significantly reduced mosquito landings and blood-feeding by wild pyrethroid-resistant An. arabiensis over one month compared to control huts.
transmission_setting: South-eastern Tanzania, malaria-endemic area with pyrethroid-resistant vectors

title: Therapeutic efficacy and safety of artesunate + amodiaquine and artemether + lumefantrine in treating uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children on the rainy south-east coast of Madagascar.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (efficacy and safety of two malaria treatments in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria), meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: children aged 6 months to 14 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate at day 28
impact_summary: Both artesunate+amodiaquine and artemether+lumefantrine were safe and highly efficacious for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children, with ACPR rates of 100% and 96% (97.7% PCR-corrected) respectively.
safety_summary: Mild and moderate adverse events, including gastrointestinal and/or nervous disorders, were reported in 11.9% (42/352) of patients.

title: Seasonal Malaria Vaccination (RTS,S/AS01) and Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SP/AQ) Extension Study
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS01) and chemoprevention (SMC) in humans; Phase 3; primary malaria focus.
interventions_raw: Tetanus/diphtheria toxoids; SMC with SP+AQ; RTS,S/AS01; SMC placebo
comparator: SMC alone (active comparator), RTS,S/AS01E alone (active comparator)
population: children enrolled at age 5-17 months, followed to age 5 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of Clinical Episodes of Malaria
impact_summary: Combining seasonal RTS,S/AS01E vaccination with seasonal malaria chemoprevention sustained substantial protection against clinical malaria over 5 years compared with either intervention alone, with no safety signals detected.
effect_estimate: 57.7% vs SMC alone; 59.0% vs RTS,S/AS01E alone
safety_summary: No safety signals were detected.
funder: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

title: LLIN Evaluation in Uganda Project (LLINEUP) - Plasmodium infection prevalence and genotypic markers of insecticide resistance in Anopheles vectors from 48 districts of Uganda.
journal: medRxiv : the preprint server for health sciences
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of malaria vector-control intervention (PBO LLINs vs conventional LLINs) with reported outcome results on parasitaemia, vector density, and resistance markers.
population: households and Anopheles mosquitoes in 48 districts (104 health sub-districts) of Uganda
primary_outcome: Plasmodium infection prevalence and genotypic markers of insecticide resistance in Anopheles vectors
impact_summary: LLIN distribution was associated with reductions in parasite prevalence and vector density, but the proportion of infective mosquitoes remained stable and pyrethroid resistance markers increased over time regardless of LLIN type.

title: Superior antibody immunogenicity of a viral-vectored RH5 blood-stage malaria vaccine in Tanzanian infants as compared to adults.
screening_reason: Published phase 1b RCT of a malaria vaccine (RH5) in humans with reported safety and immunogenicity outcomes in a malaria-endemic population.
population: healthy adults (18-35 years), young children (1-6 years), and infants (6-11 months) in a malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: Number of solicited and unsolicited adverse events post vaccination and number of serious adverse events over the study period
impact_summary: The ChAd63-MVA RH5 vaccine was well tolerated with no serious adverse events and induced higher and more functionally active (growth inhibition activity) anti-RH5 antibody responses in young children and infants compared to adults.
effect_metric: anti-RH5 IgG and growth inhibition activity (GIA)
effect_estimate: Highest anti-RH5 IgG and GIA levels observed in infants compared to young children and adults
safety_summary: Vaccinations were well tolerated with comparable adverse event profiles across groups; no serious adverse events were reported.

title: Fetal growth and birth weight are independently reduced by malaria infection and curable sexually transmitted and reproductive tract infections in Kenya, Tanzania, and Malawi: A pregnancy cohort study.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Randomized trial of malaria prevention in pregnancy (IPTp with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with reported outcome results on fetal growth and birth weight.
design: pregnancy cohort study nested within randomized trial, phase 3
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Fetal weight/birthweight Z-score
