impact_summary: Malaria and curable STIs/RTIs, individually and combined, were associated with reduced fetal growth, with the greatest impact seen in paucigravidae women with dual infections.
effect_metric: adjusted mean difference in fetal/birth weight Z-score
effect_ci: malaria: -0.31 to -0.04; STIs/RTIs: -0.26 to -0.03; both: -0.33 to -0.07
p_value: malaria P=0.01; STIs/RTIs P=0.01; both P=0.003

title: Effect of malaria prevention education on bed net utilization, incidence of malaria and treatment seeking among school-aged children in Southern Ethiopia; cluster randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating malaria prevention education (intervention) on bed net utilization, malaria incidence, and treatment seeking in school-aged children in Ethiopia.
population: school-aged children
primary_outcome: Bed net utilization, cumulative incidence of malaria, and treatment seeking from a health facility
impact_summary: Malaria prevention education had no significant effect on bed net utilization, treatment seeking, or reported cumulative incidence of malaria among school-aged children.

title: A randomized, double-blind placebo-control study assessing the protective efficacy of an odour-based 'push-pull' malaria vector control strategy in reducing human-vector contact.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria vector control interventions (push-pull strategy with spatial repellent) in humans; cluster/community trial design (not phase-dependent).
comparator: placebo (control houses with all elements but without active ingredients)
population: households in western Kenya (residents exposed to malaria vector biting)
primary_outcome: Outdoor biting rate (human landing catches) and indoor mosquito density (light-traps)
impact_summary: None of the interventions reduced outdoor biting, but the 'push' spatial repellent reduced indoor vector densities by around two thirds, dominated by Anopheles funestus, while the 'pull' trap added no benefit.
transmission_setting: high outdoor Anopheles arabiensis biting density, malaria-endemic western Kenya

title: Innovative Public-private Partnership to Target Subsidized Antimalarials in the Retail Sector (Aim 2)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria diagnostic and treatment intervention in humans; phase not applicable for community-based design.
interventions_raw: Malaria RDT & conditional voucher for ACT from retail sector
population: Household members with fever in the last 4 weeks, served by community health workers
primary_outcome: Number of Subjects With a Fever Who Receive a Malaria Test From Any Source
impact_summary: Scale-up of community-based malaria testing via CHWs is feasible and effective in increasing testing uptake, particularly among the poorest households, though wealthier households were less likely to be tested by a CHW.
effect_estimate: 1.50 (awareness of CHW); 1.53 (wealthiest households); 0.32 (wealthier households tested by CHW); 2.75 (confidence in artemether-lumefantrine); 2.43 (perceived RDT accuracy)

title: Improving outcomes for children with malaria, diarrhoea and pneumonia in Mozambique: A cluster randomised controlled trial of the inSCALE technology innovation.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results, primary focus on malaria treatment coverage in children, phase not applicable for community-based intervention, and study completed with positive findings.
comparator: iCCM only (standard care without technology intervention)
population: children 2-59 months of age with malaria, diarrhoea or pneumonia
primary_outcome: Coverage of appropriate treatment for malaria, diarrhoea and pneumonia in children 2-59 months of age
impact_summary: The inSCALE mHealth intervention increased coverage of appropriate treatment for malaria, diarrhoea and pneumonia by 26% compared to standard iCCM in Mozambique.
effect_metric: adjusted risk ratio for coverage of appropriate treatment
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa, community-based iCCM programme setting

title: Community engagement among forest goers in a malaria prophylaxis trial: implementation challenges and implications.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria chemoprophylaxis (artemether-lumefantrine vs control) in humans with reported outcome results on compliance and drug discontinuation.
population: forest-goers (adults engaged in forest work)
primary_outcome: Uptake of trial participation measured as enrolment, compliance with trial procedures, and drug intake
impact_summary: The community engagement strategy resulted in high trial enrolment (92%), completion (84%), and drug compliance, with discontinuation more common in the AL arm, among females, and among those without prior malaria history.
p_value: 0.005 (discontinuation overall); 0.01 (AL vs MV discontinuation); 0.005 (females vs males); 0.02 (no prior malaria vs prior malaria)
transmission_setting: forest-based malaria transmission, Southeast Asia, northeast Cambodia
safety_summary: Discontinuation of study drug was higher in the AL arm compared to MV (7% vs 3%, p=0.005); no other adverse events reported in abstract.

title: Efficacy and Safety Study of Tafenoquine (TQ) Co-administered With Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHA-PQP) for the Radical Cure of Plasmodium Vivax (P. Vivax) Malaria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (6-month relapse-free efficacy) testing a malaria treatment intervention (tafenoquine plus artemisinin-based combination therapy) in humans; Phase 3 trial.
interventions_raw: Tafenoquine; Matched-Placebo for Tafenoquine; Primaquine; Matched-Placebo for Primaquine; Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DHA-PQP); ACT plus PQ (Rescue medication); PQ (End of study treatment)
comparator: dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine alone (and active comparator primaquine plus DHA-PQP)
population: glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase-normal Indonesian soldiers with microscopically confirmed P vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Percentage of Participants With Relapse-free Efficacy at Six Months After Administration of Tafenoquine With DHA-PQP and DHA-PQP Alone
impact_summary: Tafenoquine plus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was statistically superior to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine alone for radical cure of P vivax malaria, but the improvement in relapse-free efficacy was not clinically meaningful.
effect_metric: hazard ratio for relapse (6-month relapse-free efficacy)
transmission_setting: chloroquine-resistant P vivax endemic area (Indonesia, military population)
safety_summary: Adverse events over first 28 days occurred in 54% (DHA-PQP alone), 58% (tafenoquine plus DHA-PQP), and 44% (primaquine plus DHA-PQP); serious adverse events occurred in 2%, 4%, and 4% of patients respectively.

title: Differential impact of dual-active ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets on primary malaria vectors: a secondary analysis of a 3-year, single-blind, cluster-randomised controlled trial in rural Tanzania.
screening_reason: This is a completed cluster-randomised controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating dual-active ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets (a malaria vector-control intervention) against standard LLINs in humans; vector-control trials are considered 'not applicable' phase and are eligible.
population: households in rural Misungwi district, indoor mosquito collections
primary_outcome: Density of different malaria vector species (Anopheles per household per night), entomological inoculation rate (EIR), and sporozoite rate
impact_summary: Chlorfenapyr pyrethroid LLINs were the most effective dual active-ingredient net against the main malaria vector An funestus sl over 3 years, significantly reducing vector density and malaria transmission intensity, while none of the dual active-ingredient LLINs controlled An arabiensis.
effect_estimate: 0.26 (chlorfenapyr pyrethroid LLIN vs pyrethroid LLIN for An funestus density)
transmission_setting: pyrethroid-resistant malaria vectors, rural endemic setting
funder: Department for International Development UK, Medical Research Council, Wellcome Trust, Department of Health and Social Care, Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation via the Innovative Vector Control Consortium

title: Housing modification for malaria control: impact of a "lethal house lure" intervention on malaria infection prevalence in a cluster randomised control trial in Côte d'Ivoire.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria infection prevalence and case incidence) evaluating a novel house-based vector-control intervention as primary purpose.
population: residents of villages in malaria-endemic area
primary_outcome: malaria infection prevalence measured by rapid diagnostic test (RDT), compared with primary trial outcome of malaria case incidence
impact_summary: House screening and EaveTubes (SET) substantially reduced malaria infection prevalence 18 months after installation compared to control villages.

title: Artesunate versus quinine: the controlled trials watershed.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing artesunate and quinine for malaria treatment with reported outcome results.

title: Predicting adherence to postdischarge malaria chemoprevention in Malawian pre-school children: A prognostic multivariable analysis.
screening_reason: Cluster randomized trial with reported outcome results on adherence to postdischarge malaria chemoprevention, a key malaria prevention intervention in humans.
design: cluster randomized implementation trial, prognostic multivariable analysis
population: pre-school children recently discharged from hospital following recovery from severe anemia
primary_outcome: Full adherence to three monthly courses of postdischarge malaria chemoprevention (PDMC)
impact_summary: No conclusive set of predictors for adherence to PDMC was identified, though children with four or more malaria infections in the past year had reduced adherence.

title: Therapeutic response to artemisinin combination therapies among individuals with Plasmodium falciparum single infection vs mixed Plasmodium species infections: a retrospective posthoc analysis in Kisumu County, western Kenya.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing ACT efficacy for malaria treatment in humans.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate-mefloquine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, artemether-lumefantrine compared against each other)
population: individuals with Plasmodium falciparum single or mixed species infections
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rate and time to reinfection/recurrent parasitemia over 42-day follow-up
impact_summary: Artesunate-mefloquine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine had faster parasite clearance than artemether-lumefantrine, and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine provided the longest duration of protection against reinfection, with no differences in clearance based on species composition.

title: Safety and Efficacy of NF135 CPS Immunization
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention (whole sporozoite CPS immunization) with reported safety and efficacy outcomes; phase not applicable for immunization studies.
interventions_raw: CPS-immunization; malaria challenge infection, P. falciparum NF135.C10; malaria challenge infection, P. falciparum NF54; CPS-immunization (A/L); Atovaquone / Proguanil Oral Tablet [Malarone]
population: healthy, malaria-naïve adults
primary_outcome: Frequency of Adverse Events After NF135.C10 CPS Immunization
impact_summary: NF135 CPS immunization was poorly tolerated, frequently requiring rescue treatment for breakthrough infections, and induced only modest sterile protection (29%) against homologous controlled human malaria infection challenge.
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection model (non-endemic setting)
safety_summary: Grade 3 adverse events occurred in 18/30 (60%) high-dose and 3/10 (30%) low-dose participants 7-21 days after first immunization; all cohort A and two cohort B participants developed breakthrough blood-stage infections requiring rescue treatment.
conditions: Malaria,Falciparum, Controlled Human Malaria Infection, Immunization; Infection

title: Protective efficacy of holed and aging PBO-pyrethroid synergist-treated nets on malaria infection prevalence in north-western Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing PBO-pyrethroid LLINs vs standard pyrethroid LLINs for malaria prevention in humans, with reported outcome results on malaria infection prevalence over 36 months.
population: households and residents in malaria-endemic communities
primary_outcome: malaria infection prevalence in relation to net condition and age
impact_summary: PBO LLINs remained more protective against malaria infection than standard pyrethroid LLINs as both types aged over 3 years, despite similar functional survival times and net degradation.
p_value: not significant (no statistical difference between net types)

title: Association between malaria and household air pollution interventions in a predominantly rural area of Ghana.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (placental malaria prevalence and infant malaria parasitaemia incidence); primary purpose includes malaria prevention assessment in humans; not early-phase.
comparator: control (standard cookstove) vs LPG vs Biolite
population: pregnant women and their infants (maternal-infant pairs)
primary_outcome: Placental malaria and malaria parasitaemia episodes in the first year of infant's life
impact_summary: Household air pollution interventions (LPG or Biolite cookstoves) were not associated with an increased risk of placental malaria or malaria parasitaemia in infants during their first year of life compared to control.
age_range: infants in first year of life; pregnant women
safety_summary: No increased risk of malaria among pregnant women or infants associated with cookstove interventions

title: Effects of maternal antenatal treatment with two doses of azithromycin added to monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for the prevention of low birth weight in Burkina Faso: an open-label randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: RCT with reported results testing malaria prevention in pregnancy (IPTp with azithromycin) in humans; not early-phase.
population: pregnant women, 16 to 35 years of age, 12 to 24 weeks of gestation
primary_outcome: Low birth weight (birth weight measured within 24 h after birth < 2500 g)
impact_summary: Adding two doses of azithromycin to monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine did not significantly reduce the incidence of low birth weight compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine alone.
safety_summary: No treatment-related serious adverse events observed; no significant difference in SAEs (13.5% SPAZ vs 16.7% SP, p=0.18) or AEs (17.1% SPAZ vs 18.8% SP, p=0.56).

title: Interplay among malnutrition, chemoprevention, and the risk of malaria in young Ugandan children: Longitudinal pharmacodynamic and growth analysis.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT comparing malaria chemoprevention strategies (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) with no chemoprevention in children, with reported outcome results on malaria hazard and growth.
comparator: no malaria chemoprevention (also compared monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, and monthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine)
population: HIV-exposed and HIV-unexposed young children, followed from age 6-24 months on chemoprevention and then off chemoprevention until age 36 months
primary_outcome: Time to incident malaria episode (malaria hazard) modeled via parametric survival analysis; height and weight growth modeled via Brody growth model
impact_summary: Stunted children had a higher malaria hazard, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine chemoprevention reduced malaria hazard compared to no chemoprevention, and each malaria episode was associated with reduced growth rate for height.
effect_estimate: 0.65 (DP vs no chemoprevention); 2.1 (stunted vs non-stunted among DP recipients); 17% increased hazard for stunted vs ZHA=0

title: Ultra-short course, high-dose primaquine to prevent Plasmodium vivax infection following uncomplicated pediatric malaria: A randomized, open-label, non-inferiority trial of early versus delayed treatment.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention intervention (primaquine regimen) in children; primary focus is P. vivax relapse prevention.
population: children aged 0.5 to 12 years with uncomplicated malaria and normal G6PD activity
primary_outcome: Appearance of any P. vivax parasitemia within 42 days
impact_summary: Early ultra-short high-dose primaquine was non-inferior to delayed treatment in preventing P. vivax infection at day 42, though associated with more abdominal pain and vomiting, with no severe adverse events.
effect_metric: risk difference in P. vivax parasitemia at day 42
safety_summary: Ultra-short high-dose primaquine was safe and tolerated without severe adverse events; abdominal pain (3.7% vs 20.9%, P<0.0001) and vomiting (0.9% vs 9.1%, P=0.01) were more common in the early treatment group.

title: The economic impacts of house screening against malaria transmission: Experimental evidence from eastern Zambia.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (malaria prevalence, labor supply, income) testing a malaria prevention intervention (house screening) in humans; phase not early; primary focus is malaria.
population: households (adults and children) in rural and peri-urban Zambia
primary_outcome: self-reported malaria prevalence, sick days due to malaria, malaria episodes, labor supply, and household income
impact_summary: House screening reduced malaria prevalence, sick days, and episodes, and increased labor supply and household income, with private benefits exceeding costs.
effect_metric: reduction in malaria prevalence and increase in labor supply/income

title: Effects of anti-malarial prophylaxes on maternal transfer of Immunoglobulin-G (IgG) and association to immunity against Plasmodium falciparum infections among children in a Ugandan birth cohort.
screening_reason: Published RCT of IPTp (Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine and Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine) for malaria prevention in pregnancy with reported outcome results on malaria incidence in children.
population: pregnant women and their infants (birth cohort)
primary_outcome: Effect of IPTp on in-utero transfer of malaria-specific IgG and association with incidence of malaria in the first birth year
impact_summary: Malaria prophylaxis with SP or DP in pregnancy did not affect cord blood antibody levels against P. falciparum antigens, and higher cord IgG levels against several antigens were associated with increased, not decreased, risk of malaria in the first year of life.
effect_estimate: 1.09-1.83 across antigens (Rh4.2, PfSEA, Etramp5Ag1, AMA1, GLURP, EBA175)
p_value: p<0.05 for cord IgG4 differences by treatment; p>0.05 for placental malaria effect on IgG subtypes
transmission_setting: malaria endemic region, Busia, Eastern Uganda
age_range: infants in first year of life; mothers of reproductive age

title: Proof-of-concept study for a long-acting formulation of ivermectin injected in cattle as a complementary malaria vector control tool.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector control intervention (long-acting ivermectin in cattle to suppress Anopheles mosquitoes); phase not applicable for vector-control cluster design.
comparator: vehicle control (untreated formulation vehicle injected cattle)
population: Cattle (local breed) used to feed Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Survival/mortality of Anopheles coluzzii mosquitoes after feeding on treated cattle blood over time (up to 210 days post-treatment)
impact_summary: Both long-acting ivermectin formulations injected in cattle significantly reduced Anopheles coluzzii mosquito survival for up to 210 days post-treatment, suggesting potential as a complementary malaria vector control tool.
transmission_setting: residual malaria transmission sustained by zoophagic vector feeding on livestock
safety_summary: Not reported; further studies needed to characterize ivermectin withdrawal times and potential environmental toxicity

title: The Impact of Antenatal Azithromycin and Monthly Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine on Maternal Malaria during Pregnancy and Fetal Growth: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine and azithromycin for malaria prevention in pregnancy with reported outcome results on parasitemia and fetal growth.
population: pregnant women, 14-26 gestation weeks
primary_outcome: Malaria parasitemia during pregnancy (by real-time PCR) and fetal growth (biparietal diameter and femur length)
impact_summary: Monthly SP and monthly SP plus azithromycin both reduced malaria parasitemia during pregnancy compared to two-dose SP, but neither intervention affected fetal biparietal diameter or femur length growth velocity, and azithromycin added no significant additional benefit over monthly SP alone.
effect_estimate: 0.64 (monthly SP vs control), 0.50 (AZI-SP vs control) for combined trimesters
follow_up: until delivery (visits every 4 weeks until 36 weeks gestation, then weekly)
age_range: pregnant women 14-26 gestation weeks at enrollment

title: Artemether-lumefantrine efficacy among adults on antiretroviral therapy in Malawi.
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemether-lumefantrine efficacy in adults with malaria, with reported outcome results (ACPR rates and treatment failure analysis); malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
comparator: daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole vs weekly chloroquine vs no prophylaxis (chemoprophylaxis arms); AL efficacy assessed within this cohort
population: Adults (≥18 years) living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART) for ≥6 months with undetectable viral load and CD4 ≥250/mm3, who developed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) / treatment failure within 28 days after artemether-lumefantrine treatment
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine achieved a PCR-corrected efficacy of 94% meeting WHO acceptable treatment criteria, but day 7 lumefantrine levels were frequently low, especially among those on efavirenz-based ART, and low levels were associated with treatment failure.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate
p_value: <0.008 (comparison of lumefantrine levels between treatment failure and ACPR groups)
follow_up: 28 days per episode, over 5 years total study duration
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on efficacy and drug levels rather than adverse events

title: Effect of a fifth round of seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children aged 5-14 years in Dangassa, an area of long transmission in Mali.
screening_reason: Open randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria incidence reduction) testing seasonal malaria chemoprevention, a primary malaria prevention intervention in children.
population: children aged 5-14 years
primary_outcome: reduction in malaria incidence in intervention group compared to control group
impact_summary: An additional fifth round of seasonal malaria chemoprevention significantly reduced malaria incidence by 51% in children aged 5-14 years compared to control.
transmission_setting: rural, long/prolonged malaria transmission area (Dangassa, Mali)

title: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of intermittent preventive treatment in infancy using sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP-IPTi): a pilot study in Nigeria.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating SP-IPTi (chemoprevention) for malaria in infants; not early-phase.
population: infants receiving routine immunizations
primary_outcome: prevalence of asymptomatic malaria parasitemia and malaria-associated hospital admissions
impact_summary: SP-IPTi was safe and well tolerated but showed no significant benefit in reducing asymptomatic parasitemia, fever, or hospitalization compared to controls.
safety_summary: SP-IPTi was found to be safe and well tolerated, with adverse events monitored via passive case-detection and cross-sectional surveys.

title: Malaria Diagnostic Testing and Conditional Subsidies to Target ACTs in the Retail Sector: the TESTsmART Trial AIM 1
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria diagnostic and treatment subsidies in the retail sector in Kenya; primary focus is malaria intervention in humans.
interventions_raw: Conditional ACT subsidy, Arm 1 levels; Conditional ACT subsidy, Arm 2 levels; Conditional ACT subsidy, Arm 3 levels; Conditional ACT subsidy, Arm 4 levels
comparator: No RDT subsidy vs 50% RDT subsidy; 67% ACT subsidy vs free (100%) ACT treatment conditional on positive test
population: Drug shop clients with malaria-like illness, including children over 1 year accompanied by a parent or guardian
primary_outcome: Number of Participants That Purchase an mRDT (Malaria Rapid Diagnostic Test)
impact_summary: Subsidizing malaria diagnostic testing reduced client expenditures by an amount roughly equal to the subsidy value, while subsidizing ACT treatment did not significantly change spending compared to free treatment.

title: Study to Investigate the Clinical and Parasiticidal Activity and Pharmacokinetics of Different Doses of Artefenomel and Ferroquine in Patients With Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported outcome results; Phase 2 is not early-phase exclusion.
place: Benin, Burkina Faso, Gabon, Kenya, Uganda
countries: Benin; Burkina Faso; Gabon; Kenya; Uganda
interventions_raw: Artefenomel (OZ439); Ferroquine (SSR97193)
population: Patients aged 14-69 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria (3000-50,000 parasites/µL)
primary_outcome: Percentage of Participants With Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR)-Corrected Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR) at Day 28 (ACPR28)
impact_summary: The contribution of artefenomel exposure to Day 28 PCR-adjusted ACPR was not demonstrated, though parasite clearance was faster with ferroquine/artefenomel combinations than ferroquine alone.
effect_metric: odds ratio (contribution of artefenomel AUC0-∞ to Day 28 ACPR)
safety_summary: No deaths; adverse events were mild-to-moderate, mostly vomiting, occurring in 51.4%-72.7% of patients across groups; no QTcF prolongation ≥500 ms or >60 ms from baseline; all treatments well tolerated.

title: Screening eaves of houses reduces indoor mosquito density in rural, western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing eave screening intervention to control in houses; vector control is a primary malaria prevention strategy; cluster/structural trials are not subject to phase restrictions.
population: rural households
primary_outcome: Indoor mosquito density (Anopheles funestus, Anopheles gambiae Complex, Culex species) collected by motorized aspiration
impact_summary: Eave screening of houses significantly reduced indoor densities of Anopheles funestus, Anopheles gambiae Complex, and Culex species compared to unscreened houses.

title: A randomized controlled trial showing safety and efficacy of a whole sporozoite vaccine against endemic malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (vaccine efficacy against endemic malaria); primary purpose is malaria prevention via whole sporozoite vaccine; not early-phase.
population: malaria-experienced adults
primary_outcome: Vaccine efficacy (1 - risk ratio) against P. falciparum infection at 6 months
impact_summary: A three-dose regimen of PfSPZ Vaccine was safe and provided significant but partial protection against P. falciparum infection in Burkinabe adults, with efficacy declining from 38% at 6 months to 15% at 18 months.
transmission_setting: endemic, seasonal malaria transmission (two 6-month transmission seasons)
safety_summary: Vaccine was well tolerated; myalgia was the only symptom that differed significantly between vaccine and placebo groups.

title: Persistence of Plasmodium falciparum HRP-2 antigenaemia after artemisinin combination therapy is not associated with gametocytes.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing primaquine addition to ACT for malaria treatment, testing HRP-2 antigen persistence post-treatment.
population: P. falciparum infected, gametocyte positive individuals
primary_outcome: Time to test negativity for HRP-2 by ultra-sensitive RDT, standard RDT, and ELISA, compared between residual gametocyte positive and negative groups
impact_summary: Persistence of residual gametocytes after ACT treatment (with or without primaquine) was not associated with prolonged HRP-2 antigenaemia or RDT positivity.
effect_estimate: uRDT HR 0.79, RDT HR 0.77, ELISA HR 0.88
p_value: uRDT p=0.28; RDT p=0.20; ELISA p=0.53

title: Safety of age-dosed, single low-dose primaquine in children with glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase deficiency who are infected with Plasmodium falciparum in Uganda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo: a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, non-inferiority trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported safety outcomes for primaquine in malaria treatment; randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled design in children with P. falciparum infection; primary endpoint and results clearly reported.
place: Uganda, Democratic Republic of the Congo
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Uganda
population: children aged 6 months to 11 years with acute uncomplicated P falciparum infection, including G6PD-deficient children
primary_outcome: Development of profound (haemoglobin <4 g/dL) or severe (haemoglobin <5 g/dL) anaemia with severity features within 21 days of treatment
impact_summary: Age-dosed, single low-dose primaquine was well tolerated in children with and without G6PD deficiency, with a safety profile similar to placebo.
effect_metric: risk difference in severe anaemia incidence
safety_summary: No participants developed profound anaemia; three developed severe anaemia (one in the G6PD-deficient primaquine group, one each in the placebo and primaquine non-G6PD-deficient groups), with no significant difference between primaquine and placebo groups.
funder: UK Government Department for International Development, UK Medical Research Council, UK National Institute for Health Research, and the Wellcome Trust Joint Global Health Trials Scheme

title: Therapeutic efficacies of artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum and chloroquine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax infection in Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (efficacy endpoints) comparing antimalarial drugs for malaria treatment in humans; meets all inclusion criteria.
comparator: active comparator (AL vs DHA/PPQ for P. falciparum; CQ vs DHA/PPQ for P. vivax)
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum or P. vivax mono-infection, age 6 months and above
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28 (AL, CQ) or day 42 (DHA/PPQ)
impact_summary: AL, CQ, and DHA/PPQ all showed high therapeutic efficacy against P. falciparum and P. vivax in Ethiopia, with ACPR rates of 98-100%.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were reported.

title: Entomological impact of mass administration of ivermectin and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in The Gambia: a cluster-randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported entomological outcome results evaluating ivermectin mass drug administration for malaria vector control in humans.
population: inhabitants of villages in Upper River Region eligible for mass drug administration
primary_outcome: Entomological impact (vector density, entomological inoculation rate, vector parity)
impact_summary: Mass drug administration with ivermectin and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine reduced vector density and entomological inoculation rate in intervention villages compared to control villages.
follow_up: until end of year following MDA
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, sub-Saharan Africa, Upper River Region, The Gambia
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; focus on entomological outcomes rather than adverse events in humans.

title: Comparative effect of artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine on gametocyte clearance in children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Madagascar.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarials for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results on gametocyte clearance.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte emergence and clearance after treatment, assessed by microscopy at day 1, 2, 3, 7, 14, 21 and 28
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine cleared gametocytes more rapidly than artesunate-amodiaquine, with gametocytes undetectable by day 14 in the AL arm versus persisting until day 21 in the ASAQ arm.
effect_estimate: AL cleared gametocytes by day 14 vs day 21 for ASAQ
transmission_setting: 5 regions of Madagascar with different malaria epidemiological facies

title: Human behavior determinants of exposure to Anopheles vectors of malaria in Sumba, Indonesia.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results (malaria incidence and vector biting rates) for a spatial repellent vector-control intervention as primary purpose.
design: observational analysis nested within a larger clinical trial
population: households in Sumba, general community members
primary_outcome: Human behavior adjusted exposure to Anopheles bites
impact_summary: Human behavior-adjusted exposure analysis showed approximately 28% less exposure to Anopheles bites in the spatial repellent intervention arm compared to placebo, despite no significant difference in raw vector biting rates alone.
effect_metric: reduction in human behavior adjusted exposure
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic, ongoing transmission despite vector control

title: Effects of ivermectin mass drug administration for malaria vector control on ectoparasites and soil-transmitted helminths: a cluster randomized trial.
journal: International journal of infectious diseases : IJID : official publication of the International Society for Infectious Diseases
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing ivermectin MDA for malaria vector control, with follow-up data on ectoparasites and helminths.
population: children aged 3 to 14 years
primary_outcome: prevalence of ectoparasites (scabies) and soil-transmitted helminths (Strongyloides stercoralis)
impact_summary: Ivermectin MDA reduced Strongyloides stercoralis prevalence shortly after administration but had no lasting effect after 2 years and did not reduce scabies prevalence.

title: Participatory development of practical, affordable, insecticide-treated mosquito proofing for a range of housing designs in rural southern Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (insecticide-treated mosquito-proof screens) with reported outcome results on mosquito density and intervention effectiveness.
comparator: unscreened houses (negative control) and untreated screens
population: rural households
primary_outcome: Indoor mosquito density (Anopheles arabiensis and Culex quinquefasciatus counts) before and after house screening
impact_summary: Screening houses, whether treated with pirimiphos-methyl or not, almost entirely excluded the malaria vector Anopheles arabiensis but was much less effective against the nuisance mosquito Culex quinquefasciatus, and insecticide treatment did not add extra protection at the household level.
effect_estimate: ≥98% for An. arabiensis; ≤46% for Cx. quinquefasciatus
p_value: P < 0.0001 for both species reductions; P = 0.676 and 0.831 for PM effect on An. arabiensis and Cx. quinquefasciatus respectively
follow_up: 5 months after screening (8 months for insecticide residual efficacy)
transmission_setting: rural southern Tanzania, area with endemic malaria transmission
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Improved adherence to test, treat, and track (T3) malaria strategy among Over-the-Counter Medicine Sellers (OTCMS) through interventions implemented in selected rural communities of Fanteakwa North district, Ghana.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria diagnosis and treatment interventions (T3 strategy) among medicine sellers in Ghana; primary outcome of RDT testing rate was measured and reported.
population: Over-the-Counter Medicine Sellers (OTCMS) and children under 10 years with fever visiting OTCMS in rural communities
primary_outcome: Proportion of children under 10 years with fever or suspected malaria visiting OTCMS and getting tested (RDT) before treatment
impact_summary: Interventions targeting OTCMS significantly improved adherence to malaria testing and treatment protocols compared to control, and increased testing rates though the difference in end-line testing rate was not statistically significant.

title: Knowledge, practices and perceptions of communities during a malaria larviciding randomized trial in the city of Yaoundé, Cameroon.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results on malaria vector control (larviciding) intervention in humans, phase not early-stage.
population: community members living in intervention and non-intervention urban areas of Yaoundé
primary_outcome: Community knowledge, perceptions and practices regarding malaria control and larviciding impact (e.g., knowledge of malaria transmission and mosquito breeding habitats)
impact_summary: People living in larviciding intervention areas were more likely to know about malaria transmission and mosquito breeding habitats, reported reduced mosquito nuisance and malaria cases, and continued to use bed nets, indicating good acceptance of the larviciding program.
effect_estimate: 2.64 (knowledge of malaria transmission mode); 1.3 (knowledge of mosquito breeding habitats)
transmission_setting: urban malaria transmission setting in Yaoundé, Cameroon

title: Safety and Efficacy of a Monoclonal Antibody against Malaria in Mali.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Phase 2 RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes for a monoclonal antibody malaria prevention intervention in endemic Mali.
population: healthy adults
primary_outcome: First P. falciparum infection detected on blood-smear examination performed at least every 2 weeks for 24 weeks (time-to-event analysis)
impact_summary: A single intravenous infusion of the monoclonal antibody CIS43LS protected healthy adults in Mali against P. falciparum infection over a 6-month malaria season, with efficacy of 88.2% at the 40 mg/kg dose and 75.0% at the 10 mg/kg dose compared with placebo.
safety_summary: The risk of moderate headache was 3.3 times as high with 40 mg of CIS43LS per kilogram as with placebo; no other evident safety concerns were noted.
funder: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases

title: Economic evaluation of postdischarge malaria chemoprevention in preschool children treated for severe anaemia in Malawi, Kenya, and Uganda: A cost-effectiveness analysis.
screening_reason: Completed RCT with reported efficacy and cost-effectiveness outcomes; primary focus is malaria chemoprevention (postdischarge DP) in a malaria-endemic setting; Phase III implementation research.
design: Markov decision model cost-effectiveness analysis using data from a placebo-controlled trial and a delivery mechanism trial
population: Preschool children discharged after hospitalisation for severe anaemia
primary_outcome: Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio expressed as cost per quality-adjusted life-year (QALY) gained
impact_summary: Both community-based and facility-based postdischarge malaria chemoprevention were cost-saving compared to standard of care in Malawi, Kenya, and Uganda, with community-based delivery being the most cost-effective strategy.
effect_metric: Incremental cost savings per child treated

title: Effect of Malaria and Malaria Chemoprevention Regimens in Pregnancy and Childhood on Neurodevelopmental and Behavioral Outcomes in Children at 12, 24, and 36 Months: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp and SMC regimens) in pregnancy and childhood with reported neurodevelopmental outcome results.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (3 doses) vs monthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in pregnancy; DP every 3 months vs monthly DP in children
population: pregnant women and their children
primary_outcome: Child neurodevelopmental outcomes (cognition, language, motor function) at 12, 24, and 36 months, and behavior, attention, memory, and executive function at 24 and 36 months
impact_summary: Malaria in pregnancy and early childhood was associated with worse cognitive, behavioral, and executive function outcomes in children, but more effective malaria chemoprevention regimens did not improve neurodevelopmental outcomes.

title: Enhancing Preventive Therapy of Malaria In Children With Sickle Cell Anemia in East Africa (EPiTOMISE)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (Proguanil, SP-AQ, DP) in children; Phase 4; primary outcome is clinical malaria incidence.
interventions_raw: Proguanil Oral Tablet; Sulfadoxine/Pyrimethanine-Amodiaquine (SP-AQ); Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine (DP)
comparator: daily Proguanil (standard of care) vs monthly SP-AQ vs monthly DP
population: children aged 1 to 10 years with homozygous hemoglobin S (sickle cell anemia)
primary_outcome: Incidence of Clinical Malaria Per Patient Year
impact_summary: Compared to daily Proguanil, monthly SP-AQ and monthly DP chemoprevention did not significantly reduce clinical malaria incidence, though DP was associated with reduced dactylitis and P. falciparum parasitization.
effect_metric: incidence rate ratio (IRR) for clinical malaria
transmission_setting: endemic malaria transmission area, though limited transmission observed in study setting
safety_summary: Serious adverse events were common and distributed between groups; more deaths occurred in the monthly SP-AQ group (n=7) versus daily Proguanil (n=2) (HR 5.44, 95% CI 0.92-32.11, p=0.064) and DP (n=1) (HR 0.61, 95% CI 0.04-9.22, p=0.89), though differences were not statistically significant.

title: Effect of long-lasting insecticidal nets with and without piperonyl butoxide on malaria indicators in Uganda (LLINEUP): final results of a cluster-randomised trial embedded in a national distribution campaign.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of long-lasting insecticidal nets (a malaria vector-control intervention) with final outcome results reported; not early-phase.
comparator: conventional (non-PBO) long-lasting insecticidal nets (PermaNet 2.0 or Olyset Net)
population: children aged 2-10 years in households across 48 districts of eastern and western Uganda
primary_outcome: Parasite prevalence by microscopy in children aged 2-10 years (as-treated population) at 25 months
impact_summary: PBO LLINs reduced malaria parasite prevalence more effectively than conventional pyrethroid-only LLINs for up to 25 months after distribution.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic areas with high pyrethroid resistance, no ongoing indoor residual spraying
safety_summary: Not reported
funder: Against Malaria Foundation, UK Department for International Development, Innovative Vector Control Consortium, and Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation

title: Safety and immunogenicity of BK-SE36 in a blinded, randomized, controlled, age de-escalating phase Ib clinical trial in Burkinabe children.
screening_reason: Phase Ib RCT of BK-SE36 malaria blood-stage vaccine in children with reported safety and immunogenicity outcomes.
population: children aged 12-24 months and 25-60 months
primary_outcome: Safety and immunogenicity of BK-SE36 vaccine
impact_summary: BK-SE36 was well tolerated and immunogenic via both intramuscular and subcutaneous routes, with higher immune response observed in the younger age cohort.
effect_metric: fold change in antibody geometric mean titers
effect_estimate: more than 2-fold change from pre-vaccination; 2-fold and 4-fold higher GMT in younger vs older cohort after 2 and 3 doses respectively
follow_up: 6 months after first vaccination (through Week 26 and beyond)
safety_summary: Local reactions, mostly mild or moderate, occurred in 91.7% of subjects; Grade 3 adverse event rates were similar across BK-SE36 and control arms (Cohort 1: 100%, 89%, 89%; Cohort 2: 83%, 82%, 83%).

title: Community-Based Malaria Testing Reduces Polypharmacy in a Population-Based Survey of Febrile Illness in Western Kenya.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria diagnostic intervention (community-based testing to guide ACT use) in humans; phase not applicable for cluster designs.
comparator: standard care (without community-based malaria testing intervention)
population: febrile individuals in the community, including children and adults
primary_outcome: Type of medicine consumed for fever (polypharmacy, dual ACT and antibiotic consumption) in relation to malaria test result and location of care
impact_summary: Community-based access to malaria diagnostic testing reduced dual consumption of ACTs and antibiotics for fever, particularly among those seeking care outside the formal healthcare sector.
effect_metric: proportion with dual ACT and antibiotic consumption
effect_estimate: declined from 22.1% at baseline to 16.6% at endline
age_range: 42% aged 5-17 years; overall population includes children and adults

title: Efficacy and immunogenicity of R21/Matrix-M vaccine against clinical malaria after 2 years' follow-up in children in Burkina Faso: a phase 1/2b randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported efficacy results at 12 months post-booster in African children; malaria vaccine is the primary intervention.
population: children aged 5-17 months at enrolment (booster given at 1 year later)
primary_outcome: Occurrence of clinical malaria (vaccine efficacy) following booster vaccination, evaluated over 1 year
impact_summary: A booster dose of R21/Matrix-M maintained high efficacy against clinical malaria, with 80% efficacy in the high-dose adjuvant group over 12 months following the booster.
p_value: p=0.0001 (first year antibody correlation); p=0.02 (second year antibody correlation)
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, Nanoro, Burkina Faso
safety_summary: R21/Matrix-M had a favourable safety profile and was well tolerated
funder: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership 2 (EDCTP2), Wellcome Trust, and NIHR Oxford Biomedical Research Centre

title: Outdoor residual spraying for malaria vector-control in Kayin (Karen) state, Myanmar: A cluster randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results assessing outdoor residual spraying for malaria vector control; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: Villages in Karen (Kayin) state; humans and cows sampled for mosquito biting rates
primary_outcome: Biting rate of malaria mosquitoes assessed with human-landing catch and cow-baited trap collection methods
impact_summary: Outdoor residual spraying rapidly and substantially reduced malaria mosquito biting rates compared to control villages over a 6-month period.
species: Anopheles (malaria vectors, species not specified as P. falciparum/vivax)
transmission_setting: Greater Mekong Subregion, outdoor and early biting mosquitoes challenge existing vector control tools

title: Efficacy of three anti-malarial regimens for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Cambodia, 2009-2011: a randomized controlled trial and brief review.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (three antimalarial regimens) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes at 42 days follow-up.
design: randomized, open-label, parallel group-controlled trial, phase 3
comparator: active comparator (three anti-malarial regimens compared against each other)
population: subjects at least 5 years old with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted efficacy at 42 days
impact_summary: DHA/PPQ and ATQ/PG had acceptable efficacy against uncomplicated falciparum malaria, while AS/MQ efficacy was only 80.6% with evidence of mefloquine resistance.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistance epicentre, Northern Cambodia-Thai border region
safety_summary: One subject withdrew from the ATQ/PG arm due to drug allergy; otherwise no major safety issues reported.

title: Overall and Gender-Specific Effects of Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria with Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapies among Schoolchildren in Mali: A Three-Group Open Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Open-label RCT of intermittent preventive treatment (artemisinin-based combination therapies) for malaria in schoolchildren with reported outcome results on P. falciparum infection, hemoglobin, and educational outcomes.
population: schoolchildren aged 6-13 years
primary_outcome: P. falciparum infection, hemoglobin concentration, and grade point average (GPA)
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with SP plus artesunate or AQ plus artesunate reduced P. falciparum infection compared with control, with SP plus artesunate improving hemoglobin and AQ plus artesunate improving GPA, and girls given SP plus artesunate showing greater GPA improvement than boys.
effect_metric: odds ratio for P. falciparum infection
transmission_setting: Mali, rural village (Kolle), seasonal malaria transmission

title: Impact of mobile phone intervention on intermittent preventive treatment of malaria during pregnancy in Burkina Faso : A pragmatic randomized trial.
journal: Revue d'epidemiologie et de sante publique
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria chemoprevention intervention (IPTp-SP) in pregnant women with primary malaria focus.
comparator: standard care (control group without mobile phone intervention)
population: pregnant women attending antenatal clinic visits
primary_outcome: Proportion of women receiving at least three doses of IPTp-SP before delivery
impact_summary: The mobile phone intervention did not significantly increase the proportion of women receiving three or more doses of IPTp-SP, but it did increase the proportion of timely ANC visits.
follow_up: from first ANC visit until delivery

title: Laboratory and experimental hut trial evaluation of VECTRON ™ T500 for indoor residual spraying (IRS) against insecticide resistant malaria vectors in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating a novel IRS insecticide against malaria vectors with reported efficacy outcomes; vector-control trials are not subject to phase restrictions.
design: experimental hut trial, laboratory cone bioassay study
population: wild free-flying Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes and laboratory mosquito strains (susceptible and pyrethroid resistant)
primary_outcome: Residual efficacy (mortality) and entomological effects (deterrence, blood-feeding inhibition, exophily) of VECTRON T500 against malaria vectors
impact_summary: VECTRON T500 showed good residual efficacy against susceptible and resistant Anopheles strains in laboratory tests and induced 55-73% mortality of wild An. gambiae s.l. in experimental huts, suggesting potential as an IRS product for resistance management.
transmission_setting: malaria endemic area with insecticide-resistant vectors
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: Daily Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or Weekly Chloroquine Among Adults on ART in Malawi
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria chemoprevention (trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and chloroquine prophylaxis) in HIV-positive adults; primary purpose is malaria prevention in humans.
interventions_raw: Standard of Care prophylaxis; Chloroquine (CQ) prophylaxis
population: Adults living with HIV on antiretroviral therapy (ART) with undetectable viral load and ≥250 CD4+ cells/μl
primary_outcome: Severe Events
impact_summary: Chemoprophylaxis with daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole or weekly chloroquine reduced malaria infection and clinical malaria incidence by approximately 90% compared to no prophylaxis, but malaria did not affect HIV viral load or CD4+ cell count.
transmission_setting: High malaria risk area in Malawi
safety_summary: Twelve cases of malaria led to hospitalization and all individuals recovered; malaria infection and clinical malaria were not associated with changes in CD4+ cell count or viral load.

title: LLIN evaluation in Uganda project (LLINEUP): The fabric integrity, chemical content and bioefficacy of long-lasting insecticidal nets treated with and without piperonyl butoxide across two years of operational use in Uganda.
journal: Current research in parasitology & vector-borne diseases
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of LLIN products (malaria prevention vector control) with reported outcome results on durability, chemical content, and bioefficacy over 25 months.
population: households receiving LLINs during Uganda's mass distribution campaign
primary_outcome: Physical condition, chemical content, and bioefficacy of LLINs over time
impact_summary: PBO-treated LLINs (Olyset Plus and PermaNet 3.0) were as physically durable as pyrethroid-only nets and initially more effective against pyrethroid-resistant mosquitoes, but their bioefficacy and PBO content declined substantially over 25 months of operational use.

title: Cellular and antibody response in GMZ2-vaccinated Gabonese volunteers in a controlled human malaria infection trial.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT reporting results of a malaria vaccine candidate (GMZ2) with controlled human malaria infection challenge, including immunogenicity and efficacy outcomes in humans.
design: controlled human malaria infection trial, randomized, phase 2
population: Gabonese adults
primary_outcome: Vaccine efficacy assessed by controlled human malaria infection with P. falciparum sporozoites; cellular and antibody immune responses
impact_summary: GMZ2 vaccination induced antibody but limited cellular immune responses, and broad antibody recognition of multiple parasite antigens rather than the GMZ2-specific response was associated with protection against controlled human malaria infection.

title: Impact of a spatial repellent product on Anopheles and non-Anopheles mosquitoes in Sumba, Indonesia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a spatial repellent vector-control intervention for malaria prevention in humans.
population: households/communities in Sumba (general population, human-landing mosquito catch collectors)
primary_outcome: Human biting rates (HBR) of Anopheles and non-Anopheles mosquitoes and malaria infection hazard rate
impact_summary: The spatial repellent reduced human biting rates for Anopheles (16.4%) and non-Anopheles mosquitoes (Aedes, Armigeres, Culex) both indoors and outdoors, though most reductions were not statistically significant except for some individual species affecting malaria infection hazard rate.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in human biting rate
effect_estimate: 16.4% (Anopheles overall); 44.3% indoors/35.6% outdoors (Aedes); 38.3% indoors/39.1% outdoors (Armigeres); 36.0% indoors/32.3% outdoors (Culex)
p_value: not significant overall, except for An. flavirostris, An. balabacensis, An. maculatus, An. aconitus, An. kochi, An. tessellatus, An. sundaicus (statistically significant)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic region contributing 5% of national malaria cases, also endemic for dengue and filariasis

title: Effectiveness of pyronaridine-artesunate against Plasmodium malariae, Plasmodium ovale spp, and mixed-Plasmodium infections: a post-hoc analysis of the CANTAM-Pyramax trial.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results (day 28 cure rates) for malaria treatment intervention; phase 3b/4 is eligible; post-hoc analysis of CANTAM-Pyramax trial.
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Gabon
population: patients with mixed-Plasmodium infections or non-falciparum mono-infections
primary_outcome: Day 28 cure rate for non-falciparum and mixed-Plasmodium infections
impact_summary: Pyronaridine-artesunate showed high day 28 cure rates (96.3% or higher) against P malariae, P ovale curtisi, P ovale wallikeri, and mixed-Plasmodium infections.
effect_estimate: 96.3% or higher (99.2% for P malariae, 97.9% for P ovale curtisi, 96.3% for P ovale wallikeri)

title: Efficacy, T cell activation and antibody responses in accelerated Plasmodium falciparum sporozoite chemoprophylaxis vaccine regimens.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results comparing accelerated chemoprophylaxis vaccine regimens against placebo using controlled human malaria infection challenge.
design: randomized, placebo-controlled, controlled human malaria infection (CHMI), phase II
population: malaria-naive volunteers
primary_outcome: Vaccine efficacy against controlled human malaria infection (CHMI)
impact_summary: Both the 10-day and 28-day accelerated PfSPZ-CVac vaccination regimens were similarly efficacious against controlled human malaria infection, with the 10-day regimen inducing stronger T cell and antibody responses.
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental, non-endemic setting)

title: Effectiveness of screened ceilings over the current best practice in reducing malaria prevalence in western Kenya: a cluster randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (PCR prevalence and anopheline density) evaluating an insecticide-treated ceiling net intervention for malaria prevention in humans.
population: children 7 months to 10 years old (epidemiological surveys); households (entomological surveys)
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum PCR-positive prevalence (PCRPfPR) and anopheline density
impact_summary: Houses with insecticide-treated ceiling nets plus bed nets had significantly lower malaria prevalence and mosquito density than houses with bed nets alone.

title: Gut and Azithromycin Mechanisms in Infants and Children II
screening_reason: Individually randomized placebo-controlled trial of azithromycin (antimalarial chemoprevention) in children with reported outcome results (malaria RDT positivity at 14 days); Phase 4, not early-phase.
interventions_raw: Azithromycin; Placebo
population: children aged 8 days to 59 months
primary_outcome: Malaria Status
impact_summary: A single oral dose of azithromycin did not reduce malaria RDT positivity compared to placebo, though caregiver-reported fever as an adverse event was less common in the azithromycin arm.
safety_summary: Caregiver-reported fever as an adverse event was less common in the azithromycin arm (OR 0.41, 95% CI 0.18-0.96, P=0.04); no significant differences in clinic visits between arms (P=0.32).

title: Study to Compare the Triple ACT AL+AQ With the ACT AL in Cambodia and Vietnam
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (ACT combination) as primary focus in Phase 3.
interventions_raw: ACT; TACT
population: male and female patients aged 2-65 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Polymerase Chain Reaction Corrected Efficacy Defined as Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR) by Study Arm
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine plus amodiaquine showed similarly high 42-day PCR-corrected efficacy compared with artemether-lumefantrine alone, with no statistically significant difference, but was associated with more mild gastrointestinal adverse events and bradycardia.
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant P. falciparum malaria in the Greater Mekong subregion
safety_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine plus amodiaquine was generally well tolerated but had more mild (grade 1-2) gastrointestinal adverse events (vomiting, nausea) and higher rates of bradycardia (61% vs 38%) compared with artemether-lumefantrine alone; early vomiting requiring retreatment occurred in 3% vs 0%.

title: The positive effect of malaria IPTp-SP on birthweight is mediated by gestational weight gain but modifiable by maternal carriage of enteric pathogens.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing IPTp-SP vs IPTp-DP in pregnant women with reported outcome results on birthweight and maternal nutritional outcomes; primary focus is malaria prevention in pregnancy.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Effect of IPTp-SP versus IPTp-DP on maternal gestational weight gain, nutritional indicators, enteric pathogen carriage, and infant birthweight
impact_summary: IPTp-SP was associated with greater maternal gestational weight gain and reduced EAEC prevalence compared to IPTp-DP, and this weight gain mediated SP's positive effect on infant birthweight, though maternal enteric pathogen carriage diminished this benefit.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio (EAEC infection) and adjusted mean birthweight difference
effect_estimate: ORadj = 0.07 (EAEC infection after 3+ doses); adjusted mean birthweight difference SP vs DP = 156.0 g
effect_ci: OR CI95 = 0.12-0.39; birthweight difference CI95 = -18.0 to 336.9 g
follow_up: from first antenatal visit until delivery
funder: multiple funding bodies listed in Acknowledgements (not specified in abstract)

title: Serological evaluation of the effectiveness of reactive focal mass drug administration and reactive vector control to reduce malaria transmission in Zambezi Region, Namibia: Results from a secondary analysis of a cluster randomised trial.
screening_reason: Cluster randomised trial reporting outcome results from a malaria intervention (reactive focal mass drug administration and reactive vector control) in humans at low transmission; phase not applicable for cluster-randomised design.
design: cluster randomised trial, secondary analysis, 2x2 factorial
comparator: standard care/reference arms (no rfMDA, no RAVC)
population: residents of study clusters in a low-transmission region tested via reactive case detection
primary_outcome: Sero-prevalence and continuous antibody responses to Plasmodium falciparum serological markers (Etramp5.Ag1, GEXP18, HSP40.Ag1, Rh2.2030, EBA175, PfMSP119, PfAMA1, PfGLURP.R2) as trial endpoints
impact_summary: Reactive focal mass drug administration and reactive vector control, alone and combined, significantly reduced Etramp5.Ag1 sero-prevalence, with serological endpoints providing improved precision and statistical power compared to qPCR prevalence.
effect_metric: adjusted prevalence ratio (aPR) for Etramp5.Ag1 sero-prevalence
transmission_setting: low transmission, seasonal malaria, Zambezi Region, Namibia
funder: Novartis Foundation (A122666), Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (OPP1160129), Horchow Family Fund (5,300,375,400)

title: Seasonal Malaria Vaccination (RTS,S/AS01) and Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SP/AQ)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS01E) and seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) interventions in children; Phase 3 trial with primary malaria focus.
interventions_raw: RABIPUR®; RTS,S/AS01; SMC with SP+AQ; SMC placebo
comparator: SMC alone, RTS,S/AS01E alone (compared against combined intervention)
population: young children
primary_outcome: Incidence of Clinical Episodes of Malaria
impact_summary: Combining seasonal RTS,S/AS01E vaccination with seasonal malaria chemoprevention substantially reduced malaria incidence and modestly reduced wasting prevalence compared to either intervention alone, but had little effect on other nutritional indicators like stunting.
effect_estimate: 0.88 (2017), 0.79 (2018) for wasting prevalence, combined vs SMC alone
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, high burden area
funder: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

title: Multi-Dose Priming Regimens of PfSPZ Vaccine: Safety and Efficacy against Controlled Human Malaria Infection in Equatoguinean Adults.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy results for PfSPZ malaria vaccine in humans; Phase 2 safety and efficacy assessment against controlled infection.
population: 18- to 32-year-old adults
primary_outcome: Vaccine efficacy against homologous controlled human malaria infection (Pf parasitemia by qPCR) 6-7 weeks after vaccination
impact_summary: Only the multi-dose priming regimen given on days 1, 8, and 29 provided significant protection against controlled human malaria infection, with 51.3% vaccine efficacy.
safety_summary: All four regimens were safe and well tolerated, with no significant differences in adverse events between vaccinees and normal saline controls or between regimens.

title: Efficacy of 3-day low dose quinine plus clindamycin versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kenyan children (CLINDAQUINE): an open-label randomized trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment in humans with reported primary outcome results (PCR-corrected ACPR rates on day 28).
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected rate of adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 28 in the per-protocol population
impact_summary: 3-day low dose quinine plus clindamycin was markedly less effective than artemether-lumefantrine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Kenyan children, with no evidence to support its use.
effect_metric: treatment difference in PCR-corrected ACPR rate
safety_summary: Three cases of severe malaria were recorded as serious adverse events in the quinine plus clindamycin group.

title: Efficacy and safety of artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria and prevalence of molecular markers associated with artemisinin and partner drug resistance in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in humans with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
design: randomized, open-label, phase IV clinical trial
population: Children aged 6 months to 10 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cumulative efficacy (treatment failure/recrudescence) at day 28 (AL) and day 42 (DP)
impact_summary: DP remained highly effective and safe for treating uncomplicated malaria in Uganda, while AL showed common recurrent infections with PCR-corrected efficacy falling below 90% at two sites.
safety_summary: No serious adverse events were reported associated with any of the regimens.

title: Bioefficacy and durability of Olyset® Plus, a permethrin and piperonyl butoxide-treated insecticidal net in a 3-year long trial in Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating LLIN durability and bioefficacy against malaria vectors, a core malaria prevention intervention.
population: households in a malaria endemic rice cultivation zone
primary_outcome: Bioefficacy (cone bioassay knockdown/mortality and tunnel test mortality/blood-feeding inhibition) and physical/chemical durability of LLINs over 3 years
impact_summary: Olyset® Plus retained WHO efficacy criteria longer (about 2 years) than Olyset® Net (1-1.5 years), but neither net met the 3-year WHO efficacy criteria, with comparable physical durability and survivorship between the two nets.
effect_metric: proportion meeting WHO efficacy criteria (knockdown/mortality/blood-feeding inhibition)
effect_estimate: Over 80% of Olyset® Plus and Olyset® Net passed WHO efficacy criteria up to 18 and 12 months respectively

title: Safety of KAE609 in Adults With Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of cipargamin for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treatment with reported primary safety outcome results; Phase 2 is not early-phase.
interventions_raw: KAE609; Coartem
population: adults with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Number of Participants With at Least 2 CTCAE Grades Increase From Baseline in Alanine Aminotransferase (ALT) or Aspartate Aminotransferase (AST)
impact_summary: Cipargamin (KAE609) at doses of 10-150 mg was well tolerated with hepatic adverse event rates similar to artemether-lumefantrine and no significant difference between groups.
effect_metric: proportion with ≥2 CTCAE Grade increase in ALT/AST
safety_summary: Cipargamin was well tolerated across all doses with no significant increase in hepatic adverse events (ALT/AST elevations) compared to artemether-lumefantrine; general safety and tolerability were similar between groups; no safety concerns identified.

title: Mechanistic Modeling of Primaquine Pharmacokinetics, Gametocytocidal Activity, and Mosquito Infectivity.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing primaquine doses and placebo in humans with reported outcome results on gametocyte clearance and mosquito infectivity, with malaria transmission-blocking as the primary focus.
design: randomized, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling study
population: adult Malians with P. falciparum gametocytemia
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic relationships for gametocyte clearance and mosquito infectivity following primaquine dosing
impact_summary: A single low dose of primaquine (0.25 mg/kg) added to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine rapidly and dose-dependently sterilized P. falciparum gametocytes, preventing mosquito infectivity.
effect_estimate: 0.25 mg base/kg dose rapidly prevented transmissibility
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; study focused on pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic modeling rather than adverse events.

title: Tafenoquine exposure assessment, safety, and relapse prevention efficacy in children with Plasmodium vivax malaria: open-label, single-arm, non-comparative, multicentre, pharmacokinetic bridging, phase 2 trial.
screening_reason: Published open-label RCT reporting efficacy and safety outcomes in children with P. vivax malaria treated with tafenoquine, a 8-aminoquinoline antimalarial for relapse prevention.
design: open-label, single-arm, non-comparative, multicentre, pharmacokinetic bridging, phase 2 trial
population: children aged 2-15 years weighing 5 kg or more with P vivax malaria and G6PD activity more than 70% of local population median
primary_outcome: Tafenoquine area under the concentration-time curve extrapolated to infinity (AUC[0-∞]) by patient body weight in the pharmacokinetic population
impact_summary: Single-dose tafenoquine, including a dispersible formulation, achieved adequate exposure across weight-based dosing groups and provided high recurrence-free efficacy with safety consistent with adults, aside from post-dose vomiting with the 50 mg dispersible tablet.
transmission_setting: community health centres in Vietnam and Colombia
safety_summary: Adverse events were consistent with previous studies; 12% (7/60) had post-dose vomiting or spitting with the 50 mg dispersible tablet, mitigated after strategy changes; no deaths occurred.
funder: GlaxoSmithKline and Medicines for Malaria Venture

title: Long-term safety of the tafenoquine antimalarial chemoprophylaxis regimen: A 12-month, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: RCT of tafenoquine antimalarial chemoprophylaxis with reported safety outcomes in healthy adults over 52 weeks; phase not early-phase (safety-only is acceptable for chemoprevention trials).
population: healthy adults
primary_outcome: Incidence of protocol-defined Serious Ophthalmic Safety Events and other safety assessments (ophthalmic, neuropsychiatric, laboratory) over 52 weeks
impact_summary: 52-week tafenoquine prophylaxis was well tolerated with no significant difference in serious ophthalmic events or overall adverse events compared to placebo, supporting its long-term safety.
safety_summary: No significant difference in overall AEs between groups (91.0% tafenoquine vs 89.9% placebo, p=0.65); higher incidence of reversible cornea verticillata (54.5%) and nausea (13.0%) with tafenoquine; psychiatric AEs similar between groups; reversible changes in hemoglobin, methemoglobin, creatinine, and BUN noted.

title: Evaluation of pilot implementation of seasonal malaria chemoprevention on morbidity in young children in Northern Sahelian Ghana.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial evaluating SMC (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine) for malaria prevention in children with reported outcome results on parasitemia, severe/mild malaria incidence, and anemia.
design: cluster-randomized, pilot implementation study, before-and-after comparison
population: young children
primary_outcome: Malaria morbidity (parasitaemia, severe and mild malaria incidence) and anaemia (haemoglobin levels) before and after SMC implementation
impact_summary: SMC implementation in Northern Ghana was associated with reduced malaria parasitaemia and anaemia and reduced severe malaria incidence compared to the non-intervention area, demonstrating feasibility and effectiveness.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; high participant retention (92.9% intervention, 89.5% non-intervention) suggested tolerability of the intervention.

title: Efficacy of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Madagascar, 2018.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drugs (ASAQ and AL) for uncomplicated falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcomes meeting WHO protocol standards.
comparator: active comparator (ASAQ vs AL, randomized by site)
population: children aged six months to 14 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria and parasitaemia 1000-100,000/µl
primary_outcome: Day-28 PCR-corrected and PCR-uncorrected cumulative therapeutic efficacy of ASAQ and AL
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed PCR-corrected therapeutic efficacies above the WHO acceptable cut-off of 90%, with no molecular evidence of artemisinin resistance detected.
transmission_setting: tropical (northwest, Ankazomborona) and equatorial (southeast, Matanga) endemic areas

title: The impact of mosquito proof lids of underground tanks "tanka" on the breeding of Anopheles stephensi in a village in western Rajasthan, India.
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial (two villages with intervention and control arms) that has reported outcome results for a malaria vector control intervention (mosquito-proof lids on underground tanks), with malaria prevention as its primary focus.
design: controlled intervention study, non-randomized, two-village comparison (intervention vs control)
comparator: control village with no lid replacement (standard/conventional lids)
population: underground water storage tanks (tankas) and village community, adult mosquito density assessments
primary_outcome: Anopheles stephensi adult mosquito density (per man-hour) and mosquito breeding presence in tankas
impact_summary: Replacement of damaged tanka lids with mosquito-proof PVC lids led to complete prevention of Anopheles stephensi breeding and a significant reduction in adult mosquito density in the intervention village compared to no reduction in the control village.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in Anopheles stephensi density per man-hour
transmission_setting: desert climate, unstable and seasonal malaria transmission
safety_summary: Not applicable; no adverse events reported as this was an environmental/entomological intervention

title: Effects of Door-to-Door Hang-Up Visits on the Use of Long-Lasting Insecticide-Treated Mosquito Nets in the Democratic Republic of the Congo: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: International journal of environmental research and public health
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria prevention intervention (LLIN use) in humans.
comparator: conventional fixed distribution from distribution centers accompanied by a mass distribution campaign
population: households with at least one child aged less than five (including pregnant women and children under 5)
primary_outcome: Use of long-lasting insecticide-treated mosquito nets (LLINs)
impact_summary: Door-to-door hang-up visits were not significantly more effective than conventional distribution in increasing LLIN use, though a possible benefit was seen among the youngest children.
age_range: children under 5, pregnant women, all study participants

title: A three-antigen Plasmodium falciparum DNA prime-Adenovirus boost malaria vaccine regimen is superior to a two-antigen regimen and protects against controlled human malaria infection in healthy malaria-naïve adults.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (DNA prime-ChAd63 boost) with reported efficacy results against controlled human malaria infection in healthy adults.
comparator: two-antigen (CA) vaccine versus infectivity controls (unvaccinated) in controlled human malaria infection
population: healthy malaria-naïve adults
primary_outcome: Time to parasitemia (vaccine efficacy) after controlled human malaria infection assessed by thick blood smears up to 28 days post-CHMI
impact_summary: The three-antigen ChAd63 CAT vaccine (CSP, AMA1, ME-TRAP) significantly protected against controlled human malaria infection compared to infectivity controls and the two-antigen CA vaccine, which showed no protective efficacy.
p_value: p=0.0406 (CAT vs controls); p=0.0229 (CAT vs CA)
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental, Pf3D7 strain via mosquito bite)
