safety_summary: Systemic adverse events were significantly higher after the ChAd63 boost than after DNA immunizations, and the CAT vaccine had increased frequencies of systemic AEs compared to CA, but these were transient and associated with increased vector dosing.

title: Therapeutic Efficacy of Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapies in Democratic Republic of the Congo and Investigation of Molecular Markers of Antimalarial Resistance.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemisinin-based combination therapies for malaria treatment with reported efficacy outcomes in humans.
comparator: active comparator (three ACT regimens compared across sites: AL, ASAQ, DP)
population: Children aged 6-59 months with confirmed uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Uncorrected and PCR-corrected cumulative efficacy at 28 days (AL and ASAQ) or 42 days (DP)
impact_summary: ACT efficacy varied by site and drug, with PCR-corrected efficacy below the WHO 90% threshold for two ACTs at one site, raising concern about emerging antimalarial resistance in DRC.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic Democratic Republic of the Congo, multiple sites

title: Effect of a single dose of oral azithromycin on malaria parasitaemia in children: a randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating azithromycin (malaria chemoprevention intervention) in children, with parasitaemia measured at 14 days and 6 months follow-up.
population: children aged 8 days to 59 months
primary_outcome: Malaria parasitaemia (by thin and thick smear and rapid diagnostic test) at 14 days and 6 months after treatment
impact_summary: A single dose of oral azithromycin did not reduce malaria parasitaemia compared to placebo at 14 days or 6 months follow-up.
effect_estimate: 20% vs 17% at 14 days; 7.6% vs 5.6% at 6 months (azithromycin vs placebo)

title: Unanticipated CNS Safety Signal in a Placebo-Controlled, Randomized Trial of Co-Administered Atovaquone-Proguanil and Amodiaquine.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported safety and pharmacokinetic outcome results assessing a malaria chemoprevention intervention (atovaquone-proguanil plus amodiaquine) in humans.
population: healthy adult males and females of Black sub-Saharan African origin
primary_outcome: Safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of co-administered atovaquone-proguanil and amodiaquine
impact_summary: Co-administration of atovaquone-proguanil and amodiaquine showed no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions but caused an unexpectedly high incidence of extrapyramidal adverse effects, leading to a recommendation against further development of the combination for malaria prophylaxis in African children.
follow_up: 3 days of treatment with follow-up assessments
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria chemoprevention setting in African children
safety_summary: Adverse events occurred in 100% of ATV-PG/AQ recipients, 91.7% of ATV-PG recipients, 91.7% of AQ recipients, and 25% of placebo recipients; 2 of 8 participants in the ATV-PG/AQ group experienced extrapyramidal adverse effects (psychiatric and physical) on day 3, unrelated to drug plasma pharmacokinetics or CYP2C8 phenotype.

title: Imatinib augments standard malaria combination therapy without added toxicity.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: safety and tolerability of imatinib + SOC, with parasite clearance and toxicity assessed
impact_summary: Adding imatinib to standard malaria therapy accelerated parasite and fever clearance and prevented delayed parasite clearance without increasing toxicity.
effect_estimate: no cases of DPC in imatinib + SOC group
transmission_setting: region in Vietnam with high rate of delayed parasite clearance
safety_summary: Imatinib + SOC-treated participants showed no increase in number or severity of adverse events and no obvious drug-related toxicities.

title: High efficacy of microbial larvicides for malaria vectors control in the city of Yaounde Cameroon following a cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing microbial larvicide efficacy for malaria vector control in humans.
population: urban residents in clusters with mosquito breeding habitats
primary_outcome: Anopheline density collected using CDC light traps
impact_summary: Larviciding with VectoMax reduced adult anopheline biting density by 68% and entomological inoculation rate by 79% in the intervention clusters compared to non-intervention clusters.
species: Anopheles (malaria vector species, not specified as P. falciparum/vivax)

title: Effectiveness of a long-lasting insecticide treatment kit (ICON® Maxx) for polyester nets over three years of household use: a WHO phase III trial in Tanzania.
screening_reason: Household-randomized controlled trial of ICON Maxx insecticide treatment for malaria vector control reporting 3-year outcome results on net efficacy and durability.
design: household-randomized, prospective, phase III trial, WHO-standard trial with cross-sectional and cohort surveys
comparator: conventional treated nets (lambda-cyhalothrin without binder) as positive control
population: households using bed nets
primary_outcome: insecticidal efficacy of treated nets (cone and tunnel bioassay mortality/feeding inhibition thresholds) over 36 months of household use
impact_summary: ICON Maxx-treated polyester nets retained sufficient insecticidal efficacy over 36 months of household use, meeting WHO durability criteria and earning full WHO recommendation, outperforming conventional treated nets.
effect_metric: percentage of nets meeting WHO efficacy threshold (combined cone and tunnel criteria)
effect_estimate: 97% (ICON Maxx) vs 67% (CTN) at 12 months; >90% ICON Maxx at 36 months
transmission_setting: north-eastern Tanzania, household net use setting

title: Cotrimoxazole versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in HIV-infected pregnant women in Bangui, Central African Republic: A pragmatic randomised controlled trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing two malaria prevention strategies (cotrimoxazole vs. sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in HIV-infected pregnant women; malaria prevention is the primary focus.
population: HIV-infected pregnant women with CD4+ count ≥350 cells/mm3
primary_outcome: Placental malaria infection defined by microscopic parasitaemia or PCR
impact_summary: Cotrimoxazole was not shown to be significantly more effective than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine IPTp in preventing placental malaria infection, but had good compliance and safety.
safety_summary: Low overall rate of adverse events in both arms; good compliance and drug safety with cotrimoxazole

title: Effect of seasonal malaria chemoprevention plus azithromycin on Plasmodium falciparum transmission: gametocyte infectivity and mosquito fitness.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT testing seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) with/without azithromycin in children, with reported outcomes on P. falciparum transmission and mosquito fitness.
comparator: placebo (SPAQ alone vs SPAQ+azithromycin) and untreated control children
population: children receiving seasonal malaria chemoprevention and untreated children from the same area
primary_outcome: Prevalence of P. falciparum gametocytes and infectivity to Anopheles gambiae mosquitoes (proportion of infectious feeds and oocyst prevalence)
impact_summary: SMC (SPAQ with or without azithromycin) reduced P. falciparum gametocyte prevalence and mosquito infection rates compared to untreated controls, but adding azithromycin unexpectedly increased gametocyte infectivity to mosquitoes.
effect_metric: proportion of infectious feeds (likelihood ratio test)
p_value: P = 0.02 (AZ effect on infectious feeds); P < 0.0001 (SMC effect on asexual and gametocyte prevalence)
safety_summary: Slight negative effect of SPAQ and SPAQ+AZ on mosquito survival compared to controls; no human safety data reported in this abstract.

title: High Prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum K13 Mutations in Rwanda Is Associated With Slow Parasite Clearance After Treatment With Artemether-Lumefantrine.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results for malaria treatment comparing artemether-lumefantrine and cipargamin in humans.
population: patients with malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and treatment efficacy after artemether-lumefantrine or cipargamin treatment
impact_summary: High prevalence of K13 R561H mutation in Rwanda was associated with delayed parasite clearance, though artemether-lumefantrine efficacy remained high with a 94.4% PCR-corrected cure rate.

title: Two chemoattenuated PfSPZ malaria vaccines induce sterile hepatic immunity.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of a malaria vaccine intervention (PfSPZ-CVac) with reported efficacy results against controlled human malaria infection.
comparator: infectivity control (unvaccinated challenge controls) and low-dose vs high-dose vaccine regimens
population: healthy adult volunteers
primary_outcome: Vaccine efficacy against homologous and heterologous controlled human malaria infection (CHMI) three months after immunization, assessed by parasitaemia
impact_summary: Higher-dose PfSPZ-CVac(PYR) and PfSPZ-CVac(CQ) regimens induced high-level, durable sterile protective efficacy against both homologous and heterologous controlled human malaria infection three months after immunization, whereas low-dose PfSPZ-CVac(PYR) gave minimal protection.
effect_estimate: Low-dose PfSPZ-CVac(PYR): 22.2% homologous; High-dose PfSPZ-CVac(PYR): 87.5% homologous, 77.8% heterologous; PfSPZ-CVac(CQ): 100% heterologous
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental, non-endemic challenge setting)
safety_summary: Not detailed in abstract beyond vaccination under prophylactic cover with pyrimethamine or chloroquine to kill liver-stage or blood-stage parasites.

title: Extended follow-up of children in a phase2b trial of the GMZ2 malaria vaccine.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy outcomes over 24 months follow-up testing a malaria vaccine (GMZ2/alum) in children; Phase 2b is not early-phase and meets all inclusion criteria.
population: children aged 12-60 months
primary_outcome: Documented fever with parasitaemia of at least 5000/μL
impact_summary: Extended 2-year follow-up showed GMZ2/alum vaccine had low overall efficacy of 6.5% against clinical malaria, with slightly higher efficacy in older children, and was well tolerated with no vaccine-related serious adverse events.
safety_summary: 187 serious adverse events (91 GMZ2, 96 rabies) recorded in 167 individuals; no GMZ2 vaccine-related serious adverse events; vaccine was well tolerated.

title: Is biological larviciding against malaria a starting point for integrated multi-disease control? Observations from a cluster randomized trial in rural Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results (mosquito species reductions) evaluating a malaria vector-control intervention (Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis larviciding) in humans' environment.
comparator: no treatment vs full vs guided larviciding intervention
population: rural villages in a malaria-endemic area (mosquito populations sampled)
primary_outcome: Reduction in abundance of non-primary target mosquito species (Culex and Aedes) following larviciding intervention
impact_summary: Larviciding had limited or no impact on Culex mosquitoes but reduced Aedes mosquito abundance by up to 34% when all breeding sites were treated.
follow_up: one intervention rainy season compared to baseline year

title: Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets Incorporating Piperonyl Butoxide Reduce the Risk of Malaria in Children in Western Kenya: A Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (PBO-LLINs) with reported outcome results on anopheline density and malaria prevalence in children.
population: children aged 7 months to 10 years
primary_outcome: Anopheline density and Plasmodium falciparum PCR-positive prevalence (PCRpfPR) in children
impact_summary: PBO-LLINs reduced both anopheline mosquito density and P. falciparum infection prevalence in children compared to standard LLINs, confirming superiority of PBO-LLINs.

title: Cost of community-led larval source management and house improvement for malaria control: a cost analysis within a cluster-randomized trial in a rural district in Malawi.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of malaria vector-control interventions (house improvement and larval source management) with reported outcome results (cost analysis).
comparator: standard national malaria control interventions (no HI/LSM arm as comparator)
population: rural community population (general population in study area)
primary_outcome: Incremental economic implementation cost per person per year of house improvement (HI), larval source management (LSM), and HI+LSM interventions
impact_summary: Community-led implementation of house improvement and larval source management in rural Malawi cost $27.04, $25.06, and $33.44 per person per year respectively, with total programme costs of $626,152, driven mainly by staff, transport, and labour costs.
effect_metric: incremental economic cost per person per year

title: Exploratory analysis of the effect of helminth infection on the immunogenicity and efficacy of the asexual blood-stage malaria vaccine candidate GMZ2.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (GMZ2) with reported efficacy and immunogenicity outcome results in humans.
population: healthy, lifelong malaria-exposed adult volunteers
primary_outcome: Time to malaria (presence of P. falciparum parasites in blood with at least one symptom) over 35 days following CHMI
impact_summary: Helminth infection, particularly with Schistosoma haematobium and soil-transmitted helminths, was associated with earlier malaria episodes and reduced vaccine immunogenicity, suggesting helminth infection may impair naturally acquired and vaccine-induced protection against malaria.

title: Persistent Submicroscopic Plasmodium falciparum Parasitemia 72 Hours after Treatment with Artemether-Lumefantrine Predicts 42-Day Treatment Failure in Mali and Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported outcome results (42-day treatment failure); primary purpose is antimalarial drug efficacy in humans; Phase 3 level evidence.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria treated with artemether-lumefantrine and other ACTs
primary_outcome: Day 42 treatment failure (microscopically detectable recurrent P. falciparum parasitemia)
impact_summary: Patients with qPCR-detectable submicroscopic parasitemia at 72 hours after artemether-lumefantrine treatment were significantly more likely to experience recurrent parasitemia by day 42 and had a shorter interval to their next clinical episode compared to those with complete clearance or other drug regimens.
transmission_setting: varying malaria transmission intensity across sites in West Africa

title: Therapeutic efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mali, 2015-2016.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported efficacy outcomes at days 28 and 42.
design: randomized, in vivo therapeutic efficacy study
population: children 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Uncorrected and PCR-corrected clinical and parasitological efficacy at days 28 and 42
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine remained effective treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Sélingué, Mali, with ASAQ showing significantly higher efficacy than AL.

title: The effect of community-driven larval source management and house improvement on malaria transmission when added to the standard malaria control strategies in Malawi: a cluster-randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: This is a cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria vector-control interventions (house improvement and larval source management) as primary interventions in humans.
comparator: standard NMCP interventions (control arm) versus house improvement, larval source management, or both combined
population: villagers/households in Malawi (all ages)
primary_outcome: Entomological inoculation rate (EIR)
impact_summary: Neither house improvement, larval source management, nor their combination further reduced malaria transmission or prevalence beyond reductions seen across all four arms over the trial period.
transmission_setting: high insecticide-treated bed net use, declining transmission setting
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Heterologous protection against malaria by a simple chemoattenuated PfSPZ vaccine regimen in a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Double-blinded randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine intervention with reported efficacy outcomes against heterologous challenge infection in human volunteers.
population: malaria-naive volunteers
primary_outcome: Vaccine efficacy against heterologous controlled human malaria infection (CHMI) with Pf7G8 strain and safety
impact_summary: 10 of 13 vaccinated participants were sterilely protected against heterologous malaria challenge while all 5 placebo recipients developed parasitemia.
safety_summary: Immunization was well tolerated with self-limiting grade 1-2 headaches, pyrexia and fatigue that diminished with each vaccination.

title: Malaria vaccine becomes first to achieve 75% efficacy goal in trial of children.
screening_reason: RCT reporting outcome results for a malaria vaccine intervention in children meeting the primary efficacy endpoint.
population: children
impact_summary: A malaria vaccine achieved 75% efficacy, becoming the first to meet the WHO's efficacy goal in a trial of children.

title: Effectiveness of Intermittent Preventive Treatment With Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaqunine Against Malaria in Pregnancy in Tanzania: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy (IPTp) with reported outcome results; malaria prevention is the primary purpose.
population: malaria-free pregnant women from moderate malaria transmission areas
primary_outcome: Prevalence of histopathologically confirmed placental malaria (active or past infection)
impact_summary: Monthly IPTp with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine significantly reduced placental malaria and low birth weight compared with IPTp-SP.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported beyond birth outcome differences; no adverse events described in abstract.

title: Improved housing versus usual practice for additional protection against clinical malaria in The Gambia (RooPfs): a household-randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (clinical malaria incidence and vector density) testing a malaria prevention intervention in humans in a malaria-endemic area.
comparator: usual practice (unmodified traditional houses) with existing malaria control measures
population: children aged 6 months to 13 years living in households with insecticide-treated nets, indoor residual spraying, and seasonal malaria chemoprevention for under-5s
primary_outcome: incidence of clinical malaria in study children with more than 50% of observations each year, and household vector density
impact_summary: Improved housing (metal roofs and screened doors/windows) did not reduce clinical malaria incidence and was in fact associated with higher incidence compared with unmodified traditional houses in an area with high coverage of insecticide-treated nets, indoor residual spraying, and seasonal malaria chemoprevention.
safety_summary: Not reported
funder: Medical Research Council, UK Department for International Development, and Wellcome Trust (Global Health Trials)

title: Efficacy of interceptor® G2, a long-lasting insecticide mixture net treated with chlorfenapyr and alpha-cypermethrin against Anopheles funestus: experimental hut trials in north-eastern Tanzania.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector-control intervention (insecticide-treated bed nets) against resistant Anopheles funestus in field conditions.
comparator: chlorfenapyr-treated net (positive control) and standard alpha-cypermethrin LLIN Interceptor LN (IG1)
population: wild, free-flying pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles funestus mosquitoes entering experimental huts
primary_outcome: Mosquito mortality
impact_summary: Interceptor G2 caused significantly higher mortality in pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles funestus than the standard pyrethroid-only LLIN, with no significant loss of efficacy after 20 washes.
effect_metric: risk ratio (mortality, unwashed IG2 vs unwashed Interceptor LN)
transmission_setting: pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles funestus, malaria-endemic north-eastern Tanzania

title: Impact and cost-effectiveness of a lethal house lure against malaria transmission in central Côte d'Ivoire: a two-arm, cluster-randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Two-arm cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (clinical malaria incidence over 2 years); primary purpose is malaria vector control in humans; phase not applicable for cluster trial.
population: children aged 6 months to 10 years, households in village-level clusters
primary_outcome: Clinical malaria incidence recorded by active case detection over 2 years in cohorts of children aged 6 months to 10 years
impact_summary: Screening plus Eave Tubes combined with insecticide-treated nets significantly reduced clinical malaria incidence in children compared with insecticide-treated nets alone.
transmission_setting: central Côte d'Ivoire, endemic malaria transmission
safety_summary: No serious adverse events associated with the intervention were reported during follow-up.

title: Social group and health-care provider interventions to increase the demand for malaria rapid diagnostic tests among community members in Ebonyi state, Nigeria: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating malaria rapid diagnostic test demand-promotion interventions (diagnosis focus) in humans.
population: children under 5, children aged 5-17 years, and adults (excluding pregnant women) in the community
primary_outcome: Proportion of children younger than 5 years with fever or malaria-like illness in the 2 weeks preceding a household survey who received a malaria rapid diagnostic test (MRDT); coprimary outcome same among those aged 5 years and older including adults
impact_summary: Both the social group intervention and the social group plus provider intervention significantly increased the proportion of children and adults receiving an MRDT compared with control, with no significant difference between the two intervention arms.
effect_estimate: 28.8% (children <5, social group arm); 32.7% (children <5, social group plus provider arm); 25.6% (children ≥5, social group arm); 28.0% (children ≥5, social group plus provider arm)
age_range: under 5 years and 5 to 17 years, plus adults
safety_summary: Not reported
funder: There was no funding source for this study.

title: Influence of cytochrome P450 (CYP) 2C8 polymorphisms on the efficacy and tolerability of artesunate-amodiaquine treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Zanzibar.
screening_reason: Randomized clinical trial comparing two malaria treatments (AS-AQ vs artemether-lumefantrine) with reported outcome results (treatment efficacy and adverse events) in a malaria population.
design: pharmacogenetic analysis of samples from randomized clinical trials
population: children under five years of age with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Association between CYP2C8*2/*3 genotype and treatment outcome (re-infection/recrudescence) and adverse events after artesunate-amodiaquine treatment
impact_summary: CYP2C8*2 and CYP2C8*3 alleles did not significantly affect treatment efficacy but were significantly associated with increased occurrence of non-serious adverse events.
p_value: P = 0.003 (adverse events); P = 0.25 and P = 0.31 (treatment outcome)
safety_summary: Carriers of CYP2C8*2 or CYP2C8*3 alleles had significantly increased occurrence of non-serious adverse events compared to wild-type homozygotes (44.9% vs 28.1%, P=0.003).

title: Randomized Controlled Trial of the Electrocardiographic Effects of Four Antimalarials for Pregnant Women with Uncomplicated Malaria on the Thailand-Myanmar Border.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria treatment in pregnant women with reported outcome results (ECG findings); malaria is the primary focus.
comparator: active comparator (artemether-lumefantrine extended regimen vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine vs artesunate-mefloquine, with chloroquine for P. vivax recurrences)
population: pregnant women with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Electrocardiographic QT interval corrected for heart rate (QTcP) at peak drug concentration
impact_summary: None of the four antimalarial regimens produced QT prolongation exceeding conventional thresholds for torsade de pointes risk in pregnant women, though dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and chloroquine caused significantly greater QTcP prolongation than artemether-lumefantrine.
effect_metric: adjusted predicted mean difference in QTcP (ms)
effect_estimate: 17.84 ms (DP vs AL+); 18.31 ms (chloroquine vs AL+); 2.45 ms (ASMQ vs AL+)
p_value: <0.001 (DP and chloroquine vs AL+); 0.47 (ASMQ vs AL+); 0.91 (DP vs chloroquine)
safety_summary: No patients had an uncorrected QT interval or QTcP exceeding 480 ms at any time; none of the treatments exceeded conventional thresholds for torsade de pointes risk.

title: Data on pilot assessment of efficacy of artemether lumefantrine when co-administered with ciprofloxacin in malaria-typhoid co-infected patients.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasitological and clinical failures, drug concentration, organ function) testing a malaria treatment intervention with direct patient outcomes.
comparator: concomitant AL and ciprofloxacin vs staggered dosing vs AL alone
population: febrile volunteers with malaria mono-infection or malaria-typhoid co-infection
primary_outcome: PCR-uncorrected Early Treatment Failure, Late Clinical Failure, Late Parasitological Failure, day 7 serum lumefantrine concentration
impact_summary: This pilot dataset describes treatment outcomes and lumefantrine pharmacokinetics when AL is co-administered with ciprofloxacin for malaria-typhoid co-infection, providing baseline data to support a future randomized efficacy trial.
safety_summary: Liver and kidney function parameters, haematological indices, and axillary body temperature were monitored across treatment groups.

title: Improving malaria preventive practices and pregnancy outcomes through a health education intervention: A randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention intervention (ITN use and IPTp uptake) in pregnant women in Nigeria; not early-phase.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Malaria preventive practices (ITN use, IPTp uptake) and pregnancy outcomes (haematocrit levels, malaria diagnosis, birth weight)
impact_summary: The health education intervention significantly improved reported ITN use, IPTp uptake, and haematocrit levels, but had no significant effect on reported malaria diagnosis or birth weight.
follow_up: 4 months post-intervention, and end of pregnancy

title: Anti-malarial efficacy and resistance monitoring of artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine shows inadequate efficacy in children in Burkina Faso, 2017-2018.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in children with reported outcome results on efficacy at day 28 and 42.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Uncorrected and PCR-corrected efficacy to day 28 for AL and day 42 for DP
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine showed inadequate efficacy in some sites in Burkina Faso, with no evidence of Pfk13-associated artemisinin resistance.
safety_summary: No Pfk13 mutation associated with artemisinin resistance was observed; no significant association found between treatment outcome and Pfmdr1 86Y mutation or Pfpm2/Pfmdr1 copy number variation

title: Small-scale field evaluation of the entomological efficacy and the residual activity of Fludora® Fusion WP-SB indoor residual spraying against Anopheles culicifacies s.l. in Gujarat, India.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of vector control (IRS) intervention for malaria with reported entomological efficacy outcomes; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
design: randomized, small-scale field trial, entomological study
comparator: unsprayed control, clothianidin alone, deltamethrin alone, bendiocarb alone
population: households in rural villages, Anopheles culicifacies s.l. mosquito populations
primary_outcome: Entomological efficacy and residual activity of indoor residual spraying measured via cone bioassay mortality and other entomological parameters (indoor resting density, excito-repellency, blood-feeding inhibition, delayed mortality)
impact_summary: Fludora Fusion WP-SB showed residual efficacy lasting 7 months and performed equal or better than deltamethrin and bendiocarb alone against pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles culicifacies.
effect_estimate: no significant difference between treatment arms
transmission_setting: rural malaria vector setting in India

title: The Duration of Protection from Azithromycin Against Malaria, Acute Respiratory, Gastrointestinal, and Skin Infections When Given Alongside Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention: Secondary Analyses of Data from a Clinical Trial in Houndé, Burkina Faso, and Bougouni, Mali.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria chemoprevention intervention (SMC+azithromycin) as primary purpose in humans.
population: children aged 3-59 months receiving seasonal malaria chemoprevention
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria, hospital admissions, deaths, gastroenteritis, pneumonia, and nonmalaria fevers with skin conditions by time since treatment administration
impact_summary: Azithromycin added to seasonal malaria chemoprevention provided broad but short-lived protection against malaria, gastroenteritis, pneumonia, and nonmalaria fevers with skin conditions, mostly within the first 2 weeks post-administration, with no evidence of protection against hospital admissions or deaths.
effect_estimate: 24.2% (malaria, first 2 weeks); 29.9% (gastroenteritis); 34.3% (pneumonia); 46.3% (nonmalaria fever with skin condition, up to 28 days)
follow_up: up to 28 days post-administration per cycle over 3 years (2014-2016)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported in this secondary analysis; focused on efficacy outcomes rather than adverse events

title: Efficacy and safety of malarial prophylaxis with mefloquine during pregnancy in Kisangani, Democratic Republic of Congo: A randomized clinical trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing mefloquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnant women in a malaria-endemic area; primary focus is malaria prevention in humans.
population: pregnant individuals receiving intermittent preventive treatment for malaria
primary_outcome: Occurrence of major and minor side-effects and efficacy outcomes including placental malaria, maternal peripheral parasitaemia and low birth weight
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with mefloquine (split dose with meal) significantly reduced placental malaria, maternal peripheral parasitaemia, and low birth weight compared to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine, with similar tolerability.
p_value: major side effects: Fisher exact = 0.5014; minor side effects: P = .0961
transmission_setting: area with intense malaria transmission and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance
safety_summary: No statistically significant difference in occurrence of major or minor side-effects between mefloquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine groups; splitting the mefloquine dose and taking it with a meal increased tolerability.

title: RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine induces IgA responses against CSP and vaccine-unrelated antigens in African children in the phase 3 trial.
screening_reason: Published Phase 3 RCT reporting outcome results (immune response data) from a malaria vaccine trial in African children; RTS,S is a primary malaria prevention intervention.
population: children aged 5-17 months at first vaccination from RTS,S/AS01E phase 3 trial sites with differing malaria transmission intensity
primary_outcome: IgA antibody responses to CSP and vaccine-unrelated P. falciparum antigens 1 month post primary immunization, and their association with protection
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01E vaccination induced increased serum IgA responses against CSP and multiple vaccine-unrelated P. falciparum antigens compared to a comparator vaccine, but no significant association between IgA levels and protection was found.
effect_estimate: 1.2 to 2-fold increase in IgA to CSP constructs
transmission_setting: two sites with different malaria transmission intensities

title: Cost-Effectiveness of PBO versus Conventional Long-Lasting Insecticidal Bed Nets in Preventing Symptomatic Malaria in Nigeria: Results of a Pragmatic Randomized Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Pragmatic RCT with reported outcome results (33.4% reduction in symptomatic malaria) comparing PBO-treated nets versus conventional LLINs for malaria prevention in an area with pyrethroid resistance; vector-control trials are not subject to phase restrictions.
population: village populations in areas with confirmed pyrethroid resistance
primary_outcome: symptomatic malaria cases (epidemiologic outcomes analyzed by village by month)
impact_summary: PBO nets reduced symptomatic malaria cases by 33.4% compared with conventional LLINs and were highly cost-effective and cost-saving from a health systems perspective.
effect_metric: percent reduction in symptomatic malaria cases
transmission_setting: area with confirmed pyrethroid insecticide resistance

title: Cost-effectiveness of intermittent preventive treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus single screening and treatment for the control of malaria in pregnancy in Papua, Indonesia: a provider perspective analysis from a cluster-randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus screening-and-treatment for malaria in pregnancy; cluster-randomized design with cost-effectiveness analysis based on trial data.
comparator: single screening and treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: incremental cost per DALY averted
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was cost-effective compared with single screening and treatment, averting more DALYs at an incremental cost of $53 per DALY averted in a moderate transmission setting.
effect_metric: incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (cost per DALY averted)
effect_estimate: $53 per DALY averted (incremental cost US$5657, 107.4 DALYs averted per 1000 women)
funder: Medical Research Council, Department for International Development, and Wellcome Trust

title: Immunogenicity and Protective Efficacy of Radiation-Attenuated and Chemo-Attenuated PfSPZ Vaccines in Equatoguinean Adults.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of malaria vaccines (PfSPZ) with reported outcome results including safety, immunogenicity, and vaccine efficacy against controlled human malaria infection in adults.
population: Equatoguinean adults
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy against homologous controlled human malaria infection (CHMI)
impact_summary: PfSPZ-CVac showed higher vaccine efficacy (55%) than PfSPZ Vaccine (27%) against homologous controlled human malaria infection despite a 27-fold lower dose.
safety_summary: No differences in solicited adverse events between vaccinees and controls in the 6 days after administration; from days 7-13, PfSPZ-CVac recipients had significantly more adverse events, likely due to Pf parasitemia.

title: Subsidise the test, the treatment or both? Results of an individually randomised controlled trial of the management of suspected malaria fevers in the retail sector in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria diagnostic test and treatment subsidies in humans, with primary purpose of improving malaria testing and appropriate ACT use in retail settings.
population: clients seeking care for suspected malaria fevers in retail outlets
primary_outcome: RDT uptake (proportion of clients purchasing a malaria rapid diagnostic test)
impact_summary: RDT uptake was high across all arms, and RDT subsidies modestly increased testing uptake, while ACT subsidy conditional on a positive RDT did not affect test purchasing behaviour.
effect_estimate: 1.025 (RDT subsidy effect on uptake); 0.994 (conditional ACT subsidy effect on RDT uptake)

title: Evaluating the impact of larviciding with Bti and community education and mobilization as supplementary integrated vector management interventions for malaria control in Kenya and Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria vector control interventions (Bti larviciding, LLINs, community education) with reported outcome results on malaria prevalence across three African sites.
population: primary school children
primary_outcome: malaria parasite prevalence among school children and adult anopheline mosquito density
impact_summary: Combining LLINs with larviciding using Bti and community education and mobilization significantly reduced malaria prevalence by 50% in the low-prevalence Tolay site in Ethiopia, but not in the higher-prevalence Kenyan sites, and there was no significant reduction in adult anopheline density at any site.
transmission_setting: varied endemicity: low prevalence in Tolay (Ethiopia), moderate in Malindi (Kenya), high in Nyabondo (Kenya)

title: Biological larviciding against malaria vector mosquitoes with Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis (Bti) - Long term observations and assessment of repeatability during an additional intervention year of a large-scale field trial in rural Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Large-scale RCT of biological larviciding (Bti) for malaria vector control with reported outcome results on Anopheles abundance reduction over multiple intervention years.
design: large-scale field trial, cluster-based, non-randomized comparison of two intervention strategies
comparator: baseline year (pre-intervention) and comparison between full vs. guided larviciding treatment
population: rural villages and semi-urban town residents/environmental breeding sites (entomological study)
primary_outcome: Reduction in adult Anopheles spp. mosquito abundance compared to baseline year
impact_summary: Biological larviciding with Bti substantially and repeatably reduced malaria vector mosquito abundance over a second consecutive intervention year, by 77.4% with full treatment and 63.5% with guided treatment compared to baseline.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in adult Anopheles abundance
transmission_setting: rural and semi-urban Burkina Faso, seasonal malaria transmission

title: Impact of Three-Year Intermittent Preventive Treatment Using Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapies on Malaria Morbidity in Malian Schoolchildren.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of intermittent preventive treatment in schoolchildren (IPTsc) with artemisinin-based combination therapies for malaria prevention in humans, with reported outcome results over three years.
population: schoolchildren aged 6-13 years
primary_outcome: incidence of clinical malaria, all-cause clinic visits, asymptomatic parasitemia, and anemia
impact_summary: Three years of intermittent preventive treatment with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine+artesunate reduced all-cause clinic visits, asymptomatic parasitemia, and anemia in schoolchildren, but had no impact on clinical malaria incidence.
effect_metric: prevalence/proportion difference in all-cause clinic visits (SP+AS vs control)

title: Evaluating effectiveness of screening house eaves as a potential intervention for reducing indoor vector densities and malaria prevalence in Nyabondo, western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (house eave screening) with reported outcome results showing reduced indoor vector densities and malaria prevalence.
design: cluster-randomized, controlled trial with permuted block randomization
population: residents of study households in a high malaria transmission area
primary_outcome: Indoor Anopheles mosquito density and malaria parasite prevalence
impact_summary: House eave screening significantly reduced indoor vector densities and malaria parasite prevalence compared to unscreened control houses.

title: Comparative functional survival and equivalent annual cost of 3 long-lasting insecticidal net (LLIN) products in Tanzania: A randomised trial with 3-year follow up.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing LLIN products for malaria prevention; vector control is a primary malaria intervention.
comparator: active comparator (three different LLIN products compared against each other: Olyset, PermaNet 2.0, NetProtect)
population: households and volunteers sleeping under LLINs
primary_outcome: LLIN functional survival (LLIN present and in serviceable condition)
impact_summary: Median LLIN functional survival was significantly lower for Olyset (2.0 years) than for PermaNet 2.0 (2.5 years) and NetProtect (2.6 years), and all nets had a functional lifespan of less than 3 years, affecting cost-effectiveness.
effect_metric: hazard ratio for net failure (functional survival)
effect_estimate: HR 0.73 (PermaNet vs Olyset); HR 0.70 (NetProtect vs Olyset)
p_value: p = 0.001 (overall); p = 0.001 (PermaNet vs Olyset); p < 0.001 (NetProtect vs Olyset)

title: Evaluation of the effectiveness of topical repellent distributed by village health volunteer networks against Plasmodium spp. infection in Myanmar: A stepped-wedge cluster randomised trial.
screening_reason: Stepped-wedge cluster RCT with reported outcome results evaluating topical repellent for malaria prevention in humans; vector-control intervention classified as not applicable phase.
population: village residents and forest dwellers, median age 18 years
primary_outcome: Plasmodium spp. infection detected by rapid diagnostic test (RDT)
impact_summary: Topical repellent distributed by village health volunteers showed no significant protection against RDT-detectable infection but was associated with protection against PCR-detectable P. falciparum infection, not P. vivax.
effect_metric: adjusted relative risk ratio (ARRR) for PCR-detectable P. falciparum infection
transmission_setting: Greater Mekong Subregion, forest and village malaria transmission
safety_summary: No adverse events were reported during the study.

title: A cluster randomized trial of delivery of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy at the community level in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of IPTp delivery intervention in pregnant women with reported outcome results on coverage and doses administered.
comparator: standard practice (IPTp delivered at health facilities)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Coverage of IPTp and antenatal care (ANC)
impact_summary: Community delivery of IPTp by community health workers increased the number of IPTp doses received and IPTp3/IPTp4 coverage compared to standard health facility delivery, without decreasing ANC coverage, though most differences were not statistically significant.

title: Efficacy and Safety of a Naphthoquine-Azithromycin Coformulation for Malaria Prophylaxis in Southeast Asia: A Phase 3, Double-blind, Randomized, Placebo-controlled Trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT with reported outcome results evaluating a fixed-dose antimalarial combination for malaria prophylaxis in humans.
population: residents 5-65 years of age in malaria-endemic villages
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy against Plasmodium infections (blood smear-positive malaria) with monthly NQAZ prophylaxis
impact_summary: Monthly single-dose naphthoquine-azithromycin coformulation was well tolerated and provided over 93% protective efficacy against Plasmodium infections compared with placebo.
follow_up: weekly follow-up during trial period (duration not specified beyond monthly dosing)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic villages along the China-Myanmar border
safety_summary: NQAZ was well tolerated; 5.6% of treatment group experienced transient elevation of liver aminotransferases versus 2.2% in placebo group (P > .05), no other serious adverse events reported.

title: Impacts of Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention on Malaria Burden among under Five-Year-Old Children in Borno State, Nigeria.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results demonstrating SMC efficacy for malaria prevention in children, a primary malaria intervention.
population: children aged 3-59 months
primary_outcome: Malaria prevalence among SMC vs non-SMC subjects/clusters measured two weeks after the 4th cycle of SMC
impact_summary: SMC significantly reduced malaria prevalence and anaemia prevalence among children under five in Borno State, Nigeria.
follow_up: 2 weeks after 4th SMC cycle (approximately 4 months total)
safety_summary: 4.9% of SMC subjects reported adverse drug reactions; SMC was deemed safe

title: Adherence to Mass Drug Administration with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine and Plasmodium falciparum Clearance in Southern Province, Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of mass drug administration with DHAp for malaria elimination that has reported outcome results on adherence and parasite clearance.
population: General population in households targeted for mass drug administration
primary_outcome: Adherence to full course of DHAp and clearance of P. falciparum asexual-stage parasitemia
impact_summary: High adherence to the 3-day DHAp regimen (84.4% completion) was observed, and DHAp effectively cleared P. falciparum asexual-stage infections, with none of 45 followed participants positive at days 3/7 post-treatment.
effect_metric: Proportion fully adhering to treatment / parasite clearance rate
transmission_setting: Malaria elimination setting, Southern Province, Zambia

title: Moving from Malaria Burden Reduction toward Elimination: An Evaluation of Mass Drug Administration in Southern Province, Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster RCT with reported results evaluating malaria chemoprevention (DHAP-based MDA) in humans; phase not applicable for cluster trials.
population: households/residents in health facility catchment areas along Lake Kariba
impact_summary: This introductory article describes a cluster RCT evaluating mass drug administration and focal mass drug administration with DHAP for malaria elimination in Southern Province, Zambia, and introduces a collection of related articles on the intervention's impact.
transmission_setting: low to moderate transmission area targeted for malaria elimination along Lake Kariba
funder: PATH Malaria Control and Elimination Partnership in Africa

title: Prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum and Non-falciparum Infections by Photo-Induced Electron Transfer-PCR in a Longitudinal Cohort of Individuals Enrolled in a Mass Drug Administration Trial in Southern Province, Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria elimination intervention (MDA/fMDA) with reported outcome results on Plasmodium prevalence and species distribution.
comparator: focal MDA vs campaign-based MDA (and PCR vs RDT diagnostic comparison)
population: individuals enrolled in a mass drug administration trial cohort
primary_outcome: Prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum and non-falciparum infections detected by PCR compared to RDT
impact_summary: PCR testing showed Plasmodium falciparum as the dominant species (98.3% of positives), RDTs had high specificity but low sensitivity compared to PCR, and MDA/fMDA appeared to reduce P. malariae prevalence while P. ovale prevalence remained unchanged.

title: Treatment Coverage Estimation for Mass Drug Administration for Malaria with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine in Southern Province, Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of malaria MDA intervention with reported outcome results on coverage and epidemiologic impact.
population: general population in Southern Province, Zambia
primary_outcome: Epidemiologic coverage and program reach of mass drug administration
impact_summary: Household visit coverage ranged from 62.9% to 77.4% across four MDA rounds, with treatment coverage of 58.8% in MDA arm and 13.3% in fMDA arm based on capture-recapture estimates.

title: Cost-Effectiveness of Focal Mass Drug Administration and Mass Drug Administration with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine for Malaria Prevention in Southern Province, Zambia: Results of a Community-Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of mass drug administration for malaria prevention with reported outcome results (cost-effectiveness and infection/case/death averted); not early-phase.
population: community residents in malaria-endemic areas of Southern Province, Zambia
primary_outcome: Cost-effectiveness measures including cost per infection averted, cost per case averted, cost per death averted, and cost per disability-adjusted life year averted
impact_summary: Mass drug administration (MDA) with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was more cost-effective than focal MDA and standard of care in reducing malaria in Southern Province, Zambia, and met WHO cost-effectiveness thresholds in 90% of simulations compared to about 50% for fMDA.
effect_metric: cost per person targeted and reached (USD)
transmission_setting: relatively higher transmission settings in Southern Province, Zambia

title: Impact of Four Rounds of Mass Drug Administration with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine Implemented in Southern Province, Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing mass drug administration with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for malaria elimination in humans.
comparator: standard of care without mass treatment
population: community members including children, in areas of varying malaria transmission
primary_outcome: malaria parasite prevalence
impact_summary: Four rounds of mass drug administration with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine significantly reduced malaria parasite prevalence, especially in lower transmission areas.
transmission_setting: varying transmission intensity, with focus on lower transmission areas (<10% baseline prevalence), high vector control coverage

title: A Longitudinal Cohort to Monitor Malaria Infection Incidence during Mass Drug Administration in Southern Province, Zambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of mass drug administration for malaria elimination with reported outcome results on infection incidence.
population: community residents in households in Southern Province, Zambia
primary_outcome: Time to first malaria infection and cumulative infection incidence based on monthly PCR testing
impact_summary: MDA was associated with reduced risk of first infection and reduced cumulative infection incidence during the first rainy season, but no significant effect was found for fMDA or for either arm over the full 18-month study period.
effect_metric: hazards ratio (first infection); incidence rate ratio (cumulative infection, first rainy season)
transmission_setting: malaria elimination setting with seasonal transmission, high coverage of case management and vector control

title: Assessment of the Acceptability of Testing and Treatment during a Mass Drug Administration Trial for Malaria in Zambia Using Mixed Methods.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-randomized controlled trial of malaria intervention (MDA/fMDA) with reported outcome results on acceptability and treatment uptake.
population: households and community members (adults and children) in health catchments
primary_outcome: Acceptability of testing and treatment (MDA/fMDA) assessed via household surveys, focus group discussions, and in-depth interviews
impact_summary: The mass drug administration campaign was highly accepted, with acceptability of prophylactic treatment for malaria-negative individuals increasing markedly from baseline to follow-up.
transmission_setting: Southern Province, Zambia; malaria-endemic region with mass drug administration trial

title: Efficacy and safety of fixed dose combination of arterolane maleate and piperaquine phosphate in comparison with chloroquine phosphate in children with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax malaria: A phase III, randomised, multicentric study.
screening_reason: Phase III RCT of antimalarial treatment for P. vivax malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcomes at 42-day follow-up.
population: children aged 6 months to 12 years with acute uncomplicated P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Proportion of aparasitaemic and afebrile patients at 72 hours
impact_summary: Fixed dose combination of arterolane maleate and piperaquine phosphate showed efficacy and safety comparable to chloroquine in treating uncomplicated P. vivax malaria in children.
effect_metric: difference in proportion aparasitaemic and afebrile at 72 hours (ITT)
safety_summary: Efficacy and safety comparable between arms; most common adverse event was vomiting; no patient discontinued due to QTc abnormality.

title: Efficacy and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine and prevalence of molecular markers associated with resistance, Guinea: an open-label two-arm randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: This is a completed RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments (ASAQ and AL) for malaria treatment in humans, with efficacy and safety outcomes measured at Day 28.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Kaplan-Meier estimate of Day 28 efficacy after correction by microsatellite-genotyping
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed high efficacy and safety with minimal molecular markers of resistance in Guinea.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sentinel sites (Maferinyah and Labé Health Districts)
safety_summary: Both ASAQ and AL were found to have high safety profiles; no early treatment failures were observed, and only late treatment failures (mostly reinfections) occurred.

title: The impact of gravidity, symptomatology and timing of infection on placental malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing intermittent preventive therapy (IPTp) for malaria in pregnant women, a primary malaria intervention; secondary analysis of placental malaria outcomes.
population: pregnant women receiving intermittent preventive therapy during pregnancy
primary_outcome: Placental malaria diagnosed by histopathology, placental blood smear, and/or placental blood loop-mediated isothermal amplification
impact_summary: Primigravidity, higher number of malaria episodes, and timing of infection (varying by gravidity) were significantly associated with increased odds of placental malaria.
effect_estimate: aOR 8.90 (primigravidity); aOR 2.35 (per malaria episode); aOR 1.14 (per week gestation at first infection in multigravidas); aOR 12.19 (primigravidity in asymptomatic women)
follow_up: enrollment at 12-20 weeks gestation through delivery

title: Epitope-based sieve analysis of Plasmodium falciparum sequences from a FMP2.1/AS02A vaccine trial is consistent with differential vaccine efficacy against immunologically relevant AMA1 variants.
screening_reason: Published RCT of a malaria vaccine (FMP2.1/AS02A) with reported outcome results (efficacy analysis and sieve analysis of breakthrough infections).
population: volunteers from a malaria vaccine efficacy field trial who later developed malaria
primary_outcome: Difference in 3D7-like T and B-cell epitope proportions and amino acid distance to 3D7 AMA1 variant between vaccinees and controls
impact_summary: Sieve analysis found a significantly greater proportion of 3D7-like T-cell epitopes mapping to the AMA1 c1L region in controls versus vaccinees, and higher IC50/lower binding affinity in vaccinee-derived epitopes, consistent with allele-specific vaccine efficacy of the FMP2.1/AS02A vaccine.
effect_metric: proportion of 3D7-like T-cell epitopes in c1L region
effect_estimate: greater in control vs vaccinee group

title: Antibody responses to the RTS,S/AS01E vaccine and Plasmodium falciparum antigens after a booster dose within the phase 3 trial in Mozambique.
screening_reason: Published results from a Phase 3 RCT of RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine with reported immunogenicity outcomes in a pediatric population.
design: phase 3, immunogenicity substudy of pediatric trial with fourth booster dose
population: children and infants (pediatric subjects in phase 3 trial, subset analyzed)
primary_outcome: Levels of total IgM, IgG, and IgG1-4 subclasses against CSP constructs and HBsAg after the booster dose
impact_summary: The booster dose of RTS,S/AS01E increased IgG, IgG1, IgG3 and IgG4 (but not IgG2 or IgM) against vaccine antigens, with responses lower than the primary immunization peak, and increased some naturally acquired antibody responses such as anti-Rh5 antibodies.

title: Efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine as first line therapy of uncomplicated malaria in Burkina Faso, 11 years after policy change.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy outcomes comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in humans.
population: participants with uncomplicated malaria, age over 6 months
primary_outcome: Treatment efficacy over 28 days of follow-up, unadjusted by PCR
impact_summary: Artesunate-amodiaquine showed significantly higher adequate clinical and parasitological response than artemether-lumefantrine, whose efficacy fell below the WHO threshold of 90% when uncorrected by PCR.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
safety_summary: All treatments had a similar and good tolerability profile.

title: Efficacy and safety of artemisinin-based combination therapy and the implications of Pfkelch13 and Pfcoronin molecular markers in treatment failure in Senegal.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating efficacy and safety of antimalarial treatments (AL, ASAQ, DP) for malaria in humans; primary focus is malaria treatment.
comparator: active comparator (AL vs ASAQ vs DP)
population: patients with suspected uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28 (AL, ASAQ) or day 42 (DP)
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine, artesunate-amodiaquine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine remained highly efficacious and well tolerated for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Senegal, with no Pfk13 or Pfcoronin resistance mutations detected.
effect_estimate: 98.8-100% (AL/ASAQ in Diourbel and Kedougou), 97.6% (DP in Kedougou)
safety_summary: All three ACT regimens (AL, ASAQ, DP) were well-tolerated

title: Protease Inhibitors to Reduce Malaria Morbidity in HIV-Infected Pregnant Women
screening_reason: Randomized Phase 3 trial with reported results comparing protease inhibitor-based vs non-PI-based ART in pregnant women living with HIV, with placental malaria as a primary outcome.
interventions_raw: Lopinavir/ritonavir; Efavirenz; Zidovudine; Lamivudine
population: pregnant women living with HIV, 12-28 weeks gestation
primary_outcome: Prevalence of Malaria Defined as Positive Placental Blood Smear
impact_summary: Anemia during pregnancy was associated with greater risk of small for gestational age, and higher vitamin D concentrations predicted lower risk of infant wasting, among pregnant WLHIV on cART.
effect_estimate: 1.88 (anemia and SGA); 0.94 (vitamin D and infant wasting)

title: Efficacy of a Spatial Repellent for Control of Malaria in Indonesia: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a spatial repellent (transfluthrin) for malaria prevention in children; meets all inclusion criteria.
population: children aged ≥6 months to ≤5 years following radical cure
primary_outcome: Time to first malaria infection and overall (total new) infections detected by monthly blood screening
impact_summary: The spatial repellent (transfluthrin passive emanator) reduced malaria infection risk, with statistically significant protective effects observed in subgroup analyses (moderate-to-high risk and baseline-infected clusters), though the overall 24-cluster effect was not statistically significant.
effect_estimate: 27.7% (first infection) and 31.3% (overall infections) in 24 clusters; 33.3% and 40.9% in 19 clusters; 60% in 12 moderate-to-high risk clusters
transmission_setting: low to moderate malaria transmission, Sumba, Indonesia

title: Delayed iron does not alter cognition or behavior among children with severe malaria and iron deficiency.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria intervention (iron therapy timing in children with severe malaria) in humans.
comparator: immediate iron therapy vs. 28-day delayed iron therapy
population: children with cerebral malaria, severe malarial anemia, or community children, with iron deficiency
primary_outcome: Cognitive and neurobehavioral outcomes at 12 months after enrollment
impact_summary: Delaying iron therapy by 28 days after severe malaria did not worsen cognitive or behavioral outcomes compared to immediate iron therapy at 12-month follow-up.

title: Plasmodium falciparum Isolates Carrying pfk13 Polymorphisms Harbor the SVMNT Allele of pfcrt in Northwestern Indonesia.
screening_reason: Published RCT randomizing symptomatic P. falciparum-infected individuals to dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine or artemether-lumefantrine with reported treatment outcomes and parasite persistence results.
design: randomized, cross-sectional survey with embedded treatment comparison, phase 3
population: symptomatic and asymptomatic P. falciparum-infected residents of three regencies in Sumatera
primary_outcome: Treatment outcome (parasitological clearance/persistence) in relation to pretreatment pfcrt, pfmdr1, and pfk13 genotypes
impact_summary: Current ACT regimens (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine) remain effective in Sumatera, but submicroscopic persistent parasites at day 28/42 were significantly associated with the pfmdr1 NF haplotype, suggesting emerging concerns for drug susceptibility.
effect_metric: odds ratio (linkage disequilibrium between pfcrt SVMNT and pfmdr1 YY haplotypes)
transmission_setting: cross-sectional survey in three regencies of Sumatera, Indonesia

title: Effect of immune regulatory pathways after immunization with GMZ2 malaria vaccine candidate in healthy lifelong malaria-exposed adults.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of GMZ2 malaria vaccine candidate with reported immunogenicity and efficacy outcomes (CHMI challenge) in malaria-exposed adults.
population: healthy lifelong malaria-exposed adults
primary_outcome: Correlation between immune regulatory pathways (sHLA-G, Treg, Breg) and plasmablast frequencies/vaccine-specific IgG concentrations; vaccine efficacy assessed via controlled human malaria infection
impact_summary: Regulatory immune responses (sHLA-G and Treg) were induced by GMZ2 vaccination and were associated with suppressed vaccine-induced immune responses and increased risk of P. falciparum infection after controlled human malaria infection.

title: Impact of Intermittent Mass Testing and Treatment on Incidence of Malaria Infection in a High Transmission Area of Western Kenya.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (clinical malaria incidence and infection incidence) testing a malaria case detection and treatment intervention in humans.
comparator: standard care (no mass testing and treatment)
population: all residents of village clusters, including asymptomatic individuals
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria disease and cumulative incidence of malaria infection
impact_summary: Six rounds of mass testing and treatment over two years did not significantly reduce the incidence of clinical malaria or cumulative malaria infection compared to control clusters.

title: Effects of Biannual Azithromycin Mass Drug Administration on Malaria in Malawian Children: A Cluster-Randomized Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results investigating azithromycin mass drug administration as a malaria intervention in human populations.
population: children aged 1-59 months
primary_outcome: prevalence of malaria parasitemia
impact_summary: Biannual azithromycin mass drug administration did not reduce malaria parasitemia, gametocytemia, or anemia compared to placebo at either the community or individual level.

title: Effect of long-lasting insecticidal nets with and without piperonyl butoxide on malaria indicators in Uganda (LLINEUP): a pragmatic, cluster-randomised trial embedded in a national LLIN distribution campaign.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomised trial of malaria prevention intervention (LLINs with/without PBO) embedded in Uganda's national campaign with reported outcome results (parasite prevalence at 6, 12, 18 months); not early-phase.
design: pragmatic, cluster-randomised trial embedded in a national LLIN distribution campaign
population: children aged 2-10 years in households selected during a national LLIN distribution campaign
primary_outcome: Parasite prevalence by microscopy in children aged 2-10 years, assessed in the as-treated population at 6, 12, and 18 months
impact_summary: PBO LLINs reduced malaria parasite prevalence more effectively than conventional LLINs for up to 18 months in Uganda, where pyrethroid resistance is high.
funder: The Against Malaria Foundation, UK Department for International Development, Innovative Vector Control Consortium, and Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation

title: Multifunctional Antibodies Are Induced by the RTS,S Malaria Vaccine and Associated With Protection in a Phase 1/2a Trial.
screening_reason: RTS,S is a malaria vaccine RCT with reported outcome results (parasitemia following challenge), phase 1/2a is acceptable (not early-phase excluded), and malaria prevention is the primary purpose.
population: healthy malaria-naive adults
primary_outcome: Induction of functional anti-CSP antibody responses and their association with protection following controlled human malaria infection challenge
impact_summary: Participants with higher levels of Fc-mediated functional anti-CSP antibodies induced by RTS,S/AS01 had a reduced probability of developing parasitemia after homologous challenge, while nonprotected subjects had higher anti-CSP IgM levels.
effect_metric: association between functional antibody levels and protection from parasitemia
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (non-endemic, experimental challenge)
safety_summary: Not detailed in abstract; RTS,S/AS01 vaccination was administered to healthy adults without reported major safety concerns.

title: Interactions Between Antenatal Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine, Drug-Resistant Plasmodium falciparum Parasites, and Delivery Outcomes in Malawi.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results from a malaria prevention trial comparing IPTp-SP versus ISTp in pregnant women, with measured birth weight and gestational age outcomes.
comparator: intermittent screening by rapid diagnostic tests (ISTp)
population: pregnant women with placental Plasmodium falciparum infections
primary_outcome: birth weight and gestational age at delivery in relation to SP resistance genotype and IPTp-SP treatment
impact_summary: The effectiveness of IPTp-SP in improving birth weight is compromised in women with A581G-bearing dhps resistance mutant parasites, without evidence that antenatal SP worsens the adverse effects of these parasites.
effect_estimate: 252 g (A581G vs wild-type); interaction effect Pinteraction=.033

title: A Phase II Pilot Trial to Evaluate CoBaT-Y017 Safety and Efficacy against Uncomplicated Falciparum Malaria versus Artemether-Lumefantrine in Benin Subjects.
journal: Evidence-based complementary and alternative medicine : eCAM
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a herbal antimalarial treatment (CoBaT-Y017) versus artemether-lumefantrine with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in malaria-infected patients.
population: Adult males with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance efficacy and safety of CoBaT-Y017 compared to Artemether-Lumefantrine
impact_summary: CoBaT-Y017 showed similar antimalarial efficacy to Artemether-Lumefantrine for parasite clearance with no statistically significant difference, and had a better safety/tolerability profile.
safety_summary: 100% (12/12) of Artemether-Lumefantrine arm experienced at least one adverse event versus 61.5% (8/13) in the CoBaT-Y017 arm; no significant changes in vital signs, biochemical, or haematological parameters.

title: Immunogenicity and safety of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine co-administered with measles, rubella and yellow fever vaccines in Ghanaian children: A phase IIIb, multi-center, non-inferiority, randomized, open, controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published phase 3b RCT of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in Ghanaian children with reported immunogenicity and safety outcome results.
comparator: RTS,S/AS01 alone and YF/MR vaccines alone (active comparator groups)
population: infants/young children receiving EPI vaccinations at 6-10.5 months of age
primary_outcome: Non-inferiority of antibody responses to circumsporozoite, hepatitis B surface antigen, measles, rubella, and yellow fever antigens when RTS,S/AS01 co-administered with YF and MR vaccines versus each given alone, measured 1 month post-vaccination
impact_summary: Co-administration of RTS,S/AS01 with Vitamin A at 6 months and with yellow fever and measles-rubella vaccines at 9 months did not impair immune responses to any vaccine antigen and had an acceptable safety profile.
safety_summary: The safety profile of all vaccines was clinically acceptable in all groups, with no negative safety effect from co-administration.

title: Effect of adding azithromycin to the antimalarials used for seasonal malaria chemoprevention on the nutritional status of African children.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria chemoprevention intervention (seasonal malaria chemoprevention plus azithromycin) in African children.
population: young children receiving seasonal malaria chemoprevention
primary_outcome: Nutritional status indicators (stunting, underweight, wasting) derived from anthropometric measurements after each transmission season
impact_summary: Adding azithromycin to seasonal malaria chemoprevention did not improve nutritional outcomes compared to placebo in children in Burkina Faso and Mali.

title: Does improving appropriate use of malaria medicines change population beliefs in testing and treatment? Evidence from a randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported results testing a malaria diagnostic and treatment intervention (RDT access and ACT use) as primary focus in humans.
population: general population
primary_outcome: Population beliefs about accuracy of negative malaria test results and effectiveness of ACT treatment, measured 12 and 18 months after intervention start
impact_summary: The intervention improving RDT access via community health workers and appropriate ACT use increased population beliefs that a negative test result is correct and that ACTs are effective.
effect_estimate: 62.4% (belief in negative test correctness) and 96.8% (belief in ACT effectiveness)

title: Large-scale field trial of attractive toxic sugar baits (ATSB) for the control of malaria vector mosquitoes in Mali, West Africa.
screening_reason: Large-scale field trial of ATSB vector-control intervention in humans with reported malaria transmission outcomes; randomized allocation to treatment/control villages; not early-phase.
design: cluster field trial (non-randomized allocation of villages), phase not applicable
population: village populations/mosquito vector populations in villages using LLINs
primary_outcome: Entomological inoculation rate (EIR) and mosquito vector density/sporozoite infection reduction in treated versus control villages
impact_summary: ATSB deployment combined with LLINs drastically reduced mosquito density, proportion of older females, sporozoite infection rates, and EIR compared to control villages, indicating a significant reduction in malaria transmission.
transmission_setting: sustained malaria transmission despite LLIN use, seasonal (rainy and dry seasons) in Mali

title: Usefulness of day 7 lumefantrine plasma concentration as a predictor of malaria treatment outcome in under-fives children treated with artemether-lumefantrine in Tanzania.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (28-day cure rates) comparing generic vs innovator artemether-lumefantrine in malaria treatment; primary focus is malaria intervention in humans.
comparator: active comparator (innovator product Coartem vs generic Artefan)
population: children with uncomplicated malaria aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28 and day 7 plasma lumefantrine concentration as predictor of treatment outcome
impact_summary: Day 7 plasma lumefantrine concentration using the recommended cut-off of ≥200 ng/ml failed to predict malaria treatment outcome in under-five children treated with artemether-lumefantrine in Tanzania, while nutritional status was found to be a significant determinant of recurrent malaria.
effect_metric: adjusted hazard ratio (nutritional status and recurrent malaria)
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Population pharmacokinetics of artesunate and dihydroartemisinin in pregnant and non-pregnant women with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Burkina Faso: an open label trial.
screening_reason: Open-label RCT comparing artesunate-mefloquine treatment in pregnant versus non-pregnant women with uncomplicated malaria; reports pharmacokinetic outcome results.
design: open label, non-randomized comparative pharmacokinetic study
population: pregnant (second and third trimester) and non-pregnant women with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Population pharmacokinetics of artesunate and dihydroartemisinin (clearance, exposure) in pregnant vs non-pregnant women
impact_summary: Pregnant women had 21% higher elimination clearance of dihydroartemisinin than non-pregnant women, leading to substantially lower drug exposure and a potentially increased risk of treatment failure and drug resistance.
effect_metric: difference in elimination clearance of dihydroartemisinin
transmission_setting: low transmission settings mentioned as context; specific endemicity not detailed

title: Mass drug administrations with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and single low dose primaquine to eliminate Plasmodium falciparum have only a transient impact on Plasmodium vivax: Findings from randomised controlled trials.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating mass drug administration for malaria elimination in humans.
population: residents of villages with high prevalence of P. falciparum infections
primary_outcome: cumulative incidence and prevalence of P. vivax infections
impact_summary: Mass drug administration with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and single low-dose primaquine had only a transient reduction in P. vivax prevalence, with no significant reduction in cumulative incidence or recurrence.
transmission_setting: Greater Mekong Subregion, high P. falciparum prevalence villages

title: Effect of group versus individual antenatal care on uptake of intermittent prophylactic treatment of malaria in pregnancy and related malaria outcomes in Nigeria and Kenya: analysis of data from a pragmatic cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Pragmatic cluster-randomized trial with reported results on malaria prevention outcomes (IPTp-SP uptake and ITN use) in pregnant women in sub-Saharan Africa.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Uptake of IPTp-SP doses and ITN use
impact_summary: Group antenatal care was associated with higher mean number of IPTp-SP doses received compared to individual antenatal care in both Nigeria and Kenya, and higher infant ITN use in Nigeria.
p_value: <0.001 (IPTp doses, both countries); 0.020 (infant ITN use, Nigeria)
