title: Optimal timing of primaquine to reduce Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte carriage when co-administered with artemether-lumefantrine.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment/transmission-blocking intervention (primaquine + artemether-lumefantrine) in humans; not early-phase.
comparator: AL only (no primaquine) and AL with primaquine on last day (day 3) vs day 1
population: children and adolescents with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, G6PD normal
primary_outcome: Gametocyte prevalence and density on days 2, 3, 4, 8, 11 and 15 (day 4 gametocyte prevalence)
impact_summary: Adding a single low-dose primaquine on the first day of artemether-lumefantrine treatment reduced day 4 gametocyte prevalence compared to adding it on the last day or not at all, though the difference was not statistically significant, and was well tolerated.
p_value: not statistically significant (haemoglobin difference p=318 [sic]; adverse events p=0.477)
safety_summary: No serious adverse events reported; 23% (26/111) of participants had mild adverse events (31 total), no significant difference between arms; primaquine on day 1 was well tolerated and as safe as later administration.

title: Long-term immunogenicity and immune memory response to the hepatitis B antigen in the RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine in African children: a randomized trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported results evaluating RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine immunogenicity and immune memory in African children; primary focus is malaria prevention vaccine intervention.
population: infants 8-12 weeks old
primary_outcome: Long-term persistence of anti-CS and anti-HBs antibodies and immune memory response to HB antigen following HepB booster
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01E vaccination effectively primed for hepatitis B, producing a strong booster response to HepB vaccine and higher anti-CS antibody levels than controls, with an acceptable safety profile.
effect_metric: geometric mean concentration of anti-HBs antibodies post-booster
transmission_setting: African children in Expanded Program of Immunization setting
safety_summary: RTS,S/AS01E co-administered with PHiD-CV, HRV and other childhood vaccines had an acceptable safety profile.

title: Efficacy and safety of artesuante-amodiaquine and artemether lumefantrine, the first line malaria treatment in six sentinel's sites of Côte d'Ivoire, West Africa.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment interventions with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in humans; phase not early.
population: patients older than 6 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 42 PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine remained highly efficacious for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Côte d'Ivoire, though delayed parasite clearance was observed in a few patients.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sentinel sites in Côte d'Ivoire
safety_summary: Both ACTs were well tolerated.

title: Adherence to the referral advice after introduction of rectal artesunate for pre-referral treatment of severe malaria at the community level: a noninferiority trial in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
screening_reason: Randomized (noninferiority) controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (rectal artesunate pre-referral) in humans with reported outcome results.
design: noninferiority community trial, pre- and post-intervention design
population: children under 5 years, their mothers/caretakers, and community health workers
primary_outcome: Adherence by mothers/caretakers to referral advice after pre-referral treatment of severe malaria with rectal artesunate
impact_summary: Adherence to referral advice after the introduction of pre-referral rectal artesunate at the community level was non-inferior to pre-intervention adherence, and the intervention was found feasible and acceptable.
transmission_setting: community-level care sites in Kasaï-Oriental, Kasaï-Central, Lomami, and Lualaba provinces

title: A Randomized Controlled Trial of Three- versus Five-Day Artemether-Lumefantrine Regimens for Treatment of Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Pregnancy in Africa.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemether-lumefantrine regimens for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in pregnancy with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: pregnant women and nonpregnant women with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy (PCR-corrected cure rate), tolerability, and pharmacokinetics of 5-day versus 3-day artemether-lumefantrine regimens
impact_summary: Both the 3-day and extended 5-day artemether-lumefantrine regimens achieved 100% PCR-corrected cure rates and were well tolerated, with the extended regimen improving overall lumefantrine drug exposure in pregnant women.
transmission_setting: areas with lower rates of malaria transmission and/or emerging drug resistance
age_range: pregnant and nonpregnant women of reproductive age
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated and safe; babies followed up to 1 year had normal development.

title: Resolving the cause of recurrent Plasmodium vivax malaria probabilistically.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing primaquine treatment versus control for P. vivax malaria relapse prevention with reported outcome results (relapse rates).
comparator: no primaquine radical curative treatment vs supervised high-dose primaquine
population: patients with recurrent Plasmodium vivax malaria on the Thailand-Myanmar border
primary_outcome: probabilistic classification of recurrent P. vivax infections as relapse, recrudescence, or reinfection
impact_summary: Without primaquine radical cure, 3 in 4 patients relapse, whereas after supervised high-dose primaquine only 1 in 40 relapse, indicating a much lower true failure rate than previously estimated.
effect_estimate: 75% without primaquine vs 2.5% (1 in 40) with supervised high-dose primaquine
transmission_setting: frequent relapsing P. vivax endemic region, Thailand-Myanmar border

title: Ivermectin for causal malaria prophylaxis: a randomised controlled human infection trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing ivermectin as malaria prevention in humans; outcome parasitaemia measured and reported.
population: healthy volunteers
primary_outcome: time to parasitaemia detected by positive thick blood smear
impact_summary: Ivermectin at 0.4 mg/kg had no significant effect on time to parasitaemia, indicating no clinically relevant prophylactic activity against pre-erythrocytic stages of P. falciparum.
effect_estimate: no significant difference between ivermectin and placebo
safety_summary: Ivermectin was safe and well tolerated at the dose used

title: Gametocyte clearance in children, from western Kenya, with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria after artemether-lumefantrine or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine treatment.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments (AL vs DP) for malaria in children, with gametocyte clearance as the primary outcome measured over 6 weeks.
population: children aged 0.5 to 12 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte clearance/prevalence and duration of gametocyte carriage after treatment
impact_summary: No significant difference was found between artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine in clearing gametocytes, with gametocytes persisting up to 42 days in a minority of children in both arms.

title: Biannual versus annual mass azithromycin distribution and malaria seroepidemiology among preschool children in Niger: a sub-study of a cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results (malaria seroepidemiology measured via MSP-119 antibody levels) comparing biannual versus annual azithromycin distribution for malaria control in a human population.
comparator: annual mass azithromycin distribution to entire community
population: preschool children ages 1-5 years
primary_outcome: MSP-119 seroprevalence and antibody levels as surrogate markers of malaria incidence
impact_summary: Targeted biannual azithromycin distribution was associated with lower malaria seroprevalence (62.7%) compared to annual distribution (68.7%).

title: Piperaquine concentration and malaria treatment outcomes in Ugandan children treated for severe malaria with intravenous Artesunate or quinine plus Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of severe malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasitological clearance and treatment failure at 42 days); primary focus on malaria intervention in humans.
comparator: intravenous artesunate plus DP vs quinine plus DP (also artemether-lumefantrine arm)
population: children treated for severe malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day parasitological treatment outcomes (parasite clearance and safety)
impact_summary: Children with low day 7 capillary piperaquine concentration (<57 ng/mL) had a two-fold higher risk of treatment failure compared to those with higher concentrations.
safety_summary: Safety of intravenous artesunate or quinine plus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was assessed as part of the parent trial; no major safety concerns highlighted in this substudy.

title: Assessing the impact of the addition of pyriproxyfen on the durability of permethrin-treated bed nets in Burkina Faso: a compound-randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Compound-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing durability and bioefficacy of pyriproxyfen-permethrin nets versus standard LLINs for malaria prevention in humans.
population: households in rural villages receiving bed nets
primary_outcome: Bioefficacy (WHO cone and tunnel test mortality/knockdown) and net survivorship (proportionate hole index) over 3 years
impact_summary: The PPF-permethrin net (Olyset Duo) maintained WHO bioefficacy criteria for 18 months versus 6 months for the standard LLIN, but both net types had poor survivorship and failed to meet WHO bioefficacy criteria by 3 years.
species: Anopheles gambiae s.l. (vector); malaria species not specified

title: Health education through mass media announcements by loudspeakers about malaria care: prevention and practice among people living in a malaria endemic area of northern Myanmar.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing loudspeaker health education intervention to control in malaria-endemic villages, measuring malaria knowledge, attitudes, practices, and morbidity.
population: people living in malaria endemic villages
primary_outcome: Change in knowledge, attitude and practice (KAP) scores related to malaria prevention and care-seeking practices
impact_summary: Loudspeaker health education announcements significantly improved malaria prevention and care-seeking practice scores and were associated with a declining trend in malaria morbidity compared to control villages.
effect_estimate: greater improvement in intervention group vs control
transmission_setting: malaria endemic, peak transmission season around June
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Counter-Selection of Antimalarial Resistance Polymorphisms by Intermittent Preventive Treatment in Pregnancy.
screening_reason: Randomized clinical trials of antimalarial chemoprevention (IPTp-mefloquine vs IPTp-SP vs IPTp-placebo) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on resistance markers and pregnancy outcomes.
comparator: IPTp-sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP) in HIV-uninfected women; placebo in HIV-infected women
population: pregnant women, HIV-uninfected and HIV-infected
primary_outcome: Prevalence of Plasmodium falciparum antimalarial resistance markers (pfcrt, pfmdr1, pfdhfr, pfdhps) and pfmdr1 copy number variation
impact_summary: IPTp-mefloquine selected for lower prevalence of the pfmdr1 86Y polymorphism compared with IPTp-SP in HIV-uninfected women, while other resistance markers were similar between groups and no effect was seen in HIV-infected women, with no association between resistance markers and pregnancy outcomes.
effect_estimate: lower in IPTp-MQ group than IPTp-SP group
transmission_setting: multi-country malaria-endemic settings (Benin, Gabon, Kenya, Mozambique)

title: Effect of Metofluthrin-Impregnated Spatial Repellent Devices Combined with New Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets (Olyset® Plus) on Pyrethroid-Resistant Malaria Vectors and Malaria Prevalence: Field Trial in South-Eastern Malawi.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector-control intervention (spatial repellents combined with bed nets) in humans; phase designation 'not applicable' is appropriate for cluster/community trials.
comparator: LLINs alone (Olyset Plus without spatial repellent)
population: residents of malaria endemic villages, including children
primary_outcome: malaria prevalence and pyrethroid-resistant vector mosquito density
impact_summary: Combined use of metofluthrin-impregnated spatial repellent devices with Olyset Plus LLINs reduced malaria infection rate in children and decreased the number of pyrethroid-resistant vector mosquitoes.

title: Atovaquone-Proguanil in Combination With Artesunate to Treat Multidrug-Resistant P. falciparum Malaria in Cambodia: An Open-Label Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of antimalarial drug combinations for P. falciparum malaria treatment in humans with reported efficacy outcome results at 42 days.
population: Patients with P. falciparum or mixed-species malaria infection
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at 42 days
impact_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil with or without artesunate remained marginally effective (~90% efficacy) in Cambodia, with artesunate co-administration providing little additional blood-stage efficacy but reducing post-treatment gametocyte carriage.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response at 42 days
transmission_setting: multidrug-resistant, artemisinin-resistant P. falciparum endemic region
safety_summary: Atovaquone-proguanil described as safe; single low-dose primaquine given to prevent gametocyte-mediated transmission; no major safety issues reported in abstract.

title: Impact of the addition of azithromycin to antimalarials used for seasonal malaria chemoprevention on antimicrobial resistance of Streptococcus pneumoniae.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SMC) with azithromycin addition in children that has reported outcome results on antimicrobial resistance.
population: children under seasonal malaria chemoprevention
primary_outcome: Sensitivity of nasopharyngeal Streptococcus pneumoniae isolates to azithromycin and other antibiotics
impact_summary: Addition of azithromycin to seasonal malaria chemoprevention antimalarials was associated with a marked increase in pneumococcal resistance to azithromycin and erythromycin that persisted one year after the last dose.

title: Methylene Blue Against Falciparum Malaria in Burkina Faso
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment (methylene blue vs primaquine as adjuncts to ACT) in children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
interventions_raw: Methylene Blue; Primaquine
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, 6-59 months
primary_outcome: Change in Haemoglobin Compared to the Baseline
impact_summary: Methylene blue combined with AS-AQ could not be shown to be non-inferior to primaquine combined with AS-AQ for haemoglobin recovery at day 7, but MB cleared asexual parasites and gametocytes faster than PQ.
effect_metric: mean haemoglobin difference between treatment groups at day 7
safety_summary: Adverse events were similar between groups except vomiting, which was more frequent in the MB arm (20/50) than the PQ arm (7/50), p = 0.003.

title: Pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics of chloroquine and artemisinin-based combination therapy with primaquine.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing ACT regimens plus primaquine for vivax malaria treatment; phase not stated but efficacy/safety outcomes presented.
comparator: artesunate-mefloquine, chloroquine, or artemether-lumefantrine (each with primaquine)
population: adult patients with acute vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Association between drug exposure (AUC, half-life) and CYP2D6 genotype with relapse, tolerance and efficacy of ACT/chloroquine plus primaquine
impact_summary: All ACT and chloroquine regimens combined with short-course primaquine were well tolerated and effective, with most recurrences due to relapse of homologous hypnozoites and no clear association between drug exposure of the long-acting schizonticidal component and risk of relapse, though impaired CYP2D6 activity was more common among patients with relapse.
effect_metric: Relative risk of related relapse (impaired vs normal CYP2D6 activity)
transmission_setting: vivax malaria endemic area of Brazil
safety_summary: All regimens were well tolerated; longer chloroquine half-lives associated with more pruritus (RR=1.09, 95% CI 1.03-1.14, p=0.001); higher chloroquine AUCs associated with reduced falls in haemoglobin by day 14 (Coef -0.02, 95% CI -0.005 to -0.03, p=0.01).

title: Safety and tolerability of artesunate-amodiaquine, artemether-lumefantrine and quinine plus clindamycin in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Kinshasa, the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (safety data) for malaria treatment in humans; not early-phase.
place: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo
design: randomized clinical trial, open-label (multi-arm, sequential treatment cohorts)
comparator: active comparator (artesunate-amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine vs quinine+clindamycin)
population: children aged 12 to 59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Safety and tolerability (incidence of drug-related adverse events) during repeated antimalarial treatment courses
impact_summary: Drug-related adverse events were common across treatment arms (54.7% ASAQ, 21.5% AL, 40.0% QnC, p<0.001) but did not increase over repeated ASAQ treatment courses, and no serious adverse events were judged related to study medication.
effect_metric: proportion with at least one drug-related adverse event
safety_summary: 50.0% of preRCT patients experienced at least one drug-related adverse event (mainly anorexia, asthenia, abnormal behavior; 3.5% severe); in RCT, drug-related AEs occurred in 54.7% (ASAQ), 21.5% (AL), and 40.0% (QnC) of patients (p<0.001); AE proportions did not increase with repeated ASAQ courses; three serious adverse events occurred but were not judged related to study medication.

title: Reduction of malaria vector mosquitoes in a large-scale intervention trial in rural Burkina Faso using Bti based larval source management.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vector control (larviciding) with reported entomological outcome results in humans' environment.
design: large-scale intervention trial, regression model, cluster-based comparison of two larviciding strategies
comparator: pre-intervention period (before-after comparison); selective vs comprehensive larviciding
population: rural villages with malaria vector mosquito populations (female Anopheles spp.)
primary_outcome: Reduction in number of female Anopheles mosquitoes caught indoors and outdoors using light traps
impact_summary: Larval source management with Bti substantially reduced female Anopheles mosquito abundance, with greater reductions achieved when all breeding sites were treated compared to selective treatment of the most productive sites.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in female Anopheles spp. abundance

title: Effectiveness of intermittent screening and treatment for the control of malaria in pregnancy: a cluster randomised trial in India.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention in pregnancy (ISTp versus PCD) in humans with primary endpoint of placental malaria.
population: pregnant women of all parities with gestational age 18-28 weeks
primary_outcome: Placental malaria, determined by placental histology
impact_summary: ISTp detected more infections than PCD but did not reduce the prevalence of placental malaria or improve pregnancy outcomes compared to passive case detection.
effect_metric: Odds ratio for placental malaria (ISTp vs PCD)

title: A Randomized Open-Label Evaluation of the Antimalarial Prophylactic Efficacy of Azithromycin-Piperaquine versus Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine in Pregnant Papua New Guinean Women.
screening_reason: Published randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial chemoprevention regimens (azithromycin-piperaquine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on parasitemia and birth outcomes.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Blood smear positivity (parasitemia) rates up to day 42 and at delivery, and tolerability up to day 7
impact_summary: AZ-PQ showed no significant difference from SP in preventing malaria parasitemia up to day 42 or at delivery, was well tolerated (though with more gastrointestinal side effects and dizziness), and was associated with higher live birth weight.
effect_metric: relative risk (blood smear positivity at delivery)
age_range: pregnant women, median gestation 26 weeks (range 14 to 32 weeks)
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; AZ-PQ was associated with more gastrointestinal side effects (31%) and dizziness (21%); 3 stillbirths occurred (1 in SP group, 2 twins in AZ-PQ group); 97% of monitored pregnancies resulted in healthy live births.

title: Declining responsiveness of childhood Plasmodium falciparum infections to artemisinin-based combination treatments ten years following deployment as first-line antimalarials in Nigeria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether-lumefantrine versus artesunate-amodiaquine in children with uncomplicated malaria, with reported treatment outcome results including parasite clearance and recurrent infection rates.
design: randomized controlled trial, multi-site, post-hoc comparative analysis, phase 3
population: children under 5 years and children under 16 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Early treatment response markers including asexual parasite positivity 1 and 2 days after treatment initiation, parasite clearance time, and parasite reduction ratio
impact_summary: Ten years after adoption of ACTs as first-line therapy in Nigeria, parasitological responses to artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine have significantly declined, with increased parasite positivity, clearance time, and recurrent infections over time.
effect_metric: Asexual parasite positivity 2 days after treatment initiation (APPD2)
transmission_setting: Multiple endemic sites across six geographical areas of Nigeria

title: Efficacy and safety of intermittent preventive treatment and intermittent screening and treatment versus single screening and treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the control of malaria in pregnancy in Indonesia: a cluster-randomised, open-label, superiority trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial testing IPT/IST chemoprevention strategies for malaria in pregnancy with reported outcome results at delivery; chemoprevention is a valid malaria intervention in the inclusion criteria.
population: pregnant women, 16-30 weeks pregnant
primary_outcome: Malaria infection in the mother at delivery
impact_summary: Both IPT and IST with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were associated with lower malaria prevalence at delivery compared with single screening and treatment, but IST results were confounded by lower baseline prevalence.
effect_estimate: IPT vs SST: RR 0.59; IST vs SST: RR 0.56
safety_summary: No differences between groups in serious adverse events in mothers or infants; most common serious adverse events were pregnancy/puerperium/perinatal-related conditions in mothers and infections/infestations in infants.
funder: Joint Global Health Trials Scheme of the Medical Research Council, Department for International Development, and the Wellcome Trust

title: An Extension to Study MALARIA-055 PRI (NCT00866619) to Evaluate the Long-term Efficacy, Safety and Immunogenicity of GSK Biologicals' Candidate Malaria Vaccine in Infants and Children in Africa
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine efficacy in children; Phase 3; primary malaria intervention.
interventions_raw: Blood sampling; Malaria Vaccine 257049 (MALARIA-055 PRI); Meningococcal C Conjugate Vaccine (MALARIA-055 PRI); Cell-culture rabies vaccine (MALARIA-055 PRI); TritanrixHepB/Hib (MALARIA-055 PRI); Polio Sabin Oral Polio Vaccine (GSK) (MALARIA-055 PRI)
comparator: comparator vaccines (meningococcal C conjugate, rabies, TritanrixHepB/Hib, oral polio) in the control group
population: Infants aged 6-12 weeks and children aged 5-17 months at initial vaccination, followed as older children (5-7 years) and younger children (3-5 years) in this extension
primary_outcome: Incidence of Severe Malaria Meeting Case Definition 1
impact_summary: Over the 3-year extension follow-up, severe malaria incidence remained low across all groups with no evidence of rebound in RTS,S/AS01 recipients, though clinical malaria incidence was higher in older RTS,S/AS01 recipients compared with controls in Nanoro.
effect_estimate: 53.7% (four-dose, older children); 23.3% (three-dose, older children); 32.1% (four-dose, younger children); 37.6% (three-dose, younger children)
follow_up: 3 additional years (up to 6-7 years postprimary vaccination)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sites in sub-Saharan Africa with ongoing transmission
safety_summary: No vaccine-related severe adverse events reported; three cerebral malaria episodes and five meningitis cases occurred; no safety signal identified

title: The Advanced Development Pathway of the RTS,S/AS01 Vaccine.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine with reported efficacy outcomes (28–36%) in African children and infants.
population: young children and infants
primary_outcome: vaccine efficacy against uncomplicated malaria
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01 showed 28% efficacy without booster and 36% with booster against uncomplicated malaria in children over a median follow-up of 48 and 38 months.

title: Clinical evaluation of the use of an mhealth intervention on quality of care provided by Community Health Workers in southwest Niger.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating an mHealth intervention to improve quality of care for malaria (and other conditions) diagnosis and treatment by community health workers in Niger.
population: Community Health Workers (Relais Communautaire) assessing children under five presenting with diarrhea, malaria and pneumonia
primary_outcome: Quality of care (QoC) score composed of diagnostic and treatment variables, as assessed by trained expert clinicians observing CHW consultations
impact_summary: mHealth-equipped Community Health Workers showed modestly improved quality of care, particularly better assessment of danger signs and referral decisions, but no significant improvement in actual treatment of malaria, pneumonia and diarrhea compared to paper-based controls.
effect_estimate: 3.4% higher QoC score (mean difference of 0.83 points)
p_value: P < 0.001 for several danger sign assessments; P = 0.012 for referral accuracy
transmission_setting: rural, poor and remote communities in southwest Niger
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events mentioned; focus was on quality of care rather than clinical safety outcomes
funder: World Vision Niger and Canada; WHO iCCM Rapid Access Expansion Program (RAcE)

title: Safety and tolerability of single low-dose primaquine in a low-intensity transmission area in South Africa: an open-label, randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (safety, tolerability, efficacy) of a malaria treatment intervention (single low-dose primaquine added to artemether-lumefantrine) in humans in a low-transmission area.
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Safety and tolerability of single low-dose primaquine added to artemether-lumefantrine, including gametocyte carriage, haemoglobin changes and adverse events
impact_summary: Single low-dose primaquine added to artemether-lumefantrine was safe and well tolerated, with no significant difference in haemoglobin drop or adverse events compared to artemether-lumefantrine alone, supporting deployment without G6PD testing.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
safety_summary: Haemoglobin concentrations similar between arms; a third of participants had a haemoglobin drop >2 g/dL not associated with primaquine but possibly with G6PD genotype; adverse events similar between arms; one serious adverse event (renal impairment) occurred in the no primaquine arm.

title: A seven-year study on the effect of the pre-erythrocytic malaria vaccine candidate RTS,S/AS01 E on blood stage immunity in young Kenyan children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine versus control with reported outcome results on antibody responses and malaria immunity over 7 years.
population: young children aged 5-17 months at enrollment, followed for 7 years
primary_outcome: IgG antibody levels to P. falciparum blood-stage antigens (AMA1, MSP1 42, EBA175, MSP3) and their association with malaria risk
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01 E recipients had slightly lower antibody levels to blood-stage antigens (MSP1 42, AMA1, EBA175) than Rabies-vaccine controls during the first 48 months, and this reduction persisted for several years, but anti-merozoite antibody levels were unreliable correlates of clinical immunity in the absence of asymptomatic infection.
effect_estimate: slightly lower in RTS,S/AS01 E arm vs Rabies control during first 48 months

title: A randomized controlled trial of azithromycin and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine as prophylaxis against malaria in pregnancy among human immunodeficiency virus-positive women.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp) in HIV-positive pregnant women with reported outcome results on parasitaemia at delivery.
population: HIV-positive pregnant women
primary_outcome: Peripheral parasitaemia at delivery
impact_summary: Azithromycin was comparable to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in preventing malaria parasitaemia at delivery among HIV-positive pregnant women, with no significant difference between groups.
follow_up: from enrollment at 16 weeks gestation to delivery
safety_summary: Both azithromycin and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine were found to be comparable in safety and tolerability; specific adverse event details not fully reported.

title: Intermittent screening and treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and intermittent preventive therapy with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine have similar effects on malaria antibody in pregnant Malawian women.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two malaria prevention strategies (IST-DP and IPT-SP) in pregnant women, a primary malaria intervention focus.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Development and maintenance of malaria antibody immunity (antibody responses to recombinant antigens and infected erythrocyte antigens) between enrolment and delivery
impact_summary: IST-DP and IPT-SP had similar effects on the development and maintenance of malaria antibody immunity in pregnant Malawian women, with minimal impact of treatment arm overall.
effect_metric: antibody response change (no significant difference between arms)

title: Impact of combining indoor residual spraying and long-lasting insecticidal nets on Anopheles arabiensis in Ethiopia: results from a cluster randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported entomological outcomes comparing malaria vector control interventions (IRS and LLINs) in humans.
comparator: IRS alone, LLIN alone, and control (no intervention)
population: villages/households in a malaria-endemic district; Anopheles arabiensis mosquito populations monitored
primary_outcome: Mosquito host-seeking density (HSD), indoor resting density (IRD), outdoor resting density (ORD), and human biting rates (HBR) of Anopheles arabiensis
impact_summary: Combining IRS and LLINs was as effective as IRS alone but more effective than LLINs alone in reducing Anopheles arabiensis densities and human biting rates.
p_value: p<0.05 (IRS+LLIN vs LLIN alone); p>0.05 (IRS+LLIN vs IRS alone)
species: P. falciparum (implied, none detected in mosquitoes)
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission, Anopheles arabiensis as sole primary vector

title: Concentration and avidity of antibodies to different circumsporozoite epitopes correlate with RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine efficacy.
screening_reason: Published Phase 3 RCT of RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine with reported outcome results (clinical malaria events) and efficacy analysis.
population: African children and infants
primary_outcome: Time to clinical malaria events during 12 months in relation to IgG concentration and avidity to CSP epitopes
impact_summary: Higher post-vaccination IgG magnitude to NANP and avidity to the C-terminus of CSP were significantly associated with RTS,S/AS01E vaccine efficacy against clinical malaria.
transmission_setting: one low (Bagomoyo) and two high (Nanoro, Kintampo) malaria transmission sites

title: Contribution of Functional Antimalarial Immunity to Measures of Parasite Clearance in Therapeutic Efficacy Studies of Artemisinin Derivatives.
screening_reason: Multinational RCT assessing efficacy of artesunate therapy for malaria with reported outcome results on parasite clearance.
population: patients with P. falciparum malaria receiving artesunate therapy
primary_outcome: parasite clearance half-life (PC½)
impact_summary: Higher levels of IgG3, complement (C1q) fixation, and opsonic phagocytosis against merozoite antigens were associated with faster parasite clearance during artesunate therapy, varying by transmission intensity.
effect_metric: mean reduction in parasite clearance half-life
transmission_setting: varying transmission intensity across 11 Southeast Asian sites

title: The impact of maternal antenatal treatment with two doses of azithromycin and monthly sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine on child weight, mid-upper arm circumference and head circumference: A randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria chemoprevention (IPTp with azithromycin and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on child anthropometry over 5 years of follow-up.
comparator: two doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (control) vs monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine vs monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus two doses of azithromycin (AZI-SP)
population: pregnant women and their children followed from birth to 5 years of age
primary_outcome: Child weight, mid-upper arm circumference, head circumference and weight-for-height Z-score at 1, 6, 12, 24, 36, 48, and 60 months
impact_summary: IPTp with azithromycin and monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine had a modest, 3-5-year positive impact on child weight, mid-upper arm circumference and head circumference, but not on weight-for-height Z-score, compared to control.
effect_metric: difference in means (weight) and hazard ratio (underweight incidence)
effect_estimate: 0.12 kg at 1 month; 0.19 kg at 6 months; hazard ratio 0.74 for underweight by 5 years
p_value: 0.003 (1 month weight); 0.007 (6 month weight); 0.002 (underweight hazard ratio)

title: Safety profile of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in infants and children: additional data from a phase III randomized controlled trial in sub-Saharan Africa.
screening_reason: Phase III RCT with reported safety and efficacy outcomes for RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in human participants; malaria prevention is the primary purpose.
population: infants (6-12 weeks) and children (5-17 months)
primary_outcome: Safety outcomes including serious adverse events, fatal SAEs, febrile convulsions, meningitis, cerebral malaria, and mortality
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01 vaccination was generally well tolerated but showed numerical imbalances in meningitis and cerebral malaria cases in children and higher all-cause mortality in vaccinated girls, considered likely chance findings warranting further evaluation.
effect_estimate: 24.2%-28.4% SAE incidence; 1.5%-2.5% fatal SAE incidence across groups
p_value: statistically significant imbalance for meningitis in children (p not specified)
safety_summary: SAE incidence 24.2%-28.4%, fatal SAE 1.5%-2.5%, vaccination-related SAEs 0.0%-0.3%; increased febrile convulsions post-vaccination with RTS,S/AS01; numerical imbalances in meningitis and cerebral malaria cases in children; higher all-cause mortality in vaccinated girls versus control girls (2.4% vs 1.3%)

title: Long-lasting insecticidal nets and indoor residual spraying may not be sufficient to eliminate malaria in a low malaria incidence area: results from a cluster randomized controlled trial in Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating malaria prevention interventions (LLINs and IRS) in humans.
comparator: LLIN alone, IRS alone, and control (untreated)
population: all age groups residing in surveyed households
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria and anaemia prevalence
impact_summary: Combining LLINs and IRS did not provide additional protection against malaria compared to LLINs or IRS alone or control, with similar clinical malaria incidence and anaemia prevalence across all four arms.
transmission_setting: low malaria incidence area, Rift Valley Ethiopia

title: Population pharmacokinetics and pharmacodynamics of the artesunate-mefloquine fixed dose combination for the treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in African children.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of artesunate-mefloquine for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in African children with reported pharmacokinetic and efficacy outcome results (recrudescence).
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: population pharmacokinetics of artesunate, dihydroartemisinin and mefloquine, and relationship between mefloquine AUC and malaria recrudescence
impact_summary: Population PK models showed large variability in AS/DHA and MQ exposure driven mainly by body weight, which is accounted for by the ASMQ fixed dose combination dosing, and no association was found between predicted MQ AUC and recrudescence.
effect_metric: association between MQ AUC and recrudescence

title: Safety and Differential Antibody and T-Cell Responses to the Plasmodium falciparum Sporozoite Malaria Vaccine, PfSPZ Vaccine, by Age in Tanzanian Adults, Adolescents, Children, and Infants.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (PfSPZ Vaccine) in humans with reported safety and immunogenicity outcome results.
population: adults, adolescents, children, and infants
primary_outcome: Safety (adverse events) and immunogenicity (antibody and T-cell responses) by age group
impact_summary: PfSPZ Vaccine was safe and well tolerated across all age groups with no significant differences in adverse events, and immune responses differed by age, with infants showing highest antibody but no significant T-cell responses.
safety_summary: No significant differences in adverse events between vaccinees and controls or between dosage regimens; vaccine was well tolerated across all age groups.

title: Comparison of malaria treatment outcome of generic and innovator's anti-malarial drugs containing artemether-lumefantrine combination in the management of uncomplicated malaria amongst Tanzanian children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemether-lumefantrine formulations for malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (cure rates, clinical/parasitological responses).
population: children aged 6 to 59 months with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: PCR uncorrected cure rate / treatment outcome (adequate clinical and parasitological response, treatment failures)
impact_summary: Generic Artefan and innovator Coartem showed equivalent and effective treatment outcomes for uncomplicated malaria in Tanzanian children, with no statistically significant difference in cure rates.
safety_summary: Only one participant (1.3%) on Artefan had temperature ≥37.5°C on day 3; no early treatment failures observed; drugs were generally well tolerated.

title: Phase II Efficacy Study of Artefenomel & Piperaquine in Adults & Children With P. Falciparum Malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artefenomel-piperaquine) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes (ACPR at Day 28); Phase 2/3 is not early-phase.
place: Benin, Burkina Faso, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Gabon, Mozambique, Uganda, Vietnam
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Benin; Burkina Faso; Gabon; Mozambique; Uganda; Vietnam
interventions_raw: Artefenomel 800mg: piperaquine 640mg; Artefenomel 800mg: piperaquine 960mg; Artefenomel 800mg: piperaquine 1440mg
population: adults and children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted ACPR at Day 28 in the PP Population (All Patients)
impact_summary: The study evaluated single-dose artefenomel-piperaquine efficacy and found molecular markers of multidrug resistance, including kelch13 mutations in Vietnam and high proportions of Pfmdr1 and Pfpm2 gene amplifications in African isolates, raising concerns about emerging piperaquine resistance.
transmission_setting: endemic regions of Asia and Africa

title: Differential Patterns of IgG Subclass Responses to Plasmodium falciparum Antigens in Relation to Malaria Protection and RTS,S Vaccination.
screening_reason: This is a published Phase 3 RCT of RTS,S malaria vaccine in African children that has reported immunogenicity and efficacy outcome results.
population: African children and infants
primary_outcome: IgG subclass responses to P. falciparum antigens in relation to malaria protection and RTS,S vaccination
impact_summary: IgG3 and IgG1 cytophilic antibody responses to specific P. falciparum antigens were associated with protection from malaria while IgG2 was associated with malaria risk, and RTS,S vaccination altered naturally acquired immunity, affecting vaccine efficacy.
transmission_setting: two sites of different malaria transmission intensity: Kintampo, Ghana and Manhiça, Mozambique

title: The prevalence and antifolate drug resistance profiles of Plasmodium falciparum in study participants randomized to discontinue or continue cotrimoxazole prophylaxis.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing cotrimoxazole prophylaxis strategies in HIV-infected individuals; malaria prevention is the primary focus with antifolate-resistance outcomes measured.
population: HIV-infected individuals on antiretroviral treatment
primary_outcome: Prevalence of antifolate-resistance mutations (pfdhfr and pfdhps) associated with sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance in P. falciparum
impact_summary: Discontinuing cotrimoxazole prophylaxis was associated with significantly higher prevalence of SP-resistance associated mutant haplotypes in P. falciparum compared to continuing cotrimoxazole, suggesting cotrimoxazole selects against SP-resistant parasites.
effect_estimate: 51.8% in STOP-CTX vs. 6.3% in CTX arm

title: Efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine versus dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria among children in Rwanda: an open-label, randomized controlled trial.
journal: Transactions of the Royal Society of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy outcomes at days 28 and 42.
population: children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28 and day 42
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were highly efficacious in treating uncomplicated malaria in Rwandan children, with DHP showing a greater post-treatment prophylactic effect against new infections.
effect_estimate: AL 98.3% vs DHP 98.9% at day 28; AL 97.3% vs DHP 98.4% at day 42
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sites (Masaka and Ruhuha), sub-Saharan Africa

title: Efficacy of Primaquine in Preventing Short- and Long-Latency Plasmodium vivax Relapses in Nepal.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of primaquine for P. vivax malaria treatment with reported outcome results showing efficacy in preventing relapses.
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: P. vivax recurrence over 1 year of follow-up
impact_summary: Chloroquine plus 14-day primaquine significantly reduced P. vivax recurrences compared with chloroquine alone over 1 year of follow-up.

title: Repeat Ivermectin Mass Drug Administrations for Control of Malaria: a Pilot Safety and Efficacy Study
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing repeated ivermectin mass drug administrations for malaria control in humans.
interventions_raw: Ivermectin; Albendazole
comparator: single dose ivermectin plus albendazole (control) vs five additional repeated doses of ivermectin (intervention)
population: village residents at least 90 cm in height; active case detection cohort of children aged 5 years or younger
primary_outcome: Incidence of Clinical Malaria Episodes
impact_summary: Repeated mass administrations of ivermectin reduced cumulative malaria incidence among young children compared with a single dose, without significantly increasing harms.
effect_metric: risk difference in episodes per child
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission during rainy season
age_range: children aged 5 years or younger (active case detection cohort); overall participants median age 15 years (IQR 6-34)
safety_summary: Risk of adverse events did not significantly differ between groups (45 [3%] in intervention vs 24 [2%] in control; risk ratio 1.63 [1.01-2.67], risk difference 1.21 [0.04-2.38], p=0.060); no adverse reactions were reported.

title: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention combined with community case management of malaria in children under 10 years of age, over 5 months, in south-east Senegal: A cluster-randomised trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, parasitaemia, anaemia, mortality).
population: children under 10 years of age (3 months to 9 years)
primary_outcome: Malaria (fever or history of fever with a positive rapid diagnostic test)
impact_summary: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention with community case management for children under 10 years given over 5 months substantially reduced malaria episodes, parasitaemia prevalence, and improved haemoglobin concentration compared to community case management alone.
safety_summary: SMC was well tolerated with no serious adverse reactions; mortality did not differ significantly between groups (rate difference 0.096/1,000 child-months, 95% CI 0.99, 1.18; p = 0.895).

title: Maternal vitamin A supplementation delays time to first episode of parasitaemia and reduces malaria parasite densities among infants in rural communities in Ebonyi State, Nigeria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on maternal vitamin A supplementation to prevent malaria parasitaemia in infants, a valid malaria prevention intervention in humans.
design: randomized, placebo-controlled, mother-infant dyad field trial
population: pregnant women (at least 6 months gestation) and their infants up to 12 months old
primary_outcome: time to first episode of parasitaemia and malaria parasite densities among infants
impact_summary: Maternal vitamin A supplementation delayed the time to first parasitaemia episode and reduced malaria parasite densities in infants compared to placebo.
effect_metric: difference in parasite density and time to first parasitaemia
transmission_setting: rural communities in Ebonyi State, Nigeria
age_range: infants up to 12 months; pregnant women in third trimester

title: Effects of a health educational intervention on malaria knowledge, motivation, and behavioural skills: a randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a health educational intervention to improve malaria prevention (ITN use and IPTp uptake) among pregnant women in Nigeria.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Total knowledge, motivation, and behavioural skills scores for ITN use and IPTp uptake
impact_summary: The health educational intervention significantly increased knowledge, motivation, and behavioural skills scores related to malaria prevention among pregnant women compared to the control group.
effect_metric: percentage difference in total scores between intervention and control groups

title: Malaria preventive behaviors among housewives in suburbs of Bandar-Abbas City, south of Iran: interventional design based on PRECEDE model.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention education intervention in an endemic area; primary focus is malaria prevention behavior promotion.
population: housewives in suburbs of Bandar-Abbas City
primary_outcome: Improvement in malaria preventive behaviors and PRECEDE model constructs (predisposing, enabling, reinforcing factors)
impact_summary: The PRECEDE model-based health education significantly improved knowledge, attitude, enabling and reinforcing factors, and malaria preventive behaviors among housewives compared to controls.

title: Sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine plus azithromycin may improve birth outcomes through impacts on inflammation and placental angiogenesis independent of malarial infection.
screening_reason: Published RCT reporting outcome results for sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine-based intermittent preventive treatment (IPTp) in pregnant women, a malaria prevention intervention with primary focus on birth outcomes.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Adverse pregnancy outcomes (low birthweight, preterm birth, small-for-gestational age) in association with biomarkers of inflammation and placental angiogenesis
impact_summary: SPAZ was associated with lower delivery inflammatory markers (AGP and CRP) and may protect against adverse pregnancy outcomes by reducing inflammation and placental angiogenesis dysregulation, independent of malarial infection status.
effect_estimate: 1.52 (CRP-preterm birth, SPCQ); 4.35 (sEng-preterm birth, SPCQ); 2.21 (sFlt1-preterm birth, SPCQ); 1.39 (sEng-low birthweight, SPCQ); 1.46 (sFlt1:PlGF ratio-low birthweight, all women)
p_value: p < 0.001 (delivery AGP and CRP levels lower in SPAZ arm)

title: Transmission-blocking Effects of Primaquine and Methylene Blue Suggest Plasmodium falciparum Gametocyte Sterilization Rather Than Effects on Sex Ratio.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT testing antimalarial interventions (primaquine and methylene blue) for malaria gametocyte sterilization with reported outcome results on transmission-blocking effects.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum gametocytemia
primary_outcome: Proportion of mosquitoes infected after feeding on patient blood (mosquito feeding assay)
impact_summary: Primaquine and methylene blue block malaria transmission by sterilizing gametocytes before affecting gametocyte density or sex ratio, rather than by skewing the sex ratio.

title: Adherence to intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in Papua New Guinean infants: A pharmacological study alongside the randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: RCT of malaria chemoprevention (IPTi with SP-AQ) in infants with reported outcome results (adherence and drug concentrations measured).
comparator: placebo, and artesunate (AS) vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (SP-AQ)
population: infants receiving intermittent preventive treatment for malaria during first year of life
primary_outcome: Adherence to the prescribed 3-dose amodiaquine regimen assessed via drug/metabolite (desethyl-amodiaquine) blood concentrations and pharmacokinetic modelling
impact_summary: Pharmacokinetic analysis showed that only 39-50% of children in the SP-AQ arm received all three scheduled doses of amodiaquine as prescribed, indicating low medication adherence for the self-administered doses given by parents at home.
effect_metric: proportion of children receiving full 3-dose regimen
safety_summary: Not reported in this sub-study; focus was on pharmacological adherence assessment rather than safety outcomes.

title: Optimal dosing of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in young children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for seasonal malaria chemoprevention in children with reported outcome results on malaria re-infection intervals.
comparator: standard mg/kg dosage per WHO 2015 guideline
population: young children aged 2.33-58.1 months
primary_outcome: interval to malaria re-infection modeled via pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (EMAX) model
impact_summary: Population-based simulations suggest that increasing dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine dosage and extending to four monthly doses could reduce malaria incidence by up to 58% during the high transmission season, especially benefiting small children who have lower drug exposures at standard dosing.
effect_metric: predicted relative reduction in malaria incidence

title: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention packaged with malnutrition prevention in northern Nigeria: A pragmatic trial (SMAMP study) with nested case-control.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results assessing seasonal malaria chemoprevention (SP-AQ) as the primary intervention in children, with malaria as primary outcome.
design: pragmatic trial with nested case-control study
comparator: SP-AQ alone (SMC without LNS) and children who did not receive interventions
population: children aged 6-24 months
primary_outcome: Coverage and adherence to SMC, anthropometric outcomes, and clinical malaria outcomes
impact_summary: Coverage of SMC was high regardless of LNS integration; LNS did not improve nutritional outcomes but SP-AQ (with or without LNS) reduced the odds of clinical malaria compared to no intervention.
effect_estimate: SP-AQ only OR=0.23; SP-AQ plus LNS OR=0.22
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Artemisia annua and Artemisia afra tea infusions vs. artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ) in treating Plasmodium falciparum malaria in a large scale, double blind, randomized clinical trial.
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with 957 randomized participants reporting outcome results (parasitemia clearance, cure rates, gametocyte carriage) for a malaria treatment intervention.
population: malaria-infected patients (pediatric and adult)
primary_outcome: D28 cure rate (absence of parasitemia)
impact_summary: Artemisia annua and Artemisia afra tea infusions achieved higher D28 cure rates and fewer adverse effects than artesunate-amodiaquine (ASAQ) in treating P. falciparum malaria.
effect_estimate: Pediatrics: 82% (A. afra), 91% (A. annua), 50% (ASAQ); Adults: 91% (A. afra), 100% (A. annua), 30% (ASAQ)
safety_summary: 5.0% of Artemisia-treated patients reported adverse effects vs. 42.8% for ASAQ; hemoglobin remained stable at 11 g/dl for A. afra but decreased to 9-9.5 g/dl for A. annua and ASAQ.

title: Susceptibility of Plasmodium falciparum to artemisinins and Plasmodium vivax to chloroquine in Phuoc Chien Commune, Ninh Thuan Province, south-central Vietnam.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled therapeutic efficacy trial in humans with reported outcome results for malaria treatment (artemisinin/ACT and chloroquine), meeting all inclusion criteria.
comparator: active comparator (AS+DHA-PPQ vs AM-LUM for falciparum; CQ for vivax)
population: patients with falciparum or vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Therapeutic efficacy (parasite clearance and recrudescence/recurrence rates) at day 42 (falciparum) and day 28 (vivax)
impact_summary: Falciparum parasites remained artemisinin susceptible with 100% curative rate, while chloroquine treatment for vivax malaria had a 13.3% clinical failure rate.
transmission_setting: low transmission, south-central Vietnam commune-level endemic setting
safety_summary: No specific adverse events reported; drug exposure to artesunate and lumefantrine comparable to published data, though blood chloroquine concentrations were lower than expected.

title: Study to Assess the Incidence of Hemolysis, Safety, and Efficacy of Tafenoquine (SB-252263, WR238605) Versus Primaquine in Subjects With Plasmodium Vivax Malaria
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT with reported outcome results comparing tafenoquine and primaquine for P. vivax malaria treatment and radical cure.
place: Brazil, Colombia, Ethiopia, Peru, Thailand, Vietnam
countries: Brazil; Colombia; Ethiopia; Peru; Thailand; Vietnam
interventions_raw: Tafenoquine; Tafenoquine Placebo; Chloroquine; Primaquine; Primaquine Placebo
population: patients with confirmed P. vivax parasitemia and normal G6PD enzyme activity, plus female patients with moderate G6PD deficiency
primary_outcome: Percentage of Participants With Clinically Relevant Hemolysis.
impact_summary: Tafenoquine showed efficacy for radical cure of P. vivax malaria but was not shown to be noninferior to primaquine, with similar hemolysis safety outcomes between groups.
effect_metric: odds ratio for recurrence (tafenoquine vs. primaquine)
transmission_setting: multi-country endemic settings (Peru, Brazil, Colombia, Vietnam, Thailand)
safety_summary: A protocol-defined decrease in hemoglobin level occurred in 2.4% of tafenoquine group and 1.2% of primaquine group (difference 1.2 percentage points, 95% CI -4.2 to 5.0); among patients with normal G6PD activity, hemoglobin decline did not differ significantly between groups.

title: Ph 2B/3 Tafenoquine (TFQ) Study in Prevention of Vivax Relapse
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing tafenoquine for P. vivax malaria radical cure (prevention of relapse) in humans; Phase 2/3; primary malaria focus.
place: Bangladesh, Brazil, Cambodia, Ethiopia, India, Peru, Philippines, Thailand
countries: Bangladesh; Brazil; Cambodia; Ethiopia; India; Peru; Philippines; Thailand
interventions_raw: Chloroquine 600mg; Chloroquine 300mg; Tafenoquine 50mg; Tafenoquine 100mg; Tafenoquine 300mg; Tafenoquine 600mg; Primaquine 15mg; Chloroquine 600mg (Part 2 ); Chloroquine 300mg (Part 2 ); Tafenoquine 300mg (Part 2); Primaquine 15mg (Part2 )
population: patients with microscopically confirmed P. vivax infection and normal G6PD activity
primary_outcome: Number of Participants With Recurrence-free Efficacy at 6 Months Post Dose
impact_summary: Single-dose tafenoquine resulted in a significantly lower risk of P. vivax recurrence than placebo in patients with phenotypically normal G6PD activity.
effect_metric: hazard ratio for risk of recurrence (tafenoquine vs placebo)
safety_summary: Tafenoquine was associated with asymptomatic declines in hemoglobin levels, which resolved without intervention.

title: Comparison of the effectiveness of two-dose versus three-dose sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in preventing adverse pregnancy outcomes in Nigeria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (parasitaemia, low birth weight) comparing two malaria prevention interventions (intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy) in humans.
population: pregnant women with gestational ages of 16-24 weeks
primary_outcome: Low birth weight (LBW), peripheral and placental parasitaemia
impact_summary: Three-dose SP for IPTp reduced peripheral and placental parasitaemia and low birth weight compared to two-dose SP, though maternal anaemia, preterm birth, clinical malaria and adverse effects were similar between groups.
safety_summary: Adverse effects of SP were similar between the two-dose and three-dose treatment arms.

title: Differential infectivity of gametocytes after artemisinin-based combination therapy of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing three ACT regimens for malaria treatment, measuring gametocyte infectivity as a primary endpoint.
comparator: active comparator (artemether-lumefantrine vs artesunate-amodiaquine vs artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine)
population: volunteers with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Infectivity of gametocytes to Anopheles gambiae following ACT treatment, assessed via direct skin feeding assays
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine significantly increased gametocyte infectivity to Anopheles gambiae, while artesunate-sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine decreased infectivity.
effect_estimate: increased infectivity (AL, AS-AQ) vs decreased infectivity (AS-SP)

title: The effect of mobile phone text message reminders on health workers' adherence to case management guidelines for malaria and other diseases in Malawi: lessons from qualitative data from a cluster-randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results on SMS reminders for malaria case management in health workers; phase not applicable for health systems intervention.
design: cluster-randomized trial with qualitative sub-study (in-depth interviews, thematic and framework analysis)
population: health workers (clinicians and drug dispensers) in health facilities managing childhood illnesses including malaria
primary_outcome: health worker adherence to case management guidelines for malaria and other childhood diseases
impact_summary: Text-message reminders were well accepted by health workers but had little effect on adherence to case management guidelines due to health systems barriers such as high workload, stock-outs, and lack of supervision.

title: Controlled Human Malaria Infection of Healthy Adults With Lifelong Malaria Exposure to Assess Safety, Immunogenicity, and Efficacy of the Asexual Blood Stage Malaria Vaccine Candidate GMZ2.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of a malaria vaccine (GMZ2) with reported outcome results including safety, immunogenicity, and efficacy endpoints from controlled human malaria infection; primary purpose is malaria prevention and it is Phase 2, not early-phase.
population: healthy adults with lifelong malaria exposure
primary_outcome: Efficacy of GMZ2 vaccine assessed by controlled human malaria infection (parasitemia and malaria symptoms after CHMI)
impact_summary: GMZ2 vaccination was well tolerated and immunogenic but showed no protective efficacy against malaria upon controlled human malaria infection, though baseline vaccine-specific antibody concentrations were associated with protection.
effect_estimate: 2/5 control, 6/10 GMZ2-Alhydrogel, 2/8 30 µg GMZ2-CAF01, 5/11 100 µg GMZ2-CAF01
follow_up: 13 weeks after last vaccination to CHMI, plus post-CHMI monitoring
safety_summary: Adverse events were similarly distributed between GMZ2 and control vaccinees; GMZ2 was well tolerated across all formulations.

title: Parasite reduction ratio one day after initiation of artemisinin-based combination therapies and its relationship with parasite clearance time in acutely malarious children.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments in children with acute malaria, comparing parasite reduction ratios and parasite clearance time across treatment arms.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate-amodiaquine, artemether-lumefantrine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine compared with each other)
population: acutely malarious children
primary_outcome: Parasite reduction ratio one day post-treatment (PRRD1) and its relationship with parasite clearance time (PCT) and PRRD2
impact_summary: PRRD1 correlated significantly with PCT and PRRD2, was higher in DHP- and AA-treated than AL-treated children, and PCT estimates derived from PRRD1 regression equations agreed well with microscopy-determined PCT, supporting its use in therapeutic efficacy studies.
effect_estimate: significant negative correlation between PRRD1/PRRD2 and PCT; significant positive correlation between PRRD1 and PRRD2
age_range: children (mean ages >15 months and >30 months noted as predictors)

title: Cost-effectiveness of a combined intervention of long lasting insecticidal nets and indoor residual spraying compared with each intervention alone for malaria prevention in Ethiopia.
journal: Cost effectiveness and resource allocation : C/E
screening_reason: Cluster RCT of malaria prevention interventions (LLINs and IRS) with reported outcome results (cost-effectiveness and malaria incidence data from the trial conducted 2014–2016).
design: cluster randomized controlled trial, cost-effectiveness analysis
comparator: LLIN alone, IRS alone, routine practice
population: residents of Adami Tullu district exposed to malaria transmission
primary_outcome: Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (cost per DALY averted)
impact_summary: Trial-based analysis found that routine practice dominated combined LLIN+IRS and single interventions due to lower costs and comparable effectiveness, while literature-based analysis suggested LLIN alone could be cost-effective.
effect_metric: incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (USD per DALY averted)

title: Malaria parasite clearance from patients following artemisinin-based combination therapy in Côte d'Ivoire.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two ACT regimens for malaria treatment with reported outcome results (parasite clearance and clinical response).
population: patients aged at least 6 months with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance rate and time
impact_summary: Both artesunate + amodiaquine and artemether + lumefantrine rapidly cleared parasites and remained highly efficacious, with PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response of 100% and 98.07% at day 42, respectively.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response

title: Population Pharmacokinetics of Mefloquine Intermittent Preventive Treatment for Malaria in Pregnancy in Gabon.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing mefloquine versus sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy with reported pharmacokinetic outcome results.
design: randomized controlled trial, population pharmacokinetic analysis
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Pharmacokinetic characteristics of mefloquine stereoisomers and carboxymefloquine metabolite when given as IPTp
impact_summary: Mefloquine IPTp given as single or split-dose regimens showed adequate exposure but concentrations at delivery were below previously suggested prophylactic threshold levels, and split-dosing significantly increased bioavailability by 5%.
effect_metric: increase in mefloquine bioavailability (split-dose vs single-dose)

title: Comparative Efficacy of Artemether-Lumefantrine and Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine for the Treatment of Uncomplicated Malaria in Ugandan Children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemether-lumefantrine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine) in humans with reported outcome results at 42 days.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: risk of recurrent parasitemia (unadjusted or adjusted to distinguish recrudescence from new infection) at 42 days
impact_summary: DHA-PQ resulted in a lower risk of recurrent parasitemia than AL, but recrudescence was uncommon and similar with both regimens, with neither treatment selecting for drug-resistance-associated genetic polymorphisms.
effect_metric: risk of recurrent parasitemia at day 42
safety_summary: No early treatment failures were reported; recrudescent infections were uncommon in both arms (1.1% DHA-PQ vs 2.2% AL, P = .25)

title: A Balanced Proinflammatory and Regulatory Cytokine Signature in Young African Children Is Associated With Lower Risk of Clinical Malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprophylaxis (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus artesunate) with reported clinical malaria outcome results in African children.
population: young African children/infants followed from birth to 4 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria up to 4 years of age in relation to cytokine responses
impact_summary: Higher proinflammatory and regulatory cytokine concentrations during the second year of life were associated with reduced clinical malaria incidence up to age 4, and chemoprophylaxis altering early malaria exposure significantly affected later T-helper cytokine production.
effect_metric: association with incidence of clinical malaria
follow_up: from birth to 4 years of age
age_range: infancy to 4 years (measurements at 2.5, 5.5, 10.5, 15, and 24 months)

title: Baseline exposure, antibody subclass, and hepatitis B response differentially affect malaria protective immunity following RTS,S/AS01E vaccination in African children.
screening_reason: This is a published Phase 3 RCT reporting outcome results for RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine in African children with identified correlates of protection against clinical malaria.
population: infants and children
primary_outcome: Immunogenicity and antibody correlates of protection against clinical malaria
impact_summary: Cytophilic IgG1/IgG3 responses to CSP C-terminus/NANP and anti-HBsAg antibodies induced by RTS,S/AS01E were associated with protection, while higher baseline malaria exposure and non-cytophilic IgG responses to CSP were associated with increased malaria risk.
effect_metric: association with malaria risk/protection (regression/machine learning correlates)
transmission_setting: two sites with different malaria transmission intensities (Kintampo, Ghana and Manhiça, Mozambique)

title: Assessment of parasite clearance following treatment of severe malaria with intravenous artesunate in Ugandan children enrolled in a randomized controlled clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of intravenous artesunate for severe malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (parasite clearance endpoints).
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day parasitological treatment outcomes and safety; parasite clearance half-life and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Parasite clearance following treatment with intravenous artesunate was rapid and adequate, suggesting artemisinin resistance has not emerged in this study area.
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission area, Eastern Uganda
safety_summary: Artesunate was well tolerated with rapid recovery from symptoms and ability to take oral medication within 24 h; no immediate adverse events were recorded.

title: New Prototype Screened Doors and Windows for Excluding Mosquitoes from Houses: A Pilot Study in Rural Gambia.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (screened doors/windows) with reported outcome results (mosquito entry reduction); phase not applicable for non-drug vector-control trials.
population: household units in a rural Gambian village
primary_outcome: Reduction in number of house-entering mosquitoes with screened doors/windows compared to control houses
impact_summary: Prototype screened doors reduced house-entering mosquitoes by 59-77% compared to control houses, with the perforated concertinaed screening door performing best.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; doors and windows found safe and well-tolerated by residents, no adverse events mentioned

title: A randomized trial of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated malaria treatment in humans with reported efficacy outcomes at 28 and 42 days.
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPRc) at day 28
impact_summary: Both dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and artemether-lumefantrine were highly and similarly efficacious against uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria after PCR correction, with no significant difference between arms.
effect_estimate: 99.4% (DHA-PQ) vs 98.1% (AL) at day 28; 99.3% vs 97.4% at day 42
safety_summary: No significant difference in QTc prolongation between DHA-PQ (12.1%) and AL (7%), p = 0.4.

title: Correction: Comparison of artemether-lumefantrine and chloroquine with and without primaquine for the treatment of Plasmodium vivax infection in Ethiopia: A randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: A published RCT comparing antimalarial treatments (artemether-lumefantrine and chloroquine ± primaquine) for P. vivax malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results.
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax infection
impact_summary: This is a correction notice for a previously published article and does not itself report new results.

title: Study to Evaluate the Efficacy and Safety of Tafenoquine for the Treatment of Plasmodium Vivax in Adults
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of tafenoquine versus chloroquine/primaquine for P. vivax malaria with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
interventions_raw: Tafenoquine; Chloroquine + Primaquine; tafenoquine; Chloroquine + Primaquine
population: adults with microscopically confirmed P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate Clinical Response (ACR) of Tafenoquine: 28 Day Cure Rate
impact_summary: Tafenoquine was associated with more frequent mild keratopathy than chloroquine/primaquine, but there was no evidence of clinically relevant ocular toxicity with either treatment.
safety_summary: Post-baseline keratopathy occurred in 31.8% of TQ patients versus 0% of CQ/PQ patients (P=0.002); mild retinal findings in 22.7% vs 8.3% (P=0.15); one retinal hemorrhage in a TQ patient; decreased visual field sensitivity in some patients in both groups (<5 dB); no clinically relevant changes in visual acuity or macular function; overall no clinically relevant ocular toxicity observed with either treatment.
funder: U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command

title: The impact of packaging and messaging on adherence to malaria treatment: Evidence from a randomized controlled trial in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial testing malaria treatment adherence interventions with reported outcome results; malaria treatment is the primary focus.
population: malaria patients receiving antimalarial treatment
primary_outcome: Adherence to antimalarial medication (completion of treatment course/untaken pills)
impact_summary: Stickers with short, targeted messages on packaging increased adherence by 9% and reduced untaken pills by 29%, while specialized pictorial packaging had no significant effect compared to standard packaging.
effect_estimate: 9% increase in adherence; 29% reduction in untaken pills

title: A pilot randomized controlled trial to compare the effectiveness of two 14-day primaquine regimens for the radical cure of vivax malaria in South India.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two primaquine regimens for vivax malaria radical cure in humans.
comparator: conventional dose primaquine (0.25 mg/kg for 14 days)
population: Patients with vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Recurrence of P. vivax infection (relapse) within 6 months, assessed by genotyping
impact_summary: Both high-dose (0.5 mg/kg) and conventional-dose (0.25 mg/kg) 14-day primaquine regimens showed similarly low relapse rates, supporting the effectiveness of the currently recommended lower dose regimen for radical cure of vivax malaria in South India.
safety_summary: One relapse was associated with low carboxyprimaquine concentrations suggesting poor adherence; no other safety issues reported.

title: Experimental huts trial of the efficacy of pyrethroids/piperonyl butoxide (PBO) net treatments for controlling multi-resistant populations of Anopheles funestus s.s. in Kpomè, Southern Benin.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (experimental hut released/recapture design) with reported outcome results comparing pyrethroid/PBO-treated nets versus conventional LLINs for malaria vector control in humans' living environment.
design: experimental hut trial, WHO cone and tunnel tests, released/recapture experiment
population: wild free-flying multi-resistant Anopheles funestus s.s. and An. coluzzii mosquito populations
primary_outcome: Mosquito mortality following exposure to LLINs in experimental huts (cone and tunnel tests)
impact_summary: Pyrethroid-PBO combination LLINs (Type 1 and Type 3) produced significantly higher mortality against multi-resistant An. funestus s.s. and An. coluzzii than conventional pyrethroid-only LLINs.
effect_estimate: Type 1/3 (PBO nets): >80% mortality vs Type 2: 65.53±8.33% and Type 4: 71.25±7.92% mortality with An. funestus; 77-87% mortality with An. coluzzii
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic area with multi-insecticide resistant Anopheles populations
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Microbial larvicides for mosquito control: Impact of long lasting formulations of Bacillus thuringiensis var. israelensis and Bacillus sphaericus on non-target organisms in western Kenya highlands.
