screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vector control intervention (microbial larvicides) with reported outcome results on non-target organisms and malaria vector density in Kenya.
population: natural mosquito larval habitats and cohabiting non-target aquatic organisms
primary_outcome: Impact of long lasting microbial larvicides on abundance, richness and diversity of non-target organisms in larval habitats
impact_summary: FourStar and LL3 larvicides significantly reduced malaria vector density but did not significantly alter abundance, richness or diversity of non-target aquatic organisms in treated habitats.
effect_metric: density of non-target organisms per habitat per sampling occasion
transmission_setting: malaria vector control in highland villages
safety_summary: LL3 and FourStar did not significantly alter abundance, richness or diversity of the 11 non-target taxa studied compared to control habitats

title: Wall-type and indoor residual spraying application quality affect the residual efficacy of indoor residual spray against wild malaria vector in southwest Ethiopia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing indoor residual spray application quality and wall types on malaria vector control with reported outcome results (knockdown and mortality rates).
design: randomized, entomological field trial comparing wall surface types and spray application quality
comparator: routine spray vs standard spray vs unsprayed control houses
population: houses with different mud wall surfaces (smooth, rough, painted) in a semi-urban/rural community
primary_outcome: Knockdown rate and mortality rate of wild Anopheles gambiae s.l. in wall bioassay tests over 17 weeks post-spray
impact_summary: Painted wall surfaces and standard (guideline-compliant) spray application showed significantly higher and more sustained residual efficacy of propoxur against Anopheles gambiae s.l. compared to rough/smooth surfaces and routine spray application.
effect_estimate: >80% (standard spray) vs <80% (routine spray, except painted wall)
transmission_setting: southwest Ethiopia, semi-urban/rural malaria endemic area
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Molecular Detection of Residual Parasitemia after Pyronaridine-Artesunate or Artemether-Lumefantrine Treatment of Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Kenyan Children.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria treatment (pyronaridine-artesunate vs artemether-lumefantrine) in humans with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and treatment failure.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Residual parasitemia at day 7 detected by qPCR and db-PCR-NALFIA
impact_summary: Both qPCR and db-PCR-NALFIA detected substantial residual submicroscopic parasitemia at day 7 after microscopically successful treatment with pyronaridine-artesunate or artemether-lumefantrine, with no significant difference between the two treatments, and db-PCR-NALFIA positivity was associated with treatment failure while qPCR positivity was not.
effect_metric: proportion with residual parasitemia at day 7 (qPCR)

title: Efficacy of Olyset Duo, a bednet containing pyriproxyfen and permethrin, versus a permethrin-only net against clinical malaria in an area with highly pyrethroid-resistant vectors in rural Burkina Faso: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of malaria vector control (insecticidal nets) with reported outcome results (clinical malaria incidence and entomological inoculation rate).
population: children aged 6 months to 5 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria (passive case detection) and entomological inoculation rate
impact_summary: PPF-treated LLINs (Olyset Duo) provided greater protection against clinical malaria and reduced entomological inoculation rate compared with standard permethrin-only LLINs in an area with highly pyrethroid-resistant vectors.
transmission_setting: intense/high malaria transmission with highly pyrethroid-resistant vectors, rural Burkina Faso

title: Treatment of adults with acute uncomplicated malaria with azithromycin and chloroquine in India, Colombia, and Suriname.
journal: Research and reports in tropical medicine
screening_reason: Double-blind randomized controlled trial comparing antimalarial drug combinations for treatment of acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in adults with reported outcome results (parasitologic cure at Day 28).
population: adults with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Parasitologic cure at Day 28
impact_summary: Azithromycin 1 g plus chloroquine QD for 3 days was inferior to established comparator agents (SPCQ in India, AP in Colombia/Suriname), but increasing azithromycin dose to 2 g improved response rates to 97%.

title: School-aged children based seasonal malaria chemoprevention using artesunate-amodiaquine in Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate-amodiaquine seasonal malaria chemoprevention in school-aged children with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: school-aged pupils
primary_outcome: Incidence of uncomplicated clinical malaria
impact_summary: Monthly artesunate-amodiaquine given as seasonal malaria chemoprevention to school-aged children reduced clinical malaria cases substantially compared to no intervention, with only 3 cases in the ASAQ arm versus 20 in the control arm.
safety_summary: ASAQ was well tolerated; most common solicited adverse events were abdominal pain (64%) and headaches (44%), of mild intensity; no effect on anemia observed.

title: Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Studies to Assess Safety and Prophylactic Efficacy of Naphthoquine-Azithromycin Combination for Malaria Prophylaxis in Southeast Asia.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria chemoprophylactic drug combination in humans; Phase 2 is not early-phase.
population: healthy volunteers and villagers in a low-endemicity area
primary_outcome: Safety and prophylactic efficacy against malaria infections
impact_summary: Monthly single doses of 400 mg or 800 mg naphthoquine-azithromycin were well tolerated and provided over 90% prophylactic efficacy against malaria infections, including 100% efficacy against P. vivax and P. ovale.
effect_estimate: 81.63% (400 mg) and 90.59% (800 mg) against P. falciparum; 100% against P. vivax and P. ovale; >90% overall (intention-to-treat)
safety_summary: Both drug regimens were well tolerated with no serious adverse events; four adverse events (transient, slight elevations of serum transaminase concentrations) occurred only in drug-treated groups and may be drug-related.

title: Intermittent screening and treatment with artemether-lumefantrine versus intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for malaria in pregnancy: a facility-based, open-label, non-inferiority trial in Nigeria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two chemoprevention strategies (ISTp-AL vs IPTp-SP) for malaria in pregnancy, a primary malaria intervention focus.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal clinic
primary_outcome: Third-trimester severe anaemia (Hb < 8 g/dl) and maternal parasitaemia; birth weight
impact_summary: ISTp-AL was associated with significantly lower third-trimester maternal parasitaemia and lower risk of low birthweight compared to IPTp-SP, with no significant difference in severe anaemia risk, though ISTp-AL was associated with more frequent fever complaints.
follow_up: through delivery (third trimester assessment at 36-40 weeks gestation)
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission with moderate sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine resistance
safety_summary: Women in the ISTp-AL arm reported fever more frequently than those in the IPTp-SP arm (p = 0.022); no other major safety differences reported.

title: Efficacy of two artemisinin-based combinations for the treatment of malaria in pregnancy in India: a randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (ACPR on day 63) comparing artemisinin-based antimalarial combinations for malaria treatment in pregnancy—a primary malaria intervention with appropriate phase.
place: India (Ranchi and Jamshedpur, Jharkhand; Rourkela, Odisha)
population: pregnant women in second or third trimester with P. falciparum mono-infection
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 63
impact_summary: Both AS+SP and AS+MQ were safe and effective, with high ACPR rates in intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses, though vomiting was more common with AS+MQ.
follow_up: 63 days post-treatment, plus follow-up at delivery and day 42 postpartum
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic regions of India (Jharkhand and Odisha states)
safety_summary: Five serious adverse events among pregnant women (4 AS+SP, 1 AS+MQ) and 13 fetal/neonatal SAEs (7 AS+SP, 6 AS+MQ), none related to study drugs; higher rate of vomiting in AS+MQ arm (6.9% vs 1.6%, p=0.001).

title: Effectiveness of pregnant women's active participation in their antenatal care for the control of malaria and anaemia in pregnancy in Ghana: a cluster randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing active participation in antenatal care (including malaria and anaemia testing) versus routine care for malaria and anaemia control in pregnant women; PRIMARY focus is malaria prevention in pregnancy.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal clinics for the first time
primary_outcome: Malaria parasitaemia and anaemia (haemoglobin levels) during pregnancy, low birth weight and pregnancy outcomes
impact_summary: The intervention allowing pregnant women active participation via point-of-care malaria and anaemia testing showed no significant beneficial effect on anaemia, parasitaemia, low birth weight, or pregnancy complications compared to routine care.
effect_estimate: 0.97 (anaemia at 8 weeks); 0.92 (anaemia at 36-40 weeks); 1.17 (parasitaemia at 8 weeks); 0.83 (parasitaemia at 36-40 weeks); 0.93 (low birth weight); 0.77 (pregnancy complications)

title: Comparison of the Cumulative Efficacy and Safety of Chloroquine, Artesunate, and Chloroquine-Primaquine in Plasmodium vivax Malaria.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (recurrence/relapse rates) comparing antimalarial treatments for P. vivax malaria in humans.
comparator: chloroquine versus artesunate versus chloroquine-primaquine (active comparators)
population: Patients with uncomplicated P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 and 1-year recurrence rates of P. vivax malaria
impact_summary: Chloroquine delayed vivax malaria relapses compared to artesunate, while adding primaquine radical cure reduced total recurrences by 92.4%.
effect_metric: reduction in total recurrences with primaquine radical cure
transmission_setting: Thailand-Myanmar border, low transmission area with chloroquine-resistant P. vivax
safety_summary: Recurrence by day 28 was associated with a mean absolute reduction in hematocrit of 1% (95% CI, 0.3%-2.0%; P = .009); no other major safety issues reported.

title: Therapeutic and Transmission-Blocking  Efficacy of Dihydroartemisinin/Piperaquine and Chloroquine against Plasmodium vivax Malaria, Cambodia.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two antimalarial drugs against P. vivax with reported efficacy outcomes; meets all inclusion criteria for malaria treatment intervention with results.
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy in clearing asexual P. vivax parasites and blocking human-to-mosquito transmission
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin/piperaquine cleared asexual P. vivax parasites faster, blocked human-to-mosquito transmission more effectively, and better prevented recurrences beyond 2 months compared with chloroquine.

title: Caregivers' compliance with referral advice: evidence from two studies introducing mRDTs into community case management of malaria in Uganda.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of malaria intervention (mRDT and ACT in community case management) with reported outcome results on referral compliance and treatment outcomes.
comparator: CHW trained to treat based on fever symptoms (control arm without mRDT)
population: children under-5 with fever seen by community health workers
primary_outcome: Caregivers' compliance with CHW referral advice
impact_summary: Compliance with CHW referral advice was low (<10%) in both moderate-to-high and low transmission settings, with nearly all children given pre-referral rectal artesunate failing to comply with referral.
transmission_setting: one moderate-to-high transmission setting and one low-transmission setting
safety_summary: Not reported as a primary safety analysis; concern raised about children receiving rectal artesunate failing to comply with referral

title: Efficacy and tolerability of artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine in the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria at two sentinel sites across Côte d’Ivore.
screening_reason: RCT comparing two antimalarial drugs (ASAQ vs AL) for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported outcome results (cure rates at day 28 and 42).
population: patients with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28 and day 42
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine were highly effective and well-tolerated for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with ASAQ showing slightly higher cure rates than AL.
effect_estimate: ASAQ 95.8% vs AL 92.5% (day 28); ASAQ 95% vs AL 92.5% (day 42)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sentinel surveillance sites in Côte d'Ivoire
safety_summary: Both drugs were well-tolerated at the clinical and biological level.

title: Wash-resistance of pirimiphos-methyl insecticide treatments of window screens and eave baffles for killing indoor-feeding malaria vector mosquitoes: an experimental hut trial, South East of Zambia.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (experimental hut trial design with treated vs. control comparisons) that reports outcome results on malaria vector mortality from an insecticide-treated vector control intervention.
comparator: IRS with pirimiphos-methyl, unwashed/washed WSEB treatments
population: Not applicable (entomological/experimental hut study, not human participants)
primary_outcome: Mosquito mortality (killing) of indoor-feeding malaria vector mosquitoes after washing of insecticide-treated window screens and eave baffles
impact_summary: Window screens and eave baffles co-treated with pirimiphos-methyl and a polyacrylate binding agent retained high insecticidal efficacy (≥94% mortality) against Anopheles arabiensis even after 20 washes, comparable to indoor residual spraying with pirimiphos-methyl.
transmission_setting: Malaria-endemic area of South East Zambia
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Study to Evaluate Immunogenicity of the Hepatitis B Antigen of the GSK Biologicals' Candidate Malaria Vaccine (257049)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in infants with reported outcome results on immunogenicity and safety; Phase 3; primary intervention is a malaria vaccine.
interventions_raw: GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) Biologicals' candidate Plasmodium falciparum malaria vaccine 257049; Engerix-B™ vaccine; Infanrix/Hib™ vaccine; Polio Sabin™ vaccine; Rotarix™ vaccine; Synflorix™ vaccine; Measles vaccine; Yellow fever vaccine
comparator: licensed hepatitis B vaccine (Engerix B) co-administered with DTaP/Hib and oral poliovirus vaccine
population: healthy infants aged 8-12 weeks
primary_outcome: Percentage of Seroprotected Subjects Against Anti-Hepatitis B (HBs) Antigen
impact_summary: Co-administration of RTS,S/AS01 with routine pediatric vaccines (PHiD-CV, HRV, DTaP/Hib) demonstrated non-inferior immune responses and an acceptable safety profile compared to hepatitis B vaccine co-administration.
effect_estimate: non-inferiority criteria met for HBV seroprotection and for PHiD-CV (9/10 serotypes), HRV, and pertussis antigens
safety_summary: Pain and low-grade fever were more frequent in the PHiD-CV group co-administered with RTS,S/AS01; no serious adverse events were considered vaccine-related; RTS,S/AS01 had an acceptable safety profile.

title: Pyronaridine-artesunate or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus current first-line therapies for repeated treatment of uncomplicated malaria: a randomised, multicentre, open-label, longitudinal, controlled, phase 3b/4 trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial treatments for malaria in humans, Phase 3b/4, with primary malaria focus and participant randomization.
population: adults and children aged 6 months and older with microscopically confirmed Plasmodium spp malaria
primary_outcome: 2-year incidence rate of all microscopically confirmed malaria episodes (ITT) and adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at days 28 and 42 (per-protocol)
impact_summary: Pyronaridine-artesunate and dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine were non-inferior to first-line ACTs (artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine) for malaria treatment and retreatment and were well tolerated.
effect_estimate: RR 1.05 (pyronaridine-artesunate vs artemether-lumefantrine); RR 0.97 (vs artesunate-amodiaquine); RR 1.22 (dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine); RR 1.25 (vs artesunate-amodiaquine)
safety_summary: Nine deaths occurred, none related to study treatment; mostly mild transient elevations in transaminases with pyronaridine-artesunate and mild QTcF prolongation with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine compared with comparators.
funder: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trial Partnership, Medicines for Malaria Venture, UK Medical Research Council, Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, German Ministry for Education and Research, University Claude Bernard, University of Science, Techniques and Technologies of Bamako, Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme, Institut de Recherche en Sciences de la Santé, Centre National de Formation et de Recherche en Santé Rurale

title: Negligible Impact of Mass Screening and Treatment on Mesoendemic Malaria Transmission at West Timor in Eastern Indonesia: A Cluster-Randomized Trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment intervention (MST) in humans; phase is not applicable for community-based trials.
comparator: no MST (MST0) versus MST3 and MST2 interventions
population: schoolchildren and community residents in households, microscopy-negative at enrollment
primary_outcome: Incidence density of microscopically patent malaria during 3 months of MST and 3 months following
impact_summary: Two or three rounds of mass screening and treatment over 3 months did not reduce malaria transmission compared to no MST, largely due to high rates of untreated microscopically subpatent infections.
effect_metric: risk ratio for incidence density of microscopically patent malaria
follow_up: 6 months (3 months during MST plus 3 months following)

title: Small-scale field evaluation of push-pull system against early- and outdoor-biting malaria mosquitoes in an area of high pyrethroid resistance in Tanzania.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (cross-over design) with reported efficacy results for a malaria vector-control intervention (push-pull system) against outdoor-biting mosquitoes in humans; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
design: partially randomized cross-over design, small-scale field evaluation
population: adult male volunteers used as mosquito collectors in experimental huts and local houses
primary_outcome: Reduction in mosquito biting rates (outdoor and indoor) comparing push-pull vs control
impact_summary: The push-pull system significantly reduced outdoor-biting of An. arabiensis and Mansonia species and indoor/outdoor biting of An. arabiensis in local households, but had no significant effect on An. funestus or Culex.
effect_estimate: 30% (outdoor, An. arabiensis, huts); 41.5% (Mansonia); 48% (indoor, An. arabiensis, households); 25% (outdoor, An. arabiensis, households)
p_value: p>0.05 for An. funestus and Culex; significant for An. arabiensis and Mansonia (exact p not stated)
transmission_setting: area of high pyrethroid resistance, malaria-endemic
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; involved adult male volunteers as human landing catch collectors

title: A Competing-Risk Approach for Modeling Length of Stay in Severe Malaria Patients in South-East Asia and the Implications for Planning of Hospital Services.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results comparing artesunate and quinine for severe malaria treatment in humans; Phase 3 status appropriate.
population: adult severe malaria patients
primary_outcome: Length of stay (time to discharge) and time to death analyzed via competing-risk survival analysis
impact_summary: Compared to quinine, artesunate increased the incidence of discharge and decreased the incidence of death, and conventional Kaplan-Meier analysis overestimated cumulative incidence compared to the competing-risk model.
follow_up: until discharge or death during hospitalisation
transmission_setting: South-East Asia, severe malaria hospitalised patients
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; analysis focused on clinical predictors of length of stay and mortality (low Glasgow coma scale, high blood urea nitrogen, acidotic base excess, shock, coma) rather than adverse events of treatment.

title: Child Health Outcomes After Presumptive Infection Treatment in Pregnant Women: A Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) in pregnant women with reported outcome results on child health.
comparator: 2 doses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (control) versus monthly SP versus monthly SP plus 2 doses of azithromycin
population: pregnant women and their children
primary_outcome: Child height/length, stunting prevalence, and mortality through 60 months; development at 60 months
impact_summary: Provision of monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus azithromycin during pregnancy reduced childhood stunting, improved child development scores, and may have reduced postneonatal mortality compared with standard 2-dose SP.
effect_metric: hazard ratio for 5-year cumulative incidence of stunting
age_range: children followed from 1 to 60 months; mothers were pregnant women

title: Exploring the impact of house screening intervention on entomological indices and incidence of malaria in Arba Minch town, southwest Ethiopia: A randomized control trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on a malaria vector-control intervention (house screening) in humans; phase not applicable for non-pharmaceutical trial.
population: household members in Arba Minch Town, including 477 participants followed for clinical malaria
primary_outcome: Indoor density of malaria vector (An. arabiensis) and incidence of clinical malaria (P. falciparum)
impact_summary: House screening with wire mesh on doors and windows reduced indoor vector density by 48% and reduced the incidence of P. falciparum malaria by 61% compared to unscreened control houses.
effect_metric: protective efficacy (incidence of P. falciparum infection)
transmission_setting: endemic, urban/peri-urban setting in southwest Ethiopia
safety_summary: Not explicitly reported; intervention was well-accepted with high durability (97.9% screened windows and 63.8% screened doors intact after 11 months); no adverse events mentioned.

title: Chitinase-3-like 1 is a biomarker of acute kidney injury and mortality in paediatric severe malaria.
screening_reason: Secondary analysis of a completed RCT evaluating inhaled nitric oxide for severe malaria in children with reported outcome results (mortality and biomarker findings); malaria is the primary focus and phase is not early-phase.
population: children aged 1-10 years with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Association of plasma CHI3L1 levels with acute kidney injury and mortality in paediatric severe malaria
impact_summary: Elevated plasma CHI3L1 levels were associated with acute kidney injury and were an independent risk factor for in-hospital and 6-month mortality in children with severe malaria.
effect_metric: relative risk (in-hospital death, per log CHI3L1)
p_value: 0.015 (in-hospital death); 0.003 (6-month mortality); 0.012 (iNO effect on CHI3L1 recovery); <0.0001 (AKI association)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic Uganda, hospital-based cohort of severe malaria cases
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; treatment with inhaled nitric oxide was associated with delayed CHI3L1 recovery but overall safety of iNO not detailed in this secondary analysis.

title: Safety and Immunogenicity of GSK Biologicals' Malaria Vaccine 257049 When Administered on 7 Schedules to African Infants
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (safety and immunogenicity data) testing an RTS,S malaria vaccine in a malaria prevention context.
interventions_raw: GSK Biological's Investigational Malaria Vaccine 257049; Engerix-B; Tritanrix HepB Hib; BCG; OPV; Rouvax
comparator: control group without RTS,S/AS01E (standard EPI schedule) / active comparator across different vaccination schedules
population: neonates and infants aged 1 to 7 days at enrollment, followed to 18 months
primary_outcome: Number of Subjects Reported With Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
impact_summary: Initiating RTS,S/AS01E vaccination after 6 weeks of age (e.g., 10-, 14- and 26-week schedule) improved anti-CS antibody responses compared with the standard 6-, 10-, 14-week schedule, while neonatal vaccination was well tolerated but produced a lower immune response.
safety_summary: No causally related serious adverse events reported; higher frequency of fever within 7 days of RTS,S/AS01E vaccination compared with control; neonatal vaccination was well tolerated.

title: Impact of treatment and re-treatment with artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine on selection of Plasmodium falciparum multidrug resistance gene-1 polymorphisms in the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcomes on artemisinin-based antimalarial treatment for malaria in humans (children with P. falciparum infections); published results analyzing treatment efficacy and drug-resistance selection.
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Uganda
population: children aged 12-59 months with P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Selection of Pfmdr1 polymorphisms (N86Y, Y184F, D1246Y) pre- and post-treatment/re-treatment with AL or ASAQ
impact_summary: Treatment and re-treatment with AL or ASAQ had limited impact on selection of Pfmdr1 variants and haplotypes associated with partner drug resistance, though Pfmdr1 86Y was associated with reduced risk of AL treatment failure.
effect_metric: Risk ratio (RR) for AL treatment failure associated with Pfmdr1 86Y allele

title: A randomized, control and comparative study of polyherbal formulation use for Malaria (Plasmodium falciparum).
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (Malarina vs. Quinine) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in humans.
population: Patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Resolution of malaria signs and symptoms
impact_summary: Malarina, a polyherbal formulation, was as effective as Quinine Bisulphate in treating malaria symptoms and was safe and well tolerated.
safety_summary: Malarina was safe and well tolerated in all patients.

title: Efficacy and safety of artemisinin-based combination therapy and chloroquine with concomitant primaquine to treat Plasmodium vivax malaria in Brazil: an open label randomized clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment interventions (artemisinin combinations and chloroquine with primaquine) in humans; primary purpose is malaria treatment in endemic setting.
comparator: chloroquine plus primaquine vs two fixed-dose artemisinin-based combination therapies plus primaquine (active comparator)
population: patients with Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Cure rate (proportion achieving parasitological cure) at day 28/42/63, with objective of establishing whether cure rates above 90% could be achieved in each arm
impact_summary: All three treatment regimens (two ACTs and chloroquine, each with primaquine) achieved cure rates above 90% at 28 and 42 days, meeting WHO efficacy criteria, though rates dropped below 90% by day 63 with confidence intervals still including 90%.
effect_ci: 95% CI included 90% for all three treatments at day 63
safety_summary: Most adverse events were mild across all treatment arms; only one of three serious adverse events was treatment-related; significant drops in haemoglobin were rare.

title: Prospective Clinical Trial Assessing Species-Specific Efficacy of Artemether-Lumefantrine for the Treatment of Plasmodium malariae, Plasmodium ovale, and Mixed Plasmodium Malaria in Gabon.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment with reported outcome results (ACPR efficacy at days 28 and 42); phase not stated but treatment trial is not early-phase.
design: prospective, single-arm, open-label, phase clinical trial
population: patients with uncomplicated P. malariae or P. ovale monoinfections or mixed Plasmodium infections
primary_outcome: Per-protocol PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on days 28 and 42
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine showed high per-protocol efficacy (90-100%) against P. malariae, P. ovale curtisi, P. ovale wallikeri, and mixed Plasmodium infections without major safety concerns.
safety_summary: Study drug-related adverse events were generally mild or moderate, without evident tolerability or safety concerns.

title: "We were being treated like the Queen": understanding trial factors influencing high paediatric malaria treatment adherence in western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment intervention (SMS reminders for artemether-lumefantrine adherence) in humans with reported outcome results (97% adherence rates).
design: randomized controlled trial (original trial); qualitative follow-up with focus group discussions
population: caregivers of children treated for malaria with artemether-lumefantrine
primary_outcome: Adherence to artemether-lumefantrine dosing
impact_summary: Both SMS reminder intervention and control arms achieved over 97% adherence to artemether-lumefantrine, and qualitative follow-up identified quality of care and trial procedures as key contributors to high adherence.

title: Intravenous artesunate plus Artemisnin based Combination Therapy (ACT) or intravenous quinine plus ACT for treatment of severe malaria in Ugandan children: a randomized controlled clinical trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (intravenous artesunate/quinine plus ACT) in humans with reported 42-day parasitological outcome results; not early-phase.
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: 42-day parasitological outcome (parasite clearance and treatment failure)
impact_summary: Intravenous artesunate led to faster parasite clearance than intravenous quinine, but both arms had high rates of parasitological treatment failure at 42 days, mostly due to re-infection rather than recrudescence.
safety_summary: Adverse events were of mild to moderate severity and consistent with malaria symptoms.

title: Factors contributing to anaemia after uncomplicated falciparum malaria in under five year-old Nigerian children ten years following adoption of artemisinin-based combination therapies as first-line antimalarials.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of three artemisinin-based combination therapies in under-five Nigerian children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria that has reported outcome results on anaemia and haematocrit changes.
comparator: active comparator (three ACT regimens compared to each other)
population: children under 5 years with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Factors/predictors contributing to anaemia (pre-treatment anaemia, early appearing anaemia, malaria-attributable and drug-attributable falls in haematocrit) following ACT treatment
impact_summary: Ten years after ACT adoption, anaemia remains common before and shortly after treatment in Nigerian children, with drug-attributable falls in haematocrit >4% being common and significantly lower in anaemic compared to non-anaemic children.
effect_metric: half-time of decline in drug-attributable fall in haematocrit deficits
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on haematological changes rather than adverse events

title: Inhibition of merozoite invasion and transient de-sequestration by sevuparin in humans with Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes in P. falciparum malaria patients receiving a novel antimalarial intervention (sevuparin) alongside standard treatment.
population: patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Safety, tolerability, and effect on circulating parasite (merozoite/ring-stage/trophozoite) numbers after sevuparin infusion
impact_summary: A single sevuparin infusion was safe and well tolerated, decreased circulating ring-stage infected erythrocytes, and caused transient appearance of mature-stage infected erythrocytes in the circulation, indicating inhibition of merozoite invasion and transient de-sequestration.
age_range: adult male volunteers and malaria patients
safety_summary: Sevuparin was found safe and well tolerated in both healthy volunteers (phase I) and malaria patients (phase I/II).

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of introducing malaria diagnostic testing in drug shops: A cluster-randomised trial in Uganda.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing malaria diagnostic intervention (mRDTs) in humans with primary focus on malaria.
population: drug shop customers with fever
primary_outcome: proportion of customers with fever appropriately treated of malaria with ACT
impact_summary: Introduction of mRDTs in drug shops improved malaria diagnosis and appropriate treatment with ACTs, at low incremental health sector cost but higher household costs compared to presumptive diagnosis.
effect_metric: incremental cost per patient appropriately treated of malaria

title: Impact of insecticide resistance in Anopheles arabiensis on malaria incidence and prevalence in Sudan and the costs of mitigation.
journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria incidence over 3 years) evaluating vector-control interventions (LLINs and IRS) for malaria prevention in humans.
population: children aged 1 to <10 years in cohorts monitored for malaria incidence
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence monitored through active case detection in cohorts of children aged 1 to <10 years
impact_summary: IRS with deltamethrin provided no additional protection against malaria compared to LLINs alone, while IRS with bendiocarb showed some evidence of additional protection.
effect_metric: incidence rate ratio (interaction IRR for LLIN+IRS vs LLIN alone by insecticide)
transmission_setting: pyrethroid-resistant and carbamate-susceptible Anopheles arabiensis malaria vector setting

title: A Randomized Trial Evaluating the Prophylactic Activity of DSM265 Against Preerythrocytic Plasmodium falciparum Infection During Controlled Human Malarial Infection by Mosquito Bites and Direct Venous Inoculation.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria chemoprevention drug (DSM265) with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in humans.
population: healthy adult volunteers undergoing controlled human malarial infection
primary_outcome: time to development of parasitemia (qRT-PCR positivity) after controlled human malarial infection
impact_summary: DSM265 given 3 or 7 days before controlled human malarial infection was safe and well tolerated, delayed time to parasitemia compared with placebo, but sterilely protected only one third of participants.
safety_summary: DSM265-related adverse events consisted of mild-to-moderate headache and gastrointestinal symptoms; drug was safe and well tolerated.

title: A village level cluster-randomized entomological evaluation of combination long-lasting insecticidal nets containing pyrethroid plus PBO synergist in Southern Mali.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported entomological outcome results evaluating combination LLINs as malaria vector control intervention.
comparator: mono-treated pyrethroid LLINs (permethrin alone, deltamethrin alone)
population: villages with indoor-resting Anopheles mosquito populations exposed to pyrethroid-resistant vectors
primary_outcome: Anopheles indoor resting density, host preference, vector longevity (parity), and sporozoite rates measured every 2 months
impact_summary: Deltamethrin+PBO LLINs showed lower Anopheles gambiae s.l. sporozoite rates than deltamethrin-only LLINs during high transmission seasons, but no significant difference overall in sporozoite rate, and no reduction in indoor resting density or parity rates; permethrin+PBO showed no improvement over permethrin alone.
effect_estimate: 3.97% (deltamethrin) vs 3.04% (deltamethrin+PBO) overall; 3.70% vs 1.95% during high transmission season
transmission_setting: seasonal, high malaria transmission rainy season

title: Chloroquine-Primaquine versus Chloroquine Alone to Treat Vivax Malaria in Afghanistan: An Open Randomized Superiority Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine±primaquine for P. vivax) with reported outcome results (recurrence rates at 1-year follow-up); adequate phase; human malaria is the primary focus.
design: open-label, randomized controlled trial, superiority, phase 3
population: patients aged 6 months and older with microscopy confirmed P. vivax infection, G6PD normal in CQ+PQ group
primary_outcome: P. vivax recurrence assessed by survival analysis over one year follow-up
impact_summary: Adding primaquine to chloroquine significantly reduced P. vivax recurrence compared to chloroquine alone, with greatest protection in the first 6 months.
safety_summary: Five of seven hospitalized patients had possible PQ-related hemolysis and PQ was stopped in six more, but none had hemoglobin fall ≥2 g/dL or below 7 g/dL; no Mediterranean variant G6PD deficiency detected by genotyping.

title: Efficacy of intermittent preventive treatment and insecticide treated nets on malaria parasitaemia in pregnancy among Igbo women in southeastern Nigeria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention interventions (IPTp-SP and insecticide-treated nets) in pregnant women with measured parasitaemia outcomes.
population: pregnant women (Igbo women)
primary_outcome: Prevalence of malaria parasitaemia in pregnancy
impact_summary: Use of IPT-SP alone or combined with ITN was associated with significantly reduced malaria parasitaemia prevalence in pregnant women compared to no intervention.
transmission_setting: tropical, malaria-endemic region of southeastern Nigeria

title: Cost-effectiveness of artemisinin-naphthoquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria in Papua New Guinean children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment interventions (artemisinin-naphthoquine vs artemether-lumefantrine) with reported outcome results in human participants.
design: open-label, randomized, parallel-group, phase 3, cost-effectiveness analysis
population: children aged 0.5-5.9 years with Plasmodium falciparum and/or Plasmodium vivax infections
primary_outcome: Incremental cost per incremental treatment success by Day 42 and cost per life year saved
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine was more effective than artemether-lumefantrine for treating uncomplicated malaria in PNG children but was more costly, making it potentially not cost-effective at current prices.
effect_estimate: $10.46 (falciparum), $14.83 (vivax) higher cost per treatment success for AN vs AL; $12,165 (girls) and $12,469 (boys) cost per life year saved
transmission_setting: Papua New Guinea, endemic for both P. falciparum and P. vivax

title: Impact of a malaria intervention package in schools on Plasmodium infection, anaemia and cognitive function in schoolchildren in Mali: a pragmatic cluster-randomised trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing malaria interventions (nets, education, intermittent parasite clearance) in schoolchildren, meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: primary schoolchildren, longitudinal cohort aged 9-12 years, cross-sectional surveys in all classes
primary_outcome: Plasmodium infection, anaemia and cognitive function (sustained attention, visual search, numeracy, vocabulary and writing)
impact_summary: A school-based malaria intervention package including LLINs, education and intermittent parasite clearance (IPCs) dramatically reduced malaria parasitaemia and gametocyte carriage, decreased anaemia, and improved sustained attention in schoolchildren.

title: γδ T Cells Are Required for the Induction of Sterile Immunity during Irradiated Sporozoite Vaccinations.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (PfSPZ) in humans with reported outcome results (protection from P. falciparum infection).
population: malaria-naive individuals and malaria-endemic population vaccinees; mouse model
primary_outcome: Protection from Plasmodium falciparum infection following PfSPZ Vaccine
impact_summary: γδ T cells are required for the induction of sterile immunity following irradiated sporozoite (PfSPZ) vaccination, acting through support of CD8α+ dendritic cell accumulation and protective CD8 T cell responses.

title: Safety and effectiveness of mass drug administration to accelerate elimination of artemisinin-resistant falciparum malaria: A pilot trial in four villages of Eastern Myanmar.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (two intervention, two control villages) with reported outcome results evaluating mass drug administration for malaria elimination in humans.
design: pilot trial, non-randomized, controlled (two intervention villages received MDA, two control villages followed pre-MDA)
comparator: control villages without MDA (LLINs and EDT only)
population: residents of villages with ≥30% malaria prevalence
primary_outcome: Malaria prevalence assessed by ultrasensitive PCR quarterly for 24 months
impact_summary: MDA with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine and single low-dose primaquine was safe and reduced asymptomatic P. falciparum prevalence and anopheline vector positivity, though the effect on prevalence was not sustained beyond three months and symptomatic incidence was unchanged.
transmission_setting: Greater Mekong Sub-region, artemisinin-resistant falciparum malaria endemic villages
safety_summary: MDA was well tolerated with no serious adverse events; mild to moderate adverse events reported in 5.6% (212/3931) of interviews.

title: Assessment of Efficacy and Safety of Arterolane Maleate-Piperaquine Phosphate Dispersible Tablets in Comparison With Artemether-Lumefantrine Dispersible Tablets in Pediatric Patients With Acute Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria: A Phase 3, Randomized, Multicenter Trial in India and Africa.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published Phase 3 RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes for malaria treatment in children, comparing two ACT regimens.
population: pediatric patients aged 6 months to 12 years with acute uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (cure rate) at day 28
impact_summary: Arterolane maleate-piperaquine phosphate dispersible tablets showed efficacy and safety comparable to artemether-lumefantrine in treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic regions of India and Africa
safety_summary: Both treatments were safe and well tolerated with a similar overall safety profile.

title: A Molecular Assay to Quantify Male and Female Plasmodium falciparum Gametocytes: Results From 2 Randomized Controlled Trials Using Primaquine for Gametocyte Clearance.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing primaquine-based chemoprevention strategies for malaria transmission reduction in humans with reported outcome results.
population: Individuals with P. falciparum gametocytemia treated for malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte sex ratio and density in relation to time since treatment and mosquito infectivity
impact_summary: Primaquine's early sterilizing effect on P. falciparum infectivity does not appear to be explained by preferential clearance of male gametocytes, but may instead relate to effects on gametocyte fitness.
effect_estimate: Females: 0.05% (IQR 0.0-0.7%); Males: 3.4% (IQR 0.4-32.9%) of baseline at day 7 in Kenya
transmission_setting: Malaria-endemic settings in Kenya and Mali

title: Studies of a Candidate Aminoquinoline Antimalarial (AQ-13)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (AQ-13 vs artemether-lumefantrine) with reported outcome results on cure rates.
interventions_raw: AQ-13 Treatment; Coartem Treatment
population: adult Malian men (≥18 years) with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Cure Rates of AQ-13 and Coartem for Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria in Adult Malian Males.
impact_summary: AQ-13 showed similar cure rates to artemether plus lumefantrine in the per-protocol analysis (meeting non-inferiority), but the intention-to-treat analysis did not meet the non-inferiority criterion, though no AQ-13 treatment failures occurred.
follow_up: 6 weeks (1 week inpatient plus 5 weeks outpatient)
safety_summary: No serious adverse events (grade 2-4); 453 less-severe adverse events (≤grade 1) reported, 214 in combination group and 239 in AQ-13 group.

title: RTS,S/AS01E Malaria Vaccine Induces Memory and Polyfunctional T Cell Responses in a Pediatric African Phase III Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine in pediatric African population with reported immunological outcome results from Phase III trial.
population: children (pediatric participants)
primary_outcome: Frequency and polyfunctionality of CSP- and HBsAg-specific CD4+ T cell responses measured by intracellular cytokine staining before and 1 month after primary vaccination
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01E vaccination induced significantly higher frequencies of polyfunctional CSP- and HBsAg-specific CD4+ T cells producing multiple cytokines compared to baseline and to rabies-vaccinated controls.

title: Comparison of effectiveness of two different artemisinin-based combination therapies in an area with high seasonal transmission of malaria in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results (cure rates with PCR adjustment).
population: Patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria recruited all year round
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted cure rate (treatment outcome) at Day 28, assessed by season of recruitment
impact_summary: Cure rates for both Artemether-Lumefantrine and Artesunate-Amodiaquine were higher during the dry season than the rainy season, largely due to a higher incidence of new infections (reinfections) during the rainy season.
transmission_setting: high seasonal malaria transmission (Sahelian, rainy vs dry season) in Nanoro, Burkina Faso

title: RTS,S/AS01 Malaria Vaccine Efficacy is Not Modified by Seasonal Precipitation: Results from a Phase 3 Randomized Controlled Trial in Malawi.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT with reported outcome results (clinical malaria episodes) testing RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in humans.
population: children (5-17 months) and infants (6-12 weeks)
primary_outcome: episodes of clinical malaria
impact_summary: Increased rainfall was associated with higher malaria rates, but there was no evidence that seasonal precipitation modified RTS,S/AS01 vaccine efficacy.
effect_metric: rate ratio for malaria per 1-inch increase in monthly rainfall

title: Preliminary efficacy investigations of oral fipronil against Anopheles arabiensis when administered to Zebu cattle (Bos indicus) under field conditions.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector control intervention (fipronil treatment of cattle to reduce Anopheles arabiensis density and sporozoite rates) in humans' living environment.
comparator: untreated control plots (cattle not treated with fipronil)
population: cattle (Zebu, Bos indicus) and indoor-resting Anopheles mosquitoes in sleeping huts
primary_outcome: Indoor resting density of Anopheles arabiensis (and other anopheline species) post-treatment
impact_summary: Oral fipronil treatment of cattle significantly reduced indoor resting density of Anopheles arabiensis in treatment plots compared to control plots, though effects on An. gambiae s.s. were not significant and An. funestus s.s. density increased over time.
transmission_setting: rural, active malaria transmission area in Western Kenya
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Effects of liver-stage clearance by Primaquine on gametocyte carriage of Plasmodium vivax and P. falciparum.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing primaquine for malaria prevention/treatment in humans with measured gametocyte carriage endpoints.
population: children
primary_outcome: Gametocyte carriage (Pv and Pf) after radical cure, detected by quantitative RT-PCR targeting pvs25 and pfs25
impact_summary: Primaquine treatment reduced the incidence of P. vivax gametocytes by 73%, but had no effect on gametocyte density or proportion of infections carrying gametocytes, and relapses contributed substantially to ongoing P. vivax gametocyte carriage.
effect_metric: percent reduction in incidence of Pv gametocytes
p_value: p<0.001 (for odds of gametocytes in mixed vs single-species infections)

title: Mass Azithromycin and Malaria Parasitemia in Niger: Results from a Community-Randomized Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community-randomized trial with reported outcome results (malaria parasitemia prevalence) testing azithromycin as a malaria intervention; cluster-randomized design is eligible; phase not applicable for community-level intervention.
population: children in trachoma trial communities
primary_outcome: malaria parasitemia prevalence measured during high-transmission season after 3 years of intervention
impact_summary: Additional mass azithromycin distributions during the low-transmission season did not significantly reduce malaria parasitemia prevalence or parasite density compared with annual mass azithromycin alone after 3 years.
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission with high- and low-transmission seasons

title: Haemoglobin changes and risk of anaemia following treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in sub-Saharan Africa.
screening_reason: Individual-patient data analysis of nine randomized controlled trials of malaria treatment in humans with reported outcome results on haemoglobin changes and anaemia risk.
design: individual-patient data pooled analysis of randomized controlled trials, mixed effect models
comparator: non-ACT (comparison between ACT and non-ACT treatments)
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, mostly children under 5 years old
primary_outcome: Change in haemoglobin concentration and risk of anaemia following treatment
impact_summary: Most patients experienced an early drop in haemoglobin after treatment start followed by a linear recovery through day 28, with the degree of the early dip determined by pre-treatment parasitaemia and parasite clearance rate rather than the specific treatment used.
effect_estimate: -12.8% nadir drop in under 5s (day 0 to ~35h); +13.8% increase from baseline by day 28
safety_summary: Severe anaemia (<5 g/dl) occurred in 2 per 1000 patients and was transient, with recovery by day 14 except one case of very severe anaemia associated with parasite recurrence at day 28; no case of delayed anaemia and no systematic difference in Hb concentrations between treatments.

title: Safety and Efficacy of Adding a Single Low Dose of Primaquine to the Treatment of Adult Patients With Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Senegal, to Reduce Gametocyte Carriage: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (primaquine added to ACTs) with reported outcome results (hemoglobin change, gametocyte carriage, adverse events) in adults with P. falciparum malaria.
population: Adults with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Change in hemoglobin concentration at day 7
impact_summary: Adding a single low dose of primaquine to ACT substantially reduced gametocyte carriage but caused a greater drop in hemoglobin among G6PD-deficient patients.
safety_summary: Primaquine was associated with a greater fall in hemoglobin in G6PD-deficient patients (0.63 g/dL greater drop), one G6PD-normal patient developed moderately severe anemia (Hb <8 g/dL), and dark urine was more frequent among primaquine recipients.

title: Single dose primaquine to reduce gametocyte carriage and Plasmodium falciparum transmission in Cambodia: An open-label randomized trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing primaquine as a malaria transmission-blocking intervention in humans.
population: Cambodian adults with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Infectiousness to Anopheles dirus mosquitoes via membrane-feeding assay and gametocyte carriage measured by microscopy and RT-PCR
impact_summary: A single 45mg dose of primaquine added to DHP rapidly and significantly reduced gametocytemia compared to DHP alone, which failed to reduce gametocytemia and prevent transmission to mosquitoes.
effect_estimate: primaquine group gametocyte-free by day 14; significantly less likely to harbor gametocytes by day 7 vs DHP-alone

title: Predicting RTS,S Vaccine-Mediated Protection from Transcriptomes in a Malaria-Challenge Clinical Trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT of RTS,S malaria vaccine in humans with reported efficacy results from controlled human malaria infection challenge.
design: controlled human malaria infection challenge trial
population: healthy adults
primary_outcome: Protection from controlled human malaria infection (CHMI) as predicted by transcriptomic signatures
impact_summary: Transcriptome analysis identified NF-κB and IFN-γ signaling pathway genes that predict RTS,S vaccine-mediated protection against controlled human malaria infection.

title: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine versus artesunate-amodiaquine for treatment of malaria infection in pregnancy in Ghana: an open-label, randomised, non-inferiority trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results comparing two antimalarial treatments for malaria in pregnancy; meets all inclusion criteria.
population: second/third trimester pregnant women with confirmed asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum parasitaemia
primary_outcome: Parasitological efficacy (PE) by days 28 and 42 (co-primary outcomes)
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was non-inferior to artesunate-amodiaquine for treating malaria infection in pregnancy, with fewer adverse events and no safety concerns.
effect_metric: adjusted difference in parasitological efficacy (DHA-PPQ minus ASAQ)
safety_summary: Both drugs were well-tolerated; DHA-PPQ recipients had fewer adverse events of vomiting, dizziness, and general weakness compared to ASAQ; no excess of adverse birth outcomes.

title: Effect of IPTp on Plasmodium falciparum antibody levels among pregnant women and their babies in a sub-urban coastal area in Ghana.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of IPTp-SP chemoprevention in pregnant women with reported outcome results on malaria antibody levels and infant malaria incidence.
population: pregnant women and their infants
primary_outcome: Anti-Plasmodium falciparum IgG and IgM antibody levels (against crude antigen and GLURP) measured over time
impact_summary: IPTp-SP was associated with a decline in antibody levels from enrolment to delivery and may have reduced malaria exposure, but this did not affect antibody transfer to the fetus or protection of infants from clinical malaria at 6 months.
safety_summary: Children did not show clinical signs of malaria at 6 months after birth; no adverse implications on malaria observed among the children.

title: Comparative analysis of the safety and tolerability of fixed-dose artesunate/amodiaquine versus artemether/lumefantrine combinations for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in pregnancy: a randomized open label study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artemisinin-based combinations for malaria treatment in pregnancy with reported safety and tolerability outcomes.
comparator: artemether/lumefantrine (active comparator); nonpregnant and nonmalarious pregnant controls
population: pregnant women in second and third trimester with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, plus nonpregnant and nonmalarious pregnant controls
primary_outcome: Safety and tolerability of AA versus AL, including liver enzyme levels and adverse event rates
impact_summary: Both artesunate/amodiaquine and artemether/lumefantrine were well-tolerated and safe in the second and third trimester of pregnancy, though adverse event rate was higher with AA (70%) than AL (10%) and mild, non-clinically significant elevations in liver enzymes occurred.
safety_summary: Elevated alkaline phosphatase in AA and AL groups compared to nonpregnant controls, and elevated ALT/AST in AL versus AA group, but changes were within normal range for pregnancy and not clinically significant; adverse events more frequent in AA group (70%) than AL group (10%), but drugs were well tolerated overall.

title: Artemisinin-based combination therapy in pregnant women in Zambia: efficacy, safety and risk of recurrent malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes comparing three ACT regimens in pregnant women with malaria, a primary malaria intervention in humans.
comparator: active comparator (three ACT regimens compared: AL vs MQAS vs DHAPQ)
population: pregnant women in second or third trimester with malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted treatment failure and risk of recurrent malaria (re-infection) during follow-up
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine had the lowest treatment failure and re-infection rates compared to artemether-lumefantrine and mefloquine-artesunate, making it preferable in high-transmission settings.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted treatment failure rate / hazard ratio for re-infection
effect_estimate: AL 4.7%, MQAS 1.3%, DHAPQ 0.8%; HR for re-infection AL 4.71, MQAS 1.59 (vs DHAPQ)
p_value: 0.01 (AL vs DHAPQ); 0.03 (AL vs MQAS); <0.01 (AL HR); 0.04 (MQAS HR)
follow_up: 63 days active follow-up, then at delivery and 1 year post-delivery
age_range: pregnant women, including subgroup under 20 years old
safety_summary: All three treatments were generally well tolerated; dizziness, nausea, vomiting, headache and asthenia were more common with MQAS than AL or DHAPQ (p<0.001); birth outcomes did not differ significantly between arms.

title: Safety and efficacy of the choline analogue SAR97276 for malaria treatment: results of two phase 2, open-label, multicenter trials in African patients.
screening_reason: Published results from two phase 2 randomized controlled trials assessing safety and efficacy of SAR97276A for malaria treatment in humans, with reported outcome data on cure rates and clinical endpoints.
place: Burkina Faso, Gabon, Benin, Tanzania, Kenya
countries: Benin; Burkina Faso; Gabon; Kenya; Tanzania
population: African adults and children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Efficacy (cure rate) of SAR97276A for treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria
impact_summary: SAR97276A monotherapy showed insufficient efficacy compared to artemether-lumefantrine and was not further developed for malaria treatment, though it was generally well tolerated.
effect_estimate: Adults IM single dose 59%, IV single dose 77%, 3-day IM adults 90%, 3-day IM children 68%; Study 2 teenagers required rescue therapy in 8/8 (once daily) and 5/8 (twice daily) vs 4/4 cured with artemether-lumefantrine
age_range: adults and children (Study 1); teenagers and children planned (Study 2)
safety_summary: SAR97276A was generally well tolerated in both studies, with an overall good safety profile despite lack of efficacy.

title: Cost-effectiveness analysis of malaria rapid diagnostic tests for appropriate treatment of malaria at the community level in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (appropriate treatment rates) testing malaria rapid diagnostic tests, a diagnostic intervention for malaria in humans.
design: randomised controlled trial, cost-effectiveness analysis, two-site comparison
comparator: presumptive diagnosis and treatment by CHWs (control arm)
population: children under 5 with fever
primary_outcome: proportion of children with fever appropriately treated for malaria with ACT
impact_summary: Use of mRDTs by CHWs improved appropriate treatment of malaria with ACT and was cost-effective in the moderate-to-high transmission area, but was a higher-cost, less cost-effective intervention in the low transmission area.
effect_metric: incremental cost per appropriately treated child (health sector perspective)
effect_estimate: US$3.0 (moderate-to-high transmission area); US$13.3 (low transmission area)
transmission_setting: two areas of moderate-to-high and low malaria transmission in rural Uganda

title: The impact of an intervention to introduce malaria rapid diagnostic tests on fever case management in a high transmission setting in Uganda: A mixed-methods cluster-randomized trial (PRIME).
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria diagnostic intervention (mRDTs) for fever case management in a high-transmission human population.
comparator: standard care (control health centers without the intervention)
population: children under five years with fever attending public health centers, and health workers
primary_outcome: Inappropriate treatment of malaria, defined as the proportion of febrile children not treated according to guidelines based on reference mRDT result
impact_summary: The PRIME intervention using mRDTs did not significantly reduce inappropriate treatment of malaria compared to control health centers.
follow_up: 3 rounds of interviews over the study period (2010-13)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on appropriateness of antimalarial treatment rather than adverse events.

title: Efficacy of phase 3 trial of RTS, S/AS01 malaria vaccine: The need for an alternative development plan.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT of RTS,S malaria vaccine with reported efficacy results; primary purpose is malaria prevention via vaccination.
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine showed relatively little efficacy in the phase III trial and will not meet the goal of malaria eradication by itself.

title: Acceptability of insecticide-treated clothing for malaria prevention among migrant rubber tappers in Myanmar: a cluster-randomized non-inferiority crossover trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported acceptability outcomes; malaria prevention via insecticide-treated clothing is the primary purpose; phase not early-stage.
population: migrant rubber tappers
primary_outcome: Acceptability of insecticide-treated clothing (ITC) compared to untreated clothing across multiple perception indicators
impact_summary: ITC was found to be non-inferior to untreated clothing on seven out of eight acceptability indicators, with high overall acceptability among migrant rubber tappers.

title: The effect of price on demand for and use of bednets: evidence from a randomized experiment in Madagascar.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating insecticide-treated bednets (a malaria prevention intervention) with reported outcome results on demand and use.
comparator: varying price levels (subsidized to full price) for ITNs
population: households eligible for insecticide-treated bednet distribution
primary_outcome: demand for and use (effective coverage) of insecticide-treated bednets (ITNs)
impact_summary: Increasing the price of ITNs by $0.55 significantly reduced both demand and effective coverage by 23.1 percentage points.
effect_metric: percentage point change in demand and effective coverage per $0.55 price increase

title: Early rising asexual parasitaemia in Nigerian children following a first dose of artemisinin-based combination treatments of falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three ACT regimens in children with acute falciparum malaria that has reported detailed outcome results on parasitaemia kinetics and other endpoints.
comparator: active comparator (three ACT regimens compared to each other)
population: children with acute falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Occurrence and kinetics of early rising asexual parasitaemia (ERAP) within 8 h of treatment initiation
impact_summary: ERAP occurred in about half of children treated with ACTs and appears to result from rapid mobilization of parasites from deep tissue following the first dose, with retained parasites subsequently eliminated.
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on parasitaemia kinetics rather than adverse events.

title: Efficacy of text-message reminders on paediatric malaria treatment adherence and their post-treatment return to health facilities in Kenya: a randomized controlled trial.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcomes testing an intervention (SMS reminders) to improve malaria treatment adherence in children with uncomplicated malaria in Kenya.
population: children below five years of age with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: adherence to medication (artemether-lumefantrine) and return to health facility on day 3
impact_summary: SMS reminders significantly increased post-treatment return to the health facility on day 3 and day 28, but had no significant effect on adherence to artemether-lumefantrine, which was already high in both groups.
effect_metric: odds ratio for return to facility on day 3

title: Vitamin A and Zinc Supplementation Among Pregnant Women to Prevent Placental Malaria: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial in Tanzania.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention (placental malaria) through vitamin A and zinc supplementation in pregnant women.
population: HIV-negative primigravid or secundigravid pregnant women in first trimester
primary_outcome: Placental malaria infection (past or current) assessed via placental samples at delivery
impact_summary: Zinc supplementation reduced the risk of histopathology-positive placental malaria, but neither vitamin A nor zinc affected PCR-positive malaria, small for gestational age births, or prematurity.
safety_summary: No safety concerns were identified.

title: Efficacy and safety of intermittent preventive treatment in schoolchildren with sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine (SP) and SP plus piperaquine in Democratic Republic of the Congo: a randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (IPTsc) in schoolchildren with reported efficacy and safety outcomes.
population: schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Haemoglobin (Hb) change
impact_summary: SP plus piperaquine (SP/PQ) significantly increased haemoglobin and reduced anaemia, malaria parasitaemia and clinical malaria compared to control, while SP alone showed smaller and mostly non-significant effects.
effect_metric: Hb change (g/dL) and percentage reduction in anaemia/parasitaemia/clinical malaria
effect_estimate: SP: Hb +0.20 g/dL; SP/PQ: Hb +0.39 g/dL; SP/PQ reduced anaemia by 28%, parasitaemia by 40%, clinical malaria by 58%
effect_ci: Hb SP: -0.61 to 0.47; Hb SP/PQ: 0.12-0.66; anaemia SP/PQ: 19-37%; parasitaemia SP/PQ: 26-52%; clinical malaria SP/PQ: 17-79%
p_value: Hb SP: P=0.168; Hb SP/PQ: P<0.01; anaemia SP/PQ: P<0.001; parasitaemia SP/PQ: P<0.001; clinical malaria SP/PQ: P<0.01
safety_summary: No deaths or severe adverse events were observed in either treatment arm.

title: Expanding access to parasite-based malaria diagnosis through retail drug shops in Tanzania: evidence from a randomized trial and implications for treatment.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating malaria RDT introduction into retail drug shops; diagnosis is a primary purpose; not early-phase.
comparator: control district (no RDT intervention) and comparison of two different retail price points
population: suspected malaria patients seeking treatment at retail drug shops (ADDOs)
primary_outcome: Proportion of suspected malaria patients receiving pre-treatment parasite-based diagnosis (RDT testing) at ADDOs
impact_summary: Introduction of RDTs into accredited drug dispensing outlets substantially increased parasite-based malaria diagnosis and improved treatment adherence without requiring a price subsidy.
effect_metric: Percentage point increase in pre-treatment testing
effect_estimate: increase from 0 to 65% of suspected malaria patients tested; overall parasite-based diagnosis increased from 19 to 74% in intervention districts vs 3 to 18% in control district
p_value: 0.03 for prior knowledge of RDT availability; 0.01 for RDT experience
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; adherence data showed 75% of RDT-positive patients received ACT and 3% of RDT-negative patients received ACT, suggesting good adherence to test results.

title: The effect of small solar powered 'Bͻkͻͻ' net fans on mosquito net use: results from a randomized controlled cross-over trial in southern Ghana.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention intervention (improving LLIN use through fans) in humans.
comparator: water filters (active comparator) and standard care/no additional intervention (Group 3)
population: Households in rural communities
primary_outcome: Net use (LLIN usage) measured via mid- and end-point and fortnightly household surveys
impact_summary: Provision of solar-powered net fans appeared to increase net use, but the increase was not statistically significant in the primary ITT or PP analyses; it was significant only in a secondary PP analysis.
effect_estimate: ITT OR 3.24; PP OR 1.17; secondary PP OR 1.95
p_value: ITT p > 0.01; PP p > 0.01; secondary PP p < 0.01
transmission_setting: malaria endemic rural area, Greater Accra, Ghana
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; no adverse events mentioned

title: Fixed-Dose Artesunate-Amodiaquine Combination vs Chloroquine for Treatment of Uncomplicated Blood Stage P. vivax Infection in the Brazilian Amazon: An Open-Label Randomized, Controlled Trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy and safety results comparing an artemisinin-based combination therapy to chloroquine for treatment of uncomplicated P. vivax malaria in humans.
population: patients with uncomplicated blood stage P. vivax infection
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) rate at day 28
impact_summary: Fixed-dose artesunate-amodiaquine was superior to chloroquine in achieving adequate clinical and parasitological responses against P. vivax infection in the Brazilian Amazon.
effect_metric: difference in adjusted-ACPR rate at day 28
transmission_setting: Brazilian Amazon, area with chloroquine-resistant P. vivax
safety_summary: Both treatments had similar safety profiles; at least one emergent adverse event occurred in 41.6% (79/190) of ASAQ group and 44.7% (85/190) of CQ group.

title: Safety, Immunogenicity and Efficacy of Prime-Boost Vaccination with ChAd63 and MVA Encoding ME-TRAP against Plasmodium falciparum Infection in Adults in Senegal.
screening_reason: RCT with reported efficacy results testing a malaria vaccine (ChAd63/MVA ME-TRAP prime-boost) as primary intervention in humans; not early-phase safety-only study.
population: healthy male adults living in a malaria endemic area
primary_outcome: Time-to-infection with P. falciparum malaria, determined by two consecutive positive PCR results
impact_summary: The ChAd63-MVA ME-TRAP prime-boost vaccine was safe and immunogenic but did not show protective efficacy against P. falciparum infection compared to controls.
effect_estimate: no significant efficacy observed (12/57 vaccinees vs 13/58 controls PCR positive)
safety_summary: Vaccine was safe and induced significant cellular immunogenicity (peak T-cell response of 932 SFC/10^6 PBMC vs 57 SFC/10^6 PBMC in controls); adverse events were monitored with no major safety concerns reported.

title: Reactive Case Detection for Plasmodium vivax Malaria Elimination in Rural Amazonia.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT of a reactive case detection strategy for P. vivax malaria elimination with reported outcome results on parasitemia detection and parasite biomass.
comparator: control households located >5 km away from index cases
population: residents of farming settlements including household and neighbor contacts of malaria index cases
primary_outcome: Proportion of P. vivax infections and parasite biomass detected via reactive case detection using microscopy and qPCR among household, neighbor, and control household members
impact_summary: Household and neighboring household members of index cases were significantly more likely to be parasitemic than control household members, but microscopy-based RCD missed about half of qPCR-detected infections and over a quarter of infections occurred in distant control households, mostly asymptomatic carriers.
effect_estimate: 49.5% of qPCR-detected infections and 76.8% of parasite biomass detected by microscopy-based RCD; 27.6% of qPCR-positive samples from control HHs
transmission_setting: rural Amazon Basin, residual/low transmission approaching elimination
safety_summary: Not reported; observational surveillance study with no intervention safety outcomes

title: Pre-referral Rectal Artesunate Treatment by Community-Based Treatment Providers in Ghana, Guinea-Bissau, Tanzania, and Uganda (Study 18): A Cluster-Randomized Trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (rectal artesunate) in humans across multiple countries; vector-control type trial, phase designation not applicable.
comparator: standard-of-care community health workers (CHW) vs trained mothers (MUMs), traditional healers (THs), and community-chosen personnel (COMs)
population: children under 5 years with febrile illness in villages remote from health facilities
primary_outcome: Coverage of prereferral rectal artesunate treatment among eligible febrile episodes in children under 5, comparing MUM vs CHW villages
impact_summary: Mothers trained to give prereferral rectal artesunate achieved higher treatment coverage than community health workers, but overall treatment access remained low and referral compliance and mortality varied by provider type.
effect_estimate: 1.84 (adjusted for country); 1.67 higher average probability of treatment adjusting for heterogeneity
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic communities remote from health facilities
safety_summary: There were more deaths in the traditional healer (TH) cluster than in other clusters (RR, 2.7 [95% CI, 1.4-5.6]; P = .0040); referral compliance was 81% overall, higher with CHWs (87%) than MUMs (82%).

title: Correction: Safety of Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention (SMC) with Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine plus Amodiaquine when Delivered to Children under 10 Years of Age by District Health Services in Senegal: Results from a Stepped-Wedge Cluster Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomized trial of SMC in children with published outcome results; malaria prevention is the primary purpose.
population: children under 10 years of age

title: Evaluation of long-lasting microbial larvicide for malaria vector control in Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized cluster trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (long-lasting microbial larvicide) with reported outcome results on mosquito density and pupal productivity.
design: randomized cluster trial, semi-natural and natural habitat evaluations
population: Anopheles gambiae larvae and adult mosquito populations in highland and lowland sites
primary_outcome: Reduction in mosquito pupal productivity and adult mosquito density (indoor and outdoor biting)
impact_summary: The FourStar long-lasting biolarvicide briquet formulation significantly reduced mosquito pupal productivity and indoor/outdoor biting adult mosquito densities in western Kenya.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in pupal productivity and adult mosquito density
effect_estimate: 87-98% pupal reduction (semi-natural), 60-100% pupal reduction (natural), 76-82% indoor and 67-75% outdoor adult mosquito density reduction
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic highland and lowland sites in western Kenya with outdoor and indoor transmission

title: Oil-Fortified Maize Porridge Increases Absorption of Lumefantrine in Children with Uncomplicated Falciparum Malaria.
