screening_reason: Published RCT of artemether-lumefantrine (first-line malaria treatment) in children with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with reported pharmacokinetic and parasitological outcomes.
population: children under 5 years with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Lumefantrine exposure till 8 hours after the first dose (AUC0-8 hr)
impact_summary: Oil-fortified maize porridge produced comparable lumefantrine absorption to milk when co-administered with artemether-lumefantrine, suggesting it can be an alternative to milk.
safety_summary: One parasitological failure (day 28 recrudescence) was observed; no other safety issues reported.

title: Using WeChat official accounts to improve malaria health literacy among Chinese expatriates in Niger: an intervention study.
screening_reason: Individually randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (health literacy questionnaire responses and malaria morbidity data) evaluating a malaria prevention intervention (health education via WeChat) in humans.
population: Chinese expatriates working in Niger
primary_outcome: Change in malaria health literacy (knowledge, attitude, practice, skills) from baseline to 4 months post-intervention
impact_summary: WeChat-based health education significantly improved malaria health literacy (knowledge, attitude, practice, skills) among Chinese expatriates compared to controls, and was associated with a decrease in reported malaria morbidity from 23.72% to 15.40%.
effect_estimate: health literacy rates increased from baseline (58.29% skills, 62% knowledge, 54% practice, 34% attitude) to above 70% for all four aspects post-intervention; greater improvement in intervention group vs controls
p_value: p<0.01 (p<0.001 for knowledge, practice, attitude, and correct RDT use)
transmission_setting: non-immune travellers and expatriate workers in malaria-endemic Niger
safety_summary: Not reported (educational intervention, no adverse events reported)

title: Effectiveness of Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention in Children under Ten Years of Age in Senegal: A Stepped-Wedge Cluster-Randomised Trial.
screening_reason: Published stepped-wedge cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating SMC (chemoprevention) effectiveness for malaria prevention in children; not early-phase.
population: children under ten years of age (initially 3-59 months, extended to up to 10 years)
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality
impact_summary: SMC substantially reduced malaria incidence and severe malaria cases in children but showed no significant difference in all-cause mortality; it also reduced malaria incidence among untreated older age groups.
effect_metric: reduction in incidence of confirmed malaria cases (RDT-confirmed)
transmission_setting: highly seasonal malaria transmission, Sahel region
age_range: 3 months to 10 years (children); adults also assessed
safety_summary: SMC was well tolerated with no serious adverse reactions attributable to SMC drugs; vomiting was the most common mild adverse event, reported in less than 1% of treatments.

title: Efficacy and safety of re-treatment with the same artemisinin-based combination treatment (ACT) compared with an alternative ACT and quinine plus clindamycin after failure of first-line recommended ACT (QUINACT): a bicentre, open-label, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Published phase 3 RCT with reported outcome results comparing ACT rescue treatments for malaria treatment failure in children.
place: Democratic Republic of the Congo, Uganda
countries: Democratic Republic of the Congo; Uganda
comparator: alternative ACT and quinine plus clindamycin
population: children aged 12-60 months with recurrent malaria infection after treatment with first-line ACT
primary_outcome: Proportion of patients with adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28, in the per-protocol population
impact_summary: Re-treatment with the same first-line ACT showed similar efficacy (ACPR) to an alternative ACT and to quinine-clindamycin for recurrent uncomplicated malaria.
effect_metric: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic settings in DR Congo and Uganda
safety_summary: No serious adverse events; artemether-lumefantrine was better tolerated than QnC (p=0.0005) and artesunate-amodiaquine (p<0.0001); most common adverse events were anorexia, asthenia, coughing, abnormal behaviour, diarrhoea, and pruritus across groups.
funder: Fonds Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek, Vlaamse Interuniversitaire Raad-Universitaire Ontwikkelings Samenwerking, European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership, and the Belgian Technical Cooperation-Programme d'Etudes et d'Expertises

title: Referral Patterns of Community Health Workers Diagnosing and Treating Malaria: Cluster-Randomized Trials in Two Areas of High- and Low-Malaria Transmission in Southwestern Uganda.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria rapid diagnostic tests versus presumptive diagnosis in community health worker programs, comparing referral patterns in high and low transmission settings in Uganda.
population: children treated by community health workers for suspected malaria
primary_outcome: Referral by community health workers to health centers
impact_summary: Community health workers using malaria rapid diagnostic tests and ACTs referred patients more frequently than those using presumptive diagnosis, but referral advice was not always given even when indicated.
effect_metric: difference in referral frequency between intervention and control arms
p_value: P < 0.001 in both moderate-to-high and low transmission settings
transmission_setting: two areas: moderate-to-high and low malaria transmission

title: Evaluation of SMS reminder messages for altering treatment adherence and health seeking perceptions among malaria care-seekers in Nigeria.
screening_reason: RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment adherence intervention (SMS reminders for RDT-based malaria care) in humans; not early-phase.
population: malaria care-seekers who purchased malaria treatment from drug shops after RDT testing, including adults and sick children
primary_outcome: treatment adherence to RDT results and use of unnecessary anti-malarials
impact_summary: Basic and expanded SMS reminders improved treatment adherence among adults, but the expanded SMS worsened treatment adherence and increased unnecessary anti-malarial use among sick children, and lowered acceptance of drug retailers' administration of RDTs.
effect_estimate: basic SMS adherence OR=1.53 (adults); expanded SMS adherence OR=1.42 (adults); expanded SMS adherence OR=0.26 (children)

title: Communication for behavioural impact in enhancing utilization of insecticide-treated bed nets among mothers of under-five children in rural North Sudan: an experimental study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention intervention (LLIN utilization through behavior change communication) in humans.
population: mothers of under-five children in rural areas
primary_outcome: utilization rate of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs)
impact_summary: The COMBI strategy significantly increased mothers' knowledge, positive attitudes, and utilization of LLINs in intervention villages compared to comparison villages.
transmission_setting: rural, endemic malaria area of Sudan

title: Host Biomarkers Are Associated With Response to Therapy and Long-Term Mortality in Pediatric Severe Malaria.
screening_reason: This is a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial evaluating an adjunctive intervention for severe malaria treatment in children that has reported outcome results.
population: children with severe malaria aged 1-10 years
primary_outcome: biomarker kinetics and association with response to therapy and mortality
impact_summary: Persistent endothelial activation and dysfunction, as reflected by biomarkers such as angiopoietin-2, predict survival and clinical recovery in children with severe malaria.
effect_estimate: higher Ang-2, CXCL10, and sFlt-1 at admission in children who died
p_value: P < .001 (Ang-2), P = .027 (CXCL10), P = .004 (sFlt-1), P < .0001 (postdischarge mortality Ang-2)

title: Antibody titres and boosting after natural malaria infection in BK-SE36 vaccine responders during a follow-up study in Uganda.
screening_reason: Published Phase Ib RCT with reported outcome results on a malaria vaccine in humans; results show clinical malaria episodes and antibody responses.
population: children and adolescents 6-20 years old, vaccine responders
primary_outcome: time to first episode of clinical malaria; anti-SE36 antibody titres in relation to natural P. falciparum infection
impact_summary: Responders to BK-SE36 vaccination with higher anti-SE36 antibody titres had lower risk of malaria infection, and antibody titres were boosted after natural infection, suggesting anti-SE36 antibodies confer protection against malaria.
safety_summary: Original phase Ib trial demonstrated safety and immunogenicity of BK-SE36 vaccine.

title: Cost-Effectiveness Analysis of Test-Based versus Presumptive Treatment of Uncomplicated Malaria in Children under Five Years in an Area of High Transmission in Central Ghana.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing malaria diagnostic strategies (mRDT-based vs. clinical judgement) in children under five in a high-transmission setting, meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: children under five years with suspected malaria
primary_outcome: appropriate treatment: a child with a positive reference diagnosis prescribed ACT or a child with a negative reference diagnosis not given an ACT
impact_summary: Introduction of malaria rapid diagnostic tests reduced unnecessary ACT prescriptions and increased the proportion of children appropriately treated compared to clinical judgement, and was found to be cost-effective.

title: Cost effectiveness of intermittent screening followed by treatment versus intermittent preventive treatment during pregnancy in West Africa: analysis and modelling of results from a non-inferiority trial.
screening_reason: Non-inferiority RCT with reported outcome results comparing two malaria-prevention strategies during pregnancy in humans; phase and results clearly documented.
design: multi-centre, non-inferiority trial; cost-effectiveness analysis and modelling, phase 3
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Incremental cost per DALY averted (based on low birth weight, severe/moderate anaemia, and clinical malaria)
impact_summary: At current SP efficacy levels observed in trial settings, switching from IPTp-SP to ISTp-AL would not be cost-effective due to higher costs and limited difference in outcomes, though ISTp-AL becomes more cost-effective as SP efficacy declines.
effect_metric: Incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (US$ per DALY averted)
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; based on non-inferiority trial outcomes for low birth weight and anaemia, with clinical malaria found inferior for ISTp-AL

title: Artemether-Lumefantrine versus Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine for Treatment of Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Children Aged Less than 15 Years in Guinea-Bissau - An Open-Label Non-Inferiority Randomised Clinical Trial.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children, meeting all inclusion criteria for a malaria treatment intervention trial.
population: children aged 6 months to 15 years with uncomplicated P. falciparum mono-infection
primary_outcome: Day 42 PCR-adjusted per protocol adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
impact_summary: Dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was not inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Guinea-Bissau, with both drugs meeting WHO recommended efficacy thresholds.
effect_metric: odds ratio (adequate clinical and parasitological response, AL vs DP)
transmission_setting: malaria endemic, resurgent transmission setting in Guinea-Bissau
safety_summary: Not specifically detailed; both treatments were noted to achieve WHO recommended efficacy and DP has been shown to be safe and efficacious in prior studies.

title: A Phase II pilot trial to evaluate safety and efficacy of ferroquine against early Plasmodium falciparum in an induced blood-stage malaria infection study.
screening_reason: Phase II RCT with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment intervention in humans.
population: Male and non-pregnant female volunteers aged 18-50 years
primary_outcome: Safety and pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic parameters of a single 800 mg dose of ferroquine following induced blood-stage P. falciparum infection
impact_summary: A single 800 mg dose of ferroquine was rapidly absorbed and effectively cleared induced P. falciparum parasitaemia, and was generally well tolerated apart from transient elevated transaminases in three subjects.
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (induced blood-stage), non-endemic setting
safety_summary: Ferroquine was overall well tolerated; transient elevated transaminase levels occurred in three subjects, possibly related to concomitant paracetamol use in two of them; no clinically significant ECG abnormalities were observed.

title: Scheduled Intermittent Screening with Rapid Diagnostic Tests and Treatment with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine versus Intermittent Preventive Therapy with Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine for Malaria in Pregnancy in Malawi: An Open-Label Randomized Controlled Trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two malaria-prevention strategies (ISTp-DP vs IPTp-SP) in pregnant women, addressing a primary malaria intervention in humans.
population: HIV-seronegative pregnant women (paucigravidae and multigravidae)
primary_outcome: Adverse live birth outcome (composite of small for gestational age, low birthweight <2,500 g, or preterm birth <37 wk) in paucigravidae; and maternal or placental plasmodium infection at delivery in multigravidae
impact_summary: Scheduled intermittent screening with RDTs and treatment with dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was not superior to IPTp-SP and was associated with higher fetal loss and more malaria at delivery.
effect_estimate: RR = 1.04 (adverse live birth outcome, all women); RR = 1.19 (malaria at delivery, all women); RR = 2.06 (fetal loss)
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission area with high SP resistance
safety_summary: ISTp-DP was associated with higher fetal loss (2.6% versus 1.3%) compared to IPTp-SP, with the highest rate among non-DP-recipients (3.1%) in the ISTp-DP arm.

title: Adding a single low-dose of primaquine (0.25 mg/kg) to artemether-lumefantrine did not compromise treatment outcome of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Tanzania: a randomized, single-blinded clinical trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment intervention (primaquine added to artemether-lumefantrine) in humans with primary efficacy endpoint achieved.
population: patients aged ≥1 year with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, excluding pregnant and lactating women
primary_outcome: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 28
impact_summary: Adding a single low-dose of primaquine (0.25 mg/kg) to artemether-lumefantrine did not compromise treatment outcome of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria compared to AL alone.

title: Supplementary effect and durability of prototype insecticide-treated eave curtains on indoor resting mosquitoes in Kadibo division, Western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing insecticide-treated eave curtains for malaria vector control in humans; vector control is a primary malaria intervention.
comparator: houses with LLINs only (bednets only, no eave screening)
population: Households in traditional East African houses (occupants of study houses) in Ahero rice irrigation scheme
primary_outcome: Indoor resting Anopheles mosquito density (An. funestus and An. arabiensis) collected via pyrethrum spray catches
impact_summary: Fully screened houses with insecticide-treated eave nets, curtains and door hangers combined with LLINs significantly reduced indoor resting malaria vector densities compared to houses with LLINs alone.
effect_estimate: 82% reduction in An. funestus (RR=0.18); 70% reduction in An. arabiensis (RR=0.30)
transmission_setting: Rural rice irrigation scheme, Western Kenya, dry and wet seasons
safety_summary: Not reported; insecticide (deltamethrin) bio-efficacy assessed via bioassays and chemical analyses showing little loss over 12-24 months

title: The effect of mass mosquito trapping on malaria transmission and disease burden (SolarMal): a stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial.
screening_reason: Stepped-wedge cluster-randomised trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (odour-baited mosquito traps) with reported outcome results (clinical malaria episodes and prevalence), non-early-phase design appropriate for cluster trials.
place: Rusinga Island, Lake Victoria, western Kenya
population: all residents of Rusinga Island enrolled in the health and demographic surveillance system
primary_outcome: clinical malaria (fever plus positive rapid diagnostic test)
impact_summary: Mass deployment of solar-powered odour-baited mosquito traps reduced malaria prevalence by about 30% but had an imprecise, non-significant effect on clinical malaria incidence.
effect_metric: adjusted effectiveness (clinical incidence); relative reduction in prevalence
transmission_setting: endemic, lake-side region with Anopheles funestus as key vector

title: A phase 2b randomized, controlled trial of the efficacy of the GMZ2 malaria vaccine in African children.
screening_reason: Phase 2b RCT with reported outcome results (malaria incidence) for a malaria vaccine intervention in children.
population: children 12-60 months old
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria defined as fever or history of fever and parasite density ≥5000/μL
impact_summary: GMZ2 vaccine reduced the incidence of malaria compared to control but with modest efficacy of 14% in the per-protocol analysis.
safety_summary: GMZ2 was well tolerated and immunogenic.

title: Population Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of Lumefantrine in Young Ugandan Children Treated With Artemether-Lumefantrine for Uncomplicated Malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT of artemether-lumefantrine treatment for uncomplicated malaria in children with reported outcome results (recurrent parasitemia at 28 days).
population: young children treated for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day recurrent parasitemia in relation to lumefantrine concentration
impact_summary: Children not receiving trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole with day 7 capillary lumefantrine concentrations below 200 ng/mL had a 3-fold higher risk of 28-day recurrent parasitemia, but this threshold did not predict recurrence in children receiving trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole.

title: Effect of quinine and artesunate combination therapy on platelet count of children with severe malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing antimalarial drugs in children with severe malaria that reports outcome results including platelet counts, efficacy, and treatment outcomes.
population: children aged 6 months to 12 years with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Fall in platelet count by ≥20% from the time of drug initiation until day 7
impact_summary: A significantly higher proportion of children on quinine had a ≥20% fall in platelet count compared to those on ACT, and ACT was significantly more efficacious than quinine.
effect_metric: proportion with ≥20% fall in platelet count
safety_summary: Despite the fall in platelet count in both groups, no bleeding occurred; quinine caused a higher incidence of thrombocytopenia than ACT.

title: A cluster randomized trial comparing deltamethrin and bendiocarb as insecticides for indoor residual spraying to control malaria on Bioko Island, Equatorial Guinea.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two IRS insecticides for malaria vector control in humans.
comparator: active comparator (deltamethrin vs bendiocarb, indoor residual spraying)
population: children aged 2-14 years living in households in clusters receiving IRS
primary_outcome: prevalence of malaria in children aged 2-14 years approximately 3 months after IRS intervention
impact_summary: Malaria prevalence was lower in the bendiocarb arm than the deltamethrin arm, but the difference was not statistically significant, suggesting bendiocarb may be more effective than deltamethrin for IRS on Bioko, likely due to vector resistance to deltamethrin.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic island setting with indoor residual spraying since 2004
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Comparison of artesunate-mefloquine and artemether-lumefantrine fixed-dose combinations for treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children younger than 5 years in sub-Saharan Africa: a randomised, multicentre, phase 4 trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with published outcome results comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children; phase 4 trial meets eligibility criteria.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated P falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected rate of adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 63 in the per-protocol population
impact_summary: Fixed-dose artesunate-mefloquine was non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated P falciparum malaria in children under 5 years, with similar efficacy and safety profiles.
effect_metric: treatment difference in PCR-corrected ACPR rate at day 63
safety_summary: Similar safety profiles between groups, with low rates of early vomiting (15.3% vs 16.8%), few neurological adverse events (2.1% vs 1.1%), and no detectable psychiatric adverse events.
funder: Agence Française de Développement, France; Department for International Development, UK; Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Netherlands; European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership; Fondation Arpe, Switzerland; Médecins Sans Frontières; Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, Switzerland

title: A comparative study of azithromycin and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine as prophylaxis against malaria in pregnancy.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing two antimalarial prophylaxis interventions for malaria prevention in pregnant women, with malaria as the primary focus.
population: antenatal clinic attendees (pregnant women)
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria parasitaemia (peripheral, placental, and cord blood) during pregnancy and at delivery
impact_summary: Azithromycin was comparable to sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine in preventing malaria in pregnancy, with similar rates of parasitaemia and tolerability between groups.
safety_summary: Drug tolerability and foetal outcomes were comparable between the AZ and SP groups.

title: Longitudinal effect of CD4 by cotrimoxazole use on malaria incidence among HIV-infected Ugandan adults on antiretroviral therapy: a randomized controlled study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (malaria incidence) comparing cotrimoxazole chemoprevention to placebo in HIV-infected adults; malaria prevention is the primary focus.
population: HIV-infected adults on antiretroviral therapy with CD4 counts ≥250 cells/µl
primary_outcome: Clinical malaria incidence (fever plus positive blood slide) and its association with CD4 count
impact_summary: CD4 count during follow-up, at enrolment, or at ART initiation was not associated with clinical malaria incidence and did not modify the effect of stopping cotrimoxazole on malaria risk.
p_value: P > 0.30 (association with CD4 strata); P = 0.56 (current CD4 and malaria incidence); P = 0.24 (parasitaemia levels)

title: Intermittent Preventive Treatment with Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine in Ugandan Schoolchildren Selects for Plasmodium falciparum Transporter Polymorphisms That Modify Drug Sensitivity.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine for intermittent preventive treatment in schoolchildren with reported outcome results (96% malaria incidence reduction), published and evaluating a primary malaria intervention.
population: schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Prevalence of pfmdr1 and pfcrt polymorphisms in P. falciparum isolates emerging at different intervals after DP treatment
impact_summary: Monthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine reduced malaria incidence by 96% compared to placebo but selected for pfmdr1 N86Y and pfcrt K76T polymorphisms associated with decreased drug sensitivity.
transmission_setting: Tororo, Uganda, high malaria transmission area

title: Safety and Immunogenicity of GSK Biologicals' Investigational Malaria Vaccine in HIV Infected Infants and Children
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS01) with reported safety and immunogenicity results in HIV-infected children; Phase 3; primary malaria intervention.
interventions_raw: GSK Biological's Investigational Malaria Vaccine 257049; Human Diploid Cell Vaccine (HDCV) or Purified Vero Cell Rabies Vaccine (PVRV, Verorab) (Aventis Pasteur);; Purified Chick Embryo Cell Culture (PCEC) Rabies Vaccine (Rabipur or equivalent) (Novartis).
population: HIV-infected infants and children aged 6 weeks to 17 months with WHO stage 1 or 2 HIV disease
primary_outcome: Number of Subjects With Serious Adverse Events (SAEs)
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01 was well tolerated in HIV-infected children with WHO stage 1 or 2 disease, with a similar overall rate of serious adverse events compared to rabies vaccine recipients and no deaths related to vaccination.
effect_metric: relative risk of serious adverse events
safety_summary: Serious adverse events occurred in 41.4% of RTS,S/AS01 recipients vs 36.6% of rabies-vaccine recipients (RR 1.1, 95% CI 0.8-1.6); within 30 days post-vaccination, 20.2% vs 11.9% had at least one SAE, mainly pneumonia, febrile convulsions, and salmonella sepsis; 5.1% vs 4.0% died, with no deaths attributed to vaccination.

title: Appropriate targeting of artemisinin-based combination therapy by community health workers using malaria rapid diagnostic tests: findings from randomized trials in two contrasting areas of high and low malaria transmission in south-western Uganda.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria rapid diagnostic tests for appropriate targeting of artemisinin-based combination therapy in children, comparing mRDT-guided vs. presumptive treatment by community health workers in Uganda.
population: children under 5 years of age with fever seen by community health workers
primary_outcome: proportion of children <5 years receiving appropriately targeted ACT treatment (defined by microscopically-confirmed parasitaemia and corresponding treatment decision)
impact_summary: Use of malaria rapid diagnostic tests by community health workers substantially improved the appropriate targeting of ACT treatment compared to presumptive diagnosis in both high and low malaria transmission areas of Uganda.
effect_estimate: 79.3% vs 30.8% (high transmission area); 90.1% vs 7.8% (low transmission area)
transmission_setting: two contrasting rural areas of moderate-to-high and low malaria transmission

title: Efficacy of topical mosquito repellent (picaridin) plus long-lasting insecticidal nets versus long-lasting insecticidal nets alone for control of malaria: a cluster randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria vector-control intervention (topical repellent plus ITNs) in humans; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: randomly selected individuals in study villages (cross-sectional surveys)
primary_outcome: Plasmodium species-specific prevalence by real-time PCR
impact_summary: Adding topical picaridin repellent to long-lasting insecticidal nets did not reduce malaria prevalence compared with nets alone, largely due to suboptimal daily repellent use.
transmission_setting: low-endemic, pre-elimination setting in the Greater Mekong subregion with outdoor transmission
safety_summary: 41 adverse event notifications from nine villages, 33 classified as adverse reactions (11 due to oral ingestion of repellent); all recovered fully and 17 advised to stop using the repellent.

title: No Reduction in Hemoglobin Level in Severe Plasmodium falciparum Malaria Treated with Artesunate in Central Sudan.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artesunate versus quinine for severe P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (hemoglobin levels).
population: patients with severe Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Hemoglobin level change from baseline to day 14 and day 28
impact_summary: There was no significant difference in hemoglobin levels between patients treated with artesunate versus quinine for severe malaria.
safety_summary: Hypotension, convulsions, and severe anemia were the main presentations; no significant hemoglobin reduction observed with artesunate treatment.

title: Seven-Year Efficacy of RTS,S/AS01 Malaria Vaccine among Young African Children.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported 7-year efficacy outcomes for RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in African children, meeting all inclusion criteria.
population: young children
primary_outcome: Clinical malaria (temperature ≥37.5°C with P. falciparum infection >2500 parasites/mm3)
impact_summary: RTS,S/AS01 was initially protective against clinical malaria but showed no overall efficacy over 7 years, with waning and eventually negative efficacy in high-exposure areas by year 5.
transmission_setting: varying malaria exposure, area with higher-than-average parasite exposure showed negative efficacy
funder: PATH Malaria Vaccine Initiative and others

title: Therapeutic efficacy trial of artemisinin-based combination therapy for the treatment of uncomplicated malaria and investigation of mutations in k13 propeller domain in Togo, 2012-2013.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results (28-day ACPR efficacy data) for malaria treatment in humans; not early-phase.
design: open-label, multi-site, phase IV therapeutic efficacy trial
comparator: active comparator (AL vs ASAQ, two active treatment arms)
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: 28-day PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine remained highly efficacious for treating uncomplicated malaria in Togo, with high PCR-corrected cure rates and low prevalence of k13 mutations.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sentinel sites in Togo (Lomé, Sokodé, Niamtougou)
safety_summary: Adverse events were negligible, ranging from 0-4.8% across all sites for both artemisinin-based combinations.

title: Evaluate Azithromycin Plus Chloroquine And Sulfadoxine Plus Pyrimethamine Combinations For Intermittent Preventive Treatment Of Falciparum Malaria Infection In Pregnant Women In Africa
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT with reported outcome results testing intermittent preventive treatment (chemoprevention) for malaria in pregnant women in Africa.
interventions_raw: Azithromycin plus chloroquine; sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine
population: pregnant women in second and third trimester
primary_outcome: Percentage Participants With Sub-optimal Pregnancy Outcome in Intent-to-Treat (IIT) Population
impact_summary: IPTp with azithromycin-chloroquine was not superior to IPTp with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine in reducing sub-optimal pregnancy outcomes, and the study was terminated early for futility.
transmission_setting: moderate to high malaria transmission regions of sub-Saharan Africa
safety_summary: IPTp-AZCQ was less well-tolerated in mothers than IPTp-SP; congenital anomalies, deaths, and serious adverse events in neonates were comparable between groups.

title: Evaluation of a topical formulation of eprinomectin against Anopheles arabiensis when administered to Zebu cattle (Bos indicus) under field conditions.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (systemic drug on cattle to reduce Anopheles arabiensis) with reported outcome results on mosquito density.
population: Homes and cattle in Samia District, western Kenya; mosquito vector populations sampled indoors
primary_outcome: Indoor resting density of Anopheles arabiensis post-treatment
impact_summary: Topical eprinomectin treatment of cattle significantly reduced indoor resting density of Anopheles arabiensis by 38% at one week post-treatment compared to control, though the effect was not sustained at two weeks and other Anopheles species increased.
effect_metric: percent reduction in indoor resting density
transmission_setting: Residual malaria transmission driven by outdoor-feeding Anopheles arabiensis in western Kenya
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Safety and High Level Efficacy of the Combination Malaria Vaccine Regimen of RTS,S/AS01B With Chimpanzee Adenovirus 63 and Modified Vaccinia Ankara Vectored Vaccines Expressing ME-TRAP.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS01B with viral vectors) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes; Phase II CHMI study is appropriate for vaccine development and not early-phase exclusion.
comparator: active comparator (RTS,S/AS01B alone) and unvaccinated controls
population: healthy malaria-naive adults
primary_outcome: Protective vaccine efficacy against controlled human malaria infection challenge
impact_summary: Both vaccination regimens showed high sterile protective efficacy against controlled human malaria infection, with combination and RTS,S/AS01B-alone groups showing similar high protection.
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection via mosquito bite challenge (non-endemic setting)
safety_summary: No suspected unexpected serious adverse reactions or severe adverse events related to vaccination were reported.

title: The Impact of an Intervention to Improve Malaria Care in Public Health Centers on Health Indicators of Children in Tororo, Uganda (PRIME): A Cluster-Randomized Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results (anemia prevalence as primary outcome); malaria diagnosis and treatment is the primary intervention focus.
comparator: standard care (control health centers without intervention)
population: children under 5 years of age in communities near public health centers
primary_outcome: Prevalence of anemia (hemoglobin < 11.0 g/dL) in children under 5 years of age in the final community survey
impact_summary: The PRIME intervention to improve malaria case management at health centers did not reduce prevalence of anemia or parasitemia in community children compared with control.

title: Clinical illness and outcomes in Nigerian children with late-appearing anaemia after artemisinin-based combination treatments of uncomplicated falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating artemisinin-based combination therapies for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Nigerian children, with clinical and parasitological outcomes measured.
comparator: active comparator (artesunate-amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine vs dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine)
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Incidence, risk factors and outcomes of late-appearing anaemia (LAA) following ACT treatment
impact_summary: Late-appearing anaemia occurred in 84 of 609 children treated with ACTs, was mostly mild and asymptomatic, and resolved uneventfully in most cases.
effect_estimate: AOR 2.0-7.5 for various predictors of LAA/failure of recovery
p_value: P<0.0001 to P=0.04 depending on predictor
safety_summary: LAA was mostly mild and asymptomatic with uneventful recovery in most children; severe cases were rare

title: Persistence of Plasmodium falciparum parasitemia after artemisinin combination therapy: evidence from a randomized trial in Uganda.
screening_reason: Randomized trial of malaria treatment (ACT with and without primaquine) in humans with reported outcome results on parasite persistence and clearance.
population: patients with Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Persistence of circulating parasite populations (transcripts and genotypes) after treatment
impact_summary: Genetically diverse ring stage parasites persisted at low levels for up to 14 days after ACT or ACT-primaquine treatment despite no clinical treatment failures.
effect_metric: prevalence of ring stage parasite transcripts
effect_estimate: >25% prevalence at day 14; >98% cleared within first 3 days
safety_summary: No clinical treatment failures observed after ACT treatment

title: Acute Kidney Injury Is Common in Pediatric Severe Malaria and Is Associated With Increased Mortality.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of inhaled nitric oxide versus placebo in pediatric severe malaria with reported outcome results on mortality and morbidity.
comparator: placebo (within a trial of inhaled nitric oxide)
population: children aged 1 to 10 years with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Incidence and staging of acute kidney injury (AKI) using KDIGO criteria and its association with mortality
impact_summary: AKI was common (45.5%) in pediatric severe malaria and was associated with increased mortality, longer hospitalization, and neurodisability, particularly in children receiving placebo, while children receiving inhaled nitric oxide had higher rates of AKI but no significant association between AKI and mortality or neurodisability.
effect_metric: relative risk of AKI in iNO vs placebo arm
p_value: 0.006 (mortality across AKI stages in placebo arm)
safety_summary: Children randomized to inhaled nitric oxide had a higher incidence of AKI (54.0%) compared with placebo (37.4%)

title: Effects of an intervention on infant growth and development: evidence for different mechanisms at work.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results on an intervention that included malaria treatment plus nutrient supplementation in infants; malaria treatment is a primary component and outcomes are reported.
population: infants aged 9 to 18 months
primary_outcome: length-for-age z-score (LAZ) and motor, language, and personal-social development scores at age 18 months
impact_summary: The intervention (lipid-based nutrient supplements plus malaria and diarrhoea treatment) had independent positive effects on both linear growth and neurodevelopment, suggesting different underlying mechanisms rather than mediation through growth alone.
effect_estimate: ~0.3 SD on LAZ and ~0.3 SD on motor, language and personal-social scores; effects decreased to 0.21, 0.27, and 0.29 respectively after adjusting for LAZ change

title: Mobile Phone Short Message Service to Improve Malaria Pharmacoadherence in Zambia.
journal: Journal of nursing scholarship : an official publication of Sigma Theta Tau International Honor Society of Nursing
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing an intervention (SMS reminders) to improve malaria treatment adherence in humans; meets all inclusion criteria despite negative findings.
population: adult malaria patients
primary_outcome: Pharmacoadherence to six-dose ACT regimen, measured via electronic pillbox (classified as probably adherent or probably nonadherent)
impact_summary: SMS reminder messages did not significantly improve pharmacoadherence to malaria medication compared to no SMS reminders.

title: Clinical and Biological Efficacy of Mirasol-treated Fresh Whole Blood for the Prevention of Transfusion-transmitted Malaria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria prevention intervention (pathogen-reduced blood transfusion) in humans; phase not applicable for transfusion/device trials.
interventions_raw: Mirasol-treated Whole Blood; Untreated Whole Blood
population: adult patients (aged ≥18 years) with blood group O+ requiring whole blood transfusion
primary_outcome: Percentage of Participants With Incidence of Transfusion-transmitted Malaria
impact_summary: Treatment of whole blood with the Mirasol pathogen reduction system significantly reduced the incidence of transfusion-transmitted malaria compared with untreated whole blood.
safety_summary: 92 (41%) of 223 patients reported 145 treatment-related emergent adverse events, with similar incidence between groups; no transfusion-related deaths occurred.

title: In vivo efficacy of artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Malawi, 2014.
screening_reason: This is a published randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (day 28 PCR-corrected efficacy rates).
population: febrile children aged 6-59 months with microscopy-confirmed uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected day 28 Kaplan-Meier cumulative success rate
impact_summary: Both artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine remained highly efficacious for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Malawi, with PCR-corrected day 28 success rates over 99%.
transmission_setting: endemic, multiple regions (northern, central, southern Malawi)

title: Malaria illness mediated by anaemia lessens cognitive development in younger Ugandan children.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention with reported outcome results (cognitive development, malaria episodes, anaemia) in infants in a malaria-endemic area.
comparator: no chemoprevention (also compared with daily trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole and monthly sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine)
population: infants enrolled at 4-6 months, followed to 2 and 3 years of age; HIV-exposed uninfected and HIV-unexposed uninfected children
primary_outcome: Early childhood neurodevelopment (Mullen Scales of Early Learning) assessed at 2 and 3 years of age, along with malaria episodes and anaemia
impact_summary: Malarial illness episodes negatively predicted cognitive performance at 2 and 3 years, an effect mediated by anaemia, and this relationship was stronger in HIV-exposed uninfected children, while dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was highly protective against malaria and anaemia but trial arm itself was not associated with neurodevelopmental outcomes.
effect_metric: association (regression coefficient) between malaria episodes and MSEL cognitive score
safety_summary: Not reported in detail; DP was highly protective against malaria and anaemia with no specific adverse events described

title: Interceptor® long-lasting insecticidal net: phase III evaluation over three years of household use and calibration with Phase II experimental hut outcomes.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcomes evaluating a malaria prevention intervention (long-lasting insecticidal nets) over three years of household use, meeting WHO Phase III evaluation criteria.
population: households in a malaria-endemic area of Tanzania
primary_outcome: Bioefficacy of nets (knock-down and kill of Anopheles gambiae) meeting WHOPES efficacy criteria via cone or tunnel bioassay over 36 months
impact_summary: Interceptor LN retained bioefficacy and insecticide content far better than conventionally treated nets over 36 months, with more than 80% meeting WHOPES Phase III criteria, leading to full WHO recommendation.
effect_metric: percentage of nets meeting WHOPES efficacy criteria at 36 months
safety_summary: A few users reported facial tingling during the first days of use but this did not deter usage; no serious adverse effects reported.

title: The Impact of Hotspot-Targeted Interventions on Malaria Transmission in Rachuonyo South District in the Western Kenyan Highlands: A Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria transmission interventions (larviciding, ITNs, IRS, mass drug administration) as primary purpose in humans.
intervention_class: MDA; ITN/LLIN; IRS; larval source management; diagnostic
comparator: standard care (malaria control following Kenyan national policy)
population: individuals residing in serologically defined malaria hotspots and surrounding communities
primary_outcome: Parasite prevalence (by nested PCR) in evaluation zones up to 500 m outside hotspots at 8 and 16 weeks post-intervention
impact_summary: Hotspot-targeted interventions modestly and transiently reduced parasite prevalence inside hotspots but had no significant effect on transmission in the surrounding evaluation zones.
effect_metric: reduction in nPCR parasite prevalence inside hotspots
transmission_setting: highly heterogeneous malaria transmission with hotspots, Western Kenyan highlands
safety_summary: Interventions were reported as safe and acceptable with intervention coverage exceeding 87%; no adverse events reported in abstract

title: Effective Antimalarial Chemoprevention in Childhood Enhances the Quality of CD4+ T Cells and Limits Their Production of Immunoregulatory Interleukin 10.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprevention (DP) in children with reported outcome results showing efficacy in reducing malaria episodes and describing immune responses.
population: children aged 6 to 24 months
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence and P. falciparum-specific T-cell responses (CD4+ T cell cytokine production)
impact_summary: Monthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine chemoprevention reduced malaria episodes and enhanced protective CD4+ T-cell responses while limiting immunoregulatory IL-10 production compared to no chemoprevention.
effect_estimate: 55% overall (97% among highly adherent) during intervention; 55% reduction in the year after cessation among highly adherent
p_value: P < .001 (overall and highly adherent during intervention); P = .004 (post-intervention year)
follow_up: additional year after cessation of chemoprevention (total ~2 years)

title: Risk factors for Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax gametocyte carriage in Papua New Guinean children with uncomplicated malaria.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarials (artemether-lumefantrine vs artemisinin-naphthoquine) in children with uncomplicated malaria, with reported outcome results on gametocytaemia risk factors.
population: children aged 0.5-5 years with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte carriage (P. falciparum and P. vivax) before and after treatment, and its risk factors
impact_summary: Low haemoglobin, low asexual parasite density and higher spleen grade were associated with pre-treatment gametocyte positivity, while post-treatment P. falciparum gametocytaemia was independently predicted by AN treatment, haemoglobin, asexual parasitaemia and day post-treatment, and P. vivax gametocytaemia was strongly predicted by presence of P. vivax asexual forms.
effect_estimate: 4.09 (AN vs AL for post-treatment P. falciparum gametocytaemia)
transmission_setting: Papua New Guinea, area with multiple Plasmodium species transmission

title: Monthly sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine combination versus daily proguanil for malaria chemoprophylaxis in sickle cell disease: a randomized controlled study at the Jos University Teaching Hospital.
journal: Nigerian journal of medicine : journal of the National Association of Resident Doctors of Nigeria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial chemoprophylaxis strategies (SP vs proguanil) for malaria prevention in sickle cell disease patients; primary malaria prevention focus; results published.
population: patients with sickle cell disease in steady state (children and adults)
primary_outcome: Proportion of patients with malaria parasite in the peripheral blood at the end of 3 months
impact_summary: Monthly sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine was more efficacious than daily proguanil in reducing malaria parasitaemia, clinical malaria attacks, and sickle cell crises among sickle cell disease patients.
effect_metric: reduction in prevalence of malaria parasitaemia
safety_summary: No significant side effects were recorded in both groups.

title: Community point distribution of insecticide-treated bed nets and community health worker hang-up visits in rural Zambia: a decision-focused evaluation.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of ITN distribution with reported outcome results on retention and usage; malaria prevention is the primary purpose; vector-control trials are exempt from early-phase exclusion.
comparator: no hang-up visit (households allocated to different CHW visit timing intervals vs none)
population: rural households in Rufunsa District, Zambia
primary_outcome: ITN retention and usage (hanging status) at 7-11 weeks and 5-6 months after distribution
impact_summary: Community point distribution achieved high attendance and retention rates, and CHW hang-up visits modestly increased short-term ITN usage but had no medium-term effect on retention or usage.
effect_estimate: 65.6% hanging at 7-11 weeks vs 63.1% at 5-6 months; CHW visit associated with increased short-term usage
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Can Rapid Diagnostic Testing for Malaria Increase Adherence to Artemether-Lumefantrine?: A Randomized Controlled Trial in Uganda.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria diagnostic intervention (rapid diagnostic testing) to improve adherence to antimalarial treatment in humans with focus on malaria.
comparator: no malaria rapid diagnostic test offered (usual care)
population: patients purchasing a course of artemether-lumefantrine at private drug shops
primary_outcome: Adherence to artemether-lumefantrine treatment assessed via home visits 3 days later
impact_summary: Offering a free malaria rapid diagnostic test did not significantly improve adherence to artemether-lumefantrine, while patients who felt healthy by day two had lower odds of completing treatment.

title: A Phase 3, Double-Blind, Randomized Study of Arterolane Maleate-Piperaquine Phosphate vs Artemether-Lumefantrine for Falciparum Malaria in Adolescent and Adult Patients in Asia and Africa.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT with reported outcome results (PCR-corrected ACPR at days 28 and 42) comparing artemisinin-based antimalarials for uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment in humans.
population: adolescent and adult patients with uncomplicated P. falciparum monoinfection, aged 12-65 years
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 28
impact_summary: Arterolane maleate-piperaquine phosphate showed comparable efficacy and safety to artemether-lumefantrine for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in adolescents and adults.
safety_summary: Overall incidence of adverse events was comparable between AM-PQP and artemether-lumefantrine groups.

title: Incremental impact upon malaria transmission of supplementing pyrethroid-impregnated long-lasting insecticidal nets with indoor residual spraying using pyrethroids or the organophosphate, pirimiphos methyl.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating incremental impact of indoor residual spraying as malaria vector control supplementing LLINs.
comparator: LLINs alone (no supplementary vector control) and comparison across pyrethroid vs organophosphate IRS formulations
population: residents of population clusters (community members tested for malaria by community health workers)
primary_outcome: Diagnostic positivity for malaria among patients tested by community health workers
impact_summary: Supplementing pyrethroid LLINs with IRS using the organophosphate pirimiphos methyl (especially the CS formulation) provided greater and longer-lasting incremental protection against malaria than supplementing with pyrethroid IRS formulations.
effect_estimate: 0.63 (PM CS, first 3 months); 0.79 (PM CS over 6 months); 0.31 (lambdacyhalothrin); 0.23 (PM EC); 0.19 (deltamethrin)
p_value: P < 0.001 (PM CS, PM EC); P = 0.006 (lambdacyhalothrin); P = 0.064 (deltamethrin)
transmission_setting: Zambia, high pre-existing LLIN usage (81.7%), pyrethroid resistance present in vector population

title: Tafenoquine treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria: suggestive evidence that CYP2D6 reduced metabolism is not associated with relapse in the Phase 2b DETECTIVE trial.
screening_reason: Published randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (relapse rates) evaluating tafenoquine for treatment of Plasmodium vivax malaria, a primary malaria intervention.
comparator: primaquine (active comparator), extensive metabolizer phenotype as reference group
population: P. vivax-infected patients treated with tafenoquine or primaquine plus chloroquine
primary_outcome: Relapse-free efficacy at six months post-dosing, assessed by CYP2D6 metabolizer phenotype (intermediate vs extensive metabolizers)
impact_summary: Reduced CYP2D6 metabolism (intermediate metabolizer phenotype) was associated with higher relapse rates in primaquine-treated patients but not in tafenoquine-treated patients, suggesting tafenoquine efficacy is less affected by CYP2D6 metabolism than primaquine.
effect_metric: relapse rate by CYP2D6 metabolizer status
effect_estimate: Relapse in 50% of PQ-treated CYP2D6 IMs vs 17% of PQ-treated EMs who remained relapse-free; no significant difference in TQ-treated IMs vs EMs

title: In Vivo Efficacy of Artesunate/Sulphadoxine-Pyrimethamine versus Artesunate/Amodiaquine in the Treatment of Uncomplicated P. falciparium Malaria in Children around the Slope of Mount Cameroon: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments with reported outcome results (cure rates, treatment failures) in children with P. falciparum malaria.
design: randomized controlled trial, open-label (implied), phase not applicable
population: children aged six months to 10 years with uncomplicated mono-infected P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR uncorrected and corrected cure rates (adequate clinical and parasitological response, ACPR) on day 28
impact_summary: Both artesunate/sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine and artesunate/amodiaquine were highly effective and well-tolerated treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with PCR corrected cure rates of 85.9% and 90.2%, respectively.
transmission_setting: endemic area around the slope of Mount Cameroon
safety_summary: The drugs were well tolerated with no serious adverse events.

title: A Randomized Comparison of Chloroquine Versus Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine for the Treatment of Plasmodium vivax Infection in Vietnam.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two antimalarial treatments for Plasmodium vivax malaria in humans.
population: Vietnamese patients with symptomatic Plasmodium vivax mono-infections
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (Kaplan-Meier intention-to-treat analysis)
impact_summary: DHA-PPQ was non-inferior to chloroquine and provided faster fever and parasite clearance, while chloroquine remained efficacious for treating P. vivax malaria in southern Vietnam.
effect_metric: absolute difference in adequate clinical and parasitological response
follow_up: 至 day 33 and beyond (recurrent parasitemia monitoring)

title: Comparison of the safety and efficacy of fixed-dose combination of arterolane maleate and piperaquine phosphate with chloroquine in acute, uncomplicated Plasmodium vivax malaria: a phase III, multicentric, open-label study.
screening_reason: Phase III RCT with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial drugs for P. vivax malaria treatment in humans.
population: patients aged 13-65 years with confirmed mono-infection of P. vivax and fever or fever in the previous 48 h
primary_outcome: proportion of aparasitaemic and afebrile patients at 72 hours
impact_summary: Fixed-dose combination of arterolane maleate and piperaquine phosphate was as effective and safe as chloroquine for treating acute uncomplicated P. vivax malaria, with similar cure rates and adverse event profiles.
effect_metric: proportion aparasitaemic and afebrile at 72h (PP population)
safety_summary: Adverse events occurred in 82.4% (FDC) vs 85.4% (chloroquine), mostly mild to moderate; common events included vomiting, headache, and prolonged QT; no deaths reported; similar safety profile between groups.

title: In Vivo Efficacy and Parasite Clearance of Artesunate + Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine Versus Artemether-Lumefantrine in Mali.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (AS+SP vs AL) with reported efficacy and parasite clearance outcomes in uncomplicated falciparum malaria; Phase 3 or equivalent efficacy study.
design: Randomized, open-label, comparative, in vivo assay, phase 3
population: patients with uncomplicated falciparum malaria, at least 6 months of age
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response at day 28 and parasite clearance time
impact_summary: Both AS + SP and AL showed high efficacy with no significant difference in cure rates or parasite clearance half-life, though children under 8 years had higher risk of treatment failure.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response
age_range: 6 months and older, particularly children under 8 years at higher risk of treatment failure

title: Intramuscular Artesunate for Severe Malaria in African Children: A Multicenter Randomized Controlled Trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing artesunate regimens for severe malaria treatment in children; meets all inclusion criteria.
population: children with severe malaria, aged 0.5-10 years
primary_outcome: Proportion of children with ≥99% reduction in parasitemia at 24 h from admission values
impact_summary: The simplified three-dose intramuscular artesunate regimen was non-inferior to the standard five-dose intramuscular regimen, but the three-dose intravenous regimen did not show non-inferiority.
effect_metric: difference in proportion with ≥99% parasitemia reduction at 24h
effect_estimate: three-dose IM: 78% vs five-dose IM: 79%; three-dose IV: 74% vs five-dose IM: 79%
effect_ci: three-dose IM vs five-dose: -7 to 5; three-dose IV vs five-dose: -12 to 1
p_value: three-dose IM: p=0.02; three-dose IV: p=0.24
follow_up: at least 7 days post-admission (for delayed anemia assessment)
safety_summary: Parenteral artesunate associated with risk of delayed anemia (hemoglobin ≤7 g/dl at ≥7 days post-admission) in 22% of children; no difference in delayed anemia between treatment arms; delayed anemia associated with increased leukocyte counts.

title: Malaria burden and anti-malarial drug efficacy in Owando, northern Congo.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination antimalarials (ASAQ vs AL) for malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy results.
population: febrile children under 12 years with acute uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected clinical and parasitological efficacy at day 28
impact_summary: Both ASAQ and AL were highly efficacious against uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria, with PCR-corrected cure rates of 100% for ASAQ and 98.0% for AL, though ASAQ was associated with more adverse events.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response
safety_summary: ASAQ was associated with more adverse events than AL, which may reduce compliance in unsupervised treatment.

title: The Effect of Indoor Residual Spraying on the Prevalence of Malaria Parasite Infection, Clinical Malaria and Anemia in an Area of Perennial Transmission and Moderate Coverage of Insecticide Treated Nets in Western Kenya.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (cluster-randomized design with 30 clusters per arm) evaluating indoor residual spraying for malaria prevention in humans, with complete outcome results reported.
design: cluster-sampled, propensity score matched, comparison district design (quasi-experimental, repeated cross-sectional surveys)
comparator: neighboring non-IRS district (ITNs alone) at moderate ITN coverage
population: residents of randomly selected compounds, including children under 5
primary_outcome: prevalence of malaria parasitemia, clinical malaria (P. falciparum infection plus history of fever), and anemia (Hb<8)
impact_summary: After two rounds of indoor residual spraying, the IRS district had significantly lower prevalence of malaria parasitemia, clinical malaria, and (in children under 5) anemia compared to the non-IRS district.
follow_up: from baseline through after second round of IRS (April-May 2009)
transmission_setting: area of intense perennial malaria transmission, lowland endemic district
age_range: all ages, with subgroup analysis in children under 5 years

title: Correction: Combination of Insecticide Treated Nets and Indoor Residual Spraying in Northern Tanzania Provides Additional Reduction in Vector Population Density and Malaria Transmission Rates Compared to Insecticide Treated Nets Alone: A Randomised Control Trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported results comparing combination vector control interventions (ITNs plus IRS) against ITNs alone for malaria transmission reduction in humans.
impact_summary: Combining insecticide treated nets with indoor residual spraying provided additional reduction in vector population density and malaria transmission rates compared to insecticide treated nets alone.

title: [Comparison of the therapeutic efficiency and of the tolerance of the artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine combination in Niger].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based combination therapies for malaria treatment with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: febrile patients with malaria
primary_outcome: adequate clinical and parasitological response at day 28
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine and artesunate-amodiaquine showed comparable efficacy and safety with no statistically significant difference between the two combinations.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitological response rate
safety_summary: No statistically significant difference in adverse effects between the two treatment arms.
funder: Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria (AMFm initiative)

title: Safety of insecticide-treated mosquito nets for infants and their mothers: randomized controlled community trial in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of insecticide-treated nets for malaria prevention with reported safety outcome results in a vulnerable population.
comparator: delayed ITN exposure (from age 6 months) vs early exposure (from birth)
population: newborns and their mothers
primary_outcome: Frequency and duration of side effects potentially related to synthetic pyrethroid (deltamethrin) exposure from ITNs
impact_summary: ITNs were found to be sufficiently safe for use in newborns and their mothers, with no significant differences in side effects between groups except more frequent headaches in mothers of infants protected from birth.
age_range: newborns to 6 months and their mothers
safety_summary: No significant differences in frequency/duration of side effects between groups except significantly higher frequency of headache in group A mothers (p=0.01); no loss to follow-up; ITNs considered sufficiently safe.

title: Safety, Immunogenicity, and Protective Efficacy of Intradermal Immunization with Aseptic, Purified, Cryopreserved Plasmodium falciparum Sporozoites in Volunteers Under Chloroquine Prophylaxis: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria vaccine intervention (PfSPZ-CVac) in humans; Phase 2 is not early-phase and thus eligible.
population: healthy adult volunteers under chloroquine prophylaxis
primary_outcome: Safety, immunogenicity, and protective efficacy (parasitemia) after controlled human malaria infection
impact_summary: Intradermal immunization with cryopreserved PfSPZ under chloroquine prophylaxis was safe but induced only minimal immune responses and did not protect against controlled human malaria infection.
safety_summary: Vaccinees (55%) and controls (60%) had similar rates of mild to moderate solicited adverse events; no serious safety concerns reported.

title: [Evaluation of the efficacy and safety of three 2-drug combinations for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in Senegal: artesunate-amodiaquine, dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine, and artemether-lumefantrine].
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing three malaria treatment interventions with reported efficacy and safety outcomes at day 28 and 42.
comparator: active comparator (three ACT regimens compared against each other)
population: adults and children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: All three artemisinin-based combination therapies (AL, ASAQ, DHAPQ) showed high and similar efficacy with PCR-corrected ACPR at day 28 ranging from 89.2% to 92.8% and were well tolerated with no serious adverse events.
safety_summary: The combinations were well tolerated, with no serious adverse events reported during follow-up.

title: Summary of anti-malarial prophylactic efficacy of tafenoquine from three placebo-controlled studies of residents of malaria-endemic countries.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported efficacy results of tafenoquine for malaria prevention in endemic-area residents, comparing drug regimens to placebo.
comparator: placebo (and mefloquine as active comparator in some studies)
population: residents of malaria-endemic African countries naturally exposed to P. falciparum
primary_outcome: Prophylactic efficacy (incidence density of malaria infection) among subjects completing loading doses with at least one maintenance dose and one blood smear during prophylactic period
impact_summary: Tafenoquine 200-mg weekly regimen provided high prophylactic efficacy against P. falciparum malaria comparable to mefloquine in African residents.

title: Safety and efficacy of re-treatments with pyronaridine-artesunate in African patients with malaria: a substudy of the WANECAM randomised trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing pyronaridine-artesunate to artemether-lumefantrine for malaria treatment in humans; phase 3b/4 is not early-phase.
population: patients aged ≥6 months and bodyweight ≥5 kg with uncomplicated microscopically confirmed Plasmodium spp malaria
primary_outcome: Incidence of hepatotoxicity (alanine aminotransferase >5x ULN or Hy's law criteria) after first treatment versus re-treatment with pyronaridine-artesunate
impact_summary: Pyronaridine-artesunate showed similar safety and efficacy on first treatment versus re-treatment of subsequent malaria episodes, supporting its wider use as an alternative artemisinin-based combination therapy.
effect_metric: adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
safety_summary: Hepatotoxicity occurred in 13 (1%) of 996 patients after first treatment versus 2 (1%) of 311 on re-treatment; no evidence of increased safety risk with re-treatment based on laboratory values, adverse events, or ECG findings.
funder: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trial Partnership, Medicines for Malaria Venture, UK Medical Research Council, Swedish International Development Cooperation Agency, German Ministry for Education and Research, University Claude Bernard (Lyon, France), Malaria Research and Training Centre (Bamako, Mali), Centre National de Recherche et de Formation sur le Paludisme (Burkina Faso), Institut de Recherche en Sciences de la Santé (Bobo-Dioulasso, Burkina Faso), Centre National de Formation et de Recherche en Santé Rurale (Republic of Guinea)

title: Risks of Hemolysis in Glucose-6-Phosphate Dehydrogenase Deficient Infants Exposed to Chlorproguanil-Dapsone, Mefloquine and Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine as Part of Intermittent Presumptive Treatment of Malaria in Infants.
screening_reason: Double-blind placebo-controlled RCT of intermittent presumptive treatment in infants (IPTi) for malaria prevention with reported hemolysis outcome results.
population: infants (asymptomatic, some with G6PD deficiency)
primary_outcome: Hemolysis measured as absolute change in hemoglobin or any post-dose hemoglobin <8 g/dL
impact_summary: Chlorproguanil-dapsone caused greater reductions in hemoglobin than sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine or mefloquine, and G6PD deficient infants had higher hemolysis risk overall, but G6PD deficiency did not specifically worsen chlorproguanil-dapsone-associated hemoglobin declines.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio for Hb <8 g/dL in homo-/hemizygous G6PD genotype
safety_summary: Chlorproguanil-dapsone reduced Hb by ~0.5 g/dL at day 7 and within 14 days, and by 0.2 g/dL within 28 days relative to placebo; homo-/hemizygous G6PD genotype associated with higher odds of Hb <8 g/dL and greater Hb reductions, but no evidence of interaction between G6PD status and CD treatment specifically.

title: Artesunate/Amodiaquine Versus Artemether/Lumefantrine for the Treatment of Uncomplicated Malaria in Uganda: A Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (AS/AQ vs AL) in humans with reported outcome results (recurrent parasitemia, safety, resistance markers).
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Risk of recurrent parasitemia within 28 days, with or without adjustment to distinguish recrudescence from new infection
impact_summary: AS/AQ treatment resulted in fewer recurrent parasitemia episodes than AL treatment across all three sites.
safety_summary: Both regimens were well tolerated; serious adverse events were uncommon (1.7% AS/AQ vs 1.0% AL).

title: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention in an area of extended seasonal transmission in Ashanti, Ghana: an individually randomised clinical trial.
journal: Tropical medicine & international health : TM & IH
screening_reason: Individually randomised controlled trial with reported outcome results testing seasonal malaria chemoprevention as a primary intervention in children in Ghana.
comparator: placebo SMC combined with artemether-lumefantrine (AL) for case management
population: children aged 3-59 months
primary_outcome: Incidence of malaria
impact_summary: Seasonal malaria chemoprevention reduced the incidence of malaria in children during the rainy season compared to placebo.
transmission_setting: area of extended seasonal malaria transmission

title: Introducing rapid diagnostic tests for malaria into registered drug shops in Uganda: lessons learned and policy implications.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing malaria RDT introduction (diagnosis intervention) in a human healthcare setting; phase not applicable for implementation trial.
comparator: standard drug shop practice without RDTs
population: patients seeking care at registered drug shops in central Uganda
primary_outcome: impact and feasibility of introducing RDTs into drug shops, including appropriate treatment with ACTs
impact_summary: Introducing RDTs into registered drug shops in Uganda was feasible and increased appropriate treatment of malaria with artemisinin-based combination therapy.

title: Combination of Insecticide Treated Nets and Indoor Residual Spraying in Northern Tanzania Provides Additional Reduction in Vector Population Density and Malaria Transmission Rates Compared to Insecticide Treated Nets Alone: A Randomised Control Trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing combined ITN+IRS versus ITN alone for malaria vector control in humans.
population: households in study clusters (general population)
primary_outcome: Anopheles gambiae s.l. vector density and entomological inoculation rate (EIR)
impact_summary: Combining IRS with bendiocarb and ITNs reduced Anopheles gambiae s.l. density by 84% and EIR compared to ITNs alone in northern Tanzania.
effect_metric: percentage reduction in mean An. gambiae s.l. density
transmission_setting: moderate LLIN coverage area with high pyrethroid resistance in An. gambiae s.s., baseline high anopheline density

title: Incidence of malaria by cotrimoxazole use in HIV-infected Ugandan adults on antiretroviral therapy: a randomised, placebo-controlled study.
screening_reason: Double-blind randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing cotrimoxazole prophylaxis versus placebo in HIV-infected adults, with malaria incidence as primary outcome; chemoprevention is a recognized malaria intervention.
population: HIV-infected adults stable on ART and CTX with CD4 cell count at least 250 cells/μl
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria (fever and positive blood slide)
impact_summary: Stopping cotrimoxazole prophylaxis in HIV-infected adults on ART was associated with a higher incidence of malaria compared with continuing cotrimoxazole, though the difference was smaller than previously reported and severe malaria was rare.
safety_summary: Fifteen participants (<1%) experienced severe malaria (incidence 0.30/100 pyrs, CI 0.18-0.49); one malaria-related death occurred in the CTX arm.

title: A randomized trial of the efficacy of artesunate and three quinine regimens in the treatment of severe malaria in children at the Ebolowa Regional Hospital, Cameroon.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of artesunate versus quinine for severe malaria treatment in children with reported efficacy outcomes including fever clearance time, parasite clearance time, and parasitaemia reduction.
population: children aged 3 months to 15 years with severe P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: fever clearance time, time to sit unsupported, time to eat, parasite clearance time, and parasitaemia reduction rate at H24
impact_summary: Artesunate resulted in significantly shorter fever and parasite clearance times and higher parasitaemia reduction at H24 compared to quinine regimens, demonstrating greater efficacy in treating severe malaria in children.

title: Artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of acute uncomplicated malaria in Congolese children under 10 years old living in a suburban area: a randomized study.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcomes comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in children; primary purpose is malaria treatment; not early-phase.
population: children under 10 years old with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria living in a suburban area
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (treatment efficacy) at day 28
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed excellent and similar efficacy in treating uncomplicated malaria in children, with sickle cell trait not affecting treatment outcomes.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response
p_value: 0.5 (AA vs AS in ASAQ group); 0.6 (AA vs AS in AL group)
safety_summary: Adverse events included nausea, jaundice, headache, dizziness, vomiting, pruritus, abdominal pain, and diarrhoea; ASAQ was associated with significantly more frequent adverse events (P < 0.05).

title: Temporal changes in haematocrit following artemisinin-based combination treatments of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing ACT treatments (artesunate-amodiaquine vs artemether-lumefantrine) for uncomplicated falciparum malaria in children, measuring haematocrit changes as a clinical outcome.
population: children with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Temporal changes in haematocrit following ACT treatment
impact_summary: Following ACT treatment for uncomplicated falciparum malaria, haematocrit commonly increased or fell, with declines in haematocrit deficit from <30% being mono-exponential and similar between treatment groups.
p_value: P < 0.0001 (correlation between anaemia half-time and recovery time); P = 0.19 or 0.63 (Bland-Altman bias)
safety_summary: Falls in haematocrit ≥5 units occurred in 23% of children between 14 and 28 days after treatment, associated with higher baseline parasitaemia; no severe adverse events reported in abstract.

title: Efficacy of Olyset® Duo, a permethrin and pyriproxyfen mixture net against wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s. from Côte d'Ivoire: an experimental hut trial.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (bed net with permethrin and pyriproxyfen) that has reported outcome results on mosquito mortality and fertility.
population: wild pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.s. mosquitoes
primary_outcome: Impact on mosquito fertility and fecundity (mortality, blood-feeding, sterilizing effect)
impact_summary: Olyset Duo (permethrin plus pyriproxyfen) had a significant impact on fertility, reducing it by 7-12% relative to control, but no effect on fecundity of wild multi-resistant An. gambiae s.s.
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa, pyrethroid-resistant malaria vector setting

title: Genetic Diversity and Protective Efficacy of the RTS,S/AS01 Malaria Vaccine.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine with reported outcome results (vaccine efficacy against clinical malaria) in children; primary purpose is malaria prevention; not early-phase.
population: infants and children (5 to 17 months and 6 to 12 weeks of age)
primary_outcome: First episodes of clinical malaria within 1 year after vaccination, stratified by circumsporozoite protein genotype match to vaccine
