impact_summary: The RTS,S/AS01 vaccine showed greater efficacy against malaria parasites whose circumsporozoite protein matched the vaccine allele than against mismatched parasites in children 5 to 17 months of age, but not in infants 6 to 12 weeks of age.
funder: National Institutes of Health and others

title: Antimalarial activity of artefenomel (OZ439), a novel synthetic antimalarial endoperoxide, in patients with Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium vivax malaria: an open-label phase 2 trial.
screening_reason: Phase 2 RCT with reported efficacy and safety outcomes in malaria treatment (primary purpose), conducted in patients with P. falciparum and P. vivax.
comparator: none (dose comparison across cohorts, no control arm)
population: adult patients with acute, uncomplicated P falciparum or P vivax malaria
primary_outcome: natural log parasite reduction per 24 h
impact_summary: A single oral dose of artefenomel at 200-1200 mg rapidly cleared parasitaemia in both P falciparum and P vivax malaria with all doses similarly effective and generally mild, reversible adverse effects.
safety_summary: No serious drug-related adverse effects; adverse events generally mild and reversible, most common was asymptomatic increase in plasma creatine phosphokinase; highest adverse event rate in 1200 mg cohort (81%).
funder: Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, Wellcome Trust, and UK Department for International Development

title: Chemopreventive Therapy for Malaria in Ugandan Children
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (DHA/PQ) in children with reported efficacy outcomes in a high-transmission setting.
interventions_raw: trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole (TS; TMP/SMX); sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (SP); dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine (DP)
population: children randomized at 6 months of age, followed to 24 months of age
primary_outcome: Incident Malaria Cases Per Person Year at Risk in HIV-unexposed Participants
impact_summary: Monthly dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine chemoprevention reduced malaria incidence overall, with protective efficacy strongly dependent on piperaquine drug exposure, reaching nearly 100% protection in children with the highest exposure.
effect_estimate: 54% overall (31% low, 67% medium, 97% high PQ exposure groups)

title: Sustained Release Formulation of Primaquine for Prevention of Relapse of Plasmodium vivax Malaria: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Comparative, Multicentric Study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (primaquine for P. vivax relapse prevention) in humans; Phase III or equivalent; not early-phase.
comparator: active comparator (conventional primaquine 15 mg for 14 days)
population: patients with microscopically confirmed P. vivax malaria who were aparasitemic and asymptomatic after chloroquine therapy
primary_outcome: Relapse of P. vivax malaria confirmed by PCR genotyping over six-month follow-up
impact_summary: Primaquine SR 15 mg and SR 30 mg showed comparable low relapse rates and safety to conventional primaquine 15 mg, with SR 30 mg showing significantly better drug compliance.
effect_estimate: 3 relapses (2.86%) with conventional primaquine 15 mg vs 1 relapse (0.93%) with primaquine SR 30 mg
safety_summary: No serious adverse events reported; safety profile comparable between conventional primaquine and SR formulations.

title: Effect of Educational Outreach Timing and Duration on Facility Performance for Infectious Disease Care in Uganda: A Trial with Pre-Post and Cluster Randomized Controlled Components.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating an infectious disease intervention (including malaria care quality) in health facilities; phase not applicable for quality-improvement cluster trials.
comparator: delayed on-site support (OSS) vs immediate OSS; extended OSS vs immediate OSS
population: outpatients at health facilities receiving infectious disease care (emergency triage, malaria, pneumonia services)
primary_outcome: Facility performance indicators for emergency triage, assessment, and treatment; malaria; and pneumonia care
impact_summary: Delayed educational outreach combined with training improved several facility performance indicators similarly to immediate outreach, and extended less-frequent outreach maintained most gains with mixed effects on individual indicators.
effect_estimate: aRR ranged from 0.67 to 2.97 across indicators
p_value: p>0.06 for arm comparisons of delayed vs immediate OSS

title: Efficacy and Safety of Artesunate-Amodiaquine versus Artemether-Lumefantrine in the Treatment of Uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum Malaria in Sentinel Sites across Côte d'Ivoire.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two antimalarial treatments (ASAQ vs AL) for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria with reported outcome results (ACPR, parasite clearance, tolerability).
population: Patients aged 2 years and above with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate Clinical and Parasitological Response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: Both Artesunate-Amodiaquine and Artemether-Lumefantrine showed high efficacy and good tolerability, with no significant difference between the two treatments.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sentinel surveillance sites in Côte d'Ivoire
safety_summary: Both drugs were well tolerated by patients with acceptable clinical and biological tolerability.

title: Ferroquine and artesunate in African adults and children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria: a phase 2, multicentre, randomised, double-blind, dose-ranging, non-inferiority study.
screening_reason: Phase 2 RCT with reported outcome results testing a malaria treatment intervention (ferroquine plus artesunate) in African adults and children.
population: African adults, adolescents, and children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum monoinfection
primary_outcome: Non-inferiority of treatment in terms of PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28 against a reference value of 90%, with a 10% non-inferiority margin
impact_summary: All three dose groups of ferroquine plus artesunate achieved high PCR-corrected cure rates (97-99%) at day 28 and met the non-inferiority hypothesis, with a safety profile consistent with malaria treatment.
effect_estimate: 97% (2 mg/kg), 99% (4 mg/kg), 99% (6 mg/kg) ferroquine plus artesunate vs 79% ferroquine monotherapy
transmission_setting: African endemic settings (Gabon, Burkina Faso, Benin, Kenya)
safety_summary: Most common adverse events were headache in cohort 1 (19%) and worsening malaria in cohort 2 (14%); occurrences were similar between treatment groups, and ferroquine plus artesunate was considered safe at all doses tested.

title: Immunogenicity of the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine and implications for duration of vaccine efficacy: secondary analysis of data from a phase 3 randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT of RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine in African children with reported immunogenicity and efficacy outcome results.
population: African children aged 5-17 months and African infants aged 6-12 weeks at first vaccination
primary_outcome: Association between anti-circumsporozoite antibody titres and magnitude/duration of RTS,S/AS01 vaccine efficacy against clinical malaria
impact_summary: Waning anti-circumsporozoite antibody titres predict the magnitude and duration of RTS,S/AS01 vaccine efficacy against clinical malaria, with efficacy waning more rapidly at higher transmission intensity.
effect_metric: antibody titre associated with 50% protection against infection
transmission_setting: varying transmission intensities across African sites

title: Inhaled Nitric Oxide as an Adjunctive Treatment for Cerebral Malaria in Children: A Phase II Randomized Open-Label Clinical Trial.
screening_reason: This is a published Phase II randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing an adjunctive treatment for cerebral malaria in humans; malaria is the primary focus and outcomes were measured.
population: children with cerebral malaria receiving intravenous artesunate
primary_outcome: Change in plasma angiopoietin-1 (Ang-1) levels after 48 hours of treatment
impact_summary: Inhaled nitric oxide as an adjunctive treatment for cerebral malaria was safe and increased blood methemoglobin and plasma nitrate levels but did not produce a greater increase in plasma Ang-1 compared to nitrogen.
effect_metric: difference in plasma Ang-1 increase at 48 hours
safety_summary: Treatment with inhaled NO was safe; 7 deaths in N2 group vs 4 in NO group; 5 patients in N2 group and 6 in NO group had neurological sequelae at discharge.

title: Efficacy of a novel sublingual spray formulation of artemether in African children with Plasmodium falciparum malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention in humans with reported outcome results; phase III or equivalent.
population: children weighing 5-15 kg with severe/complicated or uncomplicated malaria unable to tolerate oral medication
primary_outcome: Parasitological success, defined as a reduction in parasite count of ≥90% of baseline at 24 h after the first dose
impact_summary: Sublingual artemether resulted in significantly higher parasitological success rates and faster parasite clearance than intravenous quinine in African children with P. falciparum malaria.
effect_estimate: 94.3% (ArTiMist) vs 39.4% (quinine) in study 2; 93.3% vs 66.7% in study 1
transmission_setting: African children with severe, complicated, or uncomplicated malaria
safety_summary: Local tolerability of sublingual artemether was good; no differences between treatments for clinical endpoints such as fever clearance time.

title: Effectiveness and safety of artemether-lumefantrine versus artesunate-amodiaquine for unsupervised treatment of uncomplicated falciparum malaria in patients of all age groups in Nanoro, Burkina Faso: a randomized open label trial.
screening_reason: Published RCT comparing two ACT regimens for uncomplicated malaria treatment with reported outcome results (PCR-corrected cure rates at day 28) across all age groups.
population: patients of all age groups with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28
impact_summary: Under unsupervised, routine drug intake, both ASAQ and AL showed lower than expected efficacy, with PCR-corrected day 28 cure rates of 84.1% for ASAQ and 77.8% for AL, both below the WHO threshold of 90%.
effect_metric: PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
safety_summary: Both AL and ASAQ treatments were well tolerated.

title: A Non-Inferiority, Individually Randomized Trial of Intermittent Screening and Treatment versus Intermittent Preventive Treatment in the Control of Malaria in Pregnancy.
screening_reason: Individually randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two malaria prevention strategies (IPTp-SP vs ISTp-AL) in pregnant women in Africa, addressing the primary malaria prevention intervention.
place: The Gambia, Mali, Burkina Faso, Ghana
population: primi- or secundigravidae (pregnant women)
primary_outcome: Low birth weight, anemia, and placental malaria
impact_summary: Intermittent screening and treatment with RDT and artemether-lumefantrine (ISTp-AL) was non-inferior to intermittent preventive treatment with sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine (IPTp-SP) in preventing low birth weight, anemia, and placental malaria.
transmission_setting: low prevalence of SP resistance areas in West Africa
safety_summary: Hospital admissions for malaria were similar between groups; more episodes of malaria parasitemia between antenatal visits occurred in the ISTp-AL group.

title: A Cluster Randomised Trial Introducing Rapid Diagnostic Tests into Registered Drug Shops in Uganda: Impact on Appropriate Treatment of Malaria.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing a malaria diagnostic intervention (mRDTs in drug shops) as primary purpose in humans.
comparator: presumptive treatment of fevers with ACT (standard care)
population: febrile patients seeking treatment for fever in registered drug shops
primary_outcome: Proportion of febrile patients receiving appropriate treatment with ACT (malaria-positive patients receiving ACT/rectal artesunate and malaria-negative patients not given ACT)
impact_summary: Introducing rapid diagnostic tests in drug shops substantially increased appropriate treatment of malaria with ACT compared to presumptive treatment.
effect_metric: difference in proportion receiving appropriate ACT treatment

title: A randomized trial of artesunate-amodiaquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of acute uncomplicated malaria in pregnancy.
journal: International journal of gynaecology and obstetrics: the official organ of the International Federation of Gynaecology and Obstetrics
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated malaria in pregnant women; primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
population: symptomatic pregnant women (second/third trimester) with malaria parasitemia
primary_outcome: Mean interval to symptomatic relief, day-3 parasite clearance, and day-28 cure rate
impact_summary: Artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed similar efficacy for treating uncomplicated falciparum malaria in pregnancy, but adverse effects were more common with artesunate-amodiaquine.
safety_summary: Adverse effects (body weakness and pruritus) were more common among women assigned to artesunate-amodiaquine (40.0%) than artemether-lumefantrine (2.7%); P<0.001.

title: Insights Into Circulating Cytokine Dynamics During Pregnancy in HIV-Infected Beninese Exposed to Plasmodium falciparum Malaria.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results testing malaria prevention (SP-IPTp and mefloquine) in pregnant women; not early-phase.
population: HIV-infected pregnant women
primary_outcome: Circulating cytokine levels (Th1- and Th2-type) and their association with P. falciparum infection during pregnancy
impact_summary: In HIV-infected pregnant women, circulating IL-10 was associated with P. falciparum infection while IFN-γ appeared to mark anti-malarial protection, with cytokine levels changing between inclusion and delivery.

title: Mefloquine Versus Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine for Intermittent Preventive Treatment in Pregnancy: A Joint Analysis on Efficacy and Tolerability.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing two chemoprevention interventions (mefloquine vs sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine) for malaria prevention in pregnancy, a primary malaria intervention in humans.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Composite/multiple outcome analysis of efficacy (low birth weight, placental malaria, maternal anemia) and tolerability (cutaneous or neuropsychiatric adverse events, low compliance)
impact_summary: Mefloquine was found to be overall superior to sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine for intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy when jointly assessing efficacy and tolerability.
safety_summary: Tolerability assessed via cutaneous or neuropsychiatric adverse events and treatment compliance; mefloquine was non-inferior to SP on these tolerability outcomes.

title: Tailoring a Pediatric Formulation of Artemether-Lumefantrine for Treatment of Plasmodium falciparum Malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing a pediatric antimalarial formulation to standard treatment in children with P. falciparum malaria, with reported efficacy and safety outcome results.
population: African children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected cure rate at day 28
impact_summary: AL Dispersible showed high PCR-corrected cure rates at day 28 comparable to crushed AL tablets (97.8% vs 98.5%).
age_range: children <5 years of age, ≥5 kg body weight
safety_summary: AL Dispersible demonstrated a similar safety profile to crushed and intact AL tablets

title: Malaria preventive therapy in pregnancy and its potential impact on immunity to malaria in an area of declining transmission.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria preventive therapy (IPTp) in pregnancy with reported outcome results on antibody immunity in a low-transmission setting.
comparator: active comparator (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with chloroquine once vs three courses of sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine with azithromycin)
population: pregnant Melanesian women
primary_outcome: Antibody levels to merozoite antigens and opsonizing antibodies to infected erythrocytes between enrolment and delivery
impact_summary: Different antimalarial preventive chemotherapy regimens in pregnancy had limited impact on malaria immunity in this low-transmission setting, with antibodies to recombinant antigens declining similarly in both groups and no significant effect of regimen on antibody levels overall.
p_value: p<0.0001 (decline in recombinant antigen antibodies from enrolment to delivery)

title: Gametocyte Clearance Kinetics Determined by Quantitative Magnetic Fractionation in Melanesian Children with Uncomplicated Malaria Treated with Artemisinin Combination Therapy.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (artemisinin combination therapies) in humans with reported outcome results on gametocyte clearance kinetics.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum and/or Plasmodium vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Gametocyte clearance kinetics (density and prevalence) determined by quantitative magnetic fractionation and mathematical modeling
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine led to a larger initial rise in P. falciparum gametocyte density and slower clearance than artemether-lumefantrine, but was associated with less P. vivax recurrence and gametocytemia.

title: Costs and cost-effectiveness of a large-scale mass testing and treatment intervention for malaria in Southern Province, Zambia.
screening_reason: Published cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria treatment intervention (RDT-based testing and artemether-lumefantrine treatment) reporting outcome results including cost-effectiveness and malaria burden reduction.
population: community members in moderate malaria transmission area
primary_outcome: cost-effectiveness of MTAT (cost per disability adjusted life year averted) and malaria transmission/illness reduction
impact_summary: Dry-season MTAT did not sufficiently reduce malaria transmission to enable transition to case-investigation elimination strategy, but it substantially reduced malaria illness and was highly cost-effective for malaria burden reduction.
effect_metric: incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (cost per DALY averted)
transmission_setting: moderate transmission, dry-season, Southern Province Zambia

title: Health and agricultural productivity: Evidence from Zambia.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results evaluating subsidized bed nets (malaria prevention) as primary intervention in humans; cluster-randomized design appropriate for vector-control trial.
population: rural farmers
primary_outcome: harvest value / agricultural productivity
impact_summary: Farmers given access to free bed nets saw harvest value increase by US$76, about 14.7% higher than the average output value, compared to those without access.

title: Prime-boost vaccination with chimpanzee adenovirus and modified vaccinia Ankara encoding TRAP provides partial protection against Plasmodium falciparum infection in Kenyan adults.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (ChAd63/MVA-TRAP) in humans with reported efficacy outcomes; not early-phase.
population: healthy adult male volunteers
primary_outcome: Time to infection with Plasmodium falciparum as detected by PCR analysis of blood samples three times a week
impact_summary: Vaccination with ChAd63-MVA ME-TRAP reduced the risk of P. falciparum infection by 67% compared to controls during 8 weeks of monitoring.
safety_summary: Not detailed beyond vaccination being conducted with antimalarials given to clear parasitemia; no major safety issues reported in abstract.

title: [Comparison of the effectiveness of artemether and quinine for treatment of severe malaria in children, Bangui, Central African Republic].
journal: Bulletin de la Societe de pathologie exotique (1990)
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemether and quinine for severe malaria treatment in children with reported outcome results (clinical signs regression, parasite clearance, mortality).
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: regression of clinical signs and parasite clearance on day 3
impact_summary: Artemether and quinine showed similar efficacy and safety in treating severe malaria in children, with high rates of clinical and parasitological improvement and low mortality.
effect_metric: proportion with clinical/parasitological improvement at day 3
safety_summary: Death rate was 2.3%, mainly due to anemic and neurological forms; both drugs had similar safety profiles.

title: Randomized Noninferiority Trial of Dihydroartemisinin-Piperaquine Compared with Sulfadoxine-Pyrimethamine plus Amodiaquine for Seasonal Malaria Chemoprevention in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Published RCT of malaria chemoprevention (SMC) intervention with reported efficacy outcomes in children in a seasonal transmission setting.
comparator: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine (active comparator); untreated control cohort
population: children 3 to 59 months old
primary_outcome: Risk of clinical malaria (fever or history of fever with parasite density ≥3,000/μl)
impact_summary: Both DHAPQ and SPAQ were highly efficacious for seasonal malaria chemoprevention, though DHAPQ showed slightly higher risk of malaria attack than SPAQ, with an odds ratio of 1.33.
transmission_setting: highly seasonal malaria transmission, Sahel subregion
safety_summary: Both regimens were highly efficacious and well tolerated.

title: Final results from a pivotal phase 3 malaria vaccine trial.
screening_reason: Published phase 3 RCT with final results reported; malaria vaccine is a primary malaria intervention.

title: Efficacy of sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + artesunate, sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine + amodiaquine, and sulphadoxine-pyrimethamine alone in uncomplicated falciparum malaria in Mali.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (28-day efficacy measured by ACPR) in uncomplicated falciparum malaria treatment, a core malaria intervention.
comparator: SP + amodiaquine and SP alone (active comparators)
population: children aged six to 59 months with uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) at day 28, PCR-adjusted
impact_summary: SP + amodiaquine was as efficacious as SP + artesunate but both were more efficacious than SP alone in treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Mali.
effect_metric: PCR-adjusted adequate clinical and parasitological response (cACPR)
p_value: SP+AS vs SP+AQ p=0.25; SP+AS vs SP p=0.12; SP+AQ vs SP p=0.007
transmission_setting: two villages in Mali, malaria-endemic setting

title: Artemether-lumefantrine versus artemisinin-naphthoquine in Papua New Guinean children with uncomplicated malaria: a six months post-treatment follow-up study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial regimens in children with uncomplicated malaria, with reported outcome results on treatment efficacy and clinical malaria recurrence.
population: young children with uncomplicated malaria
primary_outcome: Time to first episode of clinical malaria within six months post-treatment, assessed by Kaplan-Meier survival analysis
impact_summary: Artemisinin-naphthoquine was associated with fewer clinical malaria episodes than artemether-lumefantrine over six months post-treatment.
effect_metric: proportion with first clinical malaria episode within six months

title: Improving uptake and use of malaria rapid diagnostic tests in the context of artemisinin drug resistance containment in eastern Myanmar: an evaluation of incentive schemes among informal private healthcare providers.
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported results testing malaria RDT uptake interventions among informal healthcare providers, with randomized township allocation and outcome assessment via household surveys and mystery clients.
comparator: RDT price subsidy alone (vs subsidy with financial incentives or subsidy with intensified IEC)
population: informal private healthcare providers and community members with fever in rural townships
primary_outcome: Uptake of RDT use in the community and quality of service provision among informal private healthcare providers
impact_summary: Price subsidy combined with intensified information, education and counselling led to the highest uptake of RDT use and nearly doubled correct treatment following diagnostic test results compared to subsidy alone.
effect_metric: proportion with correct treatment following diagnostic test result
effect_estimate: almost double compared to simple subsidy
transmission_setting: malaria endemic, artemisinin drug resistance containment area in eastern Myanmar, Greater Mekong Sub-region

title: Comparison of azithromycin plus chloroquine versus artemether-lumefantrine for the treatment of uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children in Africa: a randomized, open-label study.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (Day 28 PCR-corrected parasitological clearance) comparing two antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria in children.
population: children with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria, 6-59 months of age
primary_outcome: Proportion of subjects with adequate clinical and parasitological response (PCR corrected) at Day 28 in MITT and PP populations
impact_summary: Azithromycin plus chloroquine was not shown to be non-inferior to artemether-lumefantrine for treatment of uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children, with lower cure rates and more adverse events in the AZCQ group.
effect_metric: difference in PCR-corrected adequate clinical and parasitological response rate (MITT)
safety_summary: Adverse events and early/late treatment failures were more common in subjects receiving azithromycin plus chloroquine compared to artemether-lumefantrine.

title: Enhanced protection against malaria by indoor residual spraying in addition to insecticide treated nets: is it dependent on transmission intensity or net usage?
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria vector control interventions (IRS and ITNs) in humans.
population: children 0.5-14 years old
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum infection prevalence (PfPR)
impact_summary: Adding indoor residual spraying to insecticide treated nets provided additional protection against malaria infection regardless of net usage levels or transmission intensity.
effect_estimate: OR = 0.38 (IRS protection among net users); OR = 0.43 (non-net users)
transmission_setting: north-west Tanzania, varying transmission intensities including areas with pyrethroid insecticide resistance

title: Population-wide malaria testing and treatment with rapid diagnostic tests and artemether-lumefantrine in southern Zambia: a community randomized step-wedge control trial design.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Community randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a malaria treatment intervention (mass test and treatment with artemether-lumefantrine) in humans with clear primary endpoint of malaria prevalence and incidence reduction.
comparator: standard care (control group without MTAT intervention)
population: community residents including children
primary_outcome: Malaria prevalence and health facility outpatient case incidence
impact_summary: Mass test and treatment reduced malaria prevalence and outpatient case incidence but not enough to approach elimination levels.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio (prevalence); incidence rate ratio (outpatient cases)
transmission_setting: southern Zambia, moderate to low transmission targeting elimination

title: The effect of single or repeated home visits on the hanging and use of insecticide-treated mosquito nets following a mass distribution campaign--a cluster randomized, controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating ITN use and hanging following mass distribution, a vector-control malaria prevention intervention.
comparator: no additional visits (exposure to campaign messages only)
population: general population/households following mass ITN distribution campaign
primary_outcome: Net hanging and ITN use (proportion of households with all campaign nets hanging and proportion of population using an ITN the previous night)
impact_summary: Additional hang-up home visits did not significantly improve net hanging or ITN use compared to the control arm, as both increased similarly across all three study arms.
p_value: p<0.0005 for trend in net hanging increase

title: The impact of providing rapid diagnostic malaria tests on fever management in the private retail sector in Ghana: a cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing malaria rapid diagnostic tests (diagnosis intervention) in humans; not early-phase.
comparator: standard practice without rapid diagnostic tests (control arm shops)
population: clients of private drug retail shops with fever, both adults and children
primary_outcome: proportion of clients testing negative for malaria by double-read research blood slide who received an artemisinin combination therapy or other antimalarial
impact_summary: Providing rapid diagnostic tests in private drug retail shops significantly reduced antimalarial dispensing to slide-negative clients without reducing treatment of true malaria cases, and appeared safe.
transmission_setting: poor rural district, high malaria overdiagnosis setting
safety_summary: No safety concerns were identified.

title: Evaluation of intermittent preventive treatment of malaria against group B Streptococcus colonization in pregnant women: a nested analysis of a randomized controlled clinical trial of sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine versus mefloquine.
screening_reason: Published RCT with reported outcome results comparing sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine versus mefloquine for intermittent preventive treatment of malaria in pregnancy, a primary malaria intervention in humans.
design: randomized controlled clinical trial, nested analysis
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Prevalence of recto-vaginal group B Streptococcus (GBS) colonization at delivery compared between IPTp regimens
impact_summary: Sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine-IPTp did not significantly reduce group B Streptococcus colonization prevalence compared with mefloquine-IPTp.
safety_summary: GBS colonization had no impact on birth outcome, anaemia at delivery, gestational age, or birth weight

title: A Randomized Trial to Compare the Safety, Tolerability, and Effectiveness of 3 Antimalarial Regimens for the Prevention of Malaria in Nigerian Patients With Sickle Cell Disease.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing antimalarial chemoprevention regimens (IPT with MQAS/SPAQ vs daily proguanil) for malaria prevention in humans; Phase III equivalent; primary focus is malaria intervention.
population: patients with sickle cell disease
primary_outcome: Protective efficacy against malaria (incidence of malaria episodes)
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with mefloquine-artesunate was well tolerated and more effective than daily proguanil in preventing malaria in patients with sickle cell disease, while sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine showed a less certain benefit.
safety_summary: IPT was well tolerated; most common side effects were vomiting and abdominal pain; adherence to IPT was excellent while adherence to daily proguanil was poor (57% took <75% of doses).

title: Impact of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy with azithromycin-containing regimens on maternal nasopharyngeal carriage and antibiotic sensitivity of Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Staphylococcus aureus: a cross-sectional survey at delivery.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial evaluating intermittent preventive treatment with azithromycin-containing regimens for malaria in pregnancy with reported outcome results on nasopharyngeal carriage and antibiotic susceptibility.
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Maternal nasopharyngeal carriage and antibiotic susceptibility of Streptococcus pneumoniae, Haemophilus influenzae, and Staphylococcus aureus at delivery
impact_summary: Monthly SPAZ-IPTp significantly reduced maternal nasopharyngeal carriage of S. pneumoniae and H. influenzae at delivery compared to SPCQ, but was associated with an increased proportion of macrolide-resistant pneumococcal isolates.
safety_summary: Macrolide-resistant pneumococcal isolates were rare but more commonly detected in the SPAZ group (13.3% vs 2.2%, P=0.033); no other adverse safety findings reported.

title: IFNγ Responses to Pre-erythrocytic and Blood-stage Malaria Antigens Exhibit Differential Associations With Past Exposure and Subsequent Protection.
screening_reason: Published RCT of antimalarial chemoprevention with reported outcome results on malaria protection in a human population.
comparator: chemoprevention (adherent vs nonadherent) vs no chemoprevention
population: children from 1 to 3 years of age
primary_outcome: IFNγ ELISpot response to pre-erythrocytic and blood-stage malaria antigens and association with subsequent protection from malaria
impact_summary: IFNγ responses to blood-stage antigens were common and linked to recent exposure but not protective, while responses to pre-erythrocytic antigens were uncommon but associated with protection from subsequent malaria.

title: Efficacy of indoor residual spraying with dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane against malaria in Gambian communities with high usage of long-lasting insecticidal mosquito nets: a cluster-randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing indoor residual spraying as a malaria vector-control intervention in humans; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
comparator: LLINs alone (no additional indoor residual spraying)
population: children aged 6 months to 14 years
primary_outcome: Incidence of clinical malaria assessed by passive case detection and number of Anopheles gambiae sensu lato mosquitoes collected per light trap per night
impact_summary: Adding indoor residual spraying with DDT to LLINs did not significantly reduce clinical malaria incidence or vector density compared with LLINs alone.
transmission_setting: moderate seasonal transmission, high LLIN coverage, susceptible vectors

title: Efficacy and safety of the mosquitocidal drug ivermectin to prevent malaria transmission after treatment: a double-blind, randomized, clinical trial.
journal: Clinical infectious diseases : an official publication of the Infectious Diseases Society of America
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported outcome results testing ivermectin combined with artemether-lumefantrine to prevent malaria transmission in humans; primary malaria intervention with demonstrated efficacy.
population: asymptomatic Plasmodium falciparum parasite carriers
primary_outcome: Anopheles gambiae and Anopheles funestus mosquito survival and infection rates after mosquito membrane feeding
impact_summary: Adding ivermectin to artemether-lumefantrine increased mosquito mortality and reduced estimated malaria transmission potential by 27% (single dose) and 35% (repeated dose) during the first week of treatment, without evidence of reduced Plasmodium infection rates among surviving mosquitoes.
effect_metric: hazard rate ratio for An. gambiae mosquito mortality after single dose IVM
safety_summary: The AL-IVM combination was well tolerated.

title: Efficacy and safety of triple combination therapy with artesunate-amodiaquine-methylene blue for falciparum malaria in children: a randomized controlled trial in Burkina Faso.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment intervention with reported outcome results; phase IIb is not early-phase.
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: gametocyte prevalence during follow-up, determined by microscopy and QT-NASBA
impact_summary: Adding methylene blue to artesunate-amodiaquine significantly reduced gametocyte prevalence of P. falciparum compared to artesunate-amodiaquine alone, but was associated with lower hemoglobin and more vomiting.
safety_summary: Hemoglobin values were significantly lower in the AS-AQ-MB group at days 2 and 7; vomiting of study medication occurred significantly more frequently in the AS-AQ-MB group.

title: Phase 3 trial with the RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine shows protection against clinical and severe malaria in infants and children in Africa.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT of a malaria vaccine (RTS,S/AS01) with reported outcome results on clinical and severe malaria protection in African children.
population: infants and children
primary_outcome: Protection against clinical and severe malaria
impact_summary: The RTS,S/AS01 malaria vaccine demonstrated protective efficacy against clinical and severe malaria in infants and children across multiple African sites.

title: Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Schoolchildren
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria chemoprevention (intermittent preventive treatment) in schoolchildren with Phase 3 design and reported outcome results.
interventions_raw: sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine; amodiaquine + sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine; dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine; Placebo
population: schoolchildren
primary_outcome: Risk of Parasitaemia (Unadjusted by Genotyping)
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive treatment with antimalarial drug regimens reduced the risk of parasitaemia in schoolchildren compared to placebo.
funder: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

title: Safety and Efficacy of Pyronaridine Artesunate Vs Chloroquine in Children and Adult Patients With Acute Vivax Malaria
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (pyronaridine artesunate vs chloroquine) in humans with reported outcome results (cure rate on day 14).
interventions_raw: Pyronaridine - artesunate; Chloroquine
population: Children and adult patients with acute vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Crude Cure Rate on Day 14
impact_summary: Safety and Efficacy of Pyronaridine Artesunate Vs Chloroquine in Children and Adult Patients With Acute Vivax Malaria

title: Assessing a Risk Model for G6PD Deficiency
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported results testing antimalarial interventions (primaquine and chloroquine+primaquine) for malaria treatment in humans, Phase 4.
interventions_raw: primaquine; chloroquine + primaquine
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Change in Haemoglobin

title: Immunogenicity and Safety Study of GSK Biologicals' Candidate Malaria Vaccine Given at 6, 7.5 and 9 Months of Age in Co-administration With Measles, Rubella and Yellow Fever (YF) Vaccines Followed by a Booster of the Malaria Vaccine.
screening_reason: Phase 3 RCT of malaria vaccine with reported outcome results on immunogenicity.
interventions_raw: Vitamin A; Candidate Plasmodium falciparum malaria vaccine; MR-Vac; Stamaril
comparator: co-administered vaccines (measles, rubella, yellow fever) with staggered/control schedule
population: infants aged 6, 7.5 and 9 months at vaccination, receiving measles, rubella and yellow fever vaccines
primary_outcome: Anti-Circumsporozoite (Anti-CS) Antibody Concentrations, One Month Post Dose 3 of SB257049 (Primary Analysis)
impact_summary: The study evaluated immunogenicity and safety of a candidate malaria vaccine given at 6, 7.5 and 9 months of age co-administered with measles, rubella and yellow fever vaccines, followed by a booster dose.

title: Efficacy of 3 Regimens of Chloroquine and Primaquine for Treatment of P. Vivax Malaria, Cruzeiro do Sul, Acre, Brazil
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of malaria treatment (chloroquine and primaquine for P. vivax) with posted results and non-early phase.
interventions_raw: Primaquine
population: patients with P. vivax malaria
primary_outcome: Participants With Adequate Clinical and Parasitologic Response Among Patients Enrolled
impact_summary: The trial compared 3 regimens of chloroquine plus primaquine for treatment of P. vivax malaria to assess adequate clinical and parasitologic response.
funder: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

title: Artemisinin-Based Combination Therapy: Clinical Trials in Cameroon
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (cure rate on day 28) evaluating malaria treatment interventions in Phase 3.
interventions_raw: 1. Artemether-Lumefantrine (AL); 2. Amodiaquine-Artesunate (AQ-AS)
primary_outcome: Cure Rate on Day 28
funder: London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine

title: Double-blind, Randomized, Controlled Study of Safety, Immunogenicity and Efficacy of a Candidate Malaria Vaccine
screening_reason: Phase 2 RCT with reported efficacy outcome (time to first clinical P. falciparum malaria episode) in a malaria vaccine trial.
interventions_raw: FMP1/AS02A; RabAvert
primary_outcome: Subjects Time to First Clinical Episode of P Falciparum Malaria During the Efficacy Follow-up Period Adjusted for Time at Risk - Intent to Treat (ITT) Population
impact_summary: The FMP1/AS02A candidate malaria vaccine was assessed for safety, immunogenicity and efficacy against P. falciparum malaria compared to an active comparator vaccine.
funder: U.S. Army Medical Research and Development Command

title: Consistency of Immunogenicity and Non Inferiority of GSK Biologicals' Candidate Malaria Vaccine Lots in Children
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine in Phase 3 with results posted.
interventions_raw: GSK Biologicals' candidate Plasmodium falciparum malaria vaccine (257049)
population: children
primary_outcome: Anti-Circumsporozoite (Anti-CS) Antibody Titers
impact_summary: The trial evaluated consistency of immunogenicity and non-inferiority across different lots of GSK Biologicals' candidate malaria vaccine in children.

title: R21/Matrix-M Protects Against Dermal but not Against Venous Parasites in Human Challenge Studies
screening_reason: This is a randomized controlled human malaria challenge infection study (CHMI) evaluating malaria vaccine efficacy with reported outcome results (protection rates), meeting all inclusion criteria.
comparator: ME-TRAP-based viral vectored vaccine, unvaccinated/challenge control
population: healthy adult volunteers undergoing controlled human malaria infection
primary_outcome: Proportion of volunteers meeting treatment criteria (i.e., developing blood-stage parasitemia) following controlled human malaria infection via intradermal or direct venous inoculation of sporozoites
impact_summary: R21/Matrix-M vaccination protected against intradermal sporozoite challenge (0/12 met treatment criteria) but provided no protection against direct venous inoculation of sporozoites (5/5 met treatment criteria).
transmission_setting: controlled human malaria infection (experimental, non-endemic setting)

title: Efficacy of Attractive Targeted Sugar Bait stations against malaria in Western Province Zambia: epidemiological findings from a two-arm cluster randomized Phase III trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention with reported outcome results (clinical incidence and prevalence) in a Phase III setting.
comparator: no ATSB (standard of care vector control - insecticide-treated nets and/or indoor residual spraying)
population: children aged 1-14 years (clinical malaria cohort) and individuals over six months (prevalence surveys)
n_total: 70 clusters; 4494 children in cohort; 2536 individuals in cross-sectional surveys
primary_outcome: Clinical malaria incidence among two consecutive seasonal cohorts of children aged 1-14 years, followed up monthly January-June in 2022 and 2023
impact_summary: Attractive targeted sugar bait stations did not significantly reduce clinical malaria incidence or P. falciparum prevalence compared to control in rural western Zambia.
follow_up: monthly follow-up January-June 2022 and 2023 (two 6-month transmission seasons)
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission season, rural western Zambia
age_range: 1-14 years (clinical incidence cohort); over 6 months (prevalence survey)
safety_summary: No serious adverse events associated with the intervention were reported.

title: Evaluating malaria elimination strategies in military forces in Cambodia: a cluster-randomized clinical trial comparing monthly prophylaxis with focused screening and treatment
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial comparing two malaria elimination strategies (MMP vs FSAT) in humans with reported outcome results; malaria is the primary focus; phase is not applicable for cluster-randomized elimination trials.
design: cluster-randomized, factorial (sub-randomized to permethrin-treated vs sham clothing)
population: military personnel (volunteers) along the Cambodian-Thai border
primary_outcome: P. falciparum and P. vivax positivity (by RDT, PCR, microscopy) over 6 months of follow-up
impact_summary: Monthly malaria prophylaxis (MMP) was safe and more effective than focused screening and treatment (FSAT) in reducing both P. falciparum and P. vivax positivity over 6 months.
effect_metric: absolute risk reduction in Pf positivity
safety_summary: The 22.5mg weekly primaquine MMP regimen was safe, including in the 15% of volunteers with G6PD-deficiency; 32% of Pf cases treated with DP as MMP recrudesced and required rescue treatment with artesunate-mefloquine.

title: Safety and efficacy of the blood-stage malaria vaccine RH5.1/Matrix-M in Burkina Faso: interim results of a double-blind, randomised, controlled phase 2b trial in children
screening_reason: Double-blind RCT with reported interim efficacy results for a blood-stage malaria vaccine in children; Phase 2b is not early-phase.
population: children aged 5-17 months
primary_outcome: Safety and reactogenicity of RH5.1/Matrix-M; protective efficacy against clinical malaria from 14 days to 6 months post-third vaccination
impact_summary: RH5.1/Matrix-M vaccine was safe, well tolerated, and showed vaccine efficacy of 55% with a delayed third dose regimen and 40% with a monthly regimen against clinical malaria compared to pooled controls.
safety_summary: Favourable safety profile; most adverse events mild, most common were local swelling and fever; no serious adverse events reported
funder: European and Developing Countries Clinical Trials Partnership; UK Medical Research Council; National Institute for Health and Care Research Oxford Biomedical Research Centre; Division of Intramural Research, National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases; US Agency for International Development; Wellcome Trust

title: Artemether-lumefantrine-amodiaquine or artesunate-amodiaquine combined with single low-dose primaquine to reducePlasmodium falciparummalaria transmission in Ouélessébougou, Mali: a five-arm, phase 2, single-blind, randomised clinical trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment interventions to reduce transmission; Phase 2 is not early-phase.
design: five-arm, single-blind, phase 2, randomised clinical trial, per protocol analysis
comparator: artemether-lumefantrine alone (active comparator) and comparison across combination regimens with/without primaquine
population: asymptomatic P. falciparum microscopy-detected gametocyte carriers aged 10-50 years
primary_outcome: Within-person percentage reduction in mosquito infection rate at 48 hours after treatment initiation compared to pre-treatment, assessed by direct membrane feeding assay
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine, with or without amodiaquine, and artesunate-amodiaquine plus primaquine nearly eliminated mosquito infectivity within 48 hours, whereas artesunate-amodiaquine alone left substantial residual transmission.
effect_metric: median percentage reduction in mosquito infection rate
safety_summary: No serious adverse events occurred

title: Artemisinin-naphthoquine plus lower-dose primaquine to treat and prevent recurrence of Plasmodium vivax malaria: an open-label randomized and non-inferiority trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing artemisinin-naphthoquine plus primaquine versus chloroquine plus primaquine for P. vivax malaria treatment with reported outcome results on efficacy, safety, and recurrence.
population: patients with P. vivax malaria infection
primary_outcome: Recurrence-free proportion of patients with P. vivax malaria at day 182/365
impact_summary: The artemisinin-naphthoquine plus lower-dose primaquine over 3 days (ANPQ3) regimen was not non-inferior to chloroquine plus primaquine over 14 days (CQPQ14) in preventing recurrence, but cleared fever and parasites faster, had fewer severe adverse effects, and had better medication adherence.
effect_metric: difference in recurrence-free patients (percentage points) by day 182
safety_summary: No severe adverse effects in group ANPQ3; 5 (3.9%) patients with acute haemolysis in group CQPQ14 (P=0.013)

title: Artemether-lumefantrine with or without single-dose primaquine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine with or without single-dose tafenoquine to reducePlasmodium falciparumtransmission: a phase 2 single-blind randomised clinical trial in Ouelessebougou, Mali
screening_reason: Phase 2 randomized clinical trial with reported outcome results testing malaria treatment interventions (artemether-lumefantrine and sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine-amodiaquine with/without transmission-blocking drugs) in humans.
comparator: artemether-lumefantrine alone vs with primaquine; sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine alone vs with tafenoquine
population: asymptomatic individuals aged 10-50 years with P. falciparum gametocytaemia
primary_outcome: Median within-person percent change in mosquito infection rate in infectious individuals from baseline to day 2 (artemether-lumefantrine groups) or day 7 (sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine groups) post treatment, assessed by direct membrane feeding assay
impact_summary: Artemether-lumefantrine alone nearly completely prevented mosquito infections, whereas sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine plus amodiaquine left considerable post-treatment transmission that was reduced by adding tafenoquine.
effect_metric: median percentage reduction in mosquito infection rate
transmission_setting: seasonal malaria transmission setting in Mali

title: Malaria and other risk factors for malnutrition, and the impact of intermittent preventive therapy for malaria on nutritional status of school-age children in Tanzania. A cross-sectional survey and a randomized controlled open-label trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of intermittent preventive therapy for malaria in school-age children with reported outcome results on nutritional status and malaria prevalence.
design: cross-sectional survey and randomized controlled open-label trial
population: school-age children (≤10 years)
primary_outcome: nutritional status (weight, height, BMI) over time
impact_summary: Intermittent preventive therapy with DP or ASAQ did not significantly affect change in weight, height, or BMI over time compared to the control group, though malaria at baseline was associated with higher odds of stunting.
effect_metric: adjusted odds ratio (stunting associated with malaria)

title: Will a lack of fabric durability be their downfall? Impact of textile durability on the efficacy of three types of dual-active-ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets: A secondary analysis on malaria prevalence and incidence from a cluster-randomized trial in north-west Tanzania
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating dual-AI long-lasting insecticidal nets for malaria prevention; vector-control trial so early-phase exclusion does not apply.
population: community residents and a cohort of children
primary_outcome: Malaria infection prevalence and case incidence in relation to net textile condition (damaged/torn vs intact)
impact_summary: Torn nets showed reduced protection against malaria, but Chlorfenapyr-PY and PBO-PY LLINs maintained superior protection compared to pyrethroid-only nets even when torn.
effect_estimate: 0.76 (good condition vs extremely torn); 0.37 (too-torn PBO-PY vs intact PY); 0.45 (too-torn Chlorfenapyr-PY vs intact PY); 0.49 (intact Chlorfenapyr-PY vs intact PY, year 2)
transmission_setting: high malaria transmission, pyrethroid-resistant vector settings

title: Impact of textile durability on the efficacy of three types of dual-active-ingredient long- lasting insecticidal nets: A secondary analysis on malaria prevalence and incidence from a cluster-randomized trial in north-west Tanzania
screening_reason: Secondary analysis of a cluster-randomized controlled trial reporting outcome results on malaria prevalence and incidence from a vector-control intervention (dual-active-ingredient LLINs) in humans.
population: community members and a cohort of children
primary_outcome: Malaria infection prevalence and case incidence in relation to net textile condition (damaged/torn vs intact) across four LLIN types
impact_summary: Torn Dual-AI LLINs (chlorfenapyr-PY and PBO-PY) still provided better protection against malaria case incidence than intact pyrethroid-only nets, though net textile damage was not significantly associated with malaria prevalence overall.
effect_estimate: 0.76 (good condition vs extremely torn nets, all types); 0.37 (too-torn PBO-PY vs intact PY-only); 0.45 (too-torn Chlorfenapyr-PY vs intact PY-only); 0.49 (intact Chlorfenapyr-PY vs intact PY-only, year 2)
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic, pyrethroid-resistant vector setting in north-west Tanzania

title: Community benefits of mass distribution of three types of dual-active-ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets against malaria prevalence in Tanzania: evidence from a 3-year cluster-randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial reporting outcome results (malaria prevalence measured via cross-sectional surveys) for dual-AI long-lasting insecticidal nets, a primary malaria prevention intervention in humans.
design: cluster-randomized controlled trial, secondary analysis, 3-year, 5 cross-sectional surveys
population: children aged 6 months to 14 years
primary_outcome: Malaria infection prevalence (by rapid diagnostic test) among net users versus non-users at different community-level net usage levels
impact_summary: Community-level usage of more than 40% of dual-active-ingredient LLINs was associated with significant protection against malaria infection among non-net users compared to non-users in clusters with high pyrethroid-only LLIN usage.
effect_estimate: chlorfenapyr-PY: 0.44; PBO-PY: 0.55; pyriproxyfen-PY: 0.61 (community usage >40% vs PY-only >40%)
funder: Department for International Development, UK Medical Research Council, Wellcome Trust, Department of Health and Social Care (#MR/R006040/1), Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation via the Innovative Vector Control Consortium (IVCC)

title: Assessing the impact of group antenatal care on uptake of intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy in Atlantique Department, Benin, 2021-2023: a cluster randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results assessing intermittent preventive treatment for malaria in pregnancy (IPTp3), a WHO-recommended malaria prevention intervention in humans.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Coverage of at least 4 ANC visits (ANC4) and IPTp3 uptake, assessed via difference-in-difference approach comparing pre- and post-implementation household surveys
impact_summary: G-ANC did not significantly improve population-level ANC4 or IPTp3 coverage compared to individual ANC, but among women who actually participated in G-ANC, both ANC4 and IPTp3 uptake were significantly higher.
p_value: 0.004 (IPTp3 participation), 0.002 (ANC4 participation); 0.26 (IPTp3 arm comparison), 0.51 (ANC4 arm comparison)

title: Feasibility and safety of integrating mass drug administration for helminth control with seasonal malaria chemoprevention among Senegalese children: a randomized controlled, observer-blind trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing seasonal malaria chemoprevention integrated with helminth mass drug administration in children; malaria is a primary focus.
comparator: Vitamin A and Zinc plus SMC drugs (control group)
population: children aged 1-14 years
primary_outcome: Feasibility and safety (adverse events) of combining mass drug administration for helminths with seasonal malaria chemoprevention
impact_summary: Integrating MDA for schistosomiasis and STH with SMC was safe and feasible among Senegalese children, though vomiting was more common in the intervention groups than the control group.
follow_up: 6 days post-intervention (adverse events); pre- and post-intervention blood/stool sampling
safety_summary: Mild, transient vomiting occurred in 12.6% (treatment group 2), 10.6% (treatment group 1), and 4.2% (control group), a significant difference (p=0.005); praziquantel plus SMC was associated with lower risk of severe anaemia than SMC alone (not statistically significant).

title: LLIN Evaluation in Uganda Project (LLINEUP2) – Effect of long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) treated with pyrethroid plus pyriproxyfen vs LLINs treated with pyrethroid plus piperonyl butoxide in Uganda: a cluster-randomised trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomised controlled trial of malaria vector control (LLINs) with reported outcome results (malaria incidence, parasite prevalence, anaemia) in humans.
comparator: pyrethroid-PBO LLINs (PermaNet 3.0) vs pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen LLINs (Royal Guard)
population: residents of all ages in 32 high-burden districts not receiving indoor residual spraying; community surveys in children aged 2-10 years and 2-4 years for anaemia
primary_outcome: Malaria incidence in residents of all ages, estimated per cluster from enhanced health facility surveillance data
impact_summary: There was no significant difference in malaria incidence, parasite prevalence, or anaemia prevalence between clusters receiving pyrethroid-PBO LLINs and those receiving pyrethroid-pyriproxyfen LLINs two years after mass distribution.
transmission_setting: high-burden districts in Uganda not receiving indoor residual spraying
age_range: all ages (incidence); children 2-10 years (parasite prevalence); children 2-4 years (anaemia)
funder: US National Institutes for Health, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation

title: Efficacy of Quinine Plus Clindamycin Versus Artemether-Lumefantrine For The Treatment of Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria In Kenyan Children (CLINDAQUINE): An Open-Label Randomised Trial
screening_reason: This is a Phase 3 RCT comparing antimalarial treatments for uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in children with reported outcome results (ACPR rates and safety data at day 28).
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: PCR-corrected rate of adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR) on day 28 in the per-protocol population
impact_summary: Quinine plus clindamycin was markedly less effective than artemether-lumefantrine for treating uncomplicated P. falciparum malaria in Kenyan children, with no evidence supporting its use.
effect_metric: treatment difference in PCR-corrected ACPR rate
safety_summary: Three serious adverse events occurred in the quinine plus clindamycin group.

title: Durable wall lining for malaria control in Liberia: results of a cluster randomized trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results testing a novel vector-control intervention (insecticidal wall liners) for malaria prevention in humans; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
design: cluster-randomized controlled trial, paired cluster design
population: children 2-59 months
primary_outcome: Plasmodium falciparum prevalence in children 2-59 months measured by rapid diagnostic tests before and 12, 18 and 24 months after installation
impact_summary: P. falciparum prevalence after 12 months was lower in intervention clusters (34.6%) than control clusters (40.1%), but the difference was not statistically significant.

title: Community evaluation of VECTRONTM T500, a broflanilide insecticide, for indoor residual spraying for malaria vector control in Central Benin; a two arm non-inferiority cluster randomised trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial of indoor residual spraying (IRS) with broflanilide for malaria vector control that has reported outcome results including vector densities, sporozoite rates, and entomological inoculation rates.
population: Households and communities in an area with pyrethroid-resistant Anopheles gambiae s.l. and high pyrethroid-only net coverage
primary_outcome: Vector density indicated by human biting rate (bites/person/night) indoors and outdoors
impact_summary: VECTRONTM T500 was non-inferior to Fludora® Fusion in reducing indoor and outdoor human biting rates and had prolonged residual efficacy on house walls lasting over 24 months.
effect_metric: Incidence Rate Ratio (IRR) for human biting rate
transmission_setting: High-intensity pyrethroid resistance area with high coverage of pyrethroid-only nets, Central Benin
safety_summary: Perceived adverse events reported by spray operators and householders were generally very low (<6%) in both study arms.

title: Efficacy and Safety of Pyronaridine-Artesunate Versus Artemether-Lumefantrine in the Treatment of Acute Uncomplicated Malaria in Children in South-West Nigeria: An open- labelled randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarials for treatment of uncomplicated malaria in children; primary purpose is malaria treatment in humans.
population: children aged 3 to 144 months with fever and microscopically confirmed Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Day 28 adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
impact_summary: Pyronaridine-artesunate showed a significantly higher day-28 adequate clinical and parasitological response than artemether-lumefantrine in children with uncomplicated malaria in Nigeria.
effect_metric: Day 28 adequate clinical and parasitological response (ACPR)
safety_summary: Both ACTs were well-tolerated; adverse events included fever, chills and rigors, anorexia, cough and headache similar to malaria symptoms; blood chemistry and liver function tests mostly normal with occasional marginal rise; no serious adverse events in either arm.

title: Efficacy of Three Antimalarial Regimens for Uncomplicated Plasmodium Falciparum Malaria in Cambodia, 2009 – 2011: A Randomized Control Trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported efficacy outcomes for malaria treatment in humans; phase III equivalent; primary purpose is malaria intervention.
design: randomized, open-label, parallel group controlled trial, phase 3
comparator: active comparator (three antimalarial regimens compared against each other: AS/MQ, DHA/PPQ, ATQ/PG)
population: subjects at least 5 years old with uncomplicated Falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Per-protocol PCR-adjusted efficacy at 42 days
impact_summary: DHA/PPQ and ATQ/PG had acceptable efficacy against uncomplicated falciparum malaria, while AS/MQ efficacy was only 80.6% due to apparent mefloquine resistance.
transmission_setting: multi-drug resistance epicenter, Northern Cambodia-Thai border
safety_summary: One subject withdrew from the ATQ/PG arm due to drug allergy.

title: Measuring effects of ivermectin-treated cattle on malaria vectors in Vietnam: a village-randomized trial
screening_reason: Village-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results testing ivermectin-treated cattle as a malaria vector control intervention in humans' environment; not early-phase.
impact_summary: Under laboratory conditions, IVM has been shown to reduce the survival of Anopheles populations that have fed on IVM-treated mammals.

title: A randomized, double-blind placebo-control study assessing the protective efficacy of an odour-based ‘push-pull’ malaria vector control strategy in reducing human-vector contact
screening_reason: Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial with reported outcome results (biting rates, indoor densities) for a malaria vector-control intervention (spatial repellent); cluster/household-level design does not require early-phase exclusion.
impact_summary: The ‘push’ reduced indoor vector densities dominated by Anopheles funestus by around two thirds.

title: Monthly sulfadoxine/pyrimethamine-amodiaquine or dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine as malaria chemoprevention in young Kenyan children with sickle cell anemia: A randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing malaria chemoprevention regimens (SP-AQ and DP versus Proguanil) in children with sickle cell anemia with reported outcome results on clinical malaria incidence and secondary endpoints.
impact_summary: The comparative efficacy of prevention regimens is largely unknown.

title: Randomized clinical trial to assess the protective efficacy of a Plasmodium vivax CS synthetic vaccine
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of a malaria vaccine (P. vivax CS subunit) with reported efficacy outcomes (sterile protection rates) in humans.
impact_summary: A randomized, double-blind, controlled clinical trial was conducted to assess the safety and protective efficacy of the Plasmodium vivax circumsporozoite (CS) protein.

title: Malaria Positivity Following a Single Oral Dose of Azithromycin Among Children in Burkina Faso: A Randomized Controlled Trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial of an antimalarial intervention (azithromycin) in children with reported outcome results (malaria positivity by RDT at 14 days).
impact_summary:
Background:

Azithromycin is a broad-spectrum antibiotic that has moderate antimalarial activity and has been shown to reduce all-cause mortality when biannually administered to children under five in high mortality settings in sub-Saharan Africa.

title: Effectiveness of three-year old piperonyl butoxide and pyrethroid-treated long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs) versus pyrethroid-only LLINs against malaria infection: results of a cluster randomised trial in Tanzania
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of PBO-LLINs versus pyrethroid-only LLINs for malaria prevention with reported outcome results over 3 years in Tanzania; vector control is an eligible malaria intervention.
impact_summary:
Background

After decades of success in reducing malaria through the scale-up of pyrethroid long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs), malaria decline has stalled, coinciding with the rapid spread of pyrethroid resistance.

title: Improving outcomes for children with malaria, diarrhoea and pneumonia in Mozambique through the inSCALE technology innovation: A cluster randomised controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a technology intervention to improve malaria treatment and outcomes in children under 5 in Mozambique; malaria is a primary focus alongside diarrhoea and pneumonia.
impact_summary: Population surveys were conducted at baseline and after 18 months in all districts to assess the impact of the intervention on the coverage of appropriate treatment for malaria, diarrhoea and pneumonia in children 2-59months of age, on prevalence of cases of these conditions, and on a range of secon

title: Serological evaluation of a cluster randomised trial on the use of reactive focal mass drug administration and reactive vector control to reduce malaria transmission in Zambezi Region, Namibia
screening_reason: This is a cluster randomised controlled trial reporting outcome results from a 2017 trial evaluating reactive focal mass drug administration and reactive vector control for malaria transmission reduction, with serological endpoints demonstrating significant intervention effects.
impact_summary: Reductions in sero-prevalence to antigens Etramp.Ag1, Pf MSP1 19 , Rh2.2030, and Pf AMA1 were observed in study arms combining rfMDA and RAVC, but only effects for Etramp5.Ag1 were statistically significant.

title: Interaction Between Insecticide Resistance-Associated Genes and Malaria Transmission in Anopheles Gambiae S. L. During a Cluster-Randomized Controlled Trial of A “lethal House Lure” in Central Côte D’ivoire
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria vector-control intervention (EaveTubes) that has reported outcome results on insecticide resistance and malaria transmission in Anopheles mosquitoes.
design: cluster-randomized controlled trial, two-armed, entomological substudy
comparator: standard care (no household screening/EaveTubes) vs household screening plus In2Care EaveTubes
population: wild Anopheles gambiae s.l. mosquitoes captured by human landing catches
primary_outcome: Association between Kdr L1014F and Ace-1R G119S insecticide resistance mutations and Plasmodium infection status in An. gambiae s.l.
impact_summary: Kdr L1014F and Ace-1R G119S resistance mutations were significantly more frequent in An. gambiae than An. coluzzii, but neither mutation was significantly associated with Plasmodium infection status in either species.
effect_estimate: 59.64 (Kdr, An. gambiae vs An. coluzzii); 2.79 (Ace-1R, An. gambiae vs An. coluzzii)
species: Plasmodium sp. (unspecified, likely P. falciparum predominant)

title: High efficacy of microbial larvicides for malaria vectors control in the city of Yaounde Cameroon: a cluster randomised study
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of microbial larvicide (vector-control intervention) for malaria with reported outcome results (reduction in vector density and entomological inoculation rate).
population: urban residents in clusters within the city of Yaoundé (entomological outcomes)
primary_outcome: Biting anopheline density collected using CDC light traps
impact_summary: Larviciding with VectoMax G reduced anopheline breeding habitats by over 85%, adult anopheline biting density by 68%, and entomological inoculation rate by 79% compared to non-intervention areas.
safety_summary: No significant impact of the larvicide VectoMax on aquatic microfauna diversity (non-target organisms).

title: LLIN Evaluation in Uganda Project (LLINEUP) – Effect of Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets with and Without Piperonyl Butoxide on Malaria Indicators in Uganda 25 Months after Distribution: A Cluster-Randomised Trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomised trial of malaria vector control (PBO LLINs) with reported outcome results (parasite prevalence and entomology endpoints) at 25 months.
population: children aged 2-10 years in surveyed households
primary_outcome: Parasite prevalence by microscopy in children aged 2-10 years
impact_summary: PBO LLINs reduced malaria parasite prevalence and Anopheles mosquito density more than conventional pyrethroid-only LLINs 25 months after distribution.
safety_summary: Not reported; authors declare no competing interests, no safety issues mentioned.
funder: Against Malaria Foundation, UK Department for International Development, Innovative Vector Control Consortium, Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation

title: Entomological Effects of Attractive Targeted Sugar Bait Station Deployment in Western Zambia: Vector Surveillance Findings from a Two-arm Cluster Randomized Phase III Trial
screening_reason: Two-arm cluster-randomized controlled trial (Phase III) of malaria vector control intervention (ATSB stations) in humans that has reported entomological outcome results (vector abundance, parity, EIR, sporozoite prevalence).
comparator: standard vector control without ATSB stations (control clusters)
population: Anopheles funestus mosquito populations in study clusters (entomological surveillance)
primary_outcome: Entomological indicators including An. funestus parity, abundance, biting rates, sporozoite prevalence, and entomological inoculation rates (EIR)
impact_summary: ATSB deployment was associated with a non-significant 35% reduction in vector light trap density, with no significant effects on parity, HLC rates, sporozoite prevalence, or EIR.
transmission_setting: high-burden, high transmission area with Anopheles funestus as dominant vector

title: A Cluster Randomized Trial of Delivery of Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy at the Community Level in Malawi
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of IPTp delivery in pregnancy (a WHO-recommended malaria prevention strategy in humans) with reported outcome results on coverage; phase not applicable for community-level delivery trials.
design: cluster randomized controlled trial, difference in differences analysis
population: pregnant women; women who delivered in the prior 12 months
primary_outcome: Coverage of IPTp3+ (at least three doses of intermittent preventive treatment in pregnancy) and ANC visits
impact_summary: Community health worker delivery of IPTp did not significantly increase IPTp3+ coverage compared to health facility delivery, though ANC4+ coverage increased significantly more in the intervention group.
p_value: not significant (for IPTp3+); significant for ANC4+ (95% CI excludes 0)
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Effectiveness and safety of reactive focal mass drug administration (rfMDA) using dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine to reduce malaria transmission in very low-endemic setting of Eswatini: a pragmatic cluster randomised controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of a malaria elimination intervention (rfMDA vs RACD) in humans with reported outcome results on malaria incidence.
comparator: reactive case detection (RACD) using RDTs and artemether lumefantrine
population: individuals residing near confirmed malaria index cases in a very low-endemic setting
primary_outcome: cluster-level cumulative confirmed malaria incidence among clusters with cases
impact_summary: rfMDA using dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine was safe and resulted in lower cumulative malaria incidence than RACD, but the trial could not confirm its effectiveness, likely due to insufficient statistical power.
effect_estimate: 0.93 for all malaria; 0.77 for locally acquired malaria
safety_summary: No serious adverse events occurred; rfMDA using DP was safe with 98.7% adherence.

title: Improving malaria preventive practices and pregnancy outcomes through a health education intervention: a randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results on malaria prevention interventions (ITN use, IPTp uptake, haematocrit levels) in pregnant women in Nigeria.
population: pregnant women attending antenatal care
primary_outcome: Malaria preventive practices (ITN use, IPTp uptake) and pregnancy outcomes (haematocrit levels, malaria diagnosis, birth weight)
impact_summary: The health education intervention based on the IMB model significantly improved reported ITN use, reported IPTp uptake, and haematocrit levels, but had no significant effect on reported malaria diagnosis or birth weight.
follow_up: 4 months post-intervention and at end of pregnancy

title: Monitoring of Fabric Integrity and Attrition Rate of Dual-Active Ingredient Long-Lasting Insecticidal Nets in Tanzania: A Prospective Cohort Study Nested in a Cluster Randomized Controlled Trial
screening_reason: Cluster randomized controlled trial of malaria vector-control intervention (dual-active ingredient LLINs) with reported outcome results on net durability and attrition.
design: prospective cohort study nested in a cluster randomized controlled trial
population: households in villages receiving distributed LLINs
primary_outcome: survivorship and fabric integrity of LLINs assessed at 6, 12, 24, 30 and 36 months
impact_summary: All dual active ingredient LLINs had poor textile durability with median functional survival less than three years, with OlysetTM Plus performing worst and having the shortest survival.
effect_estimate: 1.9 years (Interceptor®, Interceptor® G2, Royal Guard®); 0.9 years (OlysetTM Plus)

title: Effect of biannual azithromycin distribution on antibody responses to malaria, bacterial, and protozoan pathogens among children: A cluster-randomized, placebo-controlled trial in Niger
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results assessing a malaria intervention (azithromycin distribution) in children; cluster-randomized trials are accepted and phase does not apply to this design.
design: cluster-randomized, placebo-controlled, double-masked, repeated cross-sectional secondary analysis
population: children ages 1-59 months
primary_outcome: IgG-based antibody responses (seroprevalence and seroconversion rates) to malaria, bacterial, and protozoan pathogens
impact_summary: Biannual azithromycin distribution was associated with lower Campylobacter spp. seroprevalence and seroconversion rate compared to placebo, with no significant differences for other pathogens including P. falciparum.
safety_summary: Not reported in this analysis; study noted masking of participants, investigators, and analysts and high treatment coverage

title: Efficacy and safety of artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine and prevalence of molecular markers associated with resistance, Guinea: an open-label two-arm randomised controlled trial
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial comparing two artemisinin-based antimalarial drugs with reported 28-day efficacy and safety outcomes in children with uncomplicated malaria.
design: open-label, two-arm, randomised controlled trial, phase 3
population: children aged 6-59 months with uncomplicated Plasmodium falciparum malaria
primary_outcome: Kaplan-Meier estimate of Day 28 efficacy after correction by microsatellite-genotyping
impact_summary: Both artesunate-amodiaquine and artemether-lumefantrine showed high (99-100%) corrected efficacy at Day 28 with no evidence of artemisinin resistance-associated pfk13 mutations.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic sentinel sites (Maferinyah and Labé Health Districts, Guinea)
