safety_summary: Both ASAQ and AL were found to be safe with no early treatment failures observed in any study arm.

title: Cost-effectiveness of Insecticide-treated wall liner and indoor residual spraying as additions to insecticide-treated bed nets to prevent malaria: findings from cluster randomized trials in Tanzania
screening_reason: Cluster randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (ITWL efficacy failure, IRS efficacy 57%) evaluating malaria prevention interventions (ITWL and IRS supplements to bed nets) in humans.
design: cluster-randomized, two-arm, controlled trial (44 clusters); cost-effectiveness analysis
comparator: IRS efficacy compared against LLINs alone (from Muleba trial); ITWL trial compared ITWL+LLIN vs LLIN alone
population: households in malaria-endemic areas of Muheza and Muleba, Tanzania
primary_outcome: Efficacy and cost-effectiveness of ITWL and IRS as supplements to LLINs in preventing malaria (DALYs averted, incremental cost-effectiveness ratio)
impact_summary: The ITWL trial was stopped early because the wall liner lost its insecticidal effect within 90 days, while IRS was found to be effective (57% efficacy) but more cost-effective than ITWL at averting malaria-related DALYs.
transmission_setting: malaria-endemic, seasonal transmission areas of Tanzania
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; ITWL trial was terminated due to loss of insecticidal efficacy rather than safety concerns

title: A Cluster Randomized Trial of Delivery of Intermittent Preventive Treatment of Malaria in Pregnancy at the Community Level in Burkina Faso
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of IPTp (chemoprevention for malaria in pregnancy) with reported outcome results on coverage of IPTp doses and ANC visits.
design: cluster randomized, controlled trial, difference in differences analysis
comparator: standard practice (IPTp delivered at health facilities)
population: pregnant women
primary_outcome: Coverage of IPTp and ANC attendance
impact_summary: Community delivery of IPTp by CHWs led to a higher median number of IPTp doses received and higher IPTp3/IPTp4 coverage compared to standard facility-based delivery, though differences were not statistically significant for IPTp3/IPTp4 or ANC attendance.

title: Comparing drug regimens for clearance of malaria parasites in asymptomatic adults using PCR in Kilifi County, Kenya: an open-label randomised controlled clinical trial (MalPaC)
screening_reason: Open-label RCT of antimalarial drug regimens with reported outcome results on parasite clearance and acquisition in malaria-infected adults; malaria treatment is the primary purpose.
comparator: active comparator (three different anti-malarial drug regimens compared to each other)
population: asymptomatic adults
primary_outcome: Parasite clearance and acquisition of new Plasmodium falciparum infections assessed by 18s qPCR positivity over 84-day follow-up
impact_summary: Falciparum DNA remained detectable by PCR post-treatment with incomplete parasite clearance regardless of drug regimen, though the AP+AS regimen may have partially suppressed acquisition of new infections and reduced recrudescence compared to AS and SP+AS+PQ.
effect_metric: Odds ratio for qPCR positivity in post-treatment phase (AS and SP+AS+PQ vs AP+AS)
effect_estimate: OR=7.7 (AS vs AP+AS); OR=4.2 (SP+AS+PQ vs AP+AS)
safety_summary: Not reported in abstract

title: Community case management to accelerate access to healthcare in Mali: a realist process evaluation nested within a cluster randomized trial.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized trial with reported outcome results (mortality, care utilization) testing a malaria-relevant health system intervention (community case management, CHW deployment) in humans; process evaluation of completed trial with full results published.
comparator: fixed site-based passive CHW services (control arm)
population: children under 5 and pregnant women; also CHWs, health providers and community participants
primary_outcome: Under-5 mortality and healthcare utilization (children's 24-hour treatment-seeking and pregnant women's antenatal care visits)
impact_summary: Both arms saw doubled treatment-seeking and antenatal visits and halved under-5 mortality over 3 years compared with baseline, but proactive CHW home visits had only modest effects on care utilization and no effect on under-5 mortality compared with control.

title: Efficacy of a spatial repellent for control of malaria in Indonesia: a cluster-randomized controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of spatial repellent (transfluthrin) for malaria vector control with reported outcome results (infection incidence).
population: children aged 6 months to 5 years, after radical cure
primary_outcome: Time to first malaria infection and overall (total new) infections detected by monthly blood screening
impact_summary: The spatial repellent (transfluthrin) reduced malaria infection compared to placebo, but the overall effect across 24 clusters was not statistically significant, though subgroup analyses in higher-risk clusters showed significant protective effects.
effect_estimate: 27.7% (first infection) and 31.3% (overall infections) across 24 clusters; 33.3% and 40.9% in 19 clusters with baseline infection; 60% in 12 moderate-to-high-risk clusters
transmission_setting: low to moderate malaria transmission, Sumba, Indonesia

title: Effect of biological larviciding with Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis for malaria control on non-target vector mosquito species in rural Burkina Faso – A cluster randomized trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial of biological larviciding (Bacillus thuringiensis israelensis) for malaria vector control with reported outcome results on non-target mosquito species; vector-control trials are not subject to phase restrictions.
population: residents of rural villages and a semi-urban town in Northwestern Burkina Faso
primary_outcome: Reduction in non-target mosquito (Culex and Aedes) abundance due to larviciding interventions, measured via light trap captures
impact_summary: Larviciding against malaria mosquitoes had limited or no impact on Culex mosquitoes but reduced Aedes mosquito abundance by up to 34% when all public breeding sites were treated.
follow_up: one baseline and one intervention rainy season
transmission_setting: rural and semi-urban Burkina Faso, seasonal rainy-season transmission

title: Field performance of three mosquito collection methods for assessing the entomological efficacy of dual-active ingredient long-lasting insecticidal nets.
screening_reason: Cluster RCT with reported entomological outcomes evaluating dual-active ingredient LLINs (vector control) against standard LLINs; phase not applicable for vector-control trials.
population: Anopheles mosquitoes collected in households in trial clusters
primary_outcome: Density/number of Anopheles mosquitoes collected per method
impact_summary: All three mosquito collection methods (HLC, CDC light traps, PSC) detected fewer mosquitoes in the Interceptor G2 dual-active-ingredient LLIN arm compared to other trial arms, with HLC and PSC showing stronger evidence of this effect due to more frequent collection rounds.
effect_metric: mean vector density per method per night

title: Distance to Health Centers and Effectiveness of Azithromycin Mass Administration for Children in Niger: A Secondary Analysis of the MORDOR Cluster Randomized Trial.
screening_reason: Cluster RCT with reported results on azithromycin (chemoprevention) for malaria-related child mortality in Niger; secondary analysis of completed MORDOR trial with full outcome data.
population: children aged 1 to 59 months
primary_outcome: All-cause mortality (incidence) among children aged 1 to 59 months, monitored via population-based census of person-time at risk
impact_summary: Mass azithromycin administration reduced child mortality more among children living farther from primary health centers, with mortality reduction ranging from 0% at 0 km to 28% at 10 km distance.
effect_metric: mortality reduction (%) with azithromycin vs placebo by distance to health center
effect_estimate: 0% at 0 km, 4% at 1 km, 16% at 5 km, 28% at 10 km
safety_summary: Not reported in this secondary analysis focused on mortality and distance effect modification.

title: Effectiveness of smartphone-based Community Case Management on urgent referral, re-consultation and hospitalization of children under-5 in Malawi: Results of a cluster-randomized, stepped-wedge trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized stepped-wedge trial testing a malaria case management intervention (eCCM app) with reported outcome results on referral, re-consultation, and hospitalization.
population: children under-5 presenting with acute illness at village clinics
primary_outcome: Urgent referral to higher-level health facility
impact_summary: Children in the eCCM intervention phase were more likely to be urgently referred to higher-level health facilities than those in the control phase, with no significant increase in re-consultation or hospitalization rates after adjusting for time.
safety_summary: No apparent increase in hospital admissions or repeat consultations was observed with the eCCM intervention.

title: Impact of universal home visits on child health in Bauchi State, Nigeria: a stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial.
screening_reason: Stepped-wedge cluster RCT with reported outcome results on child health interventions including diarrhoea prevention and management, though malaria is not the primary focus—appears ineligible on malaria specificity grounds upon closer reading.
comparator: pre-intervention control (children in subsequent waves before intervention)
population: children 12-18 months old born to mothers visited during pregnancy, and their households
primary_outcome: prevalence and management of childhood diarrhoea and immunisation status
impact_summary: Universal home visits to pregnant women and their spouses reduced childhood diarrhoea prevalence and improved diarrhoea management, hygiene knowledge and practices, with only a slight, non-significant improvement in full immunisation.
safety_summary: Not reported

title: Spatial Effects of Permethrin-Impregnated Bed Nets on Child Mortality: 26 Years on, a Spatial Reanalysis of a Cluster Randomized Trial.
journal: The American journal of tropical medicine and hygiene
screening_reason: Cluster randomized trial of ITNs (vector control malaria intervention) with reported outcome results (child mortality reduction); phase not applicable for cluster trials.
population: children aged 6-59 months
primary_outcome: all-cause mortality in children
impact_summary: Permethrin-impregnated bed nets reduced all-cause child mortality by 17%, with additional evidence of a spatial spillover benefit to nearby non-users.

title: Antibiotic Review Kit for Hospitals (ARK-Hospital): a stepped wedge cluster randomised controlled trial
screening_reason: Cluster-randomised controlled trial with reported outcome results evaluating a hospital antibiotic stewardship intervention (behaviour change, not malaria-related); however, primary focus is antibiotic stewardship in general hospitalized populations, not malaria prevention, treatment, or diagnosis in humans.
comparator: usual care (pre-intervention/standard practice, before ARK implementation)
population: adult acute/non-elective medical hospital admissions
primary_outcome: monthly antibiotic defined-daily-doses (DDD) per acute/medical admission (organisation-level, superiority) and all-cause 30-day mortality (patient-level, non-inferiority, margin 5%)
impact_summary: The ARK intervention led to a sustained reduction in hospital antibiotic consumption without evidence of a related increase in mortality, and was concluded to be safe and effective.
effect_metric: year-on-year percentage change in antibiotic consumption (DDD per admission)
safety_summary: 30-day mortality showed weak, inconsistent immediate (-2.7%) and sustained (+3.0%) changes not related to magnitude of antibiotic reduction; 90-day mortality odds increased over time (+3.9%) but this was not observed in admissions before COVID-19 onset; length of stay was unaffected; mortality trends attributed to COVID-19 pandemic rather than the intervention.
funder: NIHR Programme Grants for Applied Research, RP-PG-0514-20015

title: Macrolide and Nonmacrolide Resistance with Mass Azithromycin Distribution.
journal: The New England journal of medicine
screening_reason: This is a published RCT with reported results comparing azithromycin mass distribution to placebo for a malaria-endemic population (sub-Saharan Africa childhood mortality context), with primary outcomes on gut resistome and antibiotic resistance measured at 36 and 48 months.
population: preschool children 1 to 59 months of age in villages receiving mass drug administration
primary_outcome: Ratio of macrolide-resistance determinants in the azithromycin group compared with the placebo group at 48 months
impact_summary: Villages receiving twice-yearly mass azithromycin distribution for 4 years had substantially higher levels of macrolide and nonmacrolide (including beta-lactam) antibiotic resistance determinants than villages receiving placebo.
effect_metric: ratio of macrolide-resistance determinants (azithromycin vs placebo)
effect_estimate: 7.5 times as high at 48 months (7.4 times as high at 36 months)
transmission_setting: sub-Saharan Africa, mass drug administration setting
safety_summary: Not specifically reported; study focused on antibiotic resistance outcomes rather than adverse events.
funder: Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation and others

title: Daily co-trimoxazole prophylaxis to prevent mortality in children with complicated severe acute malnutrition: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised placebo-controlled trial.
screening_reason: Multicentre double-blind RCT with reported mortality and safety outcomes testing co-trimoxazole prophylaxis for treatment of complicated severe acute malnutrition in children; malaria intervention focus (prophylaxis to prevent infections in malnourished children), Phase 3, results published.
population: children aged 60 days to 59 months without HIV admitted to hospital with complicated severe acute malnutrition
primary_outcome: Mortality, assessed each month for the first 6 months, then every 2 months for the second 6 months
impact_summary: Daily co-trimoxazole prophylaxis did not reduce mortality in children with complicated severe acute malnutrition without HIV compared with placebo.
safety_summary: 63 suspected grade 3 or 4 adverse events occurred in 57 (3%) children (31 co-trimoxazole, 32 placebo); incidence rate ratio 0.98 (95% CI 0.58-1.65); most common were urticarial rash, neutropenia (more common in co-trimoxazole group), and anaemia; one child in placebo group had fatal toxic epidermal necrolysis with concurrent Pseudomonas aeruginosa bacteraemia.

title: The global network antenatal corticosteroids trial: impact on stillbirth.
screening_reason: Cluster-randomized controlled trial with reported outcome results (stillbirth as pre-specified secondary outcome) evaluating an intervention (antenatal corticosteroids) in a maternal/neonatal health context, though malaria is not the primary focus.
place: India, Pakistan, Zambia, Kenya, Guatemala, Argentina
population: pregnant women at risk of preterm birth and their newborns
primary_outcome: stillbirth (pre-specified secondary outcome of the trial; primary trial outcome was 28-day neonatal mortality)
impact_summary: The antenatal corticosteroids intervention was associated with a non-significant increased risk of stillbirth overall, with a significant increase among term births and macerated stillbirths.
safety_summary: Increase in maternal infection likely more common in intervention clusters; differences in obstetric care favored control clusters; overall increase in neonatal mortality and stillbirth associated with the intervention.

title: Pharmacometric evaluation of pre-referral rectal artesunate in children with severe malaria.
screening_reason: Randomized controlled trial (crossover design) of malaria treatment intervention (rectal vs. intravenous artesunate) with reported pharmacokinetic and parasite clearance outcome results.
population: children with severe malaria
primary_outcome: Dihydroartemisinin plasma exposure and model-predicted early parasite clearance following rectal versus intravenous artesunate
impact_summary: Rectal artesunate produced similar dihydroartemisinin exposure and predicted parasite clearance over the first 12 hours compared to intravenous artesunate, supporting its use as a pre-referral intervention.

title: Duration and association with protection of NANP-repeat-specific and C-terminus-specific anti-circumsporozoite protein IgG responses following RTS,S/AS01E vaccination: an observational ancillary immunological study of a phase 3 clinical trial.
screening_reason: This is an ancillary immunological study nested within the phase 3 RTS,S/AS01E malaria vaccine RCT that reports outcome results (antibody kinetics and association with clinical malaria protection), with malaria vaccine as the primary intervention.
design: observational ancillary immunological study of a phase 3 clinical trial
population: children aged 5-17 months
primary_outcome: IgG antibody kinetics to circumsporozoite protein (NANP-repeat and C-terminus) and association with clinical malaria risk over 1 year
impact_summary: C-terminus-specific IgG responses to circumsporozoite protein were more durable than NANP-repeat-specific responses and were independently associated with reduced malaria risk, with antibody maintenance being a stronger predictor of protection than peak responses.
follow_up: 17 months after primary vaccination; 1 year malaria risk follow-up
funder: USA National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, National Institutes of Health; PATH and Malaria Vaccine Initiative; Spanish Ministerio de Economía y Competitividad; Instituto de Salud Carlos III; CERCA programme; Secretaria d'Universitats i Recerca del Departament d'Empresa i Coneixement, Generalitat de Catalunya
